Meanwhile, Union Minister Pralhad Joshi cited El Nino and red rot disease as causes of reduced sugar production, leading to temporary raw sugar imports to meet festival demand.

National Security Advisor Ajit Doval will visit Beijing for boundary discussions with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi ahead of President Xi Jinping's India visit. The talks aim to address border issues and maintain peace along the Line of Actual Control. Meanwhile, a Trinamool Congress leader was arrested on multiple charges including economic offences and arms procurement. Political tensions also flare within the Congress over remarks on ancient texts and women's rights, with Rahul Gandhi criticizing patriarchal views, prompting backlash from the BJP.

Isro chairman Dr V Narayanan announced India's plan to establish its own space station, the Bharatiya Antariksha Station, by 2035. The first module has been approved, and the initiative reflects India's growing capabilities in space technology. Narayanan highlighted the country's use of space-based applications across over 50 areas, including Earth observation and disaster mitigation. He also mentioned upcoming projects like the Gaganyaan human spaceflight mission. The announcement occurred during the third National Space Day celebrations, which commemorated India's lunar achievements, including the Chandrayaan-3 mission. Union Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat noted the expansion of private participation in the space sector and the reduction in time for space-related activities.

Chennai police are searching Odisha for a couple suspected of murdering and dismembering Hayathun Nisha, a 38-year-old woman from Jagatsinghpur. The severed body parts were found in a suitcase on a train near Agra. Police believe the suspects may have fled to Odisha after the crime. Investigators traced the suspects to a rented residence in Chennai, where more body parts were recovered. The case began when railway staff discovered the remains in a trolley bag on August 5.

Bill Ackman has significantly altered his investment fund Pershing Square's portfolio, exiting Alphabet, Universal Music Group, and Hertz while adding Netflix and other large-cap companies. The changes reflect a strategic shift toward firms with strong software and valuation fundamentals. Ackman's new fund, Pershing Square USA, has invested 95% of its capital, with a notable 5% allocated to Netflix. The fund also plans to launch a private equity arm focused on late-stage startups.

Canada terminated trade negotiations with the US in August 2026 after the Trump administration offered limited tariff relief. The US had imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, and Ottawa responded with retaliatory measures. The talks, which began in February 2025, aimed to address new US tariffs outside the USMCA framework, including Section 232, 301, and 338 tariffs. Canada sought exemptions and tariff cuts but found the US proposals too restrictive. Prime Minister Mark Carney called the terms 'uneconomic' and 'unfair,' emphasizing the need for balanced agreements. Ajay Srivastava of GTRI suggests India should prioritize clear, binding tariff concessions in its own negotiations with the US to avoid similar imbalances.

The S&P 500 Shiller CAPE ratio reached 40 in June 2026, marking the second time in 155 years that the measure has hit this level. The CAPE ratio, developed by Yale professor Robert Shiller, uses a 10-year average of inflation-adjusted earnings to assess stock valuations. Historically, the ratio has averaged around 15.7 from 1871 to 2000, with levels above 40 occurring only during the dot-com bubble in 1999 and the 1929 market crash. While high valuations can signal market risks, the current situation differs from past episodes as earnings are growing faster than valuations. Investors are advised to remain cautious, focusing on high-quality companies and maintaining cash reserves in case of market corrections.

Bill Ackman, managing Pershing Square, has significantly altered his investment portfolio in 2026 by selling major holdings in Alphabet, Universal Music Group, and Hertz, while acquiring six new stocks in financial services, entertainment, and healthcare. The shift reflects Ackman's strategy to move beyond the AI boom, focusing instead on undervalued sectors. Pershing Square USA, a new $5 billion fund, has invested 95% of its capital, leveraging market volatility to buy discounted assets. Ackman also expanded into private companies, planning a new venture fund to invest in late-stage private businesses. His new investments include Visa, Mastercard, Netflix, S&P Global, Intercontinental Exchange, and Alcon, which he believes offer long-term value outside the AI-focused market.

RMZ Corp has appointed Ankit Samdariya as managing director of equity capital markets to support its $35 billion expansion over five years. The real estate firm plans to fund developments through debt, equity, and an IPO. Samdariya, previously at LO-GOI Group, will focus on global partnerships with pension funds and asset managers. RMZ's expansion into commercial offices and data centres requires substantial institutional capital, with recent deals involving Blackstone, Mitsui Fudosan, and Brookfield. The company is also in talks to raise $400-500 million from global investors.

Hundreds of individuals, both named and unnamed, have been booked in Jharkhand following clashes between police and student protesters in Ranchi, Giridih, and Hazaribag. The protests, organized under the Jharkhand Public Service Commission-Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission Reforms Manch, were triggered by alleged irregularities in recruitment exams and subsequent legal actions. FIRs were filed against over 200 unidentified and 28 named individuals for obstructing government work and assaulting police. The state government canceled 44 exams conducted by a private firm, leading to legal challenges and a stay order from the High Court. Protests escalated when demonstrators attempted to burn effigies of Chief Minister Hemant Soren and Rahul Gandhi, resulting in confrontations with law enforcement and political workers.

Alibaba Group announced a HK$80 billion (₹95,000 crore) share sale in Hong Kong, the largest follow-on offering by a company on record, to fund its AI initiatives. The funds will support expanding AI infrastructure and enhancing full-stack AI capabilities. The offering, which includes 710 million shares at HK$112.70 each, marks Alibaba's first new share placement since its 2019 Hong Kong listing. The company's cloud and AI business saw a 45% revenue increase in the April-June quarter, with capital expenditure rising 75%. Alibaba's CEO, Eddie Wu Yongming, expects AI computing investments to break even within three years. The fundraising follows a 75% drop in quarterly net profit due to increased AI spending, while revenue rose 9% to ₹2.24 lakh crore. Alibaba's AI push includes expanding its Qwen language models and Zhenwu chips, which have served over 650 customers on Alibaba Cloud.

A madrasa student named Muntazir was assaulted on a train from Meerut to Deoband after refusing alcohol. A group of men, reportedly under the influence, offered him a drink, which he declined. He changed seats to avoid confrontation, but the men pursued him, verbally abused him, and physically attacked him, forcing him to disembark at Khatauli station. His phone and cash were allegedly stolen. Muntazir, who teaches at a madrasa, described the incident, noting that he was not a thief. The case is not isolated, as a cleric was killed in a similar incident in April. Officials have not yet released statements on the investigation, raising concerns about safety for religious minorities on public transport.

India's IT services sector is transforming as companies adopt outcome-based contracts to meet client demands for cost reductions and increased productivity. Major firms like Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) and Cognizant are moving away from hourly billing, with TCS reporting 80% of its finance and HR contracts now tied to performance outcomes. This shift is driven by AI's ability to automate tasks, reducing reliance on large employee bases and leveling the playing field for smaller firms. Clients are pushing for more value for less, with some demanding 25-30% lower prices while expecting faster delivery. While mid-sized firms are gaining traction through agility and flexible pricing, larger companies face challenges as they adjust to a more competitive landscape. TCS, despite its size, has seen subdued growth and is implementing layoffs, signaling a shift away from traditional hiring practices.

Heavy downpours in Brazil have disrupted the production of premium arabica coffee, affecting quality and availability. The rains washed ripe coffee cherries from trees, leaving beans exposed to contamination and mold, which compromises the aromatic profile sought by premium roasters like Starbucks and Illycaffe. Simão de Lima of Expocacer cooperative estimates 20% of cherries were washed off, compared to 5-7% normally. A second wave of rain in July forced growers to restart drying, further damaging quality. Arabica coffee futures have risen 35% since June, with fine Brazilian coffees commanding premiums. ICE standards for quality may drop to 10-15% of output, down from 30-35%. While Brazil's overall production is expected to be a record, the quality issues may reduce the supply of premium arabica, impacting global markets.

Pride Hotels, a Mumbai-based hospitality chain, is expanding its portfolio to 72 properties by 2027 through 32 new hotel contracts. The company's CEO, Satyen Jain, highlighted the focus on pilgrimage and leisure travel markets, noting rising holiday frequency and consumer preference for experiential travel. Pride Hotels plans to launch an IPO by December 2026, with a proposed issue size of Rs 1,000 crore, to fund renovations, debt repayment, and operational needs. The company is also exploring a new boutique brand, Pride Lux, while addressing rising operating costs through renewable energy investments and energy-efficient equipment. Chairman S P Jain identified licensing as a major challenge for the hospitality sector, calling for streamlined approval processes. The company remains focused on the domestic market for now, though it may explore international opportunities with significant Indian tourist traffic.

The first 100 days of V.D. Satheesan's government in Kerala have been marked by a series of controversial decisions and policy reversals, undermining public confidence. Despite initial optimism following a strong electoral victory, the UDF government has faced criticism for hasty decisions, including the implementation of the PM SHRI education scheme and the controversial sale of a port stake to Adani. These moves, which the UDF had previously opposed, have drawn backlash from both the public and opposition. The government's handling of internal party dynamics, including factional struggles within the Congress, has further complicated its governance. Meanwhile, the opposition, led by Pinarayi Vijayan, remains paralyzed, struggling to recover from its electoral defeat. The article highlights the challenges Satheesan faces as he navigates a politically turbulent landscape.

Mitra Phukan, an Assamese writer and translator, explores themes of conflict, identity, and societal issues through her diverse body of work. With 18 published volumes, including novels, short stories, and biographies, she delves into topics such as insurgency, cultural tensions, and personal relationships. Her writing, influenced by her training in Shastriya Sangeet and her academic background in English Literature, blends realism with creative imagination. Phukan's novel 'The Collector’s Wife' and short story collection 'The Greatest Assamese Stories Ever Told' reflect her engagement with regional and global audiences. She emphasizes the importance of translating Assamese literature to a wider readership, highlighting the richness of the region's literary tradition. Phukan also discusses the impact of insurgency on her life and work, portraying multidimensional tragedies with a humanistic perspective.

India initiated a climate readiness assessment for cities in 2019, using the Climate Smart Cities Assessment Framework (CSCAF) in three phases. The framework measured cities' readiness across five themes, including urban planning and waste management, with results showing national readiness at 30–34%. Despite progress, the assessment halted after Phase 3, leaving no current data on city climate readiness. The report highlights the importance of measurement in driving climate action, as it provides evidence for decision-making and accountability. However, without ongoing assessments, it is unclear if cities have improved their readiness or achieved climate outcomes. The lack of consolidated data on climate actions by Indian cities also remains a challenge, with calls for continued assessments and public disclosure of all climate initiatives.

Indigenous fruits are disappearing from local diets and landscapes due to urbanization, land-use changes, and the dominance of commercial crops. These fruits offer nutritional, medicinal, and ecological benefits, yet their decline is driven by a lack of research, limited market demand, and the preference for exotic, high-yield crops. Experts emphasize that creating demand through value addition, documentation, and community support can help conserve these fruits, but commercialization must remain sustainable and community-centred. In regions like Assam and Meghalaya, local communities report a reduction in traditional fruits, with some species becoming rare or extinct. Researchers highlight the importance of indigenous crops for food security and genetic diversity, urging the need for better documentation, research, and support for farmers and home gardeners to preserve these vital resources.

Drew Breunig discusses the transition in AI model development, noting that prior to Fable, improving coding tools felt unnecessary due to the rapid release of new models. He highlights Fable's exceptional performance, though its high cost made it less accessible compared to existing models like Opus, 5.6, K3, and GLM. Breunig emphasizes the growing consideration of where to allocate development efforts in light of Fable's emergence.

NVIDIA's AI safety and security teams emphasize the importance of integrating security into AI agent stacks as agents become more capable. They highlight the role of each layer in the agent stack, including models, harnesses, and secure runtimes, and stress the need for clear boundaries and control mechanisms. Recent incidents involving frontier agents operating beyond their intended boundaries underscore the challenges of securing long-horizon agents. NVIDIA's research on Agentic Variation Operators (AVO) demonstrates how harnesses can guide agent behavior effectively. The article outlines five design rules for maintaining security, including authoritative policy location, just-in-time access, and isolation. It also discusses the importance of infrastructure enforcement and the need for consistent security practices across different agent profiles.

The article features a cartoon illustrating Ella Baron's perspectives on artificial intelligence and the ongoing drought. The visual commentary highlights the intersection of technological advancement and environmental challenges. The piece uses satire to explore the implications of AI in addressing resource scarcity. The cartoon's imagery conveys a critical stance on current drought management strategies. The artwork underscores the need for innovative solutions in times of crisis.

The PyTorch Conference North America 2026, scheduled for October 20–21 in San Jose, California, has announced its keynote lineup. The event will feature sessions on PyTorch updates, Trainium integration, agent workloads, and open science. Keynote speakers include Mark Collier from the PyTorch Foundation, Alban Desmaison and Edward Yang from Meta, and representatives from Amazon Web Services, Red Hat, NVIDIA, and Google Cloud. The program also includes sponsored talks from Qualcomm and Cohere, as well as a keynote from the Agentic AI Foundation.

A study examines the trade-off between target data repetition and model performance in language model training. Researchers found that scarce target corpora can be reused 15–20 times, with optimal repetition depending on data size, compute budget, and model scale. They introduced a repetition-aware scaling law to determine effective mixture configurations for pretraining under data constraints. The work highlights the role of generic data in regularization and provides practical recommendations for data mixtures.

A study examines the prevalence and control of human-like behaviors in large language models (LLMs), analyzing 21,000 conversations from four models. Researchers found these behaviors vary across models and user factors, with human evaluators perceiving self-referential and relationship-building behaviors as less appropriate from LLMs. System prompts can influence these behaviors, though careful evaluation is needed to avoid unintended effects. The study recommends responsible LLM design and evaluation practices.

A study evaluates how different AI models benefit from agentic memory, finding that the optimal amount of memory varies by model tier. Stronger models with headroom perform best with full guideline sets, while weaker models benefit from curated, task-specific retrieval. Saturated models show no measurable gain. The research, conducted on eight models ranging from 30B to 745B parameters, highlights that memory is distilled from an agent's past trajectories and injected at inference time without weight updates. The study uses AppWorld, a benchmark with 585 multi-step tasks, to measure performance improvements in task and scenario goal completion. Curated retrieval proved both accurate and cost-effective, with gpt-oss-120b achieving +16.1pp task completion at only +5% token cost. The findings suggest that memory should be calibrated to the model's capabilities, with prompt caching and efficient retrieval strategies helping to manage costs in production.

Multi-vector embedding models, such as those from LightOn, use late interaction to improve retrieval by preserving token-level information. Unlike dense models that compress text into a single vector, these models retain one vector per token, allowing for more precise matching. This approach is particularly effective for visual document retrieval and complex queries with multiple requirements. The models can be loaded via the sentence-transformers library, with support for various checkpoint formats. Indexing and scoring use MaxSim to align query and document tokens, enhancing retrieval quality without sacrificing speed.

NVIDIA has partnered with SB Energy to develop the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus in Ohio, which will exclusively host NVIDIA AI compute infrastructure. OpenAI will be the primary customer, utilizing NVIDIA's DSX AI factory platform. The project includes a $1.5 billion investment by NVIDIA in SB Energy, supporting the development of 8 IT-GW of AI capacity. SB Energy will build and operate the data center under a 20-year lease to OpenAI. The campus is expected to create tens of thousands of jobs and invest hundreds of millions in the local community. NVIDIA's investment aims to support SB Energy's growth and its commitments to Ohio, with the project planned to come online in phases starting in 2028.

Google Research scientists demonstrate PhotoScan, a deep learning framework that estimates body composition from smartphone photos, achieving accuracy comparable to DXA scans in predicting insulin resistance. The study highlights the limitations of BMI and traditional methods, showing that PhotoScan can measure body fat percentage, A/G ratio, and V/S ratio with high precision. Validated across clinical cohorts, PhotoScan outperforms smartwatch-based BIA sensors and offers a scalable, non-invasive alternative to DXA. The research shows that integrating body composition data from smartphone images improves insulin resistance prediction, with AUROC scores nearly matching clinical DXA data. The findings suggest a promising path for accessible, non-invasive screening of metabolic risk.

The UGM Indosat NVIDIA AI Technology Center, Indonesia's first university-based AI center, was launched to develop local AI talent and address national challenges. The initiative, supported by the government, Indosat, and NVIDIA, aims to foster AI innovation in healthcare, agriculture, and disaster response. The center provides access to advanced computing resources and global expertise, enabling researchers to tackle issues like tuberculosis detection, precision farming, and disaster preparedness. Officials emphasized the importance of AI sovereignty and economic growth through local talent development.

IBM researchers have introduced DocLang, a markup language designed to enhance AI's ability to understand and process documents. DocLang, a constrained dialect of XML, aims to reduce latency and inference costs by providing a clear structure for AI models to interpret document content. It addresses the limitations of existing formats like PDF and DOCX, which were not designed for machine understanding. By encoding semantics, layout, and reading order, DocLang offers a standardized representation that improves accuracy and consistency. The language is open and governed by the Linux Foundation, with support from tools like Docling and ABBYY's FineReader Engine. While challenges remain in adoption and implementation, IBM argues that DocLang's benefits, including reduced hallucination and improved governance, make it a valuable addition to AI workflows.

Ai2 and Hugging Face are expanding their collaboration to improve access and deployment of open AI resources. The partnership includes tripling storage capacity on the Hugging Face Hub to nearly two petabytes and removing rate limits for traffic. Since 2024, over 50 million models and datasets have been downloaded from the Hub. The collaboration supports the release of training data, intermediate checkpoints, and evaluation tools, enabling researchers to reproduce and build upon Ai2's work. Hugging Face's infrastructure will support future projects like multimodal models and scientific agents. The partnership also integrates Ai2's models into tools like LeRobot, allowing developers to use and fine-tune them. Hugging Face highlights the impact of Ai2's open research, including the olmOCR-Bench benchmark and climate-focused models like HiRO-ACE. The collaboration aims to create an ecosystem where anyone can access, inspect, and experiment with AI tools, driven by Hugging Face's infrastructure and Ai2's open, science-focused approach.

AWS has announced 34 research grants under the Build on Trainium program, offering $110 million in compute credits to support AI innovation. The grants focus on responsible AI, including topics like safety, sustainability, and synthetic data. Recipients gain access to AWS resources, datasets, and expert support. The initiative aims to democratize AI research through academic collaboration. The program emphasizes scalable access to Trainium chips for large-scale AI projects, with examples from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of Washington.

Shieldstral, a 3B open-weights multimodal safety classifier, outperforms models up to 7x its size by framing content moderation as a policy-adaptive question-answering task. Unlike traditional guardrail models, it accepts plain-language policies at inference time, unifying text and image safety evaluation without retraining. Released under Apache 2.0, it delivers calibrated safety scores across diverse benchmarks while running efficiently on a single 16GB NVIDIA GPU. The model processes requests by framing them as binary question-answering tasks, with three components: an instruction defining safety criteria, a yes/no question, and the content to evaluate. This approach allows policies to be adapted at deployment time without retraining, offering flexibility across text, image, and multimodal content. Shieldstral was trained on heterogeneous data sources, calibrated for strictness, and fine-tuned using LoRA and SLERP merging techniques. It is part of the Open Secure AI Alliance and is available for download under Apache 2.0.

The Orchard framework introduces an open-source solution for scalable agentic AI, designed to overcome infrastructure bottlenecks in research. It features Orchard Env, a Kubernetes-based environment service that supports multiple agent types and tasks without modification. The framework includes three domain-specific training recipes—Orchard-SWE, Orchard-GUI, and Orchard-Claw—demonstrating that small open-weight models can achieve strong results on complex tasks. Orchard-SWE reaches 69.7% on SWE-bench Verified using about 3 billion parameters, while Orchard-GUI achieves 68.4% across web navigation benchmarks. The project also provides training data and evaluation methods to aid the research community. By enabling training directly within real deployment harnesses, Orchard reduces the gap between research and practical application, allowing agents to be trained and evaluated in the same environments they will operate in.

Google is introducing a new feature that allows users to instantly customize their Discover feed by specifying exact topics or links they want to see or skip. The update, available via a three-dot menu in the Discover feed, lets users describe their preferences directly to the chat. For example, users can request long-form content on smart home tech while skipping product news. The feature adjusts the feed immediately and remembers user preferences. It is set to roll out in the coming days on the Google app.

A division of the UK's National Health Service (NHS), NHS Greater Manchester, has refused to adopt Palantir's federated data platform (FDP), citing trust in its homegrown system and skepticism about Palantir's technology. The NHS is facing pressure to terminate its $400 million contract with Palantir by February 2025, as political and public concerns over the company's role in data management and its use in military contexts grow. While Palantir claims the FDP improves patient care and hospital efficiency, critics argue it lacks the public trust and flexibility of local systems like the ADSP used in Greater Manchester. The debate highlights tensions between centralized data solutions and regional autonomy, with some warning that breaking the contract could undermine progress in healthcare data integration.

The diesel crisis, exacerbated by Middle East conflict and refinery damage, is causing severe global economic impacts. Refinery capacity in the Middle East has been reduced by a fifth, with 9.6 million barrels daily knocked out by hostilities. Ukraine's drone strikes on Russian refineries have further tightened the market, leaving the second-largest diesel exporter closed. Diesel prices in Europe have surged 70% from pre-war levels, now exceeding jet fuel prices. U.S. fuel exports have hit a record 1.9 million barrels daily, but are drawing down already tight inventories. Analysts warn that global diesel stocks are already tight, and the situation is expected to worsen as demand rises with colder weather. The IEA reports global refinery runs are 5.1 million barrels daily below last year's levels, with demand destruction forcing inflation risks to rise.

The Electrek Podcast discusses Tesla's decision to discontinue the Solar Roof, the launch of the Cybercab, and coverage of the Genesis GV90. The episode, sponsored by GM, highlights EV charging solutions and includes a live stream on YouTube. It also mentions an accompanying post and a Patreon for supporting the content.

GlobalData predicts Asia-Pacific will account for 55% of global biopower capacity by 2035. The report highlights growing renewable energy adoption in the region. Analysts note increased investment in biomass projects. The forecast includes projections for capacity growth across key countries. The study emphasizes policy support for sustainable energy solutions.

New Zealand's solar capacity surpassed 1 GW by the end of 2025, driven by utility-scale projects. The Ministry of Business, Innovation & Employment reported a 52% increase in solar capacity during 2025, with seven solar plants of 9 MW or larger coming online. The country's first grid-connected solar park contributed significantly to this growth. Renewables now account for 9 GW of electricity generation, with solar making up 9.1% of that. The government also aims to simplify regulations for small-scale solar installations.

Van Oord has completed the installation of monopiles at the 1.5 GW offshore wind project in Poland. The company, which specializes in offshore wind construction, said the work marks a significant milestone in the project's development. The monopile installation is a critical phase in the construction of the wind farm, which is expected to contribute substantially to Poland's renewable energy goals. The project is part of a larger initiative to expand offshore wind capacity in the Baltic Sea region. The completion of this phase brings the project closer to full operational readiness.

Romania is accelerating the deployment of battery energy storage systems (BESS) through several new projects. GEN-I Sonce began construction of a 55 MW / 220 MWh BESS in Gheorgheni, with Waldevar Energy as the contractor. Enery acquired a 400 MW / 400 MWh BESS project near Constanța, set to be connected via underground power lines. Nova Power and Gas is preparing to start construction of a 200.6 MWh BESS, part of a larger 802.4 MWh project. Hidroelectrica is involved in multiple BESS initiatives, including a 90 MW / 360 MWh system near Retezat. Repono and Gunvor Group plan a 202 MW / 404 MWh BESS in Argeș county. R.Power's 127 MW / 254 MWh Scorniçesti BESS is under construction with financing from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development. Transelectrica connected 77 MW / 150 MWh of BESS to the high-voltage network, contributing to Romania's total electricity production capacity exceeding 20 GW.

The Indian stock market showed little movement on August 21, 2026, with green energy stocks performing mixed. Kabra Extrusion and Olectra Greentech saw significant gains, while Praj Industries and Sterling and Wilson Renewable Energy declined. Battery and energy storage stocks also faced pressure. Reliance Industries and Larsen & Toubro showed minimal changes, reflecting stock-specific investor activity in the green energy sector.

Zeno Power Systems will test its americium-241 radioisotope heater unit (RHU) on the Blue Ghost mission, designed to keep spacecraft operational during the extreme lunar night. The mission, part of NASA's CLPS initiative, will demonstrate technology for sustained lunar operations. The RHU provides passive thermal energy without solar power, addressing the challenge of extreme temperature swings on the Moon. Zeno's payload includes a dedicated platform with multiple subsystems. Firefly's first Blue Ghost mission in 2025 successfully tested lunar operations during both day and night. The announcement coincided with a US presidential memorandum to boost space transport policy.

The Energy Commission of Malaysia revised NEM 3.0 guidelines for solar PV installations, covering residential and government premises. Under NEM Rakyat, residential consumers can install up to 5 kW or 12.5 kW for single- and three-phase connections, respectively. Government premises under NEM GOMEn have a maximum of 1,000 kW. The guidelines require solar systems to be connected via internal distribution boards and mandate Net Energy Metering Assessment Studies for projects over 72 kW. Battery storage and smart inverters with grid-support features are now allowed. Export credits for electricity sent to TNB are available for 10 years, after which systems must operate under a pure self-consumption model. Consumers retain environmental and carbon credits from their installations.

The New Jersey Board of Public Utilities (NJBPU) has proposed a 150MW residential battery storage initiative as part of its Garden State Energy Storage Programme (GSESP). The plan aims to integrate clean energy resources, lower costs, and improve grid resilience by enabling residents to install behind-the-meter (BTM) batteries. Residents would receive annual incentive payments over 10 years for providing grid support during peak demand periods. The proposal outlines a framework for performance-based compensation and is expected to complement the NJBPU's virtual power plant and grid modernization efforts. The NJBPU also anticipates using the proposal as a model for future storage deployments, including commercial and industrial-scale projects.

Despite the Trump administration's efforts to hinder renewable energy, solar and storage projects accounted for 90% of new U.S. power plant construction in the first half of 2026, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration. Solar-plus-storage became the grid's 'workhorse,' with Texas leading the way. New Mexico's SunZia wind project and Arizona's solar-plus-storage growth contributed significantly. While gas-fired facilities could challenge renewables, they remain uncertain. Renewables remain cheaper than fossil fuels and free of carbon emissions.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro signed an executive order on August 18 imposing legally binding requirements on data centers with peak demand over 25 MW. The order mandates compliance with energy affordability, transparency, workforce development, and environmental standards as conditions for permits, tax benefits, and utility regulation. It removes data centers from the PA Permit Fast Track Program and requires developers to document local approvals and meet clean energy targets. The initiative, part of the Governor’s Responsible Infrastructure Development (GRID) framework, aims to shift costs and risks to developers, prevent speculative projects, and ensure community engagement. The order also directs the Public Utility Commission to address data center curtailment and cost allocation during grid emergencies. While legislative efforts to codify GRID have stalled in the Senate, the executive action seeks to enforce strict guardrails on data center development.

Pennsylvania Governor Josh Shapiro has issued an executive order requiring large data centers to secure their own power resources or face potential grid curtailments during emergencies. The order aligns with a proposal by grid operator PJM Interconnection, which aims to prevent data centers from driving up power prices. Under the plan, data centers over 25 megawatts must either pay for their own energy capacity or risk being cut off during peak grid stress. The Pennsylvania Public Utility Commission is tasked with implementing rules to ensure data centers cover costs associated with grid upgrades and emergency power auctions. The order also mandates that data centers increase their use of carbon-free energy sources over the next decade. While the policy does not block data centers from operating, it introduces preferential treatment for those complying with the new requirements.

Fast-fashion company Shein plans to raise up to HK$13.86bn through its Hong Kong IPO on 1 September, offering 280 million shares priced between HK$47.60 and HK$49.50. This would value the company at nearly $27bn, significantly lower than its $100bn private valuation in 2022. The IPO follows failed attempts to list in the US and London due to regulatory challenges. Shein reported a $99m quarterly loss in July, attributing it to slowed sales after Trump removed import duty exemptions. The company faces ongoing uncertainty from US-China tariff tensions.

A large forest fire is threatening homes near residential areas in Mamak, Ankara. The fire is burning close to populated regions, raising concerns for nearby residents. Authorities are monitoring the situation as the blaze continues. The incident highlights the risk of wildfires in urban outskirts. No official details on the cause or containment efforts were provided.

Exit polls indicate Kazakhstan's pro-Tokayev Adilet party is expected to secure around 70% of the vote in parliamentary elections. This result would strengthen President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's control over the country, which is a major oil, uranium, and minerals exporter with close ties to Russia and China.

The UK government has launched a review of business rates for pubs and hotels, led by Jerry Schurder, with a report due in March 2027. The review aims to create a fairer system, following a 20% rate cut announced for pubs in England. Pub groups argue they face disproportionately high bills, citing the Fair Maintainable Trade valuation method. The review will feed into the 2029 rates revaluation, with calls for broader reforms and increased relief for small businesses. Critics, including the Shadow Chancellor, accuse the government of delaying action on a sector already struggling with tax hikes and regulation.

Donald Trump criticized Canada after U.S.-Canada trade talks collapsed, leading to a trade war. The U.S. imposed 50% tariffs on $20 billion in Canadian goods, prompting Canada to vow dollar-for-dollar retaliation. Both sides blamed each other for the breakdown, with Trump accusing Canada of benefiting from U.S. statehood without the responsibilities. The tariffs could impact 40% of Canadian small exporters, with some facing revenue drops of 50% or more. The dispute has strained U.S.-Canadian relations, affecting tourism and raising concerns about the future of the USMCA trade pact. Canadian Prime Minister Justin Trudeau called the situation a war, while U.S. trade representative Jamieson Greer stated the tariffs were a response to Canada's retaliatory measures.

Canada's trade negotiations with the US collapsed as the US imposed 50% tariffs on $20bn of Canadian goods. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the deal, citing last-minute US demands that threatened Canada's sovereignty. The dispute centers on US alcohol bans in Canada, which triggered initial tariffs. Observers suggest the talks failed due to the Trump administration's prioritization of its own interests over global economic coordination. Carney vowed to match US tariffs dollar for dollar, signaling a deepening trade war. Concerns grew as Canadian provinces were urged to reintroduce US alcohol to shelves in exchange for lower tariffs, prompting criticism from provincial leaders. Analysts warn that negotiations with the Trump administration are inherently unstable and prone to sudden breakdowns.

The Federal Reserve Board has approved National Westminster Bank Plc's application to open a representative office in Stamford, Connecticut. The announcement was made on August 20, 2026. The approval allows the London-based bank to establish a presence in the U.S. market.

The Federal Reserve Board announced enforcement actions against Stephanie R. Kilbert, a former Regions Bank employee in Birmingham, Alabama, and Crystal A. Wykle, a former United Community Bank employee in Greenville, South Carolina, for misappropriating customer funds. Both individuals faced consent prohibitions as part of the actions. The Board provided a link for additional enforcement actions but did not specify further details.

Federal Reserve official Lisa D. Cook warns that persistent inflation remains a significant risk despite signs of economic stability. She notes that the U.S. economy has not reached the 2 percent inflation target in over five years, with current annual inflation near its highest level since 2023. Cook attributes recent inflationary pressures to two unanticipated shocks: the Middle East conflict, which has driven up energy prices and may affect other goods, and increased capital expenditures tied to AI infrastructure, which has caused price increases for tech equipment and utilities. While the labor market shows stability with an unemployment rate of 4.2 percent, Cook acknowledges challenges for new entrants and concerns about AI's impact on jobs. She emphasizes that the Federal Reserve will continue to monitor data and is prepared to act if disinflation does not occur soon, reiterating her commitment to returning inflation to target. Cook also highlights that while inflation expectations remain anchored, the Fed must remain vigilant in its policy actions.

At the third annual Financial Inclusion Conference, Federal Reserve Board Governor Bowman emphasized the importance of responsible innovation in expanding financial access. He stated that banks, through innovation, can build a more inclusive financial system by lowering costs, expanding product availability, and promoting competition. The Federal Reserve acknowledged its role in encouraging responsible innovation while maintaining a safe banking system, stressing that the decision to innovate lies with individual banks. Bowman highlighted the growing use of artificial intelligence in banking, noting its potential to expand credit access for underserved populations. However, he cautioned about the legal compliance challenges associated with AI in credit decisions. The Federal Reserve emphasized the need for clear regulatory guidance and flexibility for smaller banks, while also ensuring appropriate oversight for higher-risk AI applications. The Financial Stability Board recently published a report on responsible AI adoption, offering practical guidance for financial institutions.

Sallie Mae is offering the highest CD rate of 4.35% APY for a 3-year term as of August 23, 2026. CD rates vary by institution, with longer-term CDs historically offering higher rates, though this trend has reversed in the current economic climate. The article explains how APY affects earnings, using examples to illustrate interest accumulation over time. It also outlines different CD types, including bump-up, no-penalty, jumbo, and brokered CDs, noting their features and potential trade-offs.

A recent two-day session at Anthropic focused on revising the constitution for Claude, with participants emphasizing the need for legal analogies. Key points included drawing from case law and the Talmud rather than the Torah, developing secondary literature on AI constitutions, and involving diverse AIs and human adjudicators for oversight. The discussion aimed to ensure Claude's alignment with its constitutional principles through structured evaluation and judicial review.

The Freedom 250 Grand Prix, an IndyCar race on Washington, D.C.'s National Mall, is the first and potentially last event of its kind, celebrating the nation's 250th birthday. Organizers note the race's unique challenges, including a 1.7-mile course with seven sharp turns and a 250-mile total distance, which poses overtaking difficulties. The event, planned in just seven months, faces logistical and legal hurdles, including congressional approval for the route. While Penske Corp. covers most costs, the government funds security expenses. The race, which includes free general admission tickets, is expected to draw around 140,000 spectators daily. Critics question the event's connection to the controversial Freedom 250 organization, though organizers deny any affiliation. The race concludes with plans for dismantling structures by mid-September, with the 250th anniversary celebrations continuing through 2026.

Investors sold stocks and bonds as government efforts to control borrowing costs faced limited success. The Treasury Department attempted to stabilize bond yields by buying back government debt, but yields rebounded. Carl Tannenbaum of Northern Trust cited three factors driving up bond yields: growing national debt, persistent inflation, and increased demand for long-term borrowing from tech companies building AI infrastructure. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent argued the economy is strong and inflation is temporary, but investors remained skeptical. The bond-buying program, set to end after midterms, was deemed too small and short-term by analysts. Rising yields are pushing up mortgage rates and other borrowing costs, affecting consumers and businesses.

Singaporean Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced a childcare support package to address the country's record-low birth rate and rising family pressures. The plan includes a SG$10,000 baby gift for each child, increased paid childcare leave, and reduced subsidized childcare fees to SG$150 monthly. Wong emphasized the need for a fundamental shift in family support during his National Day Rally Speech.

Alibaba's Hong Kong-listed shares are expected to open 8% lower on Monday following the company's announcement of a $10.2 billion share placement. The offering, priced at HK$112.70 per share, totals HK$80 billion and aims to fund artificial intelligence development.

SoftBank Group plans a $6.3 billion retail bond sale in Japan to fund its OpenAI investments. The 7-year bonds, priced on Sept. 4 with a coupon range of 4.3%-4.9%, are part of the company's efforts to support its $60 billion commitment to ChatGPT developer OpenAI. The offering marks SoftBank's third retail bond sale this year, following previous raises of ¥418 billion and ¥260 billion. The move follows a surge in quarterly profit driven by OpenAI valuation gains and a revised stable outlook from S&P Global Ratings.

The article highlights the psychological impact of ongoing air raid alerts on Ukrainian civilians, describing how the constant repetition has numbed people. It notes the challenges of daily life under sustained bombardment, with residents expressing exhaustion and a sense of helplessness. The piece emphasizes the emotional toll of living in a state of perpetual alert, without providing specific details on the source of the information or direct quotes from individuals.

A report by housing advocacy group Everybody's Home reveals that renting a unit now costs more than half the median take-home pay of a single worker in every Australian capital city. For someone earning $70,000, median Sydney rent would take 69 per cent of their weekly pay, while even Adelaide, the cheapest capital, would cost more than half their income. The 2026 Priced Out report found apartments nationally cost $614 per week, making up 56 per cent of the take-home income of someone earning $70,000. The group calls for more social housing and rent increase limits, noting that even high earners face significant rental stress. The report highlights Sydney, Perth, and the Gold Coast as the most expensive rental markets, with rents rising by about 10 per cent annually. Advocacy spokesperson Maiy Azize emphasized the need for government intervention to address the housing crisis.

Australia is developing new rare earth refineries to reduce reliance on Chinese imports. The initiative aims to boost domestic processing capabilities. The government is supporting infrastructure projects in key regions. Industry experts highlight strategic importance of securing supply chains. The move is part of broader efforts to enhance mineral processing independence.

Israeli authorities have threatened assassinations and evacuations in Gaza following reports of children's kites reaching Israeli communities. The Israeli army stated that four kites recovered near Nahal Oz contained no suspicious materials and posed no danger. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz warned of increased operations against those responsible for launching kites, balloons, or drones from Gaza. Hamas and Palestinian analysts criticized the threats as fabricated pretexts for further aggression, with one analyst questioning how a nuclear power could fear children's toys. The Israeli military has continued daily ceasefire violations since October 2025, resulting in significant civilian casualties.

The UK government has announced an independent review to assess business rate valuations for pubs and hotels in England and Wales, aiming to create a fairer system. The review, led by Jerry Schurder, will report by March 2027 and consider valuations before the 2029 revaluation date. Andy Burnham has proposed a 20% rate cut for hospitality venues starting April next year. Industry leaders welcomed the initiative, citing the significant burden of business rates on struggling businesses. The government plans to reform business rates, including small business relief, at John Healey’s first budget on 28 October.

Israel warned Hamas on August 24, 2026, that it would escalate operations in Gaza if launches of kites, drones, and balloons toward Israel continued. Israeli media reported that four kites were found near the Gaza border on August 23, 2026, with one shot down by the army, bringing the total recovered in recent days to around 10. The Israeli military believes Hamas was behind the launches, which did not carry explosives, and may have been testing Israel's response. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz stated that the IDF would intensify operations against those responsible if the launches continued. Hamas denied responsibility, with a political bureau member claiming the kites were launched by children seeking normalcy. Hamas also accused Israel of using the incidents as a pretext for airstrikes in central Gaza, which killed three people according to Gaza’s civil defence rescue service.

Iran announced the discovery of over 200 billion cubic metres of natural gas in Fars province, with 160 billion cubic metres potentially recoverable. The find occurs as the country's energy sector faces disruption from US-Israeli strikes on infrastructure. Petroleum Minister Mohsen Paknejad described the gas as sweet, reducing operational costs. Bloomberg noted new production from the site would likely take years. The strikes have targeted Iran's energy facilities and transport routes since late February.

Uzbekistan and Azerbaijan deepened their economic and strategic partnership by signing a Treaty on Eternal Friendship and setting a $1bn trade target by 2030. The agreement, signed during President Ilham Aliyev's state visit to Tashkent, marks a significant step in their bilateral relations. The two nations also launched joint projects in banking, energy, tourism, and mining, including the establishment of the Azerbaijan-Uzbekistan Investment Company. Trade between the countries reached $795mn in 2025, with further growth in the first half of 2026. Both leaders emphasized strengthening connectivity through the Middle Corridor and the Trans-Caspian network, aiming to boost freight traffic and logistics infrastructure. Additionally, they agreed to co-host the 2027 FIFA U-20 World Cup and initiated cultural and educational collaborations.

US President Donald Trump accused Canada of seeking 'the benefits of being a State, without being one' after trade talks collapsed, leading to new 50% US tariffs on Canadian goods. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney called the tariffs a 'miscalculation' and announced matching retaliatory measures from 8 September. Both leaders blamed each other for last-minute changes, with Carney stating Canada would not accept the US terms. The trade war threatens a $20bn worth of Canadian imports, including dairy and electronics. Canadian provinces and political leaders expressed support for Carney, warning of economic impacts. The dispute follows a failed USMCA renewal attempt, with Carney calling the trade collapse 'certainly not good news' for the North American free trade pact.

Bushfires have destroyed over 10,000 hectares of Burundi's Ruvubu National Park, with park rangers struggling to contain the flames due to limited resources. The fires, which have increased in frequency since late July, are suspected to be set by poachers seeking firewood or grazing land. Park chief manager Marc Bakundintwari noted trails leading to Tanzania may be used by individuals to ignite fires. With only 45 staff managing a 50,800-hectare park, the fires have consumed one-fifth of the protected area. The park, established in 1980, is home to diverse wildlife including 44 mammal species, 425 bird species, and Nile crocodiles.

Mykhailo Fedorov, Ukraine's former defense minister, criticized the government's governance system and called for elections despite ongoing war, sparking political debate. Fedorov's speech highlighted systemic corruption and the lack of elections since 2019, positioning him as a potential political rival to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The article notes that Fedorov's address aimed to consolidate political capital from protests demanding his reinstatement. Analysts suggest Fedorov is positioning himself as an independent political force, though no outright opposition to Zelenskyy is evident. The National Anti-Corruption Bureau launched investigations into a corruption scandal involving high-ranking officials, including Zelenskyy's deputy chief of staff, Iryna Mudra. Despite public support, Fedorov's chances of running for president depend on the possibility of holding elections, which requires a stable ceasefire—a condition he did not address in his speech.

An Iranian parliamentary speaker stated that U.S. economic sanctions against Iran demonstrate military failure. He argued that Washington has shifted to economic warfare due to its inability to prevail militarily. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the U.S. approach 'economic terrorism.' U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned of severe economic consequences for countries engaging with Iran, raising concerns about China's role. Analysts suggest Iran's leadership prioritizes survival over economic stability amid sanctions.

The Indian IPO market is experiencing a surge with 10 offerings this week, aiming to raise over Rs 3,500 crore. Symbiotec Pharmalab is the largest, seeking Rs 1,757 crore, followed by Lumino Industries and Skyways Air Services with targets of Rs 700 crore and Rs 583 crore respectively. The SME segment will see four IPOs raising collectively around Rs 183 crore. This follows a strong August with 20 mainboard IPOs raising Rs 20,850 crore and 18 SME IPOs contributing over Rs 941 crore. So far in 2026, 59 companies have raised Rs 72,000 crore through IPOs.

The Reserve Bank of India's hawkish Monetary Policy Committee minutes and rising oil prices are influencing the rupee and bond yields. India received $72.8 billion in forex inflows, providing a buffer for currency management. Analysts note that the 10-year yield floor is at 6.87%-6.88%, which could rise with more crude shocks. US Treasury yields fluctuated after a buyback announcement, with the 10-year yield dropping to 4.66% before recovering. The rupee's movement is heavily impacted by energy prices and US rate changes, with the RBI intervening to counter upward pressure on USDINR.

The Supreme Court of India clarified that changes in revenue records do not create or end property ownership. A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Augustine George Masih quashed a Madhya Pradesh High Court order that resolved a title dispute based solely on revenue records. The court emphasized that title must be established through independent evidence, not just revenue entries. It noted that while revenue records have fiscal significance, they do not confer or remove proprietary rights. The court also stated that the statutory presumption of correctness for revenue entries is rebuttable and must be weighed with other evidence.

India's ethanol blending program is facing scrutiny as it diverts subsidized rice from the food security system to ethanol distilleries at a 40% lower price. The government procures rice at a minimum support price (MSP) using taxpayer funds and sells it to ethanol producers at a significantly reduced rate, despite ethanol remaining costlier than petrol. This has sparked concerns about who is subsidizing whom and the impact on food security. The program aims to reduce petroleum imports and save foreign reserves, but its economics are questionable. The government has mandated that 40% of ethanol production must come from surplus rice stocks held by the Food Corporation of India (FCI), with experts arguing that broken rice is still fit for consumption. The program has created a surplus ethanol capacity of 700 crore litres, but the cost of ethanol remains higher than crude oil, making the economic viability of the program uncertain.

Joshua Aviles, a US Navy sailor on the USS Abraham Lincoln, shared on Facebook that his father, Luis Manuel Aviles Roa, a Nicaraguan national, was arrested by ICE during a traffic stop in Florida. The DHS confirmed the arrest, stating the man entered the country illegally and faces deportation. Aviles expressed emotional distress, highlighting his father's lawful status and the impact on his mental health during a prolonged deployment. The incident reflects a broader trend of immigration enforcement affecting military families under the current administration. DHS emphasized that military service does not exempt individuals from immigration laws.

The emerging-market carry trade, which involves borrowing in low-yield currencies like the US dollar and investing in higher-yield currencies such as the Turkish lira, has achieved its longest winning streak since 2008, returning 22% over the past seven quarters. This outperforms returns from US Treasuries and other global bond classes. The trade benefits from a weakening dollar against emerging-market currencies and high local bond yields, with Turkey and Colombia offering particularly attractive returns despite currency volatility.

A Panama-flagged cargo ship carrying 72,000 tonnes of iron ore sank off the Odisha coast in the Bay of Bengal, leaving 22 seafarers missing and two rescued. The vessel, MV Ocean Winner, departed Paradip Port on Friday and reportedly sank in deep waters on Saturday. Officials stated that the crew included 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmar citizens, and one Bangladeshi national. Rescue operations, involving the Indian Coast Guard, Navy, and merchant vessels, are underway to locate the missing crew. The ship developed a list and sank within eight minutes, according to survivors. The cause of the sinking remains under investigation, with possibilities including adverse weather, cargo issues, or mechanical failure. Authorities are also examining the loss of the vessel from tracking systems.

Crude oil prices fell over 1% on Monday as investors anticipated new US sanctions against Iran, which could disrupt Middle East oil supplies. Brent crude dropped $1.22 to $93.17 per barrel, while WTI crude fell $1.20 to $85.86 per barrel. The decline followed a week of gains after US-Iran peace talks stalled, limiting oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned of 'toughest sanctions in history' against Iran, while President Trump threatened sanctions on countries trading with Tehran. A firm raised its Brent price forecast for the quarter to $86 per barrel, citing continued production disruptions and increased Chinese demand.

Max Verstappen crashed during the Dutch Grand Prix, ending his race early after losing control in the first lap. The incident triggered a red flag and delayed the event. Lando Norris capitalized on the chaos, overtaking Kimi Antonelli to win the race and keep his title hopes alive. Norris' victory moved him into fourth in the championship standings, while Antonelli extended his lead over other contenders.

A study by the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) reveals that Gen Z traders in the derivatives market experience higher loss rates compared to older investors. Around 89% of traders below 30 incurred losses in FY26, compared to 81% of those above 60. The report highlights a shift in the retail derivatives market, with increased participation from non-metro areas and lower-income groups. About 75% of individual traders earn less than ₹5 lakh annually, contributing to 53% of aggregate losses despite accounting for only 43% of turnover. The study also notes that younger investors show greater risk appetite relative to their broader investment behavior.

The article discusses India's strategy to transition from importing medical devices to becoming a global medtech manufacturing hub. It highlights the need to move beyond assembly and focus on creating high-value, technology-driven products. Key points include the importance of developing local component manufacturing, investing in R&D for innovation, and improving quality to meet international standards. The article also emphasizes collaboration between startups, academia, and established firms to support innovation. India's medical devices market is valued at $16 billion, with exports rising from $2.5 billion to $4.1 billion. The goal is to increase the share of sophisticated, technology-intensive products in exports while maintaining strategic connections to global supply chains.

The article discusses the shift from traditional embedding-based recommenders to generative recommenders (GRs) in the context of large-scale recommendation systems. It highlights the challenges of handling massive user history data and the long-tail problem, where popular items dominate interactions. GRs, inspired by large language models (LLMs), reframe recommendation as a sequence modeling task, enabling more efficient training and inference. The NVIDIA recsys-examples repository provides optimized implementations of GR architectures like HSTU and Semantic IDs, addressing issues such as memory constraints and latency. DynamicEmb and nv-embedding-cache are introduced as tools to manage large embedding tables and improve inference performance. The article also outlines a specialized inference framework for Semantic ID-based GRs, emphasizing their unique requirements compared to LLM serving systems.

NVIDIA explores the use of AI coding agents in developing real-time endoscopic tool segmentation applications using Holoscan. The process involves iterative development cycles guided by a developer and an agent, leveraging HoloHub examples, documentation, and the Holoscan CLI. The first iteration focused on creating a new application using an existing model and video, while subsequent prompts refined visualization, added benchmarking, and optimized performance. The workflow demonstrated how agents can reuse existing components, implement new features, and maintain model integrity. The study compared different resource configurations, showing that combining CLI, skills, and documentation provided the most efficient development experience. The final application included multiple modes, automated tests, and reproducible benchmarking, highlighting the potential of agentic development in AI edge computing.

A new algorithm, ComputePN, addresses the computational challenges of evaluating complex Boolean queries on inverted indexes. The paper establishes that evaluating Boolean query DAGs is P-Complete, highlighting theoretical limits of existing methods. ComputePN uses a Positive-Negative dual representation and DAG memoization to bound evaluation time to O(|Q| · |U_active|), avoiding exponential blowup and universal scan penalties. The approach enables native execution of P-Complete queries over inverted indexes, providing a formal foundation for computational retrieval. The paper also introduces Wally, a private search system that improves performance for large-scale queries by reducing cryptographic operations.

Databricks has launched Precision Mode for its Document Intelligence API, ai_extract, to improve accuracy in complex document extraction. The feature combines custom-trained models with an agentic harness, achieving state-of-the-art results across 9,000 benchmark documents. It outperforms leading frontier models like GPT-5.6 Sol by seven percentage points in accuracy. Intercontinental Exchange highlights the tool's ability to transform complex financial documents into structured data, enabling faster analysis and decision-making. The solution addresses challenges such as long documents, dense tables, and nested schemas through a chunk-and-merge approach, demonstrating robustness against common failure modes in existing models.

The open model ecosystem on Hugging Face's Hub has expanded significantly, with Qwen emerging as a dominant force. Qwen-based models now account for 151,448 derivatives, surpassing Meta's and Llama's totals. This growth is attributed to Qwen's consistent release schedule, broad model coverage, and permissive Apache 2.0 licensing. While Chinese labs like Moonshot and MiniMax focus on large, frontier models, U.S. labs such as NVIDIA and AMD emphasize hardware compatibility and optimization. The rise of local inference tools like llama.cpp has enabled developers to run large models on consumer hardware, with Qwen's GGUF downloads reaching 39.6 million monthly. Despite the dominance of small models in downloads, the frontier models are increasingly accessible through community-driven quantization and conversion efforts.

Google's AMIE (Video) system, an advanced medical AI, demonstrates expert-level performance in real-time video consultations through a randomized study with 300 live sessions and 30 board-certified physicians. The system integrates visual and auditory cues, guides patients through virtual exams, and performs diagnostic reasoning in real time. AMIE (Video) uses an asynchronous multi-agent architecture to balance conversational speed with clinical analysis. It outperformed both text-based AMIE (Text) and human physicians in physical examination and communication skills, with patient actors preferring the video interface. However, the study used professional actors in simulated settings, and real-world validation remains essential before broader clinical adoption.

Meta has introduced Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter model derived from Muse Spark, designed for on-device agentic workflows. The model is supported by ExecuTorch, which provides end-to-end execution on NVIDIA GPUs and Apple silicon. ExecuTorch allows developers to implement models in PyTorch and export them for optimized deployment across different backends. Key features include support for text and image inputs, DFlash speculative decoding, and 128K+ token context. Prebuilt PTE artifacts are available for download, and users can build their own by selecting backend, modality, and other parameters. The system enables efficient execution with performance improvements through speculative decoding, as demonstrated in benchmark results. Meta also highlights ongoing work to enhance features like cross-session prefix sharing and continuous batching for better agentic capabilities.

PyTorch Conference North America will take place in San Jose, California, on October 20–21, 2026. Keynote speakers include leaders from Meta, NVIDIA, Google Cloud, and the PyTorch Foundation. The event will feature technical sessions and community collaboration. The PyTorch Foundation is accepting design submissions for a conference pin until August 14, with the winner receiving a complimentary ticket. Companies can also explore sponsorship opportunities to engage with the AI ecosystem.

MIT researchers, led by Ju Li, have developed a stable electrolyte for sodium-metal batteries by identifying a suitable solvent. Sodium-metal batteries offer advantages over lithium-ion batteries, including greater abundance and lower cost, but face challenges with stability and fast charging. The team discovered that a small solvent molecule, DMFSA, enables both rapid ion transport and electrolyte stability. This breakthrough addresses the trade-off between speed and stability in battery performance. The research, published in Joule, introduces a new design strategy for electrolytes based on solvent size and molecular similarity, with potential applications beyond sodium batteries.

The Science One Framework, developed by Google Cloud researchers Rui Meng and Tomas Pfister, introduces a new verifiability system called Chain-of-Evidence (CoE) to address hallucinations in AI-generated scientific research. Current autonomous research systems often produce non-existent citations, misaligned code-text, and unverifiable results. The Science One Framework, which builds evidence chains during research, achieves zero phantom references and fully verifiable scores. It outperforms existing systems like Sakana AI's AI Scientist v2 and DeepScientist on benchmark tasks such as MLE-Bench and Parameter-Golf. The CoE Audit, an automated protocol, evaluates AI-generated papers against their code and evidence, revealing that baselines hallucinate up to 21% of references. The framework maintains method-code alignment and achieves state-of-the-art performance without compromising scientific rigor. The Science One Framework is presented as an experimental prototype, not a production-ready tool.

Google Flow Music is launching Lyria 3.5, a new music generation model that offers improvements in musicality, lyrics, vocals, and creative control. The update allows users to create richer tracks with more complex melodic structures, higher quality lyrics, and more realistic vocals. It also provides greater control over tempo and duration. The model is now available in Google Flow Music.

Researchers introduce PatientAgentBench, a benchmark designed to assess patient-facing health AI agents by simulating realistic clinical scenarios. The framework evaluates agents on clinical safety, triage quality, and workflow accuracy across multiturn conversations. Existing benchmarks fail to capture the complexities of patient interactions, as they focus on static knowledge or technical tasks. PatientAgentBench uses synthetic patient data and a panel of LLMs to score agents based on clinician-vetted criteria. Findings show models struggle with routine tasks involving complex patients, often missing critical safety checks. The benchmark highlights the need for safer, more context-aware AI systems that support rather than replace human care. The framework is now available for researchers and developers to test and improve health AI systems.

Ai2 has launched the OlmoEarth Platform, a system designed to enable large-scale geospatial inference using satellite data. The platform addresses challenges in processing vast amounts of satellite imagery, including data acquisition, alignment, and efficient inference at planetary scale. It divides tasks into three stages—data preprocessing, inference, and postprocessing—each optimized for different hardware. The platform can process continent-scale areas in a day, with costs as low as fractions of a penny per square kilometer. It also handles failures automatically and supports parallel processing across thousands of compute instances. Ai2 highlights the importance of cloud-optimized formats, open standards, and efficient data pipelines in making geospatial AI accessible to organizations focused on environmental monitoring and disaster response.

The U.S. Department of Commerce’s NIST has announced funding for 14 MEP centers to help small and medium-sized manufacturers adopt advanced technologies. These centers will focus on improving production capacity, supply chain integration, and workforce development. The funding requires applicants to secure at least 50% nonfederal matching funds. NIST plans to award up to specified amounts per location, with applications due by August 21, 2026. The MEP National Network includes over 1,400 advisers and 450 service locations.

Meta has redesigned its BLOB-storage architecture to address challenges in AI training and research. The new system, built on top of the Tectonic block layer, focuses on maximizing GPU utilization by reducing storage latency and improving data access speed. Key changes include a unified metadata schema, elimination of a data proxy, and regional deployment of storage services. These updates help prevent GPU stalls during training and reduce the time researchers spend moving data across regions. The redesign also introduces distributed data caching and metadata caching to handle spikes in data access, improving overall performance and efficiency. The goal is to enable faster iteration in AI research while maintaining high performance and cost efficiency.

Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley advocates for a balance between privacy and safety, following growing public backlash over the company's surveillance technology. Concerns include 46 reported cases of police misuse of Flock's tools, including stalking. Langley apologized for the incidents but denied creating police abuse, claiming Flock's technology helps uncover such misuse. Both Democrats and Republicans have criticized Flock, with some lawmakers proposing restrictions on surveillance systems. Flock has made changes, such as reducing data retention, but critics remain skeptical. Langley urges state regulators to criminalize illegal use of Flock data and calls for greater accountability in technology.

Harvard Business School incorporates AI avatars created by HeyGen into its $699 Foundry bootcamp for entrepreneurs. The avatars provide feedback during practice pitches and board meetings, complementing live instructor sessions. New York Times reporter Sarah Kessler tested an AI version of Jeff Bussgang, noting the virtual avatar's frozen smile. Project director Katharina Rings noted students desired a more guided experience with the AI. While some students express discomfort with AI, Foundry participants generally accept the avatars, with Bussgang acknowledging their 'creepy' nature but noting student approval.

Linus Torvalds acknowledged an AI's role in debugging a Linux kernel issue, noting its initial reluctance but eventual contribution. The AI added debug code and analyzed the problem when prompted, leading Torvalds to credit it for the solution. He also remarked on the AI's training and its contrast with his own persistence. The commit message was written by the AI, reflecting its involvement in the process.

The article argues that debates over AI consciousness are a distraction from the real issue of corporate accountability. It highlights how discussions of AI as 'conscious' or 'autonomous' are used to avoid liability for harms caused by AI systems. The piece critiques the framing of AI as a 'superhuman' entity, suggesting it enables companies to evade responsibility for harms like generating illegal content or causing psychological damage. It compares these arguments to animal rights movements, noting that while philosophical musings on AI consciousness are interesting, they lack legal grounding. The author warns that granting AI legal personhood would shift liability from corporations to AI itself, undermining current legal frameworks that hold companies accountable for their products. The article concludes that focusing on AI consciousness distracts from the need for regulation and responsibility in AI development.

Exxon is among several bidders for Shell's U.S. chemicals business, valued at up to $8 billion, according to the Financial Times. The potential buyers, including LyondellBasell and Apollo Global Management, have submitted non-binding offers. Shell's U.S. chemicals division operates four facilities in Louisiana, Texas, and Pennsylvania. The company has been selling assets to reallocate capital, following its Capital Markets Day 2025 pledge. Recent sales include a wind and solar business to TotalEnergies and a Cyprus gas stake to MOL. Shell's chemicals business contributed to its strong second-quarter earnings of $9.84 billion.

Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited (TPREL) has commissioned a 190.5 MW solar Firm and Dispatchable Renewable Energy (FDRE) project in Rajasthan, bringing its total renewable utility capacity to 12.4 GW. The project, developed under SJVN FDRE Tranche-1, integrates battery storage and grid-support technologies to provide reliable renewable power. TPREL completed key components within compressed timelines despite global supply chain disruptions. The project supports India’s goal of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.

European long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) prices increased 2.3% in July, according to Pexapark, with divergent trends across regions. The Euro Composite rose to €45 ($52.5)/MWh, driven by higher forward electricity prices in the UK and Italy, which saw increases of 5.8% and 4.3%, respectively. In contrast, Nordic countries, Spain, and Portugal experienced declines of 6.3%, 3.9%, and 2.9%, respectively, due to high renewable generation and lower long-term price expectations. Twenty-four PPAs totaling 1.1 GW were announced, with solar accounting for one-third of the contracted capacity. The energy storage market also saw nine BESS agreements, highlighting evolving contractual models.

Utility-scale battery storage in the U.S. grew at an average annual rate of 70% over three years, reaching 52 gigawatts (GW) of nameplate capacity by mid-2026. Operators plan to add 54 GW more over the next two and a half years. Solar PV plants host the largest battery storage units, with the Bellefield Solar and Energy Storage Farm in California projected to become the nation's largest if its expansion plans are realized. The facility would pair 1,000 MW of solar with 1,000 MW of storage. The Manatee Solar Energy Center in Florida and the Gemini Solar Hybrid in Nevada are among the largest existing projects.

The value of energy trade between the United States and Canada fell by 11% in 2025 to $137 billion, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Despite this decline, the trade value of natural gas and electricity increased slightly due to higher prices and volumes. Crude oil accounted for 69% of the total U.S.-Canada energy trade in 2025. Meanwhile, U.S. natural gas production is forecast to reach 122.5 billion cubic feet per day in 2026, surpassing the 2025 record. Puerto Rico experienced 36 hours of power interruptions in 2025, compared to two hours in the mainland U.S. Utility-scale battery storage capacity in the U.S. grew to 43.6 gigawatts by the end of 2025, with an additional 8.3 gigawatts added in the first half of 2026. China's reduced crude oil imports in Q2 2026, due to higher prices from Hormuz disruptions, softened global demand. The U.S. also saw increased electric vehicle adoption, with 24% of new light-duty vehicles being hybrid or electric in Q2 2026.

Anthro Energy has started construction of a US-based battery materials factory in Louisville, Kentucky, set to produce advanced electrolytes for lithium-ion batteries. The facility, expected to open in late 2027, will generate 12,000 metric tons of polymer electrolyte annually, supporting up to 25 GWh of battery production. The electrolyte, used in grid storage, transportation, and consumer electronics, is designed to be safer, reducing fire risks and improving energy density. The project, funded by $24.9 million from the US Department of Energy and $18.4 million in tax credits, will create over 400 jobs. Anthro CEO David Mackanic emphasized the importance of domestic manufacturing for a resilient supply chain.

Doosan Enerbility has been contracted to supply core barrel, guard vessel, and internal supports for TerraPower's Natrium reactor. The company stated that design improvements have raised the design maturity to a level ready for manufacturing.
