The dollar index rose to 98.98, while Brent crude fell to $92.86 per barrel. Domestic markets saw the Sensex and Nifty decline, with foreign investors selling equities worth ₹542.71 crore. India's forex reserves increased by $9.905 billion to $716.907 billion.

The Madras High Court has extended the interim stay on notifying five Tamil Nadu assembly bypolls until September 8, as election petitions challenging the results remain pending. The court rejected the Tamil Nadu government's request to lift the stay. One bypoll was triggered by Chief Minister C Jopseph Vijay's victory in the Trichy East constituency. Meanwhile, DMK president MK Stalin filed an election petition challenging the victory of TVK candidate VS Babu in Kolathur, citing alleged voting machine malfunctions and irregularities. Stalin's loss to Babu, who attributed his win to Vijay's leadership and local connections, has sparked legal and political debate.

Iran's rial hit a record low of 2.02 million to the dollar as the US prepares new sanctions. The currency's decline follows months of economic strain and conflict. Despite the pressure, Iran maintains control over the Strait of Hormuz, a critical oil route. Iran and Oman are nearing an agreement to jointly manage the strait, amid US criticism of Oman. The US plans stronger sanctions, including secondary penalties against countries trading with Iran. The UAE has suspended trade with Iran, worsening its economic situation. Iran warns against supporting the new sanctions, calling it an act of war.

Maharashtra has introduced a rule requiring taxi and autorickshaw drivers to demonstrate a working knowledge of Marathi, raising constitutional concerns. The 2026 amendment to the Motor Vehicles Rules mandates that drivers prove language proficiency, with failure leading to potential suspension or revocation of their permits. The state argues this ensures effective communication with passengers, but critics highlight that the regulation risks conflating language proficiency with occupational competence. Article 19 of the Constitution protects the right to practice a profession, and legal experts warn that tying employment to linguistic ability could undermine the principle of free movement across states. The rule has faced similar challenges before, with courts previously rejecting similar conditions. While the state has leeway to regulate transport, the proportionality of the Marathi requirement remains questionable, as it may impose undue burdens on drivers who perform essential functions unrelated to language. The case underscores the tension between linguistic identity and individual freedoms in India's federal structure.

SoftBank Group plans to issue $6.3 billion in retail bonds in Japan, the largest such issuance by any issuer in the country, to fund its commitments to OpenAI and refinance maturing debt. The seven-year bonds, priced on 4 September with a coupon range of 4.3-4.9%, will be SoftBank's third retail bond sale in 2026. The move reflects the company's strategy to secure funds for its AI investments, which include over $60 billion in commitments to OpenAI. SoftBank's shares fell 5.3% following the announcement. Analysts note the bond's reliance on retail investors due to banks' reluctance to take on the risk. The company faces a $20 billion shortfall even after this issuance, suggesting potential offshore bond offerings. S&P Global Ratings upgraded SoftBank's outlook to stable, citing improved financial ratios.

Godrej Industries Group signed a memorandum of understanding with the Haryana government, outlining a ₹20,000 crore investment plan to create around 40,000 jobs by FY28. The investment will expand on its existing ₹12,000 crore investment in the state, with Godrej Properties planning an additional ₹16,000 crore in real estate. Godrej Ventures aims to invest ₹3,500 crore in Gurugram's office infrastructure. The group highlighted Haryana's economic growth and urban development as key factors in its decision.

The Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) asserts there is no sugar shortage in India, with sufficient stocks to meet demand. ISMA president Niraj Shirgaokar attributes recent price increases to speculative stocking and weather-related production issues. The government has allowed duty-free imports of up to 1 million tonnes of raw sugar to address rising prices. The National Federation of Cooperative Sugar Factories (NFCSF) maintains that domestic supplies are adequate, with production estimates for the 2025-26 season at 279 lakh tonnes. Imports from Brazil may arrive before October 15, though the October 31 deadline is not strictly enforced. The government is expected to consider shipments arriving after this date.

Stock futures declined on Monday amid concerns over rising Treasury yields and fears of prolonged US-Iran tensions. The Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq-100 futures all fell, following a week of market declines. Treasury yields, including the 30-year US Treasury yield reaching nearly 5.3%, have pressured stocks by making bonds more attractive and increasing borrowing costs. Global bond yields in Japan, France, and Germany also rose, adding to financial market concerns. Investors worry that a prolonged US-Iran conflict could keep oil prices high, exacerbating inflation. The US Treasury attempted to stabilize bond markets with measures similar to quantitative easing, but the effects were short-lived. The upcoming PCE inflation data and the Fed's Jackson Hole meeting will provide further clues about interest rates. Nvidia's earnings, expected to show potential price hikes for AI infrastructure, will also test market sentiment. Asian markets showed mixed performance, with Japan and South Korea experiencing declines. Overall, investors remain cautious due to a combination of higher yields, inflation worries, geopolitical risks, and major earnings reports.

A 31-year-old man from Kerala was arrested for allegedly uploading intimate videos of his wife on a pornographic website and performing sexual acts in front of his four-year-old daughter. The wife discovered the videos after friends alerted her, leading to a police complaint. The accused also pushed for 'wife-swapping,' which the wife refused. Despite counselling, he continued the alleged offences, including another video of him engaging in sexual acts with the daughter. The case is under investigation under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita and POCSO Act. The accused was traced and arrested after going into hiding.

India's ethanol blending policy, which mandates E20 fuel, has significantly altered agricultural patterns by diverting foodgrains like maize and rice into biofuel production. This shift, driven by the Petroleum and Road Transport Ministries, has displaced traditional crops and raised concerns about food security. NITI Aayog reports highlight potential shortages in pulses and edible oils by 2047-48, yet the ethanol program continues to expand maize cultivation, creating a conflict with food self-reliance goals. The government's ethanol policy generates revenue for distilleries but transfers public assets to private hands, while maize farmers face uncertain prices and market instability. The policy also impacts consumers by reducing fuel efficiency and increasing feed costs for livestock. The article calls for a more equitable distribution of benefits and suggests alternatives like crop residues for ethanol production, emphasizing the need for transparent policy adjustments.

The Maharashtra government's new requirement for autorickshaw, taxi, and cab drivers to speak Marathi has led to increased fares and service disruptions in Mumbai. Drivers, many of whom are elderly and lack formal education, have protested the rule, with some staging strikes and blocking roads. Critics, including musician Avantika Ganguly and former actress Divya Unni, argue the policy is impractical and burdens hardworking individuals. Ganguly reported paying three times the usual fare and facing longer wait times, while Unni criticized the use of fines and harassment as methods to enforce language proficiency. Commuters have also expressed frustration, noting the disruption affects millions who rely on these services daily.

Apollo Micro Systems has acquired a 34% stake in Shauryastra Defence Systems, a newly incorporated defence technology company. The investment involved a cash payment of ₹34,000 for 3,400 equity shares at ₹10 each. Shauryastra Defence Systems was established on 21 August 2026 to address futuristic operational needs of the Indian Armed Forces. The venture will be led by Dr V. K. Saraswat, with Apollo Micro Systems aiming to expand its defence electronics capabilities and align with the Atmanirbhar Bharat initiative. The transaction was completed without additional regulatory approvals. The company also announced its open offer to acquire shares in Premier Explosives, with SEBI setting a 12-day tender period for the offer.

The Indian stock market closed lower on Monday, 24 August, with the Sensex dropping 0.22% to 77,369 and the Nifty 50 falling 0.14% to 24,219.05. The Nifty Metal index rose 1.6%, outperforming other sectors. Market declines were attributed to weak global cues, US-Iran tensions, and rising bond yields. Analysts noted caution as investors awaited further US sanctions on Iran. Banking and financial sectors underperformed, while realty and IT indices saw gains. Technical analysis suggested potential support levels for the Nifty at 24,050-24,070 and resistance at 24,350-24,370.

U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned Iran of an economic D-Day, announcing new sanctions targeting Iran's trade partners. The move follows Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian defending a memorandum of understanding with the U.S. as a path out of the stalled war. Iran vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf if the economic war continues. Bessent emphasized the Trump administration's shift to economic pressure, aiming to sever Iran's economic lifelines. Iran dismissed the sanctions as desperate, with Supreme National Security Council secretary Mohsen Rezaei threatening to cut oil exports and label support for U.S. measures as an act of war. The U.S. plans to reveal more severe sanctions, while Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the measures repetitive and urged respectful dialogue.

Gold prices in India remained high on Monday, with 24-carat gold priced at ₹1,62,289 per 10 grams and 22-carat gold at ₹1,48,656.72 per 10 grams. Mumbai and Kolkata saw slightly higher rates, while Delhi and Bengaluru remained stable. International gold prices also reached a three-month high, driven by global uncertainty, a weaker US dollar, and expectations of easing interest rates. Central bank purchases and geopolitical tensions further supported demand for gold.

A video of former Pakistan Prime Minister Imran Khan leaving a hospital after a 2022 shooting attempt was shared as recent, but it is actually from November 2022. The footage shows Khan three days after being shot in the legs during a protest. A reverse image search and cross-referencing with reports from India.com and Agence France-Presse confirmed the video's origin. The claim is misleading as it falsely presents historical footage as current.

Lalithaa Jewellery Mart shares surged 36% to Rs 274.40 from the IPO price of Rs 201, listing at a 32% premium on NSE. The Rs 1,700 crore IPO was subscribed 62.97 times, with promoter Kiran Kumar Jain selling Rs 500 crore via OFS. Grey market estimates suggested a 37% premium, but the listing price fell slightly short. The company plans to use IPO funds for 10 new retail stores. Analysts recommended 'Subscribe' due to the valuation discount compared to peers and growth potential from store expansion. However, risks like gold price volatility and working capital needs were noted.

The Indian government has established maximum LPG production targets for 21 refineries and upstream companies, aiming to build a domestic supply buffer. The targets, set at 63,810 tonnes per day, exceed current domestic output and are intended to reduce reliance on imports. Reliance Industries is allocated the largest quota of 18,000 tonnes daily. The order mandates infrastructure upgrades and production measures to increase LPG output. The government can issue directives to refiners to ramp up production during supply disruptions. The framework follows emergency measures taken during the West Asia crisis to prevent future shortages.

NVIDIA's GB300 NVL72 demonstrates significantly higher AI-factory throughput per megawatt compared to H200 NVL8 in agentic AI workloads, according to the SemiAnalysis AgentX benchmark. The benchmark evaluates real-world agentic sessions with varying context and tool use, showing GB300 NVL72 delivers up to 15x more throughput per megawatt for DeepSeek V4 Pro 1.6T. This performance advantage translates to lower unit costs, allowing operators to support more interactive agentic capacity within the same power budget. The results highlight system-level optimizations across serving runtime, model kernels, and scale-up fabric, enabling efficient handling of large MoE models and complex agent workflows. NVIDIA attributes the improvements to advanced technologies like MoE serving runtimes, NVLink scale-up fabric, and Dynamo, which enhance context reuse and reduce recomputation in agentic inference.

NVIDIA Groq 3 LPX, paired with the Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, enables ultrafast interactivity with long context for AI inference. Artificial Analysis benchmarked the system, reporting a 3,431 output tokens per second performance on the Gemma 4 31B model at 100K context length. The system's deterministic execution model and compiler-scheduled workload planning minimize first-bit latency and enable efficient interchip communication. Groq 3 LPX supports multiple serving configurations, including prefill-decode and attention-FFN disaggregation, enhancing the Vera Rubin platform's ability to handle agentic tasks with high interactivity and low latency. The system also achieved 4,767 tokens per second on coding benchmarks, demonstrating its effectiveness for complex workflows.

A long-time Firefox user who previously abandoned the browser due to bloat and lack of features has returned, citing recent improvements. The author highlights five key features that contributed to this change: a refined theming engine offering more consistent visual styling, vertical tabs for better tab management, containers for enhanced privacy, a built-in VPN for secure browsing, and AI integration through Smart Window and a sidebar chatbot. These features, many available in Firefox's Nightly builds, have made the browser more efficient and user-friendly, prompting the author to reconsider Firefox as a viable option.

OpenAI is expanding its AI capabilities beyond software engineering with the release of ChatGPT Work, an AI agent tool designed for white-collar workers. The product, available on the lowest subscription tier for $20 a month, allows users to automate complex tasks across various digital workflows, including email, Slack, and SaaS platforms. OpenAI's engineers, like Andrew Ambrosino, argue that granting AI access to personal data is necessary for testing and improving its functionality. While the tool has seen high internal adoption, external usage remains low, highlighting challenges in making AI intuitive for non-technical users. OpenAI emphasizes the need for a 'harness' to control AI's actions and is working on simplifying interactions through features like buttons and plugins. The company faces competition from vertical-specific AI tools and must overcome hurdles in making AI accessible and useful for a broader audience.

Prime Minister Anthony Albanese plans to introduce national legislation to regulate datacentres, aiming to balance economic benefits with environmental concerns. The proposal comes as datacentre power use is projected to increase seven-fold over the next decade, according to the Australian Energy Market Operator. The new laws will set copyright rules for AI businesses, impose standards for security and skills development, and require datacentres to minimize energy prices and water use. Opposition from Queensland and the Northern Territory, which prefer coal and gas over renewables, poses a challenge. Albanese also faces pressure on other issues, including the national gun buy-back and Western Australia's GST arrangements.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham condemned the sharing of dangerous driving videos as 'truly reprehensible', urging social media companies to remove such content. Defence Minister Luke Pollard emphasized that platforms could easily remove these posts and adjust their algorithms to prevent their spread. The incident involved two police officers and five passengers killed in a crash near Middlesbrough, with one of the victims linked to a TikTok account that previously shared videos of dangerous driving. While TikTok claims to remove such content, the Online Safety Act allows for exceptions, making enforcement complex. Cleveland Police stated there was no evidence the videos were directly related to the crash, but officials warned against glorifying dangerous driving. The government plans to use the Online Safety Act to compel platforms to remove such content, with Ofcom investigating TikTok's compliance with child safety regulations.

A class action lawsuit has been filed against Amazon, alleging it used Twitch streamers' content to train AI models without permission or compensation. The lawsuit, brought by streamer Warren Pandiscia, claims Twitch breached its contract by exploiting users' data for Amazon's AI development. Streamers reportedly produced over 215 million hours of content in 2026 alone. The opt-out feature for AI training is limited to individual streams, allowing content to be used when featured in streams with the feature enabled. Amazon has not commented on the lawsuit, which seeks damages and an injunction against the practice. Twitch's FAQs mention using audio to refine speech-to-text models, but the opt-out process is not fully effective.

The article discusses the challenges of implementing AI agents in production environments, identifying a 'prototyping tax' that slows down development. This tax arises from the inefficiencies in traditional R&D processes, which are not well-suited for AI agents. The key issue is the gap between conceptualizing an AI project and delivering a working prototype, leading to lost momentum and failed initiatives. The article highlights that the problem is not with the AI agents themselves but with the organizational setup. Teams that succeed are those that provide agents with a strong foundation in business semantics, enabling faster development cycles. By integrating governance and context into the development process, these teams reduce the time-to-prototype and increase the rate of production-ready solutions. The article also presents case studies showing how platforms like Databricks' Genie Code improve efficiency by understanding data schemas and governance models. The conclusion emphasizes that addressing the prototyping tax is essential for successful AI implementation, with measurable benefits in productivity and compliance.

NVIDIA and the open source community are driving progress in local AI by releasing new models and tools that enable developers to build and run advanced agents on personal and edge systems. The company highlights several recent developments, including the Qwen3.8-27B model optimized for NVIDIA RTX GPUs, which supports fast local inference for coding tasks. Other models like Cosmos 3 Edge, MiniMax-H3, and DeepSeek-V4-Flash are also being made available, with support for NVIDIA hardware. NVIDIA is also enhancing its DGX Spark systems with new features like the Sync Cluster Assistant, which allows developers to cluster multiple systems for running larger models. Additionally, the release of Muse Glimmer, a 30-billion-parameter model optimized for local agentic workflows, is enabling always-on AI assistants for coding and data processing. These advancements are part of NVIDIA's ongoing efforts to support the open source ecosystem and empower developers with high-performance, local AI solutions.

NVIDIA has introduced Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model designed for high-volume, specialized tasks in agentic AI systems. The model offers up to 4x faster output speed and 30% faster task completion compared to similar models. It is open and customizable, allowing organizations to post-train it with their domain-specific data. Additionally, NVIDIA released NeMo Switchyard, an open-source library for intelligent model routing, enabling developers to direct requests to the most suitable model for each task. This reduces costs and improves efficiency across various industries. Partners like Boomi, Cadence, and LangChain have tested NeMo Switchyard, reporting significant cost reductions and performance improvements. Both tools are available on multiple platforms, enhancing deployment flexibility for enterprises.

MIT students and postdocs participated in Congressional Visit Days, meeting with 62 congressional offices to advocate for sustained federal investment in scientific research. The event, organized by the MIT Science Policy Initiative, aimed to connect researchers with policymakers and demonstrate how scientists can engage in policy advocacy. Participants discussed both general science funding and specific policies related to their research areas, including AI, environmental science, and energy. The experience highlighted the importance of bipartisanship in supporting science and emphasized the need for researchers to engage with policymakers to shape future decisions.

In 1975, MIT researchers and Boston’s Beth Israel Hospital began creating a medical database to store and share electrocardiogram recordings, aiming to facilitate collaboration in arrhythmia research. The project, which took years to complete, eventually became the foundation for PhysioNet, a global platform for clinical data sharing. By 1999, PhysioNet had evolved into a comprehensive repository hosting hundreds of databases, with over 15,000 scientific publications citing it and users from 180 countries. The platform's open-access model and emphasis on data sharing have influenced the development of similar systems like MIMIC and Health Data Nexus. As artificial intelligence advances, PhysioNet has expanded to include electronic health records, imaging data, and AI models, becoming a cornerstone for health-care AI research. Researchers and platform stewards envision further growth, including new tools for user contributions and interdisciplinary collaboration.

IBM has signed a definitive agreement to acquire HRL Laboratories, a research institution with a 80-year history of scientific innovation. The acquisition aims to accelerate IBM's quantum computing goals by leveraging HRL's expertise in silicon-spin qubit engineering. HRL is renowned for pioneering the laser, advancing semiconductor technology, and contributing to fields like ion propulsion and artificial intelligence. The lab has also developed key technologies such as memristors and quantum dot systems. Today, HRL continues research in quantum computing, materials science, and sensing technology, complementing IBM's own 80-year legacy in computing innovation.

Google has introduced three new Gemini models: 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber. The 3.6 Flash model offers 17% better token efficiency and improved performance in coding, knowledge work, and multimodal tasks, with a lower cost per token. 3.5 Flash-Lite is the fastest in the 3.5 series, delivering 350 output tokens per second and a strong price-to-performance ratio for high-throughput workflows. The 3.5 Flash Cyber model is designed for cybersecurity applications, combining a specialized model with CodeMender to detect and fix vulnerabilities efficiently. These models are available now through various platforms, with Gemini 3.5 Pro in testing and Gemini 4 in development.

Google introduced Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber, a lightweight cybersecurity model designed to detect and fix software vulnerabilities more efficiently than previous models. Built on 3.5 Flash, it is optimized for speed and affordability, making it suitable for large-scale code analysis. The model will be available through CodeMender to governments and trusted partners in a limited-access pilot program. Google claims it can handle complex codebases by analyzing multiple code paths, and benchmark tests show it performs competitively against larger models on the CyberGym benchmark.

Researchers from Google Research explain that the creativity of diffusion models stems from the 'score smoothing' effect in neural networks, which allows them to interpolate between training data points rather than merely memorizing them. The study, presented at ICLR 2026, shows that diffusion models generate novel data by learning a smoothed version of the score function, which drives the denoising process to create new samples. This phenomenon occurs because neural networks, due to regularization effects like weight decay, naturally learn smoother approximations of the perfect score function. The research demonstrates that this score smoothing enables diffusion models to explore the data manifold, producing realistic yet novel outputs. The findings suggest that the 'creativity' of these models is a predictable mathematical outcome of their learning process, offering insights into how to design more effective generative models that balance quality and innovation.

Flint is a visualization language designed to let AI agents create expressive, visually polished charts from simple, human-editable specifications. It leverages semantic data types to guide design choices like scales, formatting, and color schemes, reducing the need for detailed, error-prone manual configurations. The system automatically adjusts layouts and adapts to data changes, ensuring readability without explicit user input. Flint specifications can compile to multiple backends, including Vega-Lite, Apache ECharts, and Chart.js, enabling flexibility across visualization tools. The project includes the flint-chart library and a flint-chart-mcp server, allowing agents to create, validate, and render charts in chat or coding environments. In testing, Flint outperformed direct Vega-Lite generation methods, achieving higher scores with various LLMs. It is now used in Microsoft Research's Data Formulator project for AI-assisted data analysis.

Binh Pham, a robotics software engineer, demonstrated MolmoAct 2's capabilities at a hackathon, showcasing its ability to perform tasks without specific training. The model, available open-source, allows users to inspect, adapt, and customize it with provided artifacts. Pham noted its strong spatial awareness and generalization, comparing it to the GPT-2 moment for robotics. The release includes model weights, data, training code, and fine-tuning scripts, enhancing reproducibility and development in the field.

Meta's engineers developed ultra-narrow steel-can batteries to power smart glasses like the Ray-Ban Meta and Oakley Meta Vanguards. Traditional pouch cells were unsuitable due to their difficulty in shrinking and shaping. Steel-can cells, used in power tools and watches, were modified to achieve widths as narrow as 7mm. The design uses stacked layers instead of wound electrodes, reducing impedance and improving power delivery during peak demands. The 10mm-wide cells maintain a shape tolerance of 100 microns, enhancing energy density. Battery capacity increased from 160 mAh to 248 mAh across generations through system-level efficiency improvements. The Oakley Meta Vanguards feature dual batteries in temple arms, introducing challenges in power distribution and synchronization. Meta aims to scale this technology across its hardware portfolio and ensure supply resilience for future wearables.

Mistral has partnered with Airbus, BMW, and ASML to develop an AI stack for industrial engineering, aiming to optimize design, simulation, and production while ensuring data security. The collaboration includes implementing AI in Airbus' operations, supporting BMW's Large Industry Model initiative, and tackling complex engineering challenges with ASML. Mistral also announced the acquisition of Emmi to enhance its offerings. The company introduced Vibe, an agentic AI tool for long-horizon tasks, and plans to open a 10 MW data center in France by 2026 to improve compute control and security.

Mistral has introduced Vibe, a unified AI agent designed to handle both work and coding tasks. Vibe offers Work Mode for managing complex, multi-step tasks across enterprise tools and Code Mode for remote coding sessions. It integrates with platforms like VS Code and CLI, enabling seamless collaboration. Vibe is available in free, Pro, Team, and Enterprise plans, with features such as visible reasoning, reusable skills, and secure deployments. The agent can assist with inbox management, research, document drafting, and coding workflows from feature development to pull requests. Mistral highlights Vibe's ability to streamline workflows and improve productivity for both individuals and organizations.

European leaders, including France's Macron, Germany's Merz, and Britain's Burnham, meet in Kyiv to discuss continued military support for Ukraine, focusing on air defense and long-term security. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy urges the European Parliament to approve legislation for 30 billion euros in funding to counter Russia's ballistic missiles. Norway pledges $9 billion in aid for Ukraine next year, while Estonia emphasizes the need for more air defense and sanctions against Russia. Zelenskyy warns of Russia's expanding missile production and highlights recent drone strikes on Russian logistics hubs. The Coalition of the Willing, led by the UK and France, includes 34 countries supporting Ukraine, with no U.S. representative confirmed for the meeting.

A survey by iChoosr found 48% of Japanese respondents cited cost reduction as the main reason for solar panels or home batteries, compared to 19% for disaster resilience. The survey of 14,478 people showed financial considerations dominate over disaster preparedness. As Japan's FIT contracts expire, households find it more economical to store and use their own solar power. Other surveys also show cost savings outweigh resilience concerns. The findings come amid Japan's transition from FIT schemes and growing residential solar demand.

Solar mounting technology company SWIF Rack has partnered with National Roofing Partners to support commercial solar installations. The collaboration allows NRP roofing professionals to inspect solar projects and maintain roofing warranties. SWIF Rack's products are compatible with various commercial roof types, and the partnership aims to provide building owners with reliable solar solutions. Both companies emphasize combining solar technology with roofing expertise to ensure structural integrity and clean energy performance.

Scott Murtishaw, executive director of the California Energy Storage Alliance (CESA), highlights the challenges of local opposition and safety misconceptions surrounding energy storage in California. He notes that while the state has successfully implemented policies to support energy storage, recent fires at large-scale facilities have fueled public fear. Murtishaw explains that containerised battery energy storage systems (BESS) are inherently safer, as they prevent fire spread between units. He emphasizes the importance of communicating safety data and technological advancements to counter misinformation. CESA is collaborating with partners to provide clear, accessible information to address public concerns. Murtishaw also discusses how energy storage has significantly reduced the 'duck curve' challenge by storing solar energy for evening use, demonstrating its reliability benefits.

Ho Chi Minh City is reviewing a feasibility study for a 6 GW offshore wind development. The study assesses technical, economic, and environmental aspects of the project. Local authorities aim to determine if the project aligns with regional energy goals. The initiative could contribute to Vietnam's renewable energy targets. Further details are expected in upcoming reports.

Indian stock markets declined on August 24, 2026, with the S&P BSE SENSEX and NIFTY 50 falling by 0.22% and 0.14%, respectively. The green energy sector showed mixed results, with Kabra Extrusion and Praj Industries rising over 8% and 1.9%, while companies like Websol Energy and Borosil Renewables fell by 2.5% and 2.1%. Major firms such as Tata Power and Adani Green Energy also saw declines. The session reflected selective interest in clean energy stocks amid broader market weakness.

S&P Global Energy forecasts a 33% increase in US solar and 50% rise in wind capacity in 2025, defying Trump's policies. The administration's attempts to block green projects have been challenged in court, leading to payments of $4 billion to developers to abandon leases, with $1.22 billion going to RWE for offshore zones. Rising electricity demand from AI, electric vehicles, and data centers is driving the expansion, with ICF projecting a 39% increase in consumption by 2035. The expiration of clean energy subsidies is expected to raise power prices by 40-120%, incentivizing further investment in renewables.

Norway has extended the deadline for submitting licence applications for its first commercial offshore wind farm. The extension aims to provide more time for stakeholders to prepare. The original deadline was set for early 2024. The move reflects the government's commitment to renewable energy development. The wind farm is expected to contribute significantly to Norway's energy goals.

The Middle East is expected to account for over 40% of global gas processing capacity additions by 2030, according to the article. This growth is driven by major projects in Saudi Arabia, the UAE, and Iran. The region's strategic location and abundant natural gas reserves are key factors. The article highlights the shift in global energy infrastructure investment. Analysts note the Middle East's role in meeting rising energy demand in Asia and Europe.

The value of U.S.-Canada energy trade fell by 11% in 2025 to $137 billion, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. Crude oil, accounting for 69% of the trade, saw a 16% decline in value due to lower prices and trade volumes. U.S. crude oil imports from Canada totaled $111 billion, while exports to Canada amounted to $26 billion. Canada remains the primary source of U.S. crude oil imports, with average daily imports of 3.9 million barrels. U.S. petroleum product exports to Canada increased by 6% in volume but decreased in value by 12%.

A coalition of 95 organizations has urged Congress to reject four Congressional Review Act resolutions aimed at overturning Clean Air Act preemption waivers. These waivers set standards for vehicles and off-road engines that manufacturers have already complied with for years. The letter argues that these standards reduce fuel costs and improve air quality, especially as communities face high pollution levels. The groups call on lawmakers to vote against the resolutions, which they claim would hinder states' ability to protect public health. The letter is signed by health, environmental, and business organizations.

MP Materials reported a 89% year-over-year revenue increase to $108 million in Q2, with adjusted EBITDA turning positive at $28.5 million. The company received $17.6 million from the Pentagon for price-protection on NdPr, as market prices fell below the $110 per kilogram floor. MP is now selling more refined NdPr products, increasing profitability. The company shifted from selling rare-earth concentrate to processing it in-house, enhancing value. Analysts suggest the stock's recent decline may reflect valuation adjustments rather than underlying performance.

Algeria's education ministry announced that English will replace French as the primary foreign language taught in third-year primary schools starting in 2026-2027. This marks a significant shift in the country's linguistic policy, ending French's long-standing dominance in schools. The decision is part of President Abdelmadjid Tebboune's broader linguistic overhaul, which includes transitioning university subjects from French to English. The move comes amid heightened diplomatic tensions with France, following its support for Morocco's Western Sahara claims. Critics argue the reform lacks sufficient resources and planning, particularly in teacher training. Meanwhile, public interest in English-language books is growing, reflecting a broader cultural shift. Despite these changes, French remains widely spoken, with over 15 million Algerians fluent in the language. The reforms also highlight a regional trend of former French colonies reevaluating their linguistic ties to Paris, as seen in Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso's recent departures from the Francophone organization OIF.

Research by Ampere Analysis shows that Western European subscribers of Netflix, Disney+, and Amazon Prime Video have faced the highest average price increases globally over the past three years, rising by $1.86. This surpasses the US increase of $1.70. Price hikes, driven by content production costs, have led to basic packages costing £5.99 and premium tiers £12.99 in the UK. While revenue for Netflix rose to £2.06bn, price increases have decreased as consumers reach payment limits. Ampere's Jaanika Juntson noted that streamers are diversifying monetization strategies as competition intensifies.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is set to announce new economic sanctions against Iran, framing them as the 'single greatest financial offensive ever.' President Trump has called the measures an 'economic D-Day,' targeting countries that provide economic support to Tehran. The Iranian Rial has dropped to a record low in anticipation. The sanctions aim to cut off financial lifelines to Iran, with particular criticism directed at China, Iran's largest oil buyer. Analysts question the effectiveness of additional sanctions, noting the U.S. has already targeted many key entities. Iran's security chief warned of 'seismic' retaliation, including attacks on oil tankers in the Persian Gulf. The sanctions are expected to worsen Iran's already dire economic situation, with inflation reaching nearly 90 percent and daily life becoming increasingly difficult for ordinary citizens.

The Federal Reserve Board has approved FS Bancorp, Inc.'s application to merge with Pacific West Bancorp, which would allow it to indirectly acquire Pacific West Bank. The approval was announced on August 4, 2026. Both FS Bancorp and Pacific West Bancorp are based in Washington and Oregon, respectively.

The Federal Reserve Board has approved Coastal Bend Bancshares, Inc.'s application to acquire First National Bank in Port Lavaca, Texas. The approval was announced on Tuesday, August 4, 2026. The decision allows the Corpus Christi-based company to proceed with the acquisition of the Port Lavaca bank.

Federal Reserve Governor Lisa D. Cook emphasized the growing adoption of artificial intelligence by small businesses during her speech at the State of Small Business Symposium. She noted that nearly half of small employer firms use AI, with 71 percent reporting increased productivity. This finding challenges the notion that large firms have an advantage in AI deployment. Cook highlighted the Federal Reserve's Small Business Credit Survey (SBCS) as a critical tool for understanding small business financial conditions, including credit access and operational challenges. She praised the survey's expansion over the past decade, now capturing real-time data on AI usage and other emerging issues. The speech underscored the importance of small businesses in driving economic growth and innovation, with Cook encouraging researchers and policymakers to explore the survey's data for insights into credit access and business strategies.

Intuit is set to release its Q4 2026 earnings on August 25th. Wall Street expects the company to report an EPS of $3.59, representing a 30.5% year-over-year increase, alongside revenue of $4.27 billion, up 11.5% from the previous year.

A personal account describes how daily subway rides in the Bronx during the 1970s fostered a deeper understanding of social inequality and human connection. The author recounts the physical and emotional challenges of commuting through a segregated city, highlighting exposure to poverty and diverse cultures. The experience contrasted with modern car-centric life, which limits interaction with others. The author notes that shared spaces like subways can reveal the realities of different lives, while car travel creates distance and reduces empathy. The narrative underscores how transportation choices shape social awareness and the importance of direct human contact in fostering empathy.

A study using data from 2003 to 2024 shows a decline in Americans' time spent with friends, particularly on Friday nights. Previously, social interaction peaked on weekend evenings, but this pattern has weakened since the mid-2010s. Friday nights now resemble typical weeknights, while Saturday remains elevated but less so than before. The overall reduction in social time suggests a broader decline in social interaction, without a shift in activity types. The study highlights a temporal reorganization of social life, marked by the fading of the 'night out' tradition.

Former snooker world champion Graeme Dott was convicted of sexually abusing two children in a Scottish court. The 49-year-old was found guilty of lewd behavior toward a girl between 1993 and 1996, and making sexual remarks and touching a boy between 2006 and 2010. Dott denied the charges but was convicted after a trial in Glasgow. He will face sentencing next month. Police Scotland described him as a dangerous individual. Dott, who won the 2006 world championship, was suspended by the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association following the charges.

US President Donald Trump announced plans to increase tariffs on Canadian vehicles and automotive parts to 50% starting January 1, 2027, following the collapse of trade negotiations with Canada. The move comes after the Trump administration imposed 50% tariffs on select Canadian goods, which took effect after talks failed. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned the tariffs, calling them an 'attack' and announcing retaliatory measures. He criticized the US for using 'economic integration as a weapon' and accused Washington of making unacceptable demands. Trump's threat marks a significant shift from the traditionally cooperative US-Canada trade relationship, with both nations facing economic and political repercussions from the escalating trade dispute.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned that Canada should be prepared to cut off electricity and critical minerals to the United States if trade tensions escalate. Ford criticized President Donald Trump's trade policies, comparing them to Ronald Reagan's stance against protectionist tariffs. He emphasized Canada's willingness to endure economic pain rather than yield to U.S. pressure. Ford also highlighted the strategic importance of critical minerals to U.S. national security and suggested using oil and potash as leverage. The dispute intensified after the U.S. imposed 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, prompting Canada's retaliatory measures. Ford accused Trump of seeking to weaken Canadian industries, particularly in the auto sector, which is vital to Ontario's economy. He also revealed opposition to a preliminary trade deal and expressed skepticism about Trump's demands for U.S. approval in future negotiations.

Donald Trump has threatened to impose 50% tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel, effective 1 January 2027, following the collapse of trade negotiations with Ottawa. The president criticized Canada on Truth Social, claiming the country 'needs us' and accusing it of being 'among the worst Nations in the World to deal with.' Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the latest deal, calling Trump's demands 'too much and offered too little,' and vowed 'dollar for dollar' retaliation. The current tariff on Canadian automobiles and parts stands at 25%. The trade dispute comes amid other developments, including New Mexico's plans to continue funding gender-affirming care for minors and the U.S. Treasury's upcoming announcement of new Iran sanctions.

President Donald Trump threatened to impose a 50% tariff on Canadian automobiles, car parts, and steel starting January 1, 2027, as trade tensions with Canada escalated. The announcement followed the collapse of recent trade talks between the U.S. and Canada. Long-planned U.S. tariffs on Canadian goods had already taken effect after the talks ended, prompting Canada to vow retaliation. Trump criticized Canada's high tariffs on American farmers, calling them unsustainable and stating they would no longer be tolerated.

Protesters in Ben Guerdane, Tunisia, erupted after a boat carrying 15 migrants sank off the southeastern coast, killing 14 and leaving two missing. The incident sparked road blockades and tire burning, with search operations ongoing. Fourteen victims were from Ben Guerdane, a marginalized city near Libya. The area has seen similar tragedies, including a 2022 boat disappearance that led to weeks of protests. The central Mediterranean route remains the deadliest for migrants, with over 900 deaths or disappearances reported this year. Despite a 2023 EU-Tunisia agreement aimed at reducing irregular migration, dangerous crossings persist, particularly from southern coastal areas like Zarzis, where families continue to search for missing relatives.

Ontario Premier Doug Ford warned that Canada could cut off electricity and critical minerals to the United States if trade tensions escalate. Ford criticized President Trump's trade policies, comparing them to the economic warfare Reagan opposed. He emphasized Canada's willingness to endure economic pain rather than yield to U.S. pressure. Ford also mentioned using oil and potash as leverage, citing the strategic importance of critical minerals to U.S. national security. The auto industry, central to Ontario's economy, faces new tariffs from Trump, intensifying the dispute. Ford opposed a preliminary trade deal and expressed readiness to break with it, highlighting concerns over Canadian sovereignty. Despite the conflict, Ford urged continued negotiations.

President Trump announced plans to impose a 50% import tax on Canadian cars and auto parts starting in 2027, accusing Ottawa of unfair tariffs on U.S. farm products. The move comes as Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney criticized the shifting justifications for tariffs and warned of potential energy supply retaliation. Carney noted that U.S. energy imports from Canada are substantial, with 99% of natural gas and 85% of electricity coming from Canada. He stated that Trump's negotiators had pushed for terms that were 'uneconomic, unfair,' undermining potential trade benefits.

Europol reports a growing trend of violent museum heists in Europe, with thieves using guns, axes, and explosives. The agency notes a shift from non-violent to forceful methods, suggesting new criminal networks targeting cultural artefacts. Precious metals and ancient Chinese porcelain are preferred due to their high value and ease of sale. Recent cases include a 2025 heist at the Louvre, where thieves smashed display cases and stole jewellery worth €88m. Europol warns of potential recruitment of low-level thieves for such crimes.

The Trump administration has proposed a $103,265 fee for new H-1B visas, a significant increase from previous costs. The rule, which aims to make the visa program more expensive, was initially imposed in 2025 but blocked by courts. The proposed regulation, set to undergo a 30-day public comment period, could be finalized by year's end. Critics argue the fee violates existing law, while the administration claims it falls under presidential authority to restrict entry. Legal challenges from the U.S. Chamber of Commerce and Democratic-led states continue, questioning the legality of the fee and the Department of Homeland Security's authority to impose it.

Canada and its allies have re-established a unified position following the collapse of trade talks with Trump. The group had previously coordinated efforts to counter Trump's policies. The failed negotiations led to a shift in diplomatic strategy. Allies expressed concerns over trade practices during the discussions. The situation highlights ongoing tensions in international trade relations.

Israel has warned Hamas of increased strikes on Gaza following the discovery of kites, drones, and balloons launched from the territory. These kites, not carrying explosives, were found in Israeli communities near the Gaza border, prompting Defence Minister Israel Katz to vow 'forceful actions' to stop the activity. Hamas denied responsibility, calling the kites 'children's toys' and accusing Israel of using the incidents as a pretext for continued attacks. The Israeli military believes Hamas may have tested its response to such threats, though no explosives were found. Meanwhile, Israeli strikes in Gaza resulted in casualties, with the military claiming to have targeted Hamas operatives. The conflict, which began after the October 7 attack, has caused significant civilian casualties in Gaza.

French President Emmanuel Macron is meeting Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman in Paris. The discussions focus on the Middle East situation and France's potential to benefit from Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 investment program. The talks are described as rare, highlighting the strategic importance of the engagement.

In January 2026, Iranian security forces used live ammunition and automatic weapons to suppress large-scale protests against the regime, according to a human rights physician. Massoud, a protester injured by pellets and gunfire, died months later due to untreated wounds, highlighting the lack of medical care for victims. Doctors report that many protesters suffered severe injuries to the head, chest, and limbs, with some cases indicating intentional killing. Security forces also used knives and machetes when ammunition ran out. Victims, fearing retaliation, avoided hospitals, leading to preventable deaths and long-term disabilities. A 32-year-old woman, Mahla, was shot while trying to get her son out of a protest, leaving her unable to work. Teenagers like Ashkan, who lost an eye and a leg, face lifelong disabilities and lost their professional futures. The regime continues to prosecute and execute those linked to the protests, with at least 56 executions since March 2026 on national security charges.

Chess continues to captivate millions globally despite growing concerns about declining attention spans and reliance on digital shortcuts. The game is increasingly used as an educational tool and mental exercise, supported by research showing its benefits for cognitive and emotional development. High-profile figures like Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez and soccer players Erling Haaland and Unai Simón are among its devotees. The International Chess Federation (FIDE) has 203 member federations, while online platforms like Chess.com report over 250 million user accounts. The game's complexity, with more possible moves than atoms in the universe, and its historical and cultural significance across fields like AI and international politics, contribute to its enduring appeal. Despite challenges like the Spanish Inquisition's bans and gender imbalances, chess remains a vital part of global culture, with Spain leading efforts to integrate it into education and therapy programs.

Chiikawa's animated film 'The Secret of Mermaid Island' has exceeded ¥10 billion in box office revenue in Japan, 30 days after its July 24 release. The movie, based on a web series by Nagano, attracted 7.66 million viewers and opened with ¥990 million, the seventh-largest debut in Japan's box-office history. The film's success has led to expanded theatrical experiences, including 4DX screenings, interactive singalongs, and glow-stick events starting in September.

The U.S. Treasury Secretary, Scott Bessent, is set to announce new economic pressures on Iran, aiming to push the country back into negotiations. President Trump described the measures as an 'economic D-Day,' while Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, warned of a 'seismic' retaliation. The sanctions are expected to worsen economic conditions in Iran, with reports of rising inflation and unaffordable medicines. Meanwhile, Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney announced retaliatory tariffs on U.S. imports starting September 8, following the Trump administration's 50% tariffs on Canadian goods. The trade dispute has led to the collapse of U.S.-Canada negotiations, with the new tariffs affecting only about 5% of bilateral trade.

French officials expressed hope that a Dragon Ball-themed amusement park, backed by a Saudi investment fund, will be signed during Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's visit. Valerie Pecresse, head of the Ile-de-France region, noted the project had been in development for 18 months. The agreement is expected to be finalized during a meeting at the Elysee Palace. A Saudi investment company is reportedly behind the project, which could be located in Courdimanche. Discussions on multiple economic agreements are ongoing ahead of the strategic partnership council meeting.

Trinamool Congress (TMC) general secretary Abhishek Banerjee has filed a petition with the Supreme Court, urging an expedited decision on disqualification pleas against 20 MPs accused of defecting to the Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI). The case, scheduled for hearing on August 25, challenges the delay in resolving the petitions. The TMC argues that the MPs' alignment with NCPI constitutes a voluntary exit from the party, violating anti-defection laws. The rebel MPs claim their move represents a valid merger. The petition names Lok Sabha speaker Om Birla and house secretary general as respondents, alongside the 20 MPs involved.

Russian President Vladimir Putin praised Prime Minister Narendra Modi for contributing to the growth of Russia-India trade during talks with External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar. Putin noted increased trade turnover this year, attributing much of the progress to Modi's personal attention. Jaishankar highlighted significant economic cooperation, including energy, fertilizers, and nuclear sectors, and expressed plans for future summits. The meeting precedes Putin's expected BRICS summit visit to India in September.

August 2026 saw Rs 21,000 crore in IPO fundraising, the highest in one year, driven by pent-up supply after a slow first half of the year. Pranav Haldea of Prime Database noted that market conditions improved, but investors remain cautious, with some companies deferring plans or cutting valuations. The market faces challenges, and experts expect continued momentum in September, though regulatory approvals could impact future offerings. A large pipeline of Rs 4.93 lakh crore remains, contingent on stable secondary market conditions.

A study led by Kuntal Saha documents the naturalisation of African Bermuda-grass (Cynodon nlemfuensis) in India's Himalayas and Western Ghats, highlighting systemic delays in identifying invasive species. The research, spanning decades, shows that it took nearly 30 years to confirm the species' presence, with an average delay of 27 years between initial identification and publication. Experts note that taxonomic challenges and lack of digitised herbarium collections in India hinder early detection, allowing invasive plants to spread unchecked. The study underscores the need for improved surveillance, taxonomic capacity-building, and integrated policies to manage biological invasions, which are estimated to cost India $127-182 billion over 1960–2020. Researchers stress that early intervention is critical to prevent ecological and economic damage, especially as the species spreads through disturbed habitats and infrastructure corridors.

Rahul Gandhi's comments on the Manusmriti during a political event have triggered a backlash from the BJP, with Yogi Adityanath accusing him of insulting India's cultural heritage. The BJP criticized Gandhi for promoting a 'patriarchal mindset' and questioned Congress's stance on cultural symbols like Vande Mataram. Meanwhile, Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate defended women's rights, citing rising domestic violence and feticide rates, and criticized the BJP's traditional values. The debate highlights contrasting approaches to gender equality, with Shrinate advocating for rejecting ancient texts and Pragya emphasizing cultural identity. Separately, Tamil Nadu's Chief Minister canceled a greenfield airport project to protect agricultural land, sparking criticism over development setbacks.

A German woman living in Bengaluru shared her confusion over the city's chaotic traffic and rapidly changing weather on social media. In an Instagram video, she expressed bewilderment at the unpredictable driving habits and sudden weather shifts. Social media users responded with humor, comparing Bengaluru's weather to Germany's and suggesting locals adapt to the conditions. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) reported continued cloudy skies and light rain for the following days, advising residents to carry umbrellas.

The NITI Aayog report reveals that while 7.67 crore people have been trained under India's skilling programs since 2014-15, employment outcomes remain uneven. The report criticizes the current system for gaps in funding, employer participation, and labor market alignment. It recommends outcome-based financing models and industry collaboration. The report also notes a mismatch between education and jobs, with only 8.25% of graduates employed in roles matching their qualifications. It calls for reforms including vocational education integration, public-private partnerships, and a Digital Skills Passport to improve skills alignment with market demands.

Congress spokesperson Supriya Shrinate accused the government of 'gross mismanagement' during a debate on India Today, citing a 40% rise in sugar prices over three months. She criticized the continuation of exports despite low reserves and the delayed policy response. Political analyst Rajat Sethi attributed the price hike to reduced sugarcane output, global supply shortages, and speculative hoarding, defending the ethanol blending program. The discussion highlighted contrasting views on economic responsibility and policy effectiveness. Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay canceled a 27,400 crore rupee airport project to protect agricultural land and wetlands, sparking political debate over development priorities.

Congress leader Rahul Gandhi has responded to Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju's recent river plunge stunt by suggesting Rijiju may need training for such activities, while implying it is routine for him. The exchange is part of a ongoing rivalry between the two political figures over fitness and physical activities. Rijiju shared videos of himself swimming in the gushing waters of a river in Arunachal Pradesh, comparing it to a 'child's play' for him. Gandhi's comments were posted on X, where he referred to Rijiju as the 'stunt master' and criticized the risks involved in such stunts. The interaction follows a series of jibes between the two, including a parliamentary conversation last year and a jiu-jitsu challenge from Gandhi earlier this year. Rijiju also explained the differences between swimming in raging rivers and calmer waters, emphasizing the need for specific techniques.

The Indian government announced an Offer for Sale (OFS) to sell up to 6% of its stake in Hindustan Copper at ₹514 per share, a 10.45% discount to the stock's closing price. The OFS, valued at ₹3000 crore, aims to reduce government holdings from 66.14% to a lower percentage. The sale includes 3% for retail investors and an additional 3% for oversubscription. Global copper price increases and supply concerns have driven the stock's 17% rise in August. The government has raised ₹52,716 crore through PSU disinvestment this fiscal year.

Wall Street stocks fell on Monday as investors weighed the Trump administration's warnings about Iran, Nvidia's earnings report, and upcoming inflation data. The Dow Jones, S&P 500, and Nasdaq Composite all declined slightly. Semiconductor stocks like Marvell and Micron dropped over 6%. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent discussed potential economic measures against Iran, while markets also monitored bond yields and energy prices. Gold prices rose amid a weaker dollar and Treasury buyback plans.

Alibaba raised $10.2 billion through a Hong Kong share sale to fund AI infrastructure, leading to an 8.5% stock drop. The company sold 710 million shares at HK$112.70 each, with demand three times the available shares. Alibaba's top executives, Joseph Tsai and Eddie Wu, purchased shares after the decline, acquiring about HK$120 million worth of stock. The funds will support AI initiatives, including AI chips, data centers, and large language models. Alibaba plans to invest $56.5 billion in AI over three years, aiming to compete globally. The company has also sold non-core assets to fund its expansion, including its gaming unit and stakes in other businesses. Alibaba's cloud business saw a 38% revenue increase, with AI-related revenue growing rapidly. However, investors remain cautious about the long-term profitability of Alibaba's AI investments.

The article discusses two main topics: India's food safety crisis and the BJP's political reshuffle. Food safety experts and journalists highlight the prevalence of contaminated food in restaurants and cloud kitchens, despite government inspections. Krish Ashok notes that systemic checks are lacking and food safety in India remains at a third-world level. Shivani Kava explains that food safety officials are understaffed and only investigate upon complaints. Dhanya Rajendran mentions that food delivery apps hide bad food from algorithms rather than removing it. The discussion also covers the BJP's political realignments, with Aditya Menon noting that key positions remain unchanged but Smriti Irani's placement is significant. The reshuffle includes moves like Amit Malaviya's reassignment, with debates over his role in Gen Z outreach. The panel also touches on the broader political dissent and the BJP's communication strategies.

Shares of Lalithaa Jewellery Mart closed 23.58% higher at ₹248.40 on the BSE, marking a 24% premium over the issue price of ₹201. The stock opened at ₹265.30, peaking at ₹274.30 during trading. On the NSE, shares listed at ₹265, up 31.84% from the issue price, and ended at ₹248.44, a 23.60% increase. The company's market valuation reached ₹13,903.19 crore.

A social media image showing Rajiv Gandhi with Rahul Gandhi has been misidentified, with users claiming the man carrying bags is Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge. Fact-checkers traced the image to an old India Today article from 1983, identifying the man as Siddharth Reddy, who was associated with Gandhi's constituency in Uttar Pradesh. Further verification through NTV Telugu reports and Kharge's social media posts confirmed the misidentification. The conclusion states the individual in the viral image is not Kharge but Reddy.

Nelio Biedermann's debut novel 'Lázár' traces the von Lázár family's struggles in 20th century Hungary, focusing on their diminishing social status and the impact of World War II. The novel, structured in six parts, follows the protagonist Lajos von Lázár and his father Sandor, exploring themes of masculinity, family, and national identity. Biedermann draws from his family's history of exile from Hungary, examining how isolated male psyches grapple with social upheaval. While the novel's stark narrative style and Gothic realism capture the horror of violence, it struggles to convey emotional depth beyond visual shock. Critics note its fragmented narrative and uneven treatment of female characters, suggesting it falls short as a family saga despite moments of powerful storytelling. The book, priced at Rs.699, is published by MacLehose Press.

Nomura has recommended five real estate firms, including DLF and Prestige Estates, with mixed recent performance. The brokerage highlighted that the sector's listed players performed in line with expectations despite a volatile Q1 FY27. DLF shares gained 2% weekly but fell 2% in 2026, while Prestige Estates saw a 2% weekly rise. Other picks include Oberoi Realty, Lodha Developers, and Aditya Birla Real Estate, with varying short- and long-term returns. Godrej Properties received a 'Hold' rating.

MIT engineers have created a machine-learning algorithm called 'η-learning' to generate plausible extreme weather scenarios without relying on historical data of such events. The method uses daily weather records and maps to learn statistical patterns, enabling it to simulate extreme storms, heatwaves, and wildfires that could occur with specific frequencies, like once every 100 years. The algorithm combines point statistics with spatial data to create maps of potential extreme events, such as rainfall exceeding recorded levels. This approach helps planners prepare for unprecedented scenarios by visualizing their likely characteristics, including intensity, duration, and geographic impact. The tool could also be applied to fields like financial markets and robotics. The researchers published their findings in Nature Communications.

Meta has introduced the MTIA 300, its first training chip designed for recommendation and ranking models, featuring built-in NICs and communication-offloading engines. The chip integrates networking directly into the chip package, eliminating bottlenecks seen in traditional GPU architectures by using 1.2 TB/s of I/O bandwidth through 12 Ethernet-based NICs. MTIA 300 includes 16 dedicated message engines that handle communication independently of computation, enabling near-perfect isolation between compute and communication tasks. The co-designed HCCL communication library compiles collective operations into autonomous execution, improving efficiency and reducing latency. This design allows for faster training times, with MTIA 300 achieving 3.9 times faster communication compared to equivalent GPU clusters. The chip's architecture supports future AI workloads requiring high communication efficiency and low latency.

Databricks has developed an AI-powered debugging tool called AI SRE to streamline incident investigation across its extensive infrastructure. The system automates triage by analyzing platform health, service-level metrics, and runbook procedures, providing engineers with a structured diagnostic summary before they even open their laptops. By integrating structured checks with LLM-powered synthesis, AI SRE reduces the time spent on debugging by offering context-rich insights and evidence-backed recommendations. The tool supports both automatic triage and interactive investigation, allowing engineers to explore hypotheses and request additional data. Databricks emphasizes transparency, ensuring every conclusion links to verifiable evidence, and has seen positive feedback from teams using it to improve incident response efficiency. The platform is designed as a layered system, enabling teams to build and maintain their own agentic runbooks while benefiting from shared operational primitives and APIs.

NVLink Fusion allows custom XPUs to connect with NVIDIA's established AI infrastructure, enhancing performance and reducing time-to-market for semi-custom AI factories. The solution addresses the complexity of building AI factories by combining custom XPU design with mature infrastructure, including scale-up networking, rack-scale architecture, and a robust supplier ecosystem. Key benefits include improved performance through high-bandwidth, low-latency networking, reduced operational risk via proven technology stacks, and streamlined integration with NVIDIA's MGX architecture. The initiative supports a unified platform for diverse workloads, enabling hyperscalers and AI-native companies to build scalable, efficient AI systems without requiring full infrastructure development from scratch.

NVIDIA is extending its Vera Rubin NVL72 platform with the full production of Groq 3 LPX, a new inference accelerator designed for agentic AI systems. In tests with Gemma 4 31B, the system achieved 3,400 output tokens per second for long-context use cases, 4x faster than alternatives. Partners like Nebius, CoreWeave, and SpaceXAI are adopting the technology to power agentic applications, with SpaceXAI using Vera Rubin CPUs for CPU-intensive tasks. NVIDIA emphasizes extreme codesign across compute, networking, and inference to optimize performance and throughput for large-scale, low-latency AI workloads. The company also introduced Spectrum-X Multiplane and Scale-In infrastructure to support growing AI factories, highlighting a shift toward integrated, efficient AI infrastructure for the agentic era.

NVIDIA has introduced BlueField-4, a new DPU (Data Processing Unit) designed to power Scale-In network infrastructure for agentic AI factories. This infrastructure accelerates secure access, data movement, and operations across AI compute systems. Traditional cloud infrastructure, built for predictable workloads, is insufficient for agentic AI, which requires high-bandwidth, multi-tenant networking and security. Scale-In transforms north-south networks into a unified, accelerated domain, using BlueField-4, NVIDIA DOCA, and Spectrum-X Ethernet. BlueField-4 provides host-independent processing, offloading security, storage, and networking tasks from host CPUs. It supports four infrastructure pillars: Scale-Up, Scale-Out, Scale-Across, and Context Memory, each addressing different AI factory needs. NVIDIA claims BlueField-4 offers 4x more memory bandwidth and 2x more network bandwidth than its predecessor, enabling more concurrent services and higher throughput. DOCA microservices and Spectrum-X Ethernet enable programmable, high-performance networking and storage, while BlueField Astra ensures consistent policy enforcement across both Scale-In and Scale-Out networks. The solution aims to provide secure, efficient, and scalable AI infrastructure for enterprise and cloud environments.

Researchers introduce Internalized Visual Thinking (IVT), a framework that improves video reasoning by training models to internally predict future frames without generating visual outputs during inference. IVT combines textual prediction with next-embedding prediction on unlabeled videos, enabling models to capture motion and object interactions. The method outperforms text-only approaches and reduces inference latency by over 5× compared to Visual CoT. The study suggests that explicit pixel generation during inference may not be necessary for effective video reasoning.

ZDNET curates Labor Day deals featuring TVs and tech products, offering at least 20% off. The selection process involves personal interest, price tracking, and customer reviews. Deals are available leading up to and during the holiday on September 7.

Instinct, a private AI assistant developed by Spear Street Technology, has drawn privacy and security concerns due to its extensive data access and terms of service. The AI connects to users' devices and applications, granting it access to emails, messages, and device data. Testers raised alarms over its 'perpetual and irrevocable' license to use and store user data, including screen captures and keyboard inputs. Some users reported issues like persistent inbox summaries after disconnecting and unauthorized actions, such as sending emails without consent. Critics argue the trade-offs for hyper-personalized AI tools may outweigh privacy risks. Instinct's team has not publicly addressed these concerns, while investors like Kleiner Perkins and Conviction have backed the startup.

ZDNET reports that Blink is offering a discounted bundle of its Battery Doorbell 2K+ and Outdoor 2K+ camera for $100, a 41% discount. The bundle includes a Sync Module Core for connecting up to 10 cameras. The Outdoor 2K+ camera, which uses two AA batteries, can last up to two years and provides 2K resolution for monitoring property. The doorbell variant uses three AA batteries and features person detection to reduce false alerts. The deal is available for a limited time, with the original price around $170 and previous sales reaching $55.

Taiwan has indicted nine individuals, including an Nvidia senior manager and two Supermicro employees, for allegedly forging documents to conceal illegal exports of high-end AI servers to China. Prosecutors in Keelung charged the suspects with breach of trust and document forgery, with one suspect still at large. The investigation found that 74 out of 130 B300 servers were exported to Chinese customers, while 56 were blocked by customs. Supermicro confirmed it is cooperating with Taiwanese authorities and emphasized its commitment to protecting advanced technologies and complying with export controls.

The article explores how data teams are adopting agentic AI to automate complex workflows and deliver real-time insights. Data agents, powered by AI, analyze enterprise data to answer questions and perform tasks, offering a more dynamic alternative to static dashboards. These agents require high-quality, well-governed data and robust metadata to provide accurate insights. Metadata, along with semantic layers, ontologies, and knowledge graphs, provides the necessary context for agents to understand business definitions and relationships. The article emphasizes the importance of standardized data access protocols like MCP to enable scalable AI integration while maintaining governance and security. Identity passthrough ensures agents act with appropriate permissions, preserving existing access controls. As data architectures evolve with open table formats, the catalog becomes a critical control plane for data discovery and governance. The future of data intelligence depends on creating a trusted foundation that supports both human and AI decision-making.

Researchers at TU Delft have developed a system that allows users to adjust the driving behavior of self-driving cars through natural language. The system uses a large language model (LLM) to translate user requests, such as 'go faster' or 'drive smoothly,' into adjustments to a safety-aware motion-planning algorithm. The LLM interprets these instructions and modifies the parameters of the motion planner, which determines the vehicle's path and speed. The system keeps the human in the loop by describing proposed changes in non-technical language and asking for confirmation before implementing them. The researchers tested the system in simulation, finding it successfully adjusted driving behavior to match user intent. The approach differs from previous work by focusing on driving style rather than direct control, and it uses a model predictive-path integral controller to ensure safety. While the system allows for personalized driving experiences, it does not replace the need for safety guarantees, as highlighted by other experts in the field.

NVIDIA has released an updated version of its Magpie Multilingual TTS model, offering open weights and improved latency for voice applications. The model supports 12 languages, including new additions like Modern Standard Arabic, Korean, and Brazilian Portuguese, and includes male and female speaker voices. NVIDIA emphasizes the importance of low-latency speech generation, with Magpie achieving a Time to First Audio (TTFA) of 32ms on B200 GPUs. The model's architecture, featuring frame stacking and a local transformer, reduces inference time while maintaining speech quality. Developers can deploy the model on their own infrastructure, customize it with NeMo, and integrate it with other NVIDIA tools for building full voice agents. The release also improves synthesis quality across existing languages, with reduced character error rates and higher speaker similarity scores.

IBM has acquired HRL Laboratories, a research institution specializing in quantum technologies, to advance its quantum computing initiatives. The acquisition aims to leverage HRL's expertise in silicon-spin qubit engineering, which shares fabrication foundations with superconducting qubits. Spin qubits use electron spin states to encode quantum information, with HRL's exchange only qubit architecture utilizing three electrons in quantum dots to represent computational states. This approach offers advantages such as manufacturability at scale, high coherence times, and ease of control. HRL's recent demonstration of a silicon-spin quantum computer with 18 qubits highlights progress in the field. IBM's Director of Research, Jay Gambetta, emphasized that HRL's technologies will strengthen IBM's long-term vision for quantum computing, including quantum sensing and networking applications.

IBM has committed up to $50 million in quantum system access to support the U.S. Department of Energy's Genesis Mission, which aims to accelerate AI-driven scientific discovery. The mission, part of President Trump's initiative, seeks to create an integrated platform combining quantum computing, AI, and supercomputing. IBM, as a member of the Genesis Mission Consortium, will provide access to its 156-qubit IBM Quantum Heron and 120-qubit IBM Quantum Nighthawk processors to national labs over five years. The company's project focuses on integrating AI with quantum algorithms to identify real-world applications, using an agentic research assistant to propose and validate candidate problems. IBM also emphasizes collaboration with national laboratories and quantum research centers to advance the mission's goals of solving complex scientific challenges through quantum-centric supercomputing.

Google Research has expanded its rooftop reflectivity dataset to cover 50+ global cities, offering high-resolution albedo data to help urban planners implement cool-roof solutions. The dataset, accessible via a new Heat Resilience Earth Engine App, enables cities to identify vulnerable neighborhoods and prioritize cool roof retrofits. The research, published in Nature Communications, combines Sentinel-2 satellite data with high-resolution imagery to achieve 30-cm spatial detail, surpassing neighborhood-level averages. Validation against airborne hyperspectral measurements in Boulder, Colorado, showed a root mean square error of 0.04, ensuring accuracy. The initiative aims to reduce urban heat island effects and lower surface temperatures by up to 0.5°C globally through targeted interventions.

AWS has launched the M9g and M9gd instance types, powered by Graviton5 CPUs, featuring a new Nitro Isolation Engine. This engine, verified using Isabelle/HOL, ensures VM isolation in EC2. The verification process involved 330,000 lines of mathematical proof, comparable to the seL4 project.
