US 10-year Treasury yields reached a 19-month high as oil prices rose over 2% following geopolitical tensions. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh signaled potential rate hikes to combat inflation, influencing market sentiment. Analysts note upcoming employment and consumer price data will be critical before the Fed's September 16 decision. Options traders are positioning for further yield increases, with some bets on 30-year yields reaching 5.7%. Heavy corporate bond supply in September also pressures longer-term yields.

Tim Cook ended his 15-year tenure as Apple CEO on Monday, issuing a farewell memo that emphasized company culture over product announcements. He confirmed he is not leaving the company but will transition to the role of executive chairman on Tuesday. Cook praised successor John Ternus, a hardware engineering leader, for his ability to build world-changing products. The article notes Cook avoided discussing AI, regulation, or China in his message. Cook will continue managing government relations in Washington and Beijing. He signed off with a personal note expressing gratitude to employees and his enduring commitment to Apple.

Bloomberg reported that Apple veteran Phil Schiller is stepping down from his roles leading the App Store and product events. Sources indicate Schiller will retain his Apple Fellow title while working on unspecified initiatives. Eddy Cue will assume responsibility for the App Store, with Carson Oliver managing daily operations. Nola Weinstein will take over the events team, reporting to Kristin Huguet Quayle. This transition occurs as CEO Tim Cook prepares to hand over leadership to John Ternus. The report notes that Schiller was a key decision-maker for the App Store and product launches. Several other senior executives are also leaving or shifting to smaller roles at the company.

OpenAI reported that its advertising business reached a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate within 200 days of launching. The company expanded self-service ad access to over 40 countries, including India and Europe. OpenAI stated that ads are clearly identified and do not influence chatbot responses. Meanwhile, the European Union designated ChatGPT as a very large online platform under the Digital Services Act, requiring new compliance measures.

APSRTC chairman Konakalla Narayana Rao announced the corporation will launch 350 electric buses in October as part of a modernization plan. The state government has allotted 750 e-buses under the PM e-Bus scheme and is seeking an additional 300 units. Work on necessary electrical substations and charging stations is currently in progress. The chairman also highlighted the Stree Sakthi Scheme, which has provided free travel to women and persons with disabilities.

TVK and Congress leaders resolved a dispute over the next Prime Ministerial candidate. TVK acolytes supported C. Joseph Vijay after a poll showed him backing, while Congress threatened to quit the coalition. TNCC president Manickam Tagore met Chief Minister Vijay to restore ties. Tagore dismissed the poll as a fabricated story designed to create division. The alliance remains intact after the rapprochement.

Bloomberg reports that new heavy rain threatens search-and-rescue operations in the Grand Canyon following deadly floods. The US National Weather Service estimates monsoon rains dropped a month's worth of moisture over the terrain. Joshua Weiss, a Weather Prediction Center forecaster, warned that additional rain could cause significant flash floods. The National Park Service confirmed two deaths and noted that the body of a 46-year-old man was recovered. Approximately 40% of the Transcanyon Waterline was damaged, limiting water reserves and restricting park access to day use and dry camping only.

A Bandra magistrate court remanded health coach Megha Rawal to police custody for one day regarding the death of eight-year-old Ansh Gupta. Police allege Rawal was using her mobile phone while driving the Innova Crysta that struck the boy. Preliminary investigations found no evidence of alcohol consumption, though forensic analysis of her blood sample is ongoing. Defence lawyer Amar Paragonkar opposes the culpable homicide charge, claiming the incident was an unfortunate accident without intent.

The dollar edged lower on Monday as futures markets increased odds of a September interest-rate hike following Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh's hawkish remarks. Traders are now focusing on Friday's August jobs report, which economists estimate will show 55,000 new jobs. Warsh indicated further tightening may be needed to bring inflation down to 2%. Meanwhile, the euro and sterling gained ground, while the yen weakened slightly against the dollar.

President Donald Trump labeled Iran a failed nation in a Truth Social post, claiming the country has no navy or air force and faces a 300% inflation rate. The remarks followed recent military exchanges where the US struck Iranian rocket launchers and Iran retaliated with missiles and drones. While Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for diplomacy, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated Washington would continue economic pressure. International mediators, including UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, urged both sides to return to negotiations as fears of a broader regional conflict grow.

Rural Development Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan reviewed the watershed development component of the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana on Monday. The minister stated that watershed development is essential for achieving a drought-free India. Under the current scheme, 1,220 projects covering over 52 lakh hectares have been sanctioned at a total cost of ₹12,404 crore. Chouhan emphasized that projects must be assessed based on actual improvements in land productivity and farmer livelihoods rather than just expenditure. He also called for states to expedite implementation to ensure measurable outcomes on the ground.

Former Indian captain Rohit Sharma is launching his television show, Family Full House, on September 19, 2026. The program will feature challenges with popular television personalities and uses his viral cricket lines in promos. Sharma has retired from Test and T20 cricket but remains an active ODI player. Fans are also awaiting confirmation of his participation in the 2027 World Cup.

The S&P 500 enters September near a record high of 7,800, yet investors face several potential risks. Analysts highlight that while historical data suggests a positive setup, midterm election years often bring market turbulence. Key concerns include low VIX readings indicating complacency, rising 10-year Treasury yields above 4.7%, and uncertainty regarding a potential Federal Reserve rate hike. Additionally, investor sentiment remains overly bullish, and earnings growth is heavily concentrated in a few large technology companies. Experts advise watching the 7,610 support level closely as the market navigates these mixed signals.

Tamil Nadu Congress Legislature Party leader Tharahai Cuthbert stated that Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay has selected Rahul Gandhi as the alliance's Prime Ministerial candidate. Cuthbert dismissed reports of a rift between the Congress and the TVK, asserting the party operates independently. She characterized an FIR against Gandhi as evidence of BJP anxiety regarding his public support. Additionally, she explained her recent change in Assembly seating was a procedural adjustment following her appointment as floor leader.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi told President Vladimir Putin on Monday that Russia should move from endless war toward the end of war. Modi urged the Russian leader to conclude the conflict that has negatively impacted the global community.

Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi called on Russian President Vladimir Putin to conclude the war in Ukraine during a meeting at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Bishkek. Modi stated that India supports all efforts for peace and described the conflict as a need to move from an "endless war to end of war." Putin responded that Russia is moving in that direction while emphasizing the strengthening of their strategic partnership. The article notes that India is balancing its ties with Russia and Iran while negotiating a trade deal with the United States. Economic data indicates bilateral trade between India and Russia totaled nearly $60 billion in the 2026 fiscal year, with both nations aiming to reach $100 billion by the end of the decade. The SCO, founded in 2001, now includes members representing over 40% of the world's population, though analysts suggest the bloc has struggled to translate this ambition into concrete global action.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath stated the state holds enough sugar for seven months, yet wholesale prices remain among the highest in India. The article explains that warehouse stock levels do not directly determine retail prices due to complex regulatory controls. Government data indicates mills hold approximately 17.94 lakh tonnes, while the Chief Minister cited 28 lakh tonnes, a discrepancy potentially caused by unsold sugar floating in the open market. Furthermore, the Union Food Ministry sets monthly release quotas that restrict how much sugar mills can sell, regardless of available inventory. The text details how the Essential Commodities Act limits dealer stock and how the Minimum Selling Price of Rs 31 a kg influences market behavior. Industry associations report production costs exceeding Rs 41 a kg, contributing to high prices despite record cane production. Ultimately, the article argues that central regulations on quotas and pricing, rather than state stock levels, dictate sugar availability and cost for consumers.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Vladimir Putin in Bishkek to deliver India's message for peace in Ukraine. Modi stated that every day of conflict sets humanity back and urged a move from endless war to an end of war. He emphasized that India supports all efforts towards a peaceful resolution. Putin noted that Russian-Indian relations continue to strengthen based on their special partnership.

Lionel Messi announced his retirement from the Argentine national team on Monday, ending his career at 39. The decision follows the World Cup final loss to Spain and the recent death of his father, Jorge. Messi stated the choice hurt deeply but felt the time had come. He emphasized his lifelong commitment to the jersey and the fans.

The National Stock Exchange recorded a turnover of Rs 39,718 crore during its first closing auction session. NSE stated that over 98,000 unique investors participated in the event. The session coincided with the implementation of the MSCI August 2026 Index Review. Turnover was approximately 42 times higher than the previous trading session. The exchange noted the mechanism aligns Indian markets with global best practices.

The Federal Survey reports that a poll of 5,786 respondents across Tamil Nadu indicates the public values Chief Minister Vijay's corruption-free promise more than his welfare schemes. Over 43% of voters rank the anti-corruption pledge as the government's top achievement, while only 28% cite welfare programs like free gold and sarees. Despite criticism regarding power cuts and a planned Secretariat move, 58% rate the TVK government's first 100 days as good or very good. The survey also notes that 43% approve of the arrest of DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin, though opinions on the Congress-DMK split remain divided. While the Chief Minister's daily presence at work is popular, nearly half of respondents disapprove of the proposed office relocation.

India rejected an arbitration court order regarding the Indus Waters Treaty, stating the panel was illegally constituted. The Ministry of External Affairs maintained that the treaty remains suspended following the Pahalgam terrorist attack. While the Permanent Court of Arbitration ruled the treaty is in force, India claims the court lacks jurisdiction over its sovereign decisions. Consequently, India continues advancing hydropower projects in Jammu and Kashmir despite the interim prohibition.

AWS describes a new solution for enterprise agentic retrieval built on Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base and AgentCore. The authors report that this architecture allows agents to reason across multiple knowledge bases and synthesize cited answers. The solution deploys four native AWS CloudFormation stacks to automate the entire workflow. A user sends a question to the agent hosted on the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, which auto-instruments every step with OpenTelemetry spans. The agent's reasoning model plans the task and performs cross-knowledge-base routing to select the appropriate tool. The selected tool call is brokered by the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Gateway over the Model Context Protocol. AgenticRetrieveStream decomposes the question into sub-queries and retrieves iteratively from the managed datastore. Throughout the process, the runtime emits spans and metrics to Amazon CloudWatch and AWS X-Ray. The authors note that this approach removes the need to provision or patch a vector database. The solution includes two forms of evaluation: on-demand and continuous online scoring.

The FTC and 22 states filed a lawsuit alleging Amazon manipulated online auctions to overcharge over a million advertising customers. The complaint claims the scheme likely netted the company $20bn since 2019 by replacing actual auction results with higher prices. Amazon strongly disagrees with the premise, calling the suit misguided and stating it fundamentally misunderstands how advertisers operate. The company's shares fell 2.5% following the announcement. This marks another legal conflict for Amazon, which previously settled a separate FTC case for $2.5bn regarding unauthorized Prime subscriptions.

The Pentagon has added custom versions of ChatGPT and Grok to its secure GenAI.mil portal, granting access to 3 million personnel. The Department of Defense reports that over 1.7 million users have already joined the platform. These tools aim to accelerate work while keeping sensitive data within secure government channels. The additions highlight the Pentagon's strategy to partner with multiple tech firms following its dispute with Anthropic.

China's ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) is producing HBM3E chips in small quantities, according to a report from The Information citing two insiders. This development places CXMT a generation behind Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron, which are mass-producing HBM4. The report notes that CXMT is three to five years behind technically and struggles with low yields, estimated at around 25 percent in June. Additionally, the $8.6 billion raised in CXMT's Shanghai IPO was not earmarked for HBM development.

ZDNET reports that the Satechi OntheGo Foldable Stand Hub transforms a tablet into a productivity tool by combining a stand with a multi-port hub. The accessory lifts the device 7/8ths of an inch and tilts it back 23 degrees to improve ergonomics. It features a 100W USB-C input, USB-A and USB-C ports, a 4K HDMI output, and SD card slots. ZDNET notes the hub supports Samsung DeX and costs $80. The reviewer states the compact design fits easily into a tech bag.

Andrew Bailey, Bank of England governor, warns G20 finance ministers that inflated AI valuations and rising leverage threaten global financial stability. He highlights risks from leveraged ETFs and cross-investments between AI firms and hyperscalers. Bailey also flags frontier AI models as a potential catalyst for faster, cheaper cyberattacks on banks. He urges international coordination on AI regulation to mitigate these systemic risks.

Jayeeta Putatunda, forward deployed AI engineering lead at Turing, demonstrates a multi-agent workflow that converts daily financial headlines into structured analyst briefings. The system defines scope, plans coverage, searches preferred sources, validates links, generates reports, and captures feedback into memory. Putatunda built the stack on open source models to allow execution without an API key. The approach emphasizes single-purpose agents to improve traceability and reduce pipeline failures. The full codebase is available in Putatunda's GitHub repository.

The United States and Canada have renewed trade tensions, imposing tariffs on billions of dollars of goods. Analysts warn that complex supply chains mean businesses may face multiple tariff payments. While the US steel sector might gain a slight edge, the integrated automotive industry faces significant disruption on both sides of the border. Experts note that reducing US reliance on Canadian aluminum will take years due to long construction timelines and competing energy demands from the AI boom.

The Centre for Energy Research and Clean Air reported that global energy import bills rose by $330 billion between March and August due to Strait of Hormuz disruptions. In response, Saudi Arabia rerouted exports via the Red Sea and Suez Canal, while the UAE plans to double Fujairah pipeline capacity to 3.6 million barrels daily. TotalEnergies joined ADNOC in expanding this project and exploring a new Iraq-Syria pipeline route. Iraq is evaluating a four-year new pipeline or a three-year repair of an existing line, alongside talks with Turkey. Kuwait seeks to connect to UAE and Saudi ports, while Japan agreed to support regional network expansion. Gulf governments now prioritize port infrastructure as a mission-critical priority to mitigate war-induced economic shocks.

Voltalia has fully commissioned the 148 MW Bolobedu solar farm in Limpopo, South Africa, to supply Richards Bay Minerals. The facility is expected to generate around 300 GWh annually, avoiding more than 237,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions each year. During construction, the project created employment for about 800 local residents, including women and young people. The project uses a wheeling arrangement to deliver power through Eskom's national grid to the mining customer's operational sites.

Waaree Energies Limited announced it secured a Letter of Award from SECI for a 700 MW solar project with 2,800 MWh energy storage in Solapur. The company stated the deal was received on August 27, 2026, and will be developed by its subsidiary Waaree Forever Energies Private Limited. The Power Purchase Agreement covers a 25-year tenure and the firm confirmed no related-party interests exist. This award strengthens Waaree Energies' position in large-scale renewable energy development.

JA announces the Journey Ahead: JA Roadshow 2026 to demonstrate its expanding energy ecosystem across Europe. The initiative will highlight battery energy storage systems and various photovoltaic technologies including the DeepBlue 5.0 and HyperGen modules. The tour begins in Poland on September 2 and will visit multiple countries throughout the year. JA aims to position itself as an integrated energy solutions provider by combining generation, storage, and management innovations.

Apple alleges that former senior system electrical engineer Chang Liu accessed a power converter circuit schematic while working at OpenAI. The company claims Liu used this proprietary information to train an AI agent in March 2026. Apple states this new evidence emerged from a MacBook provided to the company on August 21. Consequently, Apple is asking a U.S. federal court to expedite discovery proceedings in its trade secret case against OpenAI, which has sought to dismiss the lawsuit.

Federal regulators and 22 state attorneys general sued Amazon on Monday, alleging the company secretly overcharged advertisers by manipulating auction bids. The complaint claims Amazon deceived 1.2 million brands and sellers to pocket tens of billions of dollars. Amazon responded by arguing the lawsuit misrepresented its ad auction reality and cherry-picked findings. This marks the third major federal lawsuit against the company in recent years.

The FTC and 22 U.S. states sued Amazon alleging the company illegally raised ad prices without advertiser knowledge. The lawsuit claims Amazon generated over $20 billion in profits at the expense of customers. Amazon denied wrongdoing, stating its policies aim to show relevant ads and that average costs remained flat. The agency seeks tens of billions in damages while Amazon reported a 26% rise in ad sales for the second quarter.

President Donald Trump stated that communities resisting data centers will end up backwards and poor. He urged for data to reign during remarks made on Monday. A Bloomberg columnist noted that tech leaders are financially supporting the Trump administration. Meanwhile, Semafor's Ben Smith wrote that Democrats plan to subpoena Big Tech leaders in 2027.

Japan intends to increase its defense spending to over $55 billion next year to acquire more drones and missiles. The government aims to deploy uncrewed weapons, including a new 3D-printed drone fleet, to counter threats from China, North Korea, and Russia. Beijing has criticized the plan as new militarism, while the budget represents a modest rise compared to South Korea and Taiwan. Officials note the increase may be too incremental to fully satisfy US demands.

Kalshi banned former congressman George Santos for life and fined him $71,356 after discovering he misled the public about his attendance at the State of the Union to profit on prediction markets. The company reported Santos made over $17,000 by betting against his own appearance while claiming he would attend. Federal regulators previously ordered him to return those profits and fined him $17,500. Kalshi also suspended three other political candidates for three years and fined them for wagering on their own campaigns. Laurie Buckhout, Stephen Cloobeck, and Ben Midgley all received penalties for betting on their respective races. These actions follow a settlement involving Gabriel Perez, who profited from insider knowledge of President Trump's speeches. The prediction market industry faces ongoing legal battles over whether it should be regulated as gambling or a financial product, with courts currently divided on the issue.

Venture capitalist Joshua Kushner expressed regret over his involvement in the abandoned Fifa Forward Enterprise scheme. Thrive Eternal had planned a $4.2bn investment in Fifa's commercial subsidiary before the deal collapsed amid backlash. Kushner stated he failed to appreciate the political dynamics of global football. Meanwhile, Uefa is seeking documents from Kushner and financier Greg Maffei for a potential criminal complaint against Gianni Infantino.

Andy Burnham returns to parliament facing a full in-tray of policy dilemmas and potential rebellions. The article outlines several key challenges he must address immediately. First, he must decide whether to approve drilling at the Jackdaw gasfield, a move industry estimates could supply 6% of future UK gas output, while remaining uncertain about the Rosebank oilfield. Second, Burnham prepares for a meeting with Donald Trump at the UN, despite their past mutual insults. Third, he faces pressure to drop a cap on political donations and establish an electoral reform commission. Finally, the Prime Minister must navigate a tight budget, rising energy bills, and the urgent nationalisation of Thames Water. Throughout these issues, Burnham balances manifesto pledges against fiscal realities and internal party divisions.

Gold futures opened down 1.0% on Monday, August 31, 2026, as renewed conflict in the Middle East and Federal Reserve rate expectations weighed on prices. U.S. attacks on Iranian rocket launchers marked the first escalation since July, fueling inflation concerns. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh reiterated the central bank's focus on keeping prices low during his Jackson Hole speech. The article explains that spot prices reflect current market value while futures are exchange-traded contracts settling on future dates.

The Federal Trade Commission and 22 states filed a lawsuit against Amazon alleging the company defrauded 1.2 million advertising customers by inflating auction prices. The complaint claims Amazon misrepresented competitive pricing for online ad products. FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson stated the deceptive conduct could have a staggering impact on millions of misled customers. Amazon responded by calling the allegations patently false and claiming the FTC relies on simplified communications to allege a companywide effort to deceive.

President Donald Trump issued an executive order on August 27, 2026, renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America. This action occurs during an escalating trade war with Canada, where Ontario Premier Doug Ford previously dismissed such suggestions as rhetoric. The article notes this follows Trump's 2025 orders to rename the Gulf of Mexico and Denali. While the U.S. Board on Geographic Names manages domestic names, the article explains that international waters and foreign maps remain under different jurisdictions. Mapping services like Google Maps now display names based on the viewer's location, showing Gulf of America for U.S. users and Gulf of Mexico for others. The piece details the formal domestic process for renaming places, contrasting it with the lack of an international board to enforce name changes abroad.

New South Wales has announced stricter rules limiting Year 12 students to one take-home assessment per subject to combat AI use in exams. Education Minister Prue Car stated the government is committed to protecting teaching and learning from outsourcing. Meanwhile, a Sydney man in his 20s died after being shot during a home invasion in Glen Alpine. Foreign Affairs Minister Penny Wong expressed grave concerns for 43 Australians still missing following floods in Nepal, noting that search efforts are difficult. The federal government has provided $8m in aid and is deploying an RAAF aircraft with supplies. In other news, the Treasury expects AI to help restore Australia's productivity growth to historical averages over coming years. Additionally, the Shop and Warehouse Workers Union is petitioning for a new public holiday on September 1. Property data firm Cotality reports that median capital city home prices have fallen below $1m in August due to weak buyer confidence.

The US Supreme Court ruled 5-4 that the Trump administration can proceed with building a $400m ballroom at the White House. The justices granted an emergency request, stating lower courts likely exceeded their authority in blocking the project. Chief Justice John Roberts dissented, arguing construction is likely unlawful without Congressional approval. The National Trust for Historic Preservation filed the challenge, claiming the president lacks unilateral authority to alter the historic residence. Trump expressed pleasure that the lawsuit failed to halt the work.

President Donald Trump declined to name a preferred successor for the 2028 presidential election, stating there are many candidates he does not know about. While Vice President JD Vance remains the most likely Republican to receive Trump's support, the president's vague comments may disappoint his presumed successor. Trump praised Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's current performance but refused to speculate on his future ambitions. Reports indicate Trump privately favors both Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio, though he has not confirmed a choice. The administration continues to prioritize control of the Republican Party through key endorsements, even as some endorsed candidates have faced primary defeats.

Dale Sanders, 91, became the oldest person to complete the Appalachian Trail, reclaiming a record he previously set in 2017. The Associated Press reported that Sanders fell 71 times during his journey, including incidents requiring hospitalization. He began hiking in September 2025 and finished atop Mount Katahdin in Maine. Sanders credited his support team and social media followers for his motivation. He holds other age-related records, including paddling the Mississippi River at 87.

The Supreme Court voted 5-4 to permit the White House to proceed with a $558 million ballroom project while legal challenges continue. The majority ruled that the National Trust for Historic Preservation likely lacked the legal standing to contest the work, though the court did not determine the project's ultimate legality. Chief Justice John Roberts dissented, arguing the decision undermines the separation of powers because the project lacks congressional approval. President Donald Trump expressed satisfaction with the ruling, stating the construction faces no further threats. The administration claims the ballroom is necessary for national security, while the preservation group insists the President cannot unilaterally redesign the White House. Construction crews are reportedly working 20 hours a day, with key portions expected to finish within months.

Indonesia has intensified efforts to contain haze from wildfires across six provinces in Borneo and Sumatra. The fires have destroyed part of the habitat of hundreds of orangutans and risk the survival of the species. A weak orangutan was found in Ketapang, West Kalimantan, and will be moved to a rehabilitation centre. Karmele Llano Sanchez, CEO of YIARI, stated the situation is critical and the fires are leaving orangutans without food or water.

The Supreme Court issued a divided ruling permitting the White House to continue building a $400 million ballroom. The decision allows construction to proceed despite ongoing legal challenges regarding the project's funding and scope.
The Trump administration announced a plan to pressure Iran by asking nations to cut business ties. However, China has already stated it will not cooperate with these voluntary trade restrictions.

A Belgian judge has extended pre-trial detention for one month for a Canadian national accused of spying for a third country while interning at NATO's SHAPE headquarters. The Belgian Federal Prosecutor's Office announced the decision following a rejected appeal by the defendant, identified as Claire Z. Authorities stated the investigation remains ongoing with no trial date set. While Canadian officials pledged to review security screening processes, a SHAPE spokesperson noted there is no indication military operations were disrupted.

President Donald Trump threatened to retaliate forcefully against Iranian attacks following a month-long pause in hostilities. The exchange began after US strikes on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz, prompting Tehran to target US forces in Jordan and the UAE. While Trump stated all missiles were shot down except one, Jordan intercepted eight missiles and Iran claimed heavy damage to US bases. Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian called for dialogue, contrasting with Trump's description of Iran as a failed nation. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent vowed to continue economic pressure on Tehran. The conflict persists alongside a naval counter-blockade of Iranian ports and a dispute over control of the strategic shipping lane.

Former French Prime Minister Edouard Balladur has died at age 97, his family confirmed to AFP. President Emmanuel Macron honored him as a devoted public servant who dedicated his life to the Fifth Republic. Current Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu called him a statesman with a reformist spirit. Marine Le Pen also shared condolences, praising his commitment to democratic debate. A private mass service is planned in Paris.

Kenya airport staff are striking, causing delays for thousands of passengers. The strike is happening at Kenya's main airport. Travelers are currently grounded due to the industrial action. This news is part of tonight's edition of the broadcast.

India plans to construct one of the world's largest nuclear fleets, creating a market worth tens of billions of dollars. For 15 years, a specific provision in Indian law prevented Japanese firms from participating. Last December, that legal restriction was removed, opening the market to Japanese suppliers. Tokyo now faces a strategic decision on whether to enter this market under rules that reduce supplier liability for catastrophic failures.

The UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination urged governments to implement comprehensive reparations for people of African descent. The 18-member committee stated that time cannot excuse the enduring consequences of the transatlantic slave trade. Experts called for financial and non-financial remedies alongside national action plans. The group also urged private institutions that profited from slavery to contribute to reparative efforts. Committee member Pela Boker-Wilson emphasized that governments must take concrete action beyond mere apologies.

President Donald Trump signed an executive order renaming Lake Ontario to Lake America, extending a previous move to rename the Gulf of Mexico. Geographer Jesús Burgueño notes this unilateral action bypasses standard toponymy commissions and reflects an autocratic style. While New York Governor Kathy Hochul rejects the change, companies like National Geographic are expected to comply domestically. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has publicly rejected the initiative, citing the name's Indigenous origins and historical significance. Experts warn that international bodies like the IHO and UNGEGN do not arbitrate such disputes, leaving the impact dependent on private digital mapping platforms. Some platforms may adopt dual labeling, while others refuse to propagate the change entirely.

NASA successfully launched the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope on Sunday, beginning its journey to a gravitational outpost 1.5 million kilometers from Earth. Nicky Fox, associate administrator of NASA's Science Mission Directorate, stated the mission aims to answer fundamental questions about the universe's composition and whether we are alone. The telescope features a field of view at least one hundred times larger than Hubble, allowing it to scan more than a billion galaxies. Mission scientists expect Roman to discover up to 100,000 new worlds beyond our Solar System. The instrument will utilize weak gravitational lensing to study dark matter and dark energy, addressing discrepancies in the standard model of cosmology. Julie McEnery, the project's senior scientist, described the mission as a revolution in how we observe the universe. Begoña Vila, a co-lead of operations, noted the telescope will provide an overview of the universe's structure that predecessors could not achieve. The spacecraft is expected to generate around 500 terabytes of data annually and operate for five years, with a possible five-year extension. Data will be made publicly available to the global scientific community without a proprietary period.

Nepal's disaster agency reported 939 deaths and 3,925 missing people following catastrophic flash floods. A private-sector association stated at least 900 workers remain unaccounted for at 12 hydropower projects, with about 500 trapped in tunnels. Chinese authorities reported 16 deaths and 546 missing, including over 100 Nepalis. Rescue teams are digging through sludge to find survivors while experts warn chances of survival are diminishing.

The Egyptian army announced that joint air drills with China are ongoing at multiple bases. The second edition of the Eagles of Civilization exercise aims to enhance pilot skills and includes aerial refueling training. Chinese Defense Ministry spokesperson Chen Xi stated the drills will conclude in early September. President Xi Jinping is expected to visit Cairo this week for his first trip to Egypt in a decade.

Nepal's Prime Minister Balendra Shah faces a major crisis as deadly floods kill over 900 people and leave nearly 4,800 missing. Authorities report that rescue efforts are hampered by difficult terrain and delayed international assistance. The disaster has exposed questions about the new government's crisis management capacity and coordination with local authorities. While security agencies received praise for helicopter rescues, critics argue the federal government acted too centrally without involving provincial bodies. Over 5 billion Nepali rupees have been collected for relief, showing public trust in the administration.

A failed coup attempt in Niger highlights deep fractures within the military and increasing reliance on Russian forces. Sahel expert Abdoulaye Sounaye noted that most soldiers earn less than €150 monthly while facing high risks against better-equipped insurgents. General Abdourahamane Tchiani's junta, which ousted President Mohamed Bazoum in 2023, now faces loyalty challenges as troops question leadership and resource allocation. Senegalese expert Pape Ibrahima Kane described the event as an attempted coup, suggesting the junta would have fallen without Russian Africa Corps intervention. While Algeria also supported the regime with fighter jets, the incident underscores the limits of foreign security partnerships in resolving internal structural crises.

An IMF mission led by Gavin Gray began discussions with Ukrainian authorities on Monday regarding the economic outlook and the 2027 budget. The Fund's Ukraine office stated the talks will assess progress on reforms under the $8.1 billion Extended Fund Facility program. This follows the July approval of the first review, which cleared $690 million in disbursements. Discussions focus on macroeconomic stability and structural reforms needed amid ongoing wartime spending.

The Trump administration announced a joint venture with a private Venezuelan company to develop 65 billion barrels of oil reserves, with the U.S. government taking a 55% stake. An anonymous administration official confirmed the agreement, which President Trump described as the biggest oil deal in the world. However, energy experts express skepticism regarding the deal's structure and immediate impact. The U.S. lacks a national oil company to operate the venture, and the 'at-cost' terms may deter private investors seeking market premiums. Furthermore, questions remain about the legitimacy of the acting Venezuelan government led by Delcy Rodríguez. Experts state the deal will not lower gas prices soon because the oil fields are undeveloped and production would take years to begin.

BJP and Congress exchanged sharp words on Monday following an FIR against Rahul Gandhi. The opposition party criticized the legal action after he demanded venue purification. BJP claimed he raised the issue late due to Kharge's threat to quit.

US stock indexes closed lower on Friday as rising oil prices and Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh's hawkish comments dampened investor sentiment. Despite the daily losses, all three major indexes recorded monthly gains for August. Market participants now price in a high probability of a 25-basis-point rate hike in September. Sector performance varied, with energy shares advancing while utilities lagged due to regulatory issues in California.

The FTC and 22 US states sued Amazon on August 31, alleging the company secretly inflated advertising auction prices since 2019. The complaint claims this conduct cost advertisers at least $20 billion. Amazon denied the allegations, stating its system prioritizes product relevance and saved advertisers $8 billion. The company argued the lawsuit misunderstands its auction mechanics. This marks the latest legal conflict between the two parties.

Australia raised its wheat crop forecast to 29.9 million tons for 2026/27, an increase of 12% from the previous estimate. The Department of Agriculture attributed the improvement to strong winter rains and early crop maturity. Concurrently, worsening Black Sea conflict has driven higher global demand for Australian grain. Analyst Rod Baker noted that September exports are forecast to reach nearly 1 million tons. Additionally, the department predicts wheat prices will rise by about 6% due to strong domestic and international interest.

The US Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to continue building a $400 million White House ballroom complex. The 5-4 decision found the National Trust for Historic Preservation likely lacked standing to challenge the project. Chief Justice John Roberts dissented, arguing the ruling did not resolve whether the construction was lawful. Trump called the lawsuit baseless and celebrated the victory for his military complex project.

The U.S. Supreme Court voted 5-4 to allow President Donald Trump to proceed with his White House ballroom project. Chief Justice John Roberts joined the dissenters, arguing the project was likely unlawful. The court ruled the National Trust for Historic Preservation lacked standing to sue, though the case continues in lower courts. The decision permits construction while the legality of the project remains unfinally decided.

India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri stated that 51 of 227 Indian nationals recruited into the Russian army have died, while 139 have been discharged. New Delhi continues discussions with Moscow regarding the release and repatriation of remaining citizens. The government warned Indians against risky job offers linked to the conflict. Additionally, the Supreme Court directed the Centre to appoint a nodal officer to coordinate with affected families.

The Supreme Court collegium recommended Chhattisgarh High Court judge Sanjay Kumar Agrawal as the full-time chief justice of the Rajasthan High Court. This appointment follows allegations of corruption and favouritism against acting chief justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma by Justice Sandeep Mehta. Justice Mehta wrote to the CJI citing specific instances of alleged misconduct, including selective case transfers and improper handling of appeals. In response, CJI Surya Kant stated that allegations against sitting judges must be addressed through established institutional mechanisms. Meanwhile, lawyers in Jaipur and Jodhpur protested and announced a strike demanding Sharma's removal. Justice Sharma has since opted out of judicial work until September 5.

Eight Assam workers rescued from Nepal after flash floods on August 26 returned home Sunday, while eight colleagues remain missing. Nepalese military helicopters spotted the stranded men on a hilltop after two days without food or water. Survivors described seeing death up close during the disaster at the Upper Trishuli-1 Hydropower Project. The Assam government opened helplines for families, but no direct contact has been made with the missing workers yet.

Karur Vysya Bank Managing Director Ramesh Babu stated that physical branches remain vital for retail and MSME customers despite digital banking growth. The bank opened 16 new locations across five states, bringing its total network to 919 branches. KVB reported total business of ₹2,27,267 crore as of June 30, with deposits at ₹1,22,587 crore and advances at ₹1,04,680 crore. The bank plans to deepen its presence in metropolitan and rural markets while strengthening mobile banking access.

RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat stated that India has historically served the world as a 'vishwa guru' rather than a 'super power'. Speaking in Toronto, he emphasized the civilisational principle of 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam', meaning the entire world is one family. Bhagwat highlighted that India's tradition involves helping others without discrimination and cited historical examples like aiding Polish refugees during World War II. He also called for embracing diversity while recognizing the underlying unity of humanity.

The Haridwar District Congress Committee filed a police complaint against BJP Uttarakhand State President Mahendra Bhatt and 15 others. Workers led by Aman Garg staged a protest demanding an FIR under the SC/ST Act following a ritual at Ramlila Ground. Congress alleges the act reflects a casteist mindset and violates constitutional protections against untouchability. BJP officials denied involvement, stating the ritual was for religious decorum.

Massive flash floods struck Nepal on August 26, killing over 780 people and leaving thousands missing, including Indian tourists. Nepal authorities issued fresh flood warnings as water levels rose, prompting rescue operations involving 7,451 security personnel. Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle stated Nepal will need at least a few billion dollars for recovery, though the Foreign Ministry declined foreign search-and-rescue teams. Researchers from ICIMOD and the US Geological Survey believe a glacial collapse triggered the disaster. India has sent relief material and offered humanitarian assistance, while China paused its own rescue efforts due to renewed flood risks. The Nepal government has also paused all examinations to focus on the crisis.

Amazon describes a new architecture for building multi-tenant agentic chat applications that leverage enterprise data. The solution utilizes Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base to handle ingestion, storage, and retrieval while maintaining strict per-user data isolation. Key components include Amazon Cognito for authentication, Amazon SQS for decoupling uploads, and Amazon DynamoDB for tracking indexing status. The system enforces security boundaries by deriving user identity from verified JSON Web Tokens rather than trusting client values. Amazon states that the service manages complex agentic retrieval workflows, including iterative planning and multi-hop retrievals, ensuring access permissions are honored at every step. The architecture supports direct document ingestion through custom connectors, allowing files to become retrievable within seconds. Best practices outlined by the authors include using queues to absorb upload bursts and monitoring ingestion latency to predict throughput limits. The approach allows teams to focus on product-specific logic like chat interfaces while the managed service handles the underlying infrastructure.

Alexander Hurst argues that global leaders agree the AI arms race is disastrous and requires an external pause. The article states that an international agreement is unlikely because nations are incentivized to continue developing AI capabilities. Hurst identifies ASML as a critical choke-point, noting its EUV lithography machines are essential for advanced chip production. The author reports that a ban on ASML exports would force the global AI industry to stop developing. Hurst writes that Europe should impose this restriction to gain regulatory leverage and prevent falling behind in AI compute. The piece concludes that Europe must play this single card now to halt the race before it is too late.

The Quick Charge podcast reports that Apple CEO Tim Cook is leaving the company. The episode also covers Slate Auto's new high-roof cargo truck variant and Waev's Tiger Li-Ion airport tug. The Tiger tug can tow over 60,000 lbs and costs nearly $20,000 annually less than diesel models. The podcast includes sponsor segments for GM Energy Pass and EnergySage.

Intertek CEA analysts report that Section 232 tariffs and minimum import prices will push U.S. solar module prices back to 2023 levels. The policy, effective December 4, 2026, imposes a 15% ad valorem tariff and sets minimum import prices of 38 cents per watt for modules. Current spot pricing has risen to roughly 46 cents per watt due to stacked tariffs. Christian Roselund and Joseph C. Johnson of Intertek CEA state that domestic assembly will likely dominate the market by 2027, benefiting vertically integrated companies. However, policy uncertainty may stifle new investment in upstream silicon processing. Analysts suggest creative supply chain frameworks could allow non-integrated assemblers to remain profitable while meeting minimum price requirements.

Brendan Haley of Efficiency Canada argues that strategic energy management helps Canadian firms offset trade war costs without importing equipment. He warns federal funding for the Green Industrial Facilities and Manufacturing Program expires in March 2027. Examples include Trans-Atlantic Preforms cutting energy use by 35% and Lethbridge Iron Works saving $1.1 million annually. Haley urges the government to expand the program as a low-risk tariff response strategy.

Mexico's Federal Electricity Commission (CFE) published its 2026-30 Development Program, outlining MXN 651 billion ($32.9 billion) in investments for generation, transmission, and distribution. The utility plans to add 18.6 GW of new capacity, with 82% coming from renewable technologies. Most of this renewable growth will occur through mixed-investment models involving private-sector partners. Specifically, CFE identifies 30 solar projects totaling 4.90 GW, bringing the total explicitly identified solar capacity to 5.48 GW. While the program mentions electricity storage, it does not specify a quantified project pipeline or capacity targets. The utility also lists a 20 MW green hydrogen project scheduled for 2030. Through these initiatives, CFE expects its direct generation capacity to rise from 46.6 GW to 70 GW by 2030.

JA announced the Journey Ahead: JA Roadshow 2026 to demonstrate its expanding portfolio of solar and energy storage technologies across Europe. The company stated that grid instability and rising electrification are driving demand for integrated solutions combining generation, storage, and intelligent management. The tour will visit over 10 countries between September and October, featuring battery energy storage systems and latest-generation TOPCon modules. JA aims to highlight its evolution from a PV manufacturer into an integrated energy solutions provider.

Reuters reports that North American Blue Energy Partners will replace Chinese and Russian operators in several Venezuelan oil fields. The U.S. government holds a 35% stake and rights to 20% of production at cost. White House officials state the deal aims to scale production by investing up to $100 billion. Alejandro Betancourt, the company owner, claims the transaction will benefit both Venezuelans and Americans. Previously operated by Sinopec and Roszarubezhneft, the fields now shift to U.S. control.

Crude oil prices climbed after President Trump threatened new strikes on Iran. Brent crude traded at $91.48 per barrel, while West Texas Intermediate reached $86.97. Shipping data indicates tanker traffic in the Strait of Hormuz remains low compared to pre-war levels. Analysts warn that global oil market buffers are exhausting as U.S. inventories near minimum levels. Diesel supply is also tightening due to export bans and regional refinery damage.

The US added a record 20.2 gigawatt-hours of battery storage capacity in the second quarter of 2026, according to a new report from the Solar Energy Industries Association and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Utility-scale projects drove this growth, with Arizona, Texas, and California leading installations. The report notes that battery storage supplied more electricity to the US grid in the first eight months of 2026 than during all of 2025. Conversely, residential battery installations fell 27% year over year due to changes in federal tax credits. Benchmark raised its storage forecast through 2030 by 11.5% to 683 GWh as demand outpaces previous expectations. US battery manufacturing also expanded, with Tesla bringing a new Texas factory online.

A new study published in Environmental Science & Technology identifies 1,222 chemicals in food-contact materials that pose serious health risks but lack sufficient safety data. Jane Muncke of the Food Packaging Forum Foundation stated that 87 percent of over 15,000 chemicals used in packaging have no accessible information for risk assessment. The research highlights that many hazardous substances, including PFAS and phthalates, are already detected in human samples like breast milk and blood. Experts recommend regulators adopt mixture allocation factors and group-based restrictions to better protect consumers from combined chemical exposures. The Food Packaging Coalition maintains that current packaging designs prevent chemical transfer, while the study authors argue for a shift toward proving safety before market approval.

Carbon Brief reports that the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP7) has released seven new emissions scenarios to replace the previous Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSPs) used in the IPCC's sixth assessment report. These scenarios reflect a world where a coal-dominated future is no longer plausible, resulting in a significantly narrower range of projected warming between 1.6C and 3.3C above pre-industrial levels by 2100. The highest scenario now predicts 3.3C warming, which is substantially lower than the 4.6C to 4.9C range produced by earlier generations of models. However, the analysis indicates that avoiding an overshoot of the 1.5C Paris Agreement target is now unavoidable, with the very-low scenario peaking at around 1.8C mid-century before falling back close to 1.5C by 2100. The socioeconomic assumptions underlying these scenarios describe a more crowded and less wealthy planet, with the global human population projected to peak at 10.1 billion people around 2080 in the medium pathway. Every scenario that limits warming relies heavily on carbon dioxide removal, with cumulative removals by 2150 ranging from 655GtCO2 in the very-low scenario to 2,360GtCO2 in the low-to-negative scenario. The authors note that while the high-end scenarios have shifted downward, the lower-end scenarios have shifted modestly upward due to the failure of global emissions to decline rapidly after 2020.

A new study published in Climate Risk Management finds that greater financial access for women strengthens household resilience to climate shocks in sub-Saharan Africa. The authors report that women-headed households with formal financial tools were better able to withstand short-term economic crises caused by extreme weather. However, the researchers state that financial inclusion alone cannot address long-term vulnerabilities like droughts or sea-level rise without tackling wider gender inequality. Using data from 25,511 households across 37 countries, the study shows that while financial access improves women's political and economic empowerment, it does not fully erase cultural barriers to social empowerment. Experts note that without structural changes such as gender-sensitive credit schemes and land-titling programs, women remain disproportionately vulnerable to climate impacts despite increased financial inclusion.

Tim Cook announced his departure from Apple CEO after 15 years, calling it the greatest privilege of his life. He will transition to executive chairman while John Ternus assumes daily operations. Cook credited Apple employees for his success and highlighted the company's growth under his leadership.

OpenAI denied Apple's allegations of trade secret theft in a U.S. District Court filing. The AI company stated Apple failed to prove confidential information was stolen by former employees. OpenAI argued Apple's own policies complicate data separation for departing staff. The lawsuit marks a sharp escalation between the two rivals after a previous partnership.

John Ternus assumes the role of Apple's chief executive on Tuesday, succeeding Tim Cook after a 15-year tenure. Analysts suggest Ternus will prioritize hardware innovation while maintaining the existing supply chain structure. The new leader faces significant challenges regarding China dependence and navigating political pressure from the White House. Cook will transition to executive chairman, focusing on global policymaker engagement. Ternus must deliver a foldable iPhone at the September 9 event just days into his new position.

A source familiar with the matter said Anthropic signed a $35 billion cloud deal with Nvidia-backed Lambda for a Texas data center. The project, developed by Hut 8 in Nueces County, covers approximately 350 megawatts of capacity. Nvidia will hold the lease on the facility, which aims to meet growing demand for Anthropic's AI services. Anthropic previously announced a separate $45 billion commitment to rent cloud computing power from Nscale.

The FTC and 22 states sued Amazon on Monday, alleging the company secretly overcharged advertisers by more than $20bn. The lawsuit claims Amazon manipulated its ad auctions to inflate costs, which were then passed to consumers. Amazon spokespersons called the legal action a misguided lawsuit and denied the allegations. Regulators seek to stop the practices and force refunds.

Researchers Joshua Goodman and Samuel Nitkin analyzed data on tutoring chains, household spending, and test scores to assess student achievement impacts. They found that opening a center raises district scores but widens racial gaps, with effects largest for White and Asian students. The study notes these private investments deepen educational inequality while helping their specific users.

UK 10-year gilt yields rose to 5.223%, the highest since June 2008, driven by rising oil prices and inflation fears. Brent crude climbed above $91 a barrel following renewed fighting in the Middle East that disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Global bond markets sold off broadly, with Japanese and German yields also reaching multi-year highs. Meanwhile, Shein shares tumbled after its Hong Kong listing, as regulatory changes targeting small-package imports eroded its business model. Analysts note that global oil buffers are depleting as US inventories reach minimum levels. The Bank of England is not expected to raise rates until later this year, while the European Central Bank is widely anticipated to increase rates by 0.25 percentage points in September.

Researchers Jolevski, Melo, and Moore report that generative AI adoption is widespread. They note that substantial aggregate labor-market disruption is not yet visible. However, workers perceive substantial displacement risk. This perception increases when firsthand use reveals AI can perform key tasks for their job.

A columnist argues that reactions to the Hugging Face hack are overly dramatic and emotionally driven. The author compares current fears to past overreactions regarding DDT, Y2K, and global warming. He calls for technocratic solutions rather than hysterical responses to AI cybersecurity risks. The writer requests quantitative estimates of potential costs as a percentage of GDP.

Andrew Bailey, head of the Bank of England, warned financial institutions to prepare for severe AI-driven cyber threats. In a letter to G20 leaders, he urged firms to restore systems from bare metal if needed. Bailey joined other central bankers at Jackson Hole who expressed concern over near-term AI risks to critical infrastructure.

Chinese leader Xi Jinping pledged stronger ties with Russia following a meeting with President Vladimir Putin at the Shanghai Cooperation Organization summit in Kyrgyzstan. A China adviser in the Biden administration told The New York Times that the gathering allows Beijing to demonstrate global options while Washington alienates allies. A Foreign Policy columnist argued the event also aims to stabilize China's tense relationship with India.

White Oak Armory LLC filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in Tennessee, citing a disputed tax debt to the state. The retailer's website showed no firearms or ammunition for sale as of late August. Industry data indicates a broader decline in gun sales, with total units falling 4.1% in 2025 and rifle sales rising while handgun and shotgun sales dropped significantly in 2026.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced the state joined a federal lawsuit accusing Amazon of misleading advertisers about auction pricing. Regulators allege the company secretly charged full winning bids instead of second prices for over seven years. The FTC and 21 other states claim this practice extracted tens of billions from businesses and raised consumer prices. Amazon denies the allegations, calling the case misguided and stating it disagrees with claims that advertisers were misled.

California Attorney General Rob Bonta announced the state joined a federal lawsuit accusing Amazon of misleading advertisers about auction pricing. Regulators allege the company secretly charged full winning bids instead of second prices for over seven years. The FTC and 21 other states claim this practice extracted tens of billions from businesses and raised consumer prices. Amazon denies the allegations, calling the case misguided and stating it disagrees with claims that advertisers were misled.

Apple escalated its lawsuit against OpenAI by filing a court brief alleging the AI company is destroying evidence. The filing claims former Apple engineer Chang Liu downloaded confidential circuit schematics and used them at OpenAI. Apple argues Liu is central to the case involving over 400 former employees who joined the AI firm. OpenAI has requested dismissal of the trade secrets lawsuit.

Prime Minister Mark Carney's Liberal Party secured three seats in special elections held on Monday, Aug 31, boosting the government's parliamentary majority. Carney credited voters for their trust during this consequential time for Canada. The victory occurred as relations with the United States soured following collapsed trade talks and the imposition of 50-per cent duties. A recent poll indicated that 76 per cent of the public praised Carney's stance toward Washington. Although Carney was not known for his charisma, he has managed to kindle a patriotic flame among Canadians weary of American attacks.

The New South Wales Independent Commission Against Corruption heard testimony from Charles Perrottet regarding allegations of prohibited donations from developer Jean Nassif. Perrottet insisted he never requested funds for political results, though he admitted to adding a 'political flavour' to advice given to a lobbying firm. The inquiry examined a $2m donation claim linked to damaging the careers of David Elliott and David Chandler. Perrottet stated he did not know if he was aware of a $150,000 payment made to the lobbying company Beckington following a dinner meeting. Counsel assisting expressed shock at Perrottet's explanation of his interactions with Nassif. Meanwhile, Nassif withdrew from a scheduled appearance after receiving a medical certificate. The investigation continues while Perrottet's wife also faced questioning about her involvement with the lobbying firm.

Experts warn that a global pause on US immigrant visa appointments could increase uncertainty for Asian workers. This development follows President Donald Trump's administration tightening legal immigration through new screening and higher costs.

Indonesia is accelerating its aluminum expansion by building new coal-fired smelters, a move driven by supply disruptions in the Middle East caused by the Iran war. The Associated Press reports that global aluminum prices have risen due to these conflicts, prompting Southeast Asian nations to seek alternative production sources. While China has invested heavily in these projects, environmental groups warn that the plans contradict Indonesia's climate commitments and threaten local communities with increased pollution. The Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air notes that if all projects proceed, the country's bauxite reserves could be depleted in less than 12 years. Critics argue that labeling these coal-dependent minerals as 'transition' resources constitutes greenwashing, as the energy source remains heavily polluting.

Zambia's President Hakainde Hichilema is set to be sworn in for a second term on Tuesday following a disputed election and the detention of his main opponent. Hichilema won 60% of the vote, while runner-up Brian Mundubile alleged election tampering but could not challenge the result due to sealed courts. EU observers noted issues with the vote tallying process, including delays in recording results. Security forces raided a property linked to Mundubile, killing a former cabinet minister and arresting opposition politicians. Mundubile and his running mate were detained and charged with treason, which they denied. Hichilema, who took office in 2021, aims to build on his economic stabilization efforts. African leaders from Kenya, Botswana, Zimbabwe, Namibia, and Tanzania are expected to attend the inauguration ceremony at the National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka.

Hindu pilgrims traveling to Mount Kailash are among the missing following deadly floods in Nepal triggered by climate change. The Indian government reported 287 missing nationals, while China and Nepal have identified 853 foreigners as unaccounted for. Many pilgrims were near the Gyirong Port Immigration Office when a glacier collapse caused a flash flood that destroyed the facility. Sadhguru, leader of the Isha Foundation, noted his group lost contact with 77 pilgrims and guides. Historians suggest that increased tourism and infrastructure development may have contributed to the disaster by altering the fragile mountain ecosystem. Environmental groups warn that rising temperatures have doubled glacier melt rates in the past 25 years, posing future risks to the region.

Social media users criticized Airlink for flying low over a packed stadium. The airline stated the maneuvers were rehearsed and approved by the Civil Aviation Authority. Two bespoke Embraer aircraft performed the flyby in team colors. The event was intended to celebrate the upcoming rugby match.

A jury found former gang leader Duane Davis guilty of orchestrating the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur. Prosecutors argued Davis ordered the shooting and supplied the weapon used by his nephew. Davis admitted to being in the vehicle during the drive-by shooting in a 2008 police interview. His defense team claimed his admissions were fiction intended to sell books. Davis will face sentencing on October 13 and plans to appeal the verdict.

China expressed strong opposition to Taiwan attending the Pacific Islands Forum hosted by Palau. Beijing's envoy, Qian Bo, stated that Taiwan is not a dialogue partner for the forum. The special envoy warned Palau of unspecified consequences regarding the invitation. Palau remains one of a dozen nations maintaining diplomatic relations with Taiwan.

Kenyan aviation workers ended a strike that halted operations at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport in Nairobi. The Kenya Aviation Workers Union called off the action after reaching an agreement with the Kenya Airports Authority. The two-day stoppage caused significant flight delays and cancellations, leaving many travelers stranded. Union members cited unfair hiring practices and poor compensation as reasons for the industrial action.

Annette Young welcomes Joseph Shea, a glaciologist at the University of Northern BC, to discuss the Nepal floods. Shea argues the disaster was a compound event involving simultaneous glacier failure and a massive landslide. His analysis places the catastrophe within the broader transformation of the Himalayas under climate change. Scientists may increasingly need to identify subtle precursors to such cascading hazards.

A World Weather Attribution study states human-induced climate change reduced early wet season rainfall in Jamaica and Puerto Rico. Researchers found the drought made extreme dry spells significantly more likely in both nations. Authorities in Puerto Rico implemented water rationing due to critically depleted reservoirs. Experts noted that outdated infrastructure and high leakage rates worsened the water crisis. The study attributes the immediate cause to the North Atlantic Oscillation, while forecasting El Niño will increase drying later this year.

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority reported that over 11,000 people have been rescued in Nepal following deadly flash floods. Spokesperson Shanti Mahat stated that at least 16 helicopters are currently deployed for search-and-rescue operations in affected areas. Authorities issued a notice warning of high flood possibilities in Nuwakot and Rasuwa districts due to rising water levels in smaller rivers and streams. The government has intensified its search and rescue efforts in the flood-hit regions.

A photographer described documenting young girls sold by their parents in Afghanistan as the hardest report they have ever done. The article highlights the severe human rights violations occurring in the region. The photographer emphasized the emotional toll of witnessing these transactions firsthand.

A former gang member was found guilty of murdering the late rap icon Tupac Shakur. The verdict concludes a long legal process regarding the 1996 shooting. The court ruled the defendant responsible for the fatal attack.

Musicologist Lydia Hamessley discusses the musical influences behind Dolly Parton's rise to fame. Hamessley notes that Parton's music draws inspiration from Appalachian traditions and her storytelling ability. The professor describes Parton as both an artisan and an artist who instinctively develops song ideas. Hamessley wrote a book on Parton's songs after interviewing the country star.

The United States blocked a global drought agreement at the UNCCD summit in Ulaanbaatar, Mongolia, championing the toughest position against African demands for funding. Delegates postponed the decision until COP18 in 2028, while other nations resorted to linguistic workarounds to avoid specific terms like 'gender' and 'civil society,' which some jokingly called 'Voldemort words.' Although the US rejected key issues, negotiators secured a guarantee that droughts remain a standalone agenda item. The summit also approved agreements on sand and dust storms, private-sector engagement, and grasslands, with Brazil pledging to restore over 63,000 square miles of degraded land. A new $1.3 billion financing package and a drought resilience fund were launched to support projects in 23 countries.

Recent widespread blackouts in eastern Libya have severely impacted water production and supply in the Cyrenaica region. The Great Man-Made River Authority reported that recurring electrical disturbances knocked dozens of wells offline, forcing water supply reductions and the deployment of water tankers for residents and hospitals. A July 23 outage linked to a generating unit shutdown forced 143 wells out of service, affecting daily urban and agricultural needs. While Libya possesses vast oil reserves and strong solar potential, persistent infrastructure failures point to governance and planning issues rather than resource scarcity. Analysts note that the disconnect between resource-rich eastern regions and administrative centers in Tripoli complicates service delivery. Some citizens express nostalgia for the predictability of services under previous regimes, highlighting the political weight of these failures.

Rescue teams in China and Nepal are searching for more than 4,700 missing people after catastrophic flooding along the border. Authorities have raised the death toll to over 900 as teams face difficult conditions in the worst-hit areas. The disaster was caused by a massive glacier calving event that released ice, water, and mud into the valley. While Nepal provides regular updates on victims, Chinese officials have been slow to release specific details about missing foreigners. A researcher attributed the rapid glacier collapse to global warming, which destabilizes the ice. Spiritual leader Jaggi Vasudev called for better coordination between the two governments to handle such regional crises.

A five-member National Company Law Tribunal Bench stayed an order approving a ₹6.25-crore repayment plan proposed by Essel Group founder Subhash Chandra. The Special Bench, headed by Justice Anupinder Singh Grewal, found no clear majority view among members regarding the plan's scope under Section 419(5) of the Companies Act, 2013. Consequently, the tribunal issued notices to parties and sought replies before making a final decision. Meanwhile, the Bench restrained Mr. Chandra from alienating his properties directly or indirectly while the matter is under review. The proceedings relate to personal guarantees for Essel Group-linked borrowings, where admitted claims total around ₹22,000 crore against the proposed ₹6.25 crore contribution. Creditors had previously approved the plan with 80.814% voting share, though objections remained regarding low recovery and asset examination. The dispute remains separate from corporate insolvency proceedings involving the group and regulatory actions concerning Zee Entertainment Enterprises.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated India on a 7.8% GDP growth in the April-June 2026 quarter. He attributed this achievement to resilience despite global instability and supply chain disruptions. The Prime Minister reiterated his appeal for citizens to choose domestic travel and weddings while avoiding unnecessary gold purchases. He stated that emphasizing self-reliance will help India become a developed nation by its centenary.

HDFC Bank is exploring an appeal at the NCLAT against an NCLT order accepting Subhash Chandra's repayment offer. The bank opposed the resolution, noting its admitted claim was 3.2% of the total ₹22,006 crore. LIC Housing Finance also stated it will continue pursuing borrowers despite the insolvency ruling. Both lenders emphasized that the order does not affect corporate liabilities or their security interests.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed the 26th SCO Summit in Bishkek, emphasizing the need to dismantle terrorism's entire ecosystem. He stated that countries using terrorism as a policy tool must receive a strong message. Modi outlined security, connectivity, and opportunity as India's vision pillars for the organization. He also highlighted the importance of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving global conflicts.

Shares of Titan Company, Kalyan Jewellers, Thangamayil Jewellery, and Sky Gold declined following Prime Minister Narendra Modi's second appeal for citizens to avoid purchasing gold. The Prime Minister previously requested the public refrain from buying gold for weddings to conserve foreign exchange reserves. India imports an average of 60 tonnes of gold monthly, costing nearly $6 billion. While experts like John Paulson see long-term growth potential, the immediate market reaction remains negative.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay released water from the Mettur Dam on Tuesday. The release aims to meet drinking water needs and support samba cultivation in Cauvery delta districts. This action follows a delay caused by low water levels in the basin reservoir. The event marks a shift from the traditional June 12 opening for kuruvai cultivation.

Bajaj Auto shares rose 3% following a 28% year-on-year increase in August sales. The company sold 5,35,764 units, with exports surging 53% to 2,41,850 units. Two-wheeler sales grew 30% to 4,43,748 units, while domestic sales rose 10%. The stock reached a 52-week high of Rs 12,470 and trades at a P/E ratio of 28.31. Foreign Institutional Investors increased their stake to 9.01% in the June 2026 quarter.

Bloomberg reported that Phil Schiller stepped down from running the App Store and Apple's product launch events. He will remain as an Apple Fellow to work on unnamed projects. Carson Oliver will manage the App Store, while Nola Weinstein will oversee product events. This change coincides with John Ternus becoming CEO on September 1.

Instagram announced it is replacing its "AI creator" label with a new "AI-generated profile" tag to improve clarity for users. The platform stated it will restrict the reach of accounts featuring undisclosed AI-generated people. Real creators using AI tools for editing will not automatically receive the new profile label. Instagram noted the policy addresses user feedback regarding realistic virtual influencers that initially appear to represent real individuals.

Tata Motors Ltd announced a 49 percent increase in total commercial vehicle sales for August, reaching 44,411 units. The company stated that domestic sales grew 33 percent to 36,619 units, while international volumes surged 227 percent to 7,792 units. These figures represent a significant year-on-year improvement compared to August of the previous year.

John Ternus will succeed Tim Cook as Apple's chief executive officer on September 1, following a 25-year tenure that included leading all hardware programs. Cook, who will become executive chairman, stated he is confident in Ternus's abilities and character. Ternus, who joined Apple in 2001, is known for his focus on unseen details, such as arguing for 25 screw grooves instead of 35. He previously led the transition to Apple Silicon and oversaw the development of the Vision Pro. The company reported its strongest June quarter ever, though challenges like geopolitical uncertainty and supply chain issues remain. Ternus now faces the task of launching a foldable iPhone and advancing Apple's AI ambitions.

Adani Group stocks displayed mixed performance on Tuesday following the MSCI index reshuffle implemented on August 31. Adani Green Energy rallied over 4% to reach ₹1,271.10, while Adani Energy Solutions fell 5% to ₹1,391. Reuters reported that the index changes are expected to trigger significant fund flows, with Adani Energy Solutions attracting approximately $310 million. The broader Indian market recovered opening losses, with the Sensex rising 0.26% to 77,161.36. V K Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments Limited stated that while global headwinds from crude prices and bond yields may impact the market, fundamentals support a Nifty range of 23,000-25,000. Rising crude oil prices and US bond yields continue to create concerns about inflation and borrowing costs.

Indian equity markets opened cautiously on Tuesday as elevated crude oil prices and renewed US-Iran tensions dampened investor sentiment. The Nifty 50 fell below 24,100, while the Sensex declined over 80 points. ITC and Bharti Airtel led gains, whereas TCS and Nestle India faced declines amid a global risk-off mood. Domestic markets found support from robust GDP growth of 7.8 per cent in the April-June quarter, though foreign institutional investors sold nearly ₹7,985 crore. Analysts noted that while the 24,000 level remains key support, rising US Treasury yields and global headwinds could negatively impact equity markets in the near term.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi returned to Instagram to highlight India's 7.8% GDP growth in the first quarter of FY27 while criticizing opposition narratives. The Prime Minister urged citizens to prioritize Indian products and avoid foreign travel or weddings to support self-reliance. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman credited the NDA government and Indian citizens for the strong economic performance. Data from the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation confirmed the real GDP figure, which exceeded the Reserve Bank of India's earlier estimate. Officials noted that the quarterly figures are provisional and subject to future revisions based on updated source information.

The Indian economy grew 7.8% in the first quarter of the current fiscal year, defying the largest oil shock in history according to National Statistics Office data. Experts warn this growth does not rule out a slowdown over the full fiscal year. A 16-year-old girl was allegedly gang-raped on a 47-km bus ride between Greater Noida and Delhi, with police arresting the driver and conductor. The FDA cracked down on ten companies in Navi Mumbai and Noida for selling repackaged expired food products like Lay's and Thums Up.
