Commissioning is scheduled for 2028, with manufacturing of key components already advanced at Everllence facilities in Berlin and Oberhausen. The project utilizes Rhine river water and ammonia refrigerant, marking a significant step in industrial-scale climate-neutral district heating.

The Minnesota Department of Transportation is offering $41.2 million to fund up to 40 new EV fast-charging sites in Greater Minnesota. MnDOT commissioner Nancy Daubenberger stated the funding aims to reduce range anxiety for long-distance travelers. Applications for the grants are due by November 2, with awards expected in late 2026 or early 2027. Federal funds will cover 80% of eligible project costs.

Maine regulators selected Clearway Energy to develop an 800-megawatt wind farm in northern Maine, which would increase the state's onshore wind capacity by approximately 66%. The Maine Public Utilities Commission also chose Avangrid Networks to build the necessary high-voltage transmission line to connect the project to the regional grid. Maine plans to purchase 600 MW of the output, while the remaining 200 MW will supply other New England states. Officials estimate the projects will generate between $387 million and $425 million in net benefits for customers over their operating lives. However, the projects still require final approval of power purchase agreements, transmission arrangements, and various permits before construction can begin.

Rosatom Director General Alexei Likhachev said the company is considering a Murmansk site to complete floating nuclear power units. He stated this decision responds to the scale of future orders for these units. The report notes that while the Baltic Shipyard remains a key partner, Rosatom may create its own production links where necessary. Likhachev explained that the choice of Murmansk is due to the nearby Atomflot fleet and port infrastructure.

Hochtief has reached an agreement to acquire Autmatec, a German specialist in transmission line infrastructure, pending regulatory approval. The transaction value remains undisclosed, though Autmatec reported approximately €50m in 2026 revenue. Hochtief CEO Juan Santamaría stated the deal aligns with its strategy to invest in high-growth infrastructure markets. The acquisition aims to integrate Autmatec's technical capabilities with Hochtief's engineering scale to support major European grid modernization projects.

The Energy Transition Coalition reports that record levels of clean energy investment have not yet resulted in emissions reductions. The organization highlights a gap between financial spending and actual environmental outcomes in the current energy transition landscape.

Farrans has begun construction on the Berkswell Battery Energy Storage System for BW ESS in the West Midlands. The 200MW/857MWh facility near Solihull is expected to power over 500,000 homes for four hours once operational. BW ESS co-owns the project with AIP Management and selected Farrans for its infrastructure experience. Farrans project manager Barry McDonagh described the site as a significant step toward a more resilient UK energy network.

Bloomberg News reported that ByteDance secured a $29.6 billion loan, exceeding its initial $20 billion request. People familiar with the matter told Bloomberg the company gathered strong bank commitments. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

Korea Electric Power Corp proposed that Samsung Electronics pay 20 trillion won and SK Hynix pay 5 trillion won in advance for power through 2031. The Chosun Ilbo reported the suggestion based on an internal KEPCO document. KEPCO stated participation details remain unfinalized while Samsung and SK Hynix declined to comment. The utility aims to fund grid expansion for semiconductor and AI data centre projects.

Jon Fiva shared statistics from new research regarding publication bias in economics and political science. The data indicates that instrumental variable estimates are significantly larger than OLS estimates. Additionally, significant results are far more likely to be published in experimental economics than null findings.

A new PwC report indicates that 46% of UK households do not experience improved living standards despite national economic growth. Researchers found a stark North-South divide, with every region in northern England, the Midlands, and Wales showing lower spending power than the national average. Conversely, London and the South East recorded spending power significantly above average. The study defines household spending power as income after taxes and housing costs, adjusted for household size. While Prime Minister Andy Burnham has pledged to address regional inequalities, political debate continues regarding the effectiveness of his growth strategies and the proposed No10 North initiative. PwC argues that future devolution must ensure local areas retain revenues generated by local growth to truly improve community prosperity.

Writer Derek Thompson interviewed Pangram founder about generative text detection. Pangram recently helped expose AI use at The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal. Thompson noted re-summarizing key points as a new tell for AI writing. However, Thompson fears AI-writing witch hunts would be an unwelcome addition to online life.

Nikkei reported that rapid data center construction across Asia is triggering environmental and health concerns from local communities. While demand remains strong, developers are shifting investments to regions with less opposition. Barclays bankers told Bloomberg that lenders have distributed nearly $29 billion since the start of the year but are becoming more selective. Analysts noted that issues arise primarily when developers fail to engage with the community.

ADP released data showing private nonfarm payroll employment growth fell short of forecasts. The report indicates a gain of 38,000 jobs instead of the 47,000 expected by Bloomberg consensus. Analysts note this figure does not show a dropoff in employment. The data compares ADP estimates against Bureau of Labor Statistics benchmark revisions.

The author examines the federal budget balance excluding IEEPA tariff revenue, noting the figure improves through 2025Q3 before refunds begin. CBO estimates the FY2027 cyclically adjusted balance at -5.8% of potential GDP, suggesting elevated real rates. The author states uncertainty remains regarding how the war, refunds, and tariff challenges will affect the balance. Paweł Skrzypczyński's calculations are cited to show uncertainty in customs revenue figures.

Fortune Coconut Whan Neng at MacPherson Market & Food Centre continues to press fresh coconut milk without preservatives. Third-generation successor Lee Zhao Yuan, 27, plans to take over the family business within five years. The stall processes around 300 coconuts daily to yield up to 100 litres of milk. Lee Zhao Yuan uses TikTok and social media to attract younger customers to the traditional trade. The business sells white and brown grated coconut flesh at S$7/kg and S$6.50/kg respectively. Fortune Coconut Whan Neng is located at #01-60, MacPherson Market & Food Centre, 89 Circuit Road, Singapore 370089.

A family of a Florida shooting victim has sued OpenAI, alleging the gunman used ChatGPT to plan the attack. The company now faces a U.S. criminal investigation for failing to report potential threats. Recent mass shootings in the U.S. and Canada have highlighted concerns over AI use in public killings. Regulators and safety advocates are now warning about the risks of AI-enabled violence.

President Trump stated that Apple Maps has updated the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America, calling the change binding. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum confirmed the president contacted Apple directly about the update. Google also adopted the new name for U.S. users, while MapQuest declined to change it. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney condemned the move as part of a broader trade dispute.

Amazon announced a multi-year deal granting Prime Video exclusive local streaming rights for six NHL teams beginning in the 2026-2027 season. The participating franchises include the Carolina Hurricanes, Anaheim Ducks, Columbus Blue Jackets, Dallas Stars, Minnesota Wild, and St. Louis Blues. NHL Chief Media Officer David Proper stated that the clubs selected Amazon's offer after reviewing various proposals. The agreement includes games, pre- and post-game shows, and other team programming for fans in regional territories.

The United States implemented new tariffs on drones and components to decrease dependence on Chinese suppliers. President Donald Trump signed an order citing national security threats posed by imports. Drones weighing over 25 kilograms face a 100% duty, while smaller models incur a 25% charge. China opposed the move, warning it would disrupt the global supply chain. DJI, which holds more than two-thirds of the market, has faced US restrictions since 2022.

Donald Trump intensified trade tensions with Canada, stating the nation has unfairly exploited US farmers and tourists for decades. He previously imposed 50% tariffs on $20bn of Canadian goods, prompting threats of retaliatory measures. Simultaneously, a US judge blocked a new executive order attempting to restrict birthright citizenship, ruling it almost certainly unconstitutional. In domestic politics, House Democrats rejected a Republican proposal to cap the Supreme Court at nine justices by a vote of 212-206. Lawmakers also introduced a resolution to halt the administration's unauthorized boat strikes against drug cartels. The Trump administration denied New York's request for federal disaster assistance following a major snowstorm that caused $168m in damage. Additionally, Arizona Democrat Adelita Grijalva condemned new border wall construction on Tohono O’odham tribal lands. Trump also commented on Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's return to the UK, expressing happiness about their move while criticizing their treatment of the royal family.

French President Emmanuel Macron and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham are scheduled to hold their first talks on Thursday following a meeting at the Bayeux Tapestry exhibition. The leaders discussed migrant boats crossing the Channel and the war in Ukraine. Macron played a key role in securing the tapestry loan, viewing it as a step toward healing post-Brexit relations. Downing Street confirmed that a surge team of 45 French officers will be deployed to tackle larger migrant vessels. Both leaders emphasized continued support for Ukraine and the importance of EU-UK cooperation. However, an expert warned that the talks might lack substance on EU negotiations.

Lawyers for former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores filed motions in Manhattan federal court to dismiss drug trafficking charges based on immunity. Their attorneys argued that U.S. courts cannot try a recognized foreign head of state and that Venezuela's sovereignty prevents prosecution. Judge Alvin K. Hellerstein has scheduled oral arguments for November 17 before the trial set for next June. Both defendants have pleaded not guilty to conspiracy charges involving cocaine trafficking.

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a temporary ban on generative AI tools for students through eighth grade. Officials describe this as the most expansive prohibition in the United States, affecting roughly 600,000 public school students. The policy halts use of about 40 educational AI tools while officials study children's technology use. High schoolers remain exempt, receiving AI literacy classes instead. Teachers retain permission to use AI for lesson planning and administrative tasks. The decision emphasizes human connection in education and aligns with the district's teaching ideals.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres warns the world has entered a danger zone as a supersized El Niño develops. The World Meteorological Organization reports sea temperatures could rise nearly 4C above average, potentially making this the strongest event since 1950. Officials state the phenomenon will last until at least February 2027, bringing droughts to South America and Asia while increasing typhoon risks in the Pacific. Australia faces marine heatwaves, and Indonesia battles extensive wildfires. Experts note that while early warning systems are being strengthened, structural issues like poor housing and weak healthcare systems remain major vulnerabilities for affected populations.

President Donald Trump stated the US confronts Iran to protect Israel and the West. Iran claimed it laid new naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Germany investigates state-sponsored sabotage after power grid attacks near Cologne. Venezuela signed major energy deals with Chevron and Eni. G20 nations reached consensus on global technology policy. Türkiye remains top in FIBA World Cup 2027 European Qualifiers rankings. Nordic football associations seek EU action regarding FIFA governance concerns.

Hundreds of Moroccan migrants live in tents on Ceuta's El Trampolín beach, avoiding official centers due to fears of deportation. Residents Nebil Tazi and Hamza Mohammed describe difficult living conditions and a desire to reach Europe or find work. Local tensions remain high following the arrival of approximately 80,000 migrants, prompting demonstrations against the Spanish government's lack of policy.

An international consortium published a study in Nature identifying 1,260 genetic variants associated with the Big Five personality traits. The research analyzed data from 1.14 million people across 46 cohorts to map these genetic influences. Michel Nivard, a lead author, noted that while genetics plays a role, environmental factors remain decisive in shaping personality. The study found that family environment has less impact on personality than on traits like intelligence. Nivard emphasized that no single 'personality gene' exists, as each variant contributes only a microscopic effect. The findings suggest that genetic scores can only predict personality when averaged across large populations, not for individuals. Additionally, the research linked specific traits to behaviors such as neighborhood choice and smoking rates.

The article examines how John Ternus shapes Apple's hardware direction under Tim Cook. Ternus oversees engineering for major product lines including the iPhone, iPad, and Mac. His team recently launched the iPhone Air, Apple's thinnest model, developed in close coordination with Johny Srouji's chip division. Srouji now serves as chief hardware officer, unifying hardware technologies and engineering under one executive. The report notes Apple still uses Qualcomm modems in some 2026 models despite building its own C1X chip. Rumors suggest a foldable phone and new smart glasses may launch in September 2026. Ternus also faces the challenge of integrating AI features into Apple's hardware following delays in Apple Intelligence.

UDF nominees in the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit Syndicate oppose a decision to cancel a July 2026 order allowing officials to sign past exam registers. K. B. Sabu stated that blanket cancellation is impractical as it would delay degree certificates. The university authorities confirmed the August 22 decision to cancel the earlier order and launch a probe into documentation irregularities. Officials who signed registers after the July decision included those who had retired from service.

JD(U) national working president Sanjay Jha stated that the India-Bangladesh Ganga Water Treaty negatively impacts Bihar's interests. Speaking to The Hindu, he argued the 1996 agreement has hurt the state despite diplomatic messaging benefits. The treaty expires on December 31, 2026, amid current political tensions between India and Bangladesh. The Ministry of External Affairs has not yet responded to queries regarding Jha's remarks.

Apple Maps has updated its US interface to display Lake America instead of Lake Ontario, following a similar change by Google Maps. President Donald Trump announced the name change is complete and binding on social media. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney rejected the change, noting the name's 400-year history. MapQuest declined to rename the lake and remains Lake Ontario.

Apple has confirmed its annual hardware event will take place on September 9, marking CEO John Ternus's first product launch. The company is reportedly preparing to unveil a foldable iPhone Ultra alongside updated iPhone 18 Pro models and a refreshed Apple Watch lineup. Several devices, including the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2, are expected to be delayed to spring 2027. The event will stream online starting at 10 am Pacific Time.

Seven Indigenous Siekopai women in Ecuador's Amazon are leading a conservation effort to protect vulnerable river turtles. The group, known as the Tari Nomiowa'i or "Turtle Women," combines ancestral knowledge with modern technology to safeguard nests along the Aguarico River. During the 2025-26 nesting season, the women collected 235 eggs and successfully released 208 hatchlings into the river. Their work addresses threats such as pollution, predation, and flooding that endanger the yellow-spotted Amazon River turtle. Janeth Piaguaje, a community leader, noted that the project honors their spiritual connection to nature while passing knowledge to younger generations. The initiative demonstrates how local communities can effectively lead conservation when traditional ecological knowledge is paired with digital tools. While the releases represent a positive short-term outcome, continued protection remains essential for long-term population recovery.

Business Insider interviewed four former employees of Meta, Google, Intel, and Microsoft who were laid off without warning. The report details their prolonged job searches, significant financial losses, and the erosion of their sense of security. One applicant submitted over 8,000 applications while another faced a year-long unemployment period. The article highlights how high salaries and tenure at major tech firms failed to protect these workers from sudden job loss.

Indian government bonds gained value on Thursday after large foreign currency inflows increased rupee liquidity. The Reserve Bank of India attracted $136.38 billion through special schemes, while banks raised $127.23 billion in deposits. Kotak Mahindra Bank stated concerns about aggressive sterilisation may be overstated. However, high oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields dampened demand for longer-dated securities.

Amazon India announced the creation of over 1.6 lakh temporary positions across its operations network to handle the upcoming festive season surge. The company stated these roles span 400 cities, including tier 2 and 3 locations, and involve picking, packing, and delivering orders. Abhinav Singh, Vice President of Operations at Amazon India, noted that many associates will continue working beyond the festive period. Meanwhile, Meesho expects to generate approximately 10 lakh seasonal job opportunities through its seller and logistics ecosystems. The marketplace reported that nearly 1.3 lakh sellers plan to hire seasonal workers for packaging and inventory management. PTI reported that the festive season is likely to create 2.5–2.7 lakh temporary jobs across various sectors, with significant demand from tier II and III cities. The TeamLease Festive Season Workforce Report 2026 projected that South India will account for 36.3 per cent of these frontline opportunities.

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang told IANS that India must accelerate its AI development to match the technology's rapid pace. He described AI as essential economic infrastructure and advised governments to regulate only practical harms rather than hypothetical risks. Huang noted that AI systems have improved significantly in reliability over the past two years. He also stated there were no discussions regarding additional US semiconductor tariffs during the G20 ministerial.

The Reserve Bank of India reported a $127 billion mobilisation through non-resident deposits, exceeding market expectations. This influx bolsters the central bank's capacity to support the currency against the US dollar. Traders anticipate the rupee opening between 94.30 and 94.35. The Reserve Bank of India stated that the actual figure is far higher than anyone had expected.

Lionel Messi posted a Michelob ULTRA advertisement declaring the GOAT debate settled days after retiring from international football. The video features a receipt listing his 207 appearances and 125 goals for Argentina alongside major titles won in 2021, 2024, and 2024. The ad highlights his 21 World Cup goals and notes he won the 2022 tournament while Cristiano Ronaldo did not. Messi and Ronaldo have faced each other 36 times, with Messi's teams winning 16 matches. The article states Messi finished his international career with 125 goals compared to Ronaldo's 146.

The Apple board approved a new compensation package for CEO John Ternus, raising his annual salary to $3 million and granting restricted stock units worth $2.5 million. His total disclosed stock exposure is approximately $110 million, with potential future payouts reaching $148 million based on performance. Tim Cook transitions to Executive Chairman with a reduced $2 million salary and a $45 million equity award. Ternus officially assumed the CEO role on September 1, 2026. The article notes that while the filing details salary and equity, it does not specify potential cash bonuses, which are typically valued at double the base salary.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated on September 2 that he does not believe a trade deal exists between India and Iran. His comments followed a meeting between Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian at the SCO Summit in Bishkek. Rubio emphasized that many nations communicate with the Iranian regime but warned against helping Iran evade sanctions or fund terrorism. Meanwhile, an Iranian readout noted Pezeshkian appreciated New Delhi's support during recent conflicts and urged dialogue to resolve regional issues. The leaders discussed peace efforts amid heightened tensions in West Asia, including recent Iranian attacks on US bases.

Analyst Nagaraj Shetti recommends eClerx Services and UNO Minda shares for short-term investment. The article notes that domestic benchmarks Nifty 50 and Sensex gained 0.35% on Thursday, driven by banking stocks and higher foreign currency mobilization. While oil prices eased near $95 a barrel, the overall Nifty 50 trend remains weak with potential resistance around 24,100-24,200 levels. Shetti highlights that eClerx shows a bullish flag breakout pattern, whereas UNO Minda recently broke down from a triple-top consolidation. The report includes a disclaimer that these views belong to individual analysts, not LiveMint. Readers are advised to consult certified experts before making investment decisions.

Benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty rose in early trade on Thursday after three sessions of losses, driven by bank stocks and global market trends. The Sensex climbed 334.16 points to 76,904.51, while the Nifty advanced 95.45 points to 24,009.90. Analysts attributed the positive sentiment to easing U.S. bond yields and record foreign-currency deposit inflows. V. K. Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments noted that recent selling pressure likely came from retail investors rather than institutions. Meanwhile, FIIs bought equities worth ₹6,688.37 crore on Wednesday, while DIIs purchased shares worth ₹2,812.98 crore.

The Supreme Court set aside a ₹425 crore penalty on Gujarat diamond trader Vijay Ghanshyam Gadiya after the original order relied on non-existent case laws generated by AI. A bench of justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu remanded the case to an officer of the same rank, cautioning that while AI can be an assistive tool, it must not drive adjudication decisions. The court left it to the appointing authority to decide on any action against the customs officer who issued the flawed order.

Fact-checkers determined a viral video of people in floodwaters is not from Nepal. Reverse image searches found the clip on Instagram in July, predating the floods. Visual inconsistencies included skyscrapers in a hilly region and people lacking distinct facial features. Multiple AI detection tools confirmed the video was synthetic with high confidence scores. The video is being shared to falsely depict real flood visuals.

Tamil Nadu CB-CID registered a case after detecting an AI-generated deepfake video impersonating Chief Minister Vijay on social media. Police found the Hindi audio video asked viewers to contact a WhatsApp number for financial assistance. Authorities approached Meta for logs and requested the fake video's removal. The investigation continues to trace creators of similar scams reportedly circulating from Pakistan-based accounts.

Police in Delhi are investigating a murder-suicide case after finding a 28-year-old woman dead and a man critically injured at Hotel Prince in Lahori Gate. Deputy Commissioner of Police Niharika Bhatt stated the woman had multiple stab injuries while the man attempted suicide. The couple, from Bihar and Rajasthan respectively, had checked in two days prior. Authorities are currently contacting their families and conducting further inquiries into the incident.

Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha alleges the Aam Aadmi Party orchestrated his removal from Punjab's draft voter list. Chadha stated the deletion was a political vendetta while AAP officials claim he is responsible for maintaining his registration. The Election Commission conducted the Special Intensive Revision independently of the state government. Chadha plans to use available remedies to correct the record before the final roll releases in October 2026.

LiveMint reports that gold and silver prices rebounded following a correction triggered by the Jackson Hole meeting. Emkay Wealth Management states gold has stronger support around $4,060, while silver faces potential resistance near $68 and $74. Vivek Choksey of Emkay notes the long-term case for gold remains constructive if interest rates soften. Augmont's Renisha Chainani adds that gold currently finds support between $4,400 and $4,410, whereas silver holds above $66. Both metals continue to benefit from a weakening U.S. dollar and easing Treasury yields. The article concludes that while both assets offer long-term value, silver remains more volatile due to its sensitivity to industrial demand.

Private equity firms and their portfolio companies are increasingly utilizing India's deepening capital markets for initial public offerings. A McKinsey survey indicates India is emerging as a top pick in Asia-Pacific private markets. In FY2025-26, PE-backed listings accounted for 35% of total main-board IPO issuances. Major firms like Blackstone and Warburg Pincus have successfully listed or divested stakes in sectors ranging from real estate to mutual funds. While some investors express caution regarding valuation incentives, the trend signals a shift toward institutional acceptance. Experts note that future success depends on whether these listings foster long-term capital formation rather than serving merely as exit corridors.

TMC General Secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleges BJP supporters vandalised a Kolkata office on Thursday morning. He claims armed attackers ransacked the premises and demanded Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari's resignation. Banerjee stated the Kolkata Police did not respond for nearly two hours. He also cited previous attacks on TMC leaders since the BJP came to power in West Bengal on May 4.

BJP MP Raghav Chadha alleges the AAP government deleted his name from Punjab's draft voter list as political revenge. The AAP states the Election Commission handled the revision and that Chadha resides in Delhi. Chadha claims an AAP officer marked him as shifted despite guidelines requiring MPs' inclusion. The AAP says Chadha should have transferred his registration to Delhi. Punjab is currently in the third phase of the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee alleged that armed BJP men vandalised the party's Camac Street office in Kolkata early Thursday. Banerjee claimed intruders damaged equipment and took mobile phones, while BJP MLA Sajal Ghosh denied any party involvement. The TMC shared unverified CCTV footage and demanded arrests, whereas the BJP dismissed the incident as staged. Banerjee further criticized the police response and called for the Chief Minister's resignation.

Lumino Industries shares rose nearly 40% from their IPO price of Rs 82 to reach a high of Rs 114.48 on the NSE. The company's Rs 700-crore IPO was subscribed over 124 times, with qualified institutional buyers showing the highest interest. Proceeds will largely repay borrowings and fund capital expenditure. Analysts Shivani Nyati and Sunny Agrawal from Swastika Investmart and SBI Securities respectively highlighted attractive valuations and potential debt reduction benefits. However, they noted risks related to high dependence on government clients. Nyati advised partial profit booking for allottees while suggesting fresh investors wait for consolidation before buying.

IFCI shares rallied over 16% in two days as the National Stock Exchange IPO approaches. SEBI Chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey stated the regulator is close to approving the draft prospectus. The exchange plans an offer-for-sale of 14.89 crore shares representing about 6% of its capital. Existing shareholders including State Bank of India and insurance companies will sell portions of their holdings. Dolat Capital Market initiated coverage with a bearish call on NSE shares in July.

Indian stock indices Sensex and Nifty posted a partial recovery on Thursday following three consecutive sessions of losses. The rebound remained fragile due to elevated oil prices and renewed Middle East tensions. GIFT Nifty futures indicated a positive start, while the Sensex traded over 188 points higher. Analysts noted that investor sentiment deteriorated as fighting between the US and Iran escalated. Brent crude remained near $96 per barrel despite President Trump's comments on the conflict.

The article explores how Uttam Kumar remains a defining figure in Bengali cinema decades after his death. Critics found the 2024 film Oti Uttam apathetic, yet it became a box-office hit that proved his magic still enchants audiences. Uttam Kumar died in 1980 at age 53, but his name remains synonymous with Bengali cinema and culture. His career began with eight flops between 1948 and 1952 before he achieved stardom with Basu Paribar in 1952. He formed an iconic pairing with Suchitra Sen, appearing together in 30 films over 22 years. Unlike many stars, Uttam played darker, flawed characters and took supporting roles for artistic reasons. Satyajit Ray cast him in Nayak, portraying a middle-class youth, and later in Chiriyakhana as Byomkesh Bakshi. Soumitra Chatterjee acknowledged Uttam's unmatched popularity, comparing their rivalry to rival football clubs. Uttam represented the honest, middle-class Bengali man and became a symbol of Bengaliness. His mass adulation is compared to that of Rudolph Valentino in Hollywood. As Satyajit Ray noted, there will never be another like Uttam Kumar.

Hugging Face introduces funes, a tool that transforms coding agent session logs into durable, queryable memory. The software indexes traces locally without requiring external accounts or hosted models. It supports multiple agents like Claude Code and Codex while preserving raw evidence from original turns. The tool allows users to bind memories to specific projects for sharing across machines and teams. Benchmarks show recall is significantly cheaper than traditional handoffs or compaction methods. Hugging Face states the project is open source and relies on existing infrastructure like Lance datasets.

University Startups has launched Trinity, an agentic AI solution designed to help students with disabilities create personalized postsecondary transition plans. The tool automates the creation of legally mandated Individualized Education Programs (IEPs) by guiding students through conversations about their goals and strengths. To address scaling challenges, the company partnered with g/d/n/a to build a multi-agent architecture on AWS that separates specialized tasks like college and employment recommendations. This system retrieves data from over 30,000 college records and 1,000 occupations while maintaining strict HIPAA and FERPA compliance through field-level encryption. Trinity currently serves districts in more than a dozen U.S. states and is expanding into Saudi Arabia and Kuwait. Educators report the platform reduces IEP planning time to under ten minutes while increasing student agency.

A South African academic researcher declined a job offer to train an AI system designed to replace teaching and assessment roles. The author, who recently completed a Ph.D. on AI in agriculture, was interviewed by an AI system rather than a human recruiter. Despite the role offering 600 rand per hour in a country with high youth unemployment, the researcher stopped pursuing the position after the AI suggested retaking an assessment. The article highlights a growing trend where skilled professionals in Africa are recruited to transfer judgment and expertise to machines that may eventually automate their work. The author questions the ethics of handing over pedagogical judgment to algorithms and continues seeking traditional academic employment.

WIRED analyzed Flock Safety's AI-powered surveillance software, which allows police to search video feeds using written descriptions of people. The company recently implemented new safeguards after facing backlash over misuse, including a Texas deputy searching 83,000 cameras for a woman who had an abortion. However, experts warn that Flock's guardrails may discourage but not stop abusive uses. The AI model, running on Flock's servers, decides which descriptions officers can search for without departmental oversight. While the system blocks searches based on race and religion, it only warns against political and cultural expression, a category experts say is heavily protected under the First Amendment. Flock states that officers cannot run prohibited searches, but the company did not explain how warnings are triggered for religion and nationality. Data flows both ways, with Flock receiving officer search queries and subsequent actions, though the company did not disclose how long these records are kept. Over 46 of 50 recent officer misconduct cases involving license plate readers involved Flock. Flock claims local agencies set rules, but critics argue the technology enables mass surveillance that requires structural reform beyond targeting individual bad actors.

Uber launched the UKs first self-driving minicab service in London on Thursday. The company operates 15 autonomous vehicles, each requiring a human safety driver. Fares match standard UberX, Electric, or Comfort rates. BBC journalist Zoe Kleinman became the first British reporter to test the ride.

TechCrunch announces the return of the Builders Stage at its Disrupt 2026 conference, scheduled for October 13-15 at the Moscone Center in San Francisco. The event targets founders, investors, and operators seeking practical advice on scaling startups through candid conversations and case studies. Over 10,000 attendees are expected to join sessions covering fundraising, hiring, go-to-market strategies, and AI integration. The agenda features industry leaders like Grant Lee of Gamma and Robby Stein of Google discussing specific challenges such as competing for AI talent and navigating the Series A landscape in 2027. Speakers will address how product decisions must evolve at scale and how companies can achieve viral growth while maintaining retention. The stage also explores M&A as an early-stage strategy and the psychological demands of founding a high-growth company. Ticket prices are set to increase, prompting organizers to encourage early registration. The event aims to provide actionable insights for building companies that can transition from seed funding to significant market traction.

Palo Alto Networks acquired Console, an AI startup, for $500 million in cash and stock, sources say. The deal values Console at $157 million, providing a rapid return for investors including CEO Nikesh Arora. Palo Alto Networks plans to integrate Console into its Cortex platform to enhance autonomous security capabilities. This acquisition marks the cybersecurity firm's seventh purchase in 2026.

The Asian Development Bank proposed a $259.91 million project to expand low-carbon power infrastructure in Bangladesh's Chattogram Hill Tracts. The initiative aims to increase electricity access from 49% to 68% by 2032 and connect 88,000 additional households. Funding includes a $175 million concessional loan from ADB and contributions from the Government of Bangladesh and the Bangladesh Power Development Board. The project will construct six new substations, upgrade existing infrastructure, and install solar-powered systems for water and community facilities. It also plans to establish digital complaint centers, childcare facilities, and support sustainable livelihoods through training and business incubation.

Analysts warn that damaged refineries in the Middle East and Russia will likely sustain elevated global fuel prices into 2027. The International Energy Agency reports that global refining capacity remains nearly 5 million barrels per day below year-ago levels. Experts state that rebuilding lost capacity will take years, leaving crude oil surplus but unable to reach the market. Phillips 66 executives note that approximately 8.4 million barrels per day of refining capacity are currently offline due to conflict-related damage.

Hitachi Energy has signed a long-term agreement with Daikin Industries to secure C4-FN gas for its SF6-free switchgear. Daikin will manufacture the specialty gas at a Frankfurt facility starting in 2027. This move adds European capacity to Hitachi's existing Asian sources to improve supply resilience. Hitachi Energy reports that its EconiQ equipment can cut CO2-equivalent emissions by 99% compared to conventional SF6-insulated equipment. The company has recorded over 4,000 EconiQ orders across 40 countries.

A Chinese research group developed a steric-gated dual-site chelation strategy to improve perovskite solar cell efficiency and stability. Lead author Cong Chen explained that their ADA-DA additive passivates defects while maintaining charge transport. The team achieved 27.39% efficiency in a single cell and 22.33% in a bifacial module. Independent verification confirmed these results, and the modules retained 99.6% power output after 5,000 hours of testing.

Poland has confirmed that all foundations are in place for the Bałtyk 2 and 3 nuclear power projects. The announcement marks a significant milestone in the country's nuclear energy expansion plans. Officials stated that construction can now proceed to the next phase.

Europe faces critically low gas storage levels, prompting a fierce competition for limited LNG supplies with Asia ahead of winter. Analysts warn that blocked shipments from Qatar and high demand could intensify the global fight for fuel. Current storage stands at 66%, requiring over $8.1 billion in purchases to reach safety targets. ING strategists note that while Europe currently attracts spot LNG, competition is expected to rise significantly if Qatari cargoes remain absent through year-end.

Ford has set an internal goal to sell 100,000 Fathom electric trucks in the model's first year of sales. People familiar with the matter told the Wall Street Journal that production will begin in Q1 2027. The vehicle is expected to start under $30,000, positioning it as a top-selling non-Tesla EV. Ford plans to use lessons from the Ford Lightning to keep costs down.

Experts report that 82 percent of the world's oceans are currently experiencing marine heat waves, with this year setting new temperature records. Global Climate Risks states these events are becoming more common, intense, and widespread, driven by anthropogenic warming that has absorbed over 90 percent of excess heat. NOAA scientists note that warming has tripled the number of extreme heat days since 1940. The article details how acute heat waves differ from gradual warming by causing rapid ecosystem shifts, such as coral bleaching affecting 84 percent of reef areas and massive algal blooms. Historical data from the 2014-2016 'Blob' illustrates severe impacts, including a 20 percent drop in humpback whales and the collapse of kelp forests. Catherine Gregory of the University of Bern describes current conditions as the most extreme in the Western Mediterranean and Pacific regions. Scientists warn that the current El Niño event may expand these heat waves, compounding damage to marine species like seabirds and sea lions.

The Trump administration is proposing new Clean Water Act regulations that would restrict state and tribal authority to block energy projects like pipelines. EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin argues these rules prevent states from improperly vetoing projects based on non-water-quality factors. Environmental advocates warn the changes will significantly reduce federal water protections. The proposal specifically narrows state reviews to point source discharges and limits tribal participation to those with full water quality standards programs. The EPA states these measures are necessary to ensure legal compliance and support cooperative federalism. If finalized, the rules could impact upcoming projects such as the Constitution Pipeline in New York.

Heerema Marine Contractors completed installing 100 wind turbine foundations and two substation jackets for the Bałtyk 2 and Bałtyk 3 offshore wind farms in Poland. The company said the four-month campaign utilized the semi-submersible crane vessel Thialf and nearly 35 support vessels. Jointly developed by Equinor and Polenergia, the 1.44GW project is expected to power over two million households. First power is anticipated in 2027, with full commercial operations planned for 2028.

An OWC-led consortium will conduct a feasibility study for Morocco's first offshore wind farm. The project aims to assess technical and economic viability for the country's emerging renewable energy sector.

Environmental organizations ClientEarth and Beyond Fossil Fuels criticize the European Commission's approval of Germany's new capacity market design. The European Commission approved the mechanism on September 2, allowing Germany to proceed with auctions starting September 9. ClientEarth lawyer Stéphanie Nieuwbourg described the decision as astonishing, noting the design effectively subsidizes fossil fuel gas generation. The mechanism is estimated to cost between €15.6 billion and €35.2 billion over its lifetime. Critics argue the rules exclude batteries and demand response from the initial 9GW tenders, favoring gas plants with higher capacity credits. While the Commission deemed the aid appropriate, ClientEarth plans to examine the approval process and its potential market-distorting effects. Industry voices warn that current designs lock in gas capacity while reducing revenues for storage assets.

Hyundai is breaking ground this week on a nearly $6 billion steel mill in Ascension Parish, Louisiana, scheduled to open in 2029. The facility will initially operate on natural gas, producing significantly less carbon than traditional coal mills but still generating harmful air pollution. Kimberly Terrell of the Environmental Integrity Project stated the plant will be a major source of regulated pollutants, while local resident Courtney Harris expressed concern over long-term community costs. Hyundai-Posco Louisiana Steel claims its products will have a carbon footprint 70% lower than conventional methods and that the company meets all environmental standards. Experts note that while the gas-fueled design is cleaner than coal, the industry is currently moving toward direct-reduced-iron production due to cost and efficiency, with green hydrogen remaining a future goal rather than an immediate reality.

The article states that Europe's renewables expansion is shifting value toward flexibility. It notes this trend without citing specific sources or data points. The text focuses on the changing dynamics of the energy sector.

The #ElbowsUp for Climate campaign reports that over 26 million Canadians in more than 930 communities have experienced climate impacts so far this year. The new map documents extreme heat, unsafe air quality, flooding, and other hazards affecting the majority of the population. Campaign co-chair David Miller stated that evacuation preparations have become normalized, linking economic threats with climate disasters. The group is calling for federal investment in clean energy and a national resilience strategy.

China's carbon dioxide emissions fell by 1% in the second quarter of 2026, driven primarily by a sharp decline in oil consumption rather than coal reductions. The National Bureau of Statistics reports that oil use dropped 9% overall, with transport consumption falling 16% amid disruptions to supply from the Strait of Hormuz. Electric vehicles and public transport became key factors in this shift, with EV usage surging to displace significant amounts of fuel. Despite a rebound in coal-fired power generation, total emissions decreased because the reduction in oil use outweighed the increase from coal. The analysis highlights that structural changes in transportation, including increased EV adoption and charging volumes, played a major role in reducing oil demand. However, power sector emissions rose 3.0% in the first half of 2026 due to curtailment of solar and wind output, which forced greater reliance on coal. Government plans released in the quarter signal a higher bar for new coal projects but also allow for increased renewable curtailment limits in some provinces. While emissions remain below their 2023-24 peak, the trend reflects a complex balance between slowing energy demand growth and the continued expansion of clean energy capacity.

Researchers published a study in Communications Earth & Environment arguing that limiting global warming to well below 2°C requires stringent methane reductions alongside net-zero CO2 targets. The authors report that even under ambitious national net-zero goals, failing to cut methane leads to peak warming exceeding 1.85°C. Their analysis indicates that to stay under 1.7°C with a 2050 net-zero CO2 target, methane emissions must fall by at least 69% by 2050. Conversely, current policies project a 20% methane increase by 2050, which would push peak warming above 2°C regardless of CO2 efforts. The team suggests decoupling methane and CO2 metrics to clarify necessary emission cuts. They find that meeting the Global Methane Pledge could reduce peak warming by 0.15°C, with 0.05°C achievable at no net cost.

Tesla will unveil its two-seater Cybercab at an event in Austin on Thursday, according to reports. CEO Elon Musk describes the autonomous vehicle as essential for transforming the company into a dominant force in driverless transportation. The electric-vehicle maker has expanded its robotaxi service to several cities in Texas and Florida since June 2025. Analysts view driverless vehicles as central to Tesla's future, though regulatory hurdles and slower-than-expected growth remain concerns.

French Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot announced that France has started testing two Tesla vehicles equipped with Full Self Driving technology. The ministry aims to verify data from the Netherlands and Tesla before a potential European Union vote next month or early December. Officials expect results by mid to late September to inform the decision on approving the system across the bloc.

Layoff.fyi reports that more than 6,300 tech jobs were eliminated in just a few days. Uber reduced its workforce by 10% while PayPal cut 2,200 positions globally, with over 1,000 losses occurring in India. These moves reflect broader restructuring plans and cost-cutting measures across the technology sector amid an AI boom.

New York Fed economist Kartik B. Athreya shares takeaways from the Jackson Hole symposium regarding financial innovation in payments. The author reports that central banks are examining how blockchain technology and smart contracts might alter traditional payment systems. Athreya notes that while these innovations offer benefits like real-time transactions, they also pose risks to consumer well-being and non-bank financial institutions. The economist highlights New York Fed research on stablecoins, warning that digital assets remain vulnerable to runs and shocks similar to traditional bank deposits. Furthermore, the post explores how a shift to stablecoins could impact banks' ability to gather information and lend capital. Athreya concludes that regulators must carefully evaluate whether new payment tools facilitate necessary transactions or merely transfer risks to the public.

House Republicans expressed frustration with President Trump's tariff policies during a closed-door meeting with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. Lawmakers discussed the US-Canada trade war and the removal of beef tariffs, with Rep. Zach Nunn noting the need to address constituents. Representatives described Greer as receptive to their critiques and planned to raise concerns at an upcoming White House dinner.

The author argues that high AI-driven growth can offset a falling labor share of income, reducing the need for redistribution. The analysis shows that even if labor's share drops significantly, aggregate worker income can remain stable if the economy expands rapidly. Three scenarios illustrate this: an econ-pessimist view requiring 2.7% GDP transfers, an econ-optimist view needing no transfers, and a techno-optimist view requiring only 5.3% transfers despite a 22.9% labor share. The author notes that compensation could involve shifting taxes rather than raising rates. While individual workers may still face job losses, the overall compensation problem is manageable if productivity growth is substantial. The author concludes that growth is beneficial and that labor share alone does not determine AI's distributional impact.

Ludlow Food Festival organizers state that rising costs and economic pressures make the event's current format unsustainable without increased visitor numbers. The 32nd annual festival, held at Ludlow Castle from September 11 to 13, features over 100 exhibitors and various entertainment options. Organizers note that while the event survived previous downturns, it now faces a critical crossroads regarding its future structure. To attract more attendees, the festival has introduced new features including a food theatre, cookery school, and children's workshops.

Saudi AI firm HUMAIN plans to launch a large global venture capital fund this year, according to CEO Tareq Amin. The fund will operate offices in the US, Saudi Arabia, France, and the UK to accelerate investment pace. HUMAIN will only back companies that commit to using Saudi data centers or bringing staff to the country. The firm has already secured a 16 gigawatt power commitment and signed agreements with US tech giants for semiconductor supply. CEO Amin stated that data centers are treated like critical national infrastructure due to the US-Iran war, requiring hardened security defenses. HUMAIN has not slowed demand from AI companies, noting its compute costs are about 30% cheaper than elsewhere globally.

The benchmark BSE Sensex index fell more than 400 points during the final five minutes of Thursday's trading session. The decline occurred during the closing auction session on the monthly derivatives expiry day. The index slipped from 76,554.20 to 76,152.86 between 3:25 pm and 3:30 pm. Sensex eventually closed at 76,152.86, down 417.49 points or 0.55 per cent from its previous close.

The article seeks information from UK homeowners regarding property damage potentially caused by recent heatwaves. It also provides links for submitting details or reading terms and privacy policies.

The US Mint launched a $1 coin featuring Donald Trump's portrait to celebrate America's 250th anniversary. The Mint stated the coins are legal tender but not currently in circulation. Federal law usually prohibits living presidents from appearing on currency, but a specific design clause allowed this exception. The coins are made of copper, zinc, manganese, and nickel, not gold. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent also announced plans for a new $250 bill with Trump's portrait.

Reader's Digest recently released a report ranking the most affordable vacation destinations based on the estimated cost of a three-night trip for two adults. The study considered lodging, airfare, meals, and drinks to provide a broader sense of weekend expenses. While actual costs depend on location and travel timing, the list offers budget-conscious travelers options with diverse attractions. Concord, North Carolina, combines shopping, outdoor fun, and family attractions. Phoenix, Arizona, pairs desert adventure with big-city museums and dining. Macon, Georgia, appeals to music and history lovers with its museums and cultural sites. Brownsville, Texas, provides a coastal alternative to inland Texas cities. These destinations prove that a memorable autumn getaway does not require a significant financial investment.

Gloria Steinem, a pioneering American feminist and journalist, has died at the age of 92. Her family announced her peaceful passing at her New York City home, noting her lifelong dedication to equality. Steinem utilized rigorous journalism and activism to bring feminist perspectives into the mainstream, campaigning against issues ranging from domestic violence to the Vietnam War. Her career included undercover work for Esquire magazine and co-founding Ms. magazine in 1971. Throughout her life, she addressed the intersection of race and sexism while facing criticism for her past support of Bill Clinton and initial stance on transgender rights. Steinem remained active in politics until her death, co-chairing the 2017 Women's March on Washington and expressing hope to live to 100 just before her passing.

The Trump administration filed court papers supporting OpenAI in its copyright dispute with the New York Times. The Justice Department argued that training AI models on internet content promotes public benefits and national security. The New York Times stated the administration favors AI companies at the expense of creators. The lawsuit involves claims that OpenAI uses journalistic work without permission or payment. Other news organizations and writers have also joined the legal challenge against OpenAI.

Senators Alex Padilla and Joseph Morelle wrote to Homeland Security officials demanding the release of $39.6 million for election security. President Donald Trump dismissed recent Iranian attacks on US targets as a "love tap" after American forces conducted heavy retaliatory strikes. Trump faces pressure to avoid further escalation before the November midterm elections, even as his approval ratings have dropped to a record low. The World Meteorological Organization warns that the El Niño weather phenomenon is set to intensify into a very strong event by late 2024. UN chief Antonio Guterres described the situation as the world entering a danger zone of extreme weather. The agency noted an exceptionally high likelihood of nearly 100 per cent that El Niño will persist through February. Saulo cautioned that the event could deliver a massive blow to global communities and economies, urging disaster management authorities and climate-sensitive sectors to prepare immediately.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez told lawmakers there is no evidence Morocco orchestrated the recent migrant influx into Ceuta. This statement follows a police report characterizing the event as a planned operation rather than spontaneous migration.

Time Out magazine compiled a ranking of the world's most beautiful hotels based on visits by its experts. Ashford Castle in Ireland took the number one spot among 33 properties. The hotel features 83 rooms and a spa with a bronze conservatory. Other top European entries include Four Seasons Hotel Firenze and ION Adventure Hotel in Iceland.

Belgium health authorities report nearly 3,000 excess deaths during successive summer heatwaves. The Sciensano institute noted a 7% increase in deaths during the third heatwave between late July and mid-August. Total excess mortality reached 2,935, with the highest rate occurring in early July. Belgium confirmed summer 2026 as its hottest on record, averaging 20.3C at the Uccle station. Regional comparisons show Germany, Spain, and France also recorded high heat-related death tolls this year.

President William Ruto ordered a crackdown on foreigners operating small-scale businesses to protect local traders. He promised to fast-track legislation restricting foreign involvement in such trades while maintaining openness to investment. The move addresses tensions between locals and migrants, including refugees, who work in Kenya's informal economy. Ruto emphasized that investors should create jobs rather than compete as hawkers. The government noted that about 857,000 refugees are registered, with many working outside camps.

Gloria Steinem, a leading figure in the US women's liberation movement, has died at age 92. Her foundation announced she passed peacefully at her New York City home surrounded by loved ones. Steinem co-founded Ms. magazine and campaigned for reproductive rights, same-sex marriage, and equal pay throughout her career. She witnessed the recent reversal of the Roe v. Wade decision after decades of advocacy. Her foundation stated she continued working for equality until the very end.

Senegalese consumers in Dakar have started an online campaign to protest increasing prices. The movement highlights sharp rises in meat and onion costs alongside fuel and rent hikes. Organizers launched the hashtag #30DaysForTheRightPrice to alert authorities to the situation. FRANCE 24 reports that the campaign aims to protect vulnerable households from these economic pressures.

Moroccan migrants in Ceuta are calling for the right to apply for asylum, arguing that other nations are permitted to do so. At least 5,000 migrants remain in the enclave after a July influx of over 70,000 people. Residents claim these individuals strain public resources while living in makeshift camps. Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez accused right-wing social media accounts linked to Russia and Israel of exploiting the crisis.

Gloria Steinem, a prominent figure in the US women's movement, has died at age 92. Her career began as a journalist before she shifted to activism following a 1969 abortion rights speak-out. Steinem co-founded Ms. Magazine in 1972 and remained a vocal advocate for issues like genital mutilation and Korean reconciliation well into her 80s. She often spoke about overcoming her fear of public speaking to reach audiences at rallies and campuses. Steinem expressed frustration that her appearance was frequently highlighted over her work, noting that people often attributed her success to her looks rather than her efforts. She faced hostility from various quarters, including President Richard Nixon, yet continued collaborating on projects until shortly before her death.

Cuban families face severe hardships as the new school year begins under conditions of extreme poverty and systemic shortages. The article reports that many mothers cannot afford uniforms, lack electricity for basic needs, and struggle to feed their children. Education Minister Naima Trujillo acknowledged the difficulty in meeting the demand for uniforms for nearly 1.4 million students due to a lack of power, fuel, and money. Additionally, a teacher shortage of 21,000 has reduced coverage to 73%, while low salaries drive professionals away. A recent study by the Cuban Observatory for Human Rights indicates that 94% of the population lives in extreme poverty. Despite these challenges, students attended patriotic ceremonies, though many schools operate with significant delays and resource gaps. Experts warn that the crisis is causing severe mental health effects on children and caregivers.

Gloria Steinem, a leading figure in the US women's movement, died at 92. Her foundation announced her peaceful passing in New York City on Wednesday. Steinem co-founded Ms. Magazine and the National Women's Political Caucus, advocating for issues like abortion rights and equal pay. She received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2013 and remained active in activism until her death.

Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune announced the reinstatement of the death penalty for arsonists following unprecedented wildfires that devastated forests and killed dozens. While official reports cite 12 deaths in Jijel, local accounts suggest the toll is far higher. Tebboune attributed the fires to climate change but also ordered investigations into criminal responsibility. The government declared the region a disaster area and mobilized resources for relief and reconstruction.

Czech President Petr Pavel told CNN that Russia employs sabotage and disinformation to undermine European trust and divide member states. He noted Moscow resorts to these hybrid tactics because it cannot launch an open attack on NATO. Pavel argued that this strategy has backfired by strengthening EU and NATO unity. Meanwhile, Czech authorities are tightening monitoring of Russian diplomats following German accusations regarding a drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport. Foreign Minister Petr Macinka and Prime Minister Andrej Babis confirmed preparations for new security measures and pledged cooperation with partners.

People familiar with the matter said Hongkong Land is pursuing over $1 billion property deals in Tokyo as part of Jardine Matheson's strategy shift. The firm has approached Blackstone and Hulic regarding specific assets in central Tokyo. However, sources noted the company faces challenges in securing suitable properties or co-investment partners during the current market cycle.

United Nations mediators have secured an agreement for Libyan rival governments to hold elections within two years. The UN Support Mission in Libya stated this marks a significant step toward ending the transitional period. Experts note that while the deal resolves previous legal disagreements, its success remains uncertain. Analysts warn that past political agreements in Libya failed to be implemented. Concerns persist regarding whether elites will accept election results or divide resources instead. External powers like Russia and Turkey continue to support opposing factions in the east and west. The agreement aims to restructure the electoral commission and strengthen legal frameworks for a secure process.

AMD and Delhi University announced a partnership to train approximately 10,000 students in artificial intelligence and semiconductor technologies over the next year. Under the signed Memorandum of Understanding, AMD will introduce its AI Engage Developer Program to provide industry-relevant skills. Jaya Jagadish, Country Head & SVP Engineering at AMD India, stated the initiative aims to give students early access to platforms powering real-world AI development. Prof Yogesh Singh, Vice-Chancellor of Delhi University, noted the collaboration will help create a stronger pipeline of AI developers to support India's digital economy. The program offers hands-on access to AMD's ROCm AI software platform, learning resources, and developer GPU cloud credits.

Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge stated that a purification ritual at his Haldwani rally site constituted an act of untouchability. He announced his party would approach Rajya Sabha Chairman C.P. Radhakrishnan regarding the incident. Kharge criticized the silence of Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah on the matter. He also questioned the rule of law after the BJP filed an FIR against Rahul Gandhi in Uttarakhand. The Congress leader urged supporters to peacefully protest against such discriminatory acts.

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated in Kyiv that India is prepared to assist in ending the Russia-Ukraine conflict in any possible manner. His remarks followed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's recent calls for a peaceful resolution during a meeting with Vladimir Putin. Jaishankar is currently on a three-day visit to Ukraine and Poland to hold bilateral consultations. The visit occurs amid heightened hostilities and concerns in New Delhi following an Indian death in Kyiv and attacks on merchant vessels.

Microsoft's 2026 Work Trend Index finds India has the highest share of Frontier Professionals among ten markets. Puneet Chandok stated that 32 per cent of Indian AI users employ agents in multi-step workflows, double the global average. The study highlights strong leadership alignment and human oversight in Indian organizations. Major firms like Infosys and TCS show rapid enterprise adoption of Microsoft 365 Copilot. Microsoft says India's advantage combines high adoption with retained human judgment.

U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick stated that Anthropic is aligned with the Trump administration after a federal judge ruled in the company's favor. The judge sided with Anthropic in its legal dispute with the American military regarding AI safety on the battlefield. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had previously blocked certain military contracts because Anthropic refused to allow its models for domestic surveillance or autonomous weapons. Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown later emphasized the importance of data centers at a G20 event in North Carolina.

People.com reports that Oracle founder Larry Ellison filed for divorce from Barbara Boothe in 1986, three months after their daughter Megan was born. Ellison stated in a 2003 book that he chose to maintain a friendly relationship with Boothe for the children's wellbeing. Boothe raised the siblings and nurtured their love of cinema, amassing over 3,000 VHS tapes. This early exposure helped David Ellison found Skydance Media and Megan Ellison found Annapurna Pictures.

Google announced the release of Gemini 3.8 Flash and Gemini 3.8 Flash Cyber. The company stated the new model works harder on complex tasks and outperforms larger frontier models on engineering benchmarks. Google also introduced the Fairwind Program, which offers the Cyber model exclusively to governments and trusted partners for infrastructure protection.

Microsoft Work Trend Index 2026 data shows India holds 32% of global frontier AI professionals, double the world average. Puneet Chandok stated these users redefine workflows while maintaining human judgment. The report highlights that 63% of Indian AI users prioritize quality control, the highest among surveyed nations. Microsoft places responsibility for enterprise adoption on leadership rather than junior staff. Chandok advises young workers to focus on shipped projects instead of degrees.

Autoline Industries shares jumped nearly 16% after the company announced a new business award from Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Ltd. The order is expected to generate approximately ₹100 crore in additional annual revenue. Autoline stated the award reflects confidence in its engineering and manufacturing capabilities. The components will supply both internal combustion engine and electric vehicle models. Managing Director Shivaji Akhade emphasized the company's focus on quality and delivery.

Reliance Jio launches JioPC, a cloud service that boosts older computers with up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage. The company says the setup takes less than five minutes and requires no new hardware. JioPC offers two pricing tiers starting at Rs 1,000 for two months.

The NHRC bench has requested Action Taken Reports from MeitY, MIB, and Delhi Police regarding CSAM advertisements on Instagram. The commission emphasized examining the case under the POCSO Act and questioning Meta's role as an intermediary. A BBC investigation previously found Instagram promoted ads linking to explicit content. Meta stated the allegations were inaccurate and highlighted its AI detection efforts.

New U.S. tariffs on drones took effect Thursday, targeting imports to reduce reliance on China. President Donald Trump signed the order in August, citing national security threats. Drones weighing over 25 kilograms face a 100% duty, while smaller models incur a 25% charge. China opposed the move, warning it would disrupt global supply chains. DJI, which holds more than two-thirds of the global market, has previously faced U.S. restrictions.

Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal stated that India requires a tariff advantage over competing economies before the final US trade deal is announced. Goyal noted that India secured favorable terms in sensitive sectors like agriculture and fisheries while reporting 7.8% GDP growth for the April-June quarter. Conversely, the Congress party questioned these economic figures as statistical adjustments. Previous negotiations faced delays after the US Supreme Court struck down global tariffs, creating uncertainty about the final agreement's timeline and specific terms.

India will finalize its Bilateral Trade Agreement with the US only after Washington offers preferential tariff terms compared to competitors, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said. While a senior US official claimed the deal was effectively finalized in July, India insists on better rates for its exporters. The agreement aims to expand market access and deepen economic ties between the two nations.

India faces heightened drought risks as El Niño strengthens, yet systemic flaws in the declaration process leave many affected areas undetected. The 2016 drought manual relies on multiple indicators, but inconsistent implementation and staffing shortages hinder effective relief distribution. Past El Niño events reduced agricultural output by 5 to 7%, and current forecasts indicate a 14% rainfall deficit since the monsoon began. Political factors often influence drought declarations, with research showing relief may be misdirected for electoral gain. While the Indian Council on Agricultural Research advises on climate-resilient seeds, 315 districts remain vulnerable, and only 10 central financial assistance requests were made between 2020 and 2025.

The authors report that cases of immune-mediated inflammatory diseases have risen over the last two decades. They argue that a disconnect from nature contributes to immune dysregulation, potentially leading to conditions like asthma and rheumatoid arthritis. The commentary suggests today's children face greater risks due to rapid urbanization and reduced outdoor exposure. Scientists propose that the immune system requires microbial diversity from natural environments to develop proper tolerance. The authors note that urban planning strategies prioritizing green spaces could support healthier immune system development in future generations.

The Indian Air Force will hold major combat exercises near the Pakistan border in September. AAP leader Satyendar Jain was granted bail by Rouse Avenue Court in an ACB case. India reported 7.8% GDP growth in the latest quarter. A Telangana state minister was dropped amid cabinet infighting.

The Kerala CPI(M) is confronting significant internal dissent following a historic electoral defeat, with the party's vote share dropping to 21.77 per cent. The Central Committee acknowledged leadership failures in candidate selection and noted a widening gap between the party and its rank and file. While General Secretary MA Baby has urged cadres to speak openly about the loss, tensions remain regarding whether the leadership will accept full responsibility. The upcoming State Committee meeting in Kozhikode from September 13 to 15 is expected to test the party's commitment to self-criticism and organizational reform. Members are increasingly questioning decisions on candidate selection and the handling of communal issues, challenging the leadership to address these concerns publicly.
The Mettur Dam water level was recorded at 92.14 feet on Thursday, significantly below the full reservoir level of 120 feet. Inflow into the dam was 8,041 cusecs while discharge was 7,000 cusecs.

West Bengal police arrested former Panihati chairman Somnath Dey in Bengaluru on charges of hastily cremating the body of a junior doctor raped and murdered at RG Kar Medical College. Police officers aware of the matter stated Dey had been absconding since June before being caught. The arrest follows earlier detentions of two other TMC leaders and a state-ordered inquiry into the cremation process. Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari highlighted irregularities in the cremation schedule and lack of family documentation.

The Canadian Food Inspection Agency is assessing risks to imports after Indian authorities raided a Mumbai warehouse seizing nearly $80,000 in food products with fake labels. Officials found chemicals and machines used to alter expiry dates and nutrition information on brands like PepsiCo and Nestle. The CFIA stated it has no evidence these specific items entered Canada but remains vigilant against food fraud. Major food companies denied involvement in the illegal export operation.

The Supreme Court refused to hear a public interest litigation challenging government orders restricting outsider entry into public schools in Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan. The Bharatiya Janita Party governments in both states mandated prior permission for photography, videography, and interviews inside schools. The petitioner argued these restrictions violate fundamental rights under Articles 14, 19, and 21 of the Constitution. Live Law reported the court declined to entertain the challenge against the orders issued in August.

Researchers introduce NeoMME, a family of 260M and 800M multilingual multimodal encoders designed for efficient visual document retrieval. Unlike many generative visual language models, NeoMME processes both text tokens and raw image patches through a single bidirectional Transformer trained from scratch. The authors report that NeoMME-Retriever returns dense and late-interaction embeddings in one forward pass, with both model sizes lying on the ViDoRe v3 Pareto frontier for nDCG@10 and model size. Hierarchical token pooling and asymmetric quantization reduce late-interaction index storage from roughly 1.5 MB to 6 kB per page while retaining more than 95% of baseline nDCG@10. At a matched 2048×2048 image input size on an NVIDIA L40S GPU, the 260M model encodes about 51 pages per second, or about twice ColModernVBERT's throughput. The authors release all model checkpoints under the Apache 2.0 license and make the implementation available in Hugging Face Transformers.

Researchers from IIT Delhi report that crop-residue burning significantly increases black carbon pollution across North India, particularly during the post-monsoon season. The research highlights a strong geographical variation in exposure and mortality, affecting vulnerable populations disproportionately. Policymakers are urged to enforce existing bans more strictly or adopt cost-reduction strategies for residue disposal to mitigate these impacts effectively.

The project is expected to cut annual carbon dioxide emissions by approximately 1.77 lakh tonnes.
