Congress leader Jairam Ramesh claims the 7.8% GDP growth figure is unreliable and demands an explanation from the Centre. The party argues that shrinking the base year artificially inflates growth numbers. While the Ministry of Statistics reports a 7.8% increase, Congress cites expert estimates suggesting significantly lower real growth. Conversely, PM's Economic Advisory Council member Sanjeev Sanyal denies data manipulation, attributing changes to pandemic-related methodology updates.

The article reports that global bond markets are experiencing a sell-off driven by rising US Treasury yields and inflation concerns. The author explains that investors are demanding higher returns as they avoid locking funds into long-term bonds. Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary, is attempting to stabilize yields through large-scale bond purchases and diplomatic efforts to prevent Japanese holders from selling US Treasuries. The text argues that the Trump administration refuses to cut spending or raise taxes, worsening the budget deficit. Additionally, the Iran war is expected to increase defense outlays and oil prices, further straining the economy. The author concludes that this situation undermines US financial hegemony and the dollar's global standing.

The article argues that Bangladesh should not join the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement merely to appease Pakistan or send a signal to India. Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman stated Dhaka would view an invitation positively as a measure for the self-defense of the global Muslim community. However, the piece suggests this rationale is insufficient without a specific security assessment. The Mecca Pact, founded by Saudi Arabia, Türkiye, and Pakistan, remains loosely defined with mechanisms still being developed. Bangladesh's participation would primarily benefit Pakistan by adding strategic leverage on India's eastern flank. The author notes that Bangladesh's actual security concerns involve border issues with India, the Rohingya crisis, and trade routes, none of which the pact's members can address. Instead, Bangladesh could pursue bilateral cooperation, such as buying Turkish equipment or seeking Saudi investment. Maintaining the ability to work with rival nations is described as a valuable strategic asset for Bangladesh's export-dependent economy.

PC Jeweller announced it has cleared debt owed to nine of 14 consortium banks and discharged over 96% of remaining dues. The company expects to become debt-free this month, strengthening its balance sheet. Shares rose 18% in August following a 37% profit increase. The firm raised over ₹2,700 crore via a warrant issue earlier this year.

Nuh district recorded the lowest performance in Haryana Board class 10 results with a 69 percent pass rate. The article reports that many government schools lack basic facilities like water and proper seating. NITI Aayog included the district in its aspirational list in 2018 to improve education and infrastructure. Eight years later, residents question the quality of mid-day meals and building conditions remain poor.

Inox Wind shares increased 2% following a Rs 755 crore turnkey order from Indian Oil Corporation Limited. The company secured a 100 MW project including ten years of post-commissioning operations and maintenance services. Group CEO Kailash Tarachandani stated the repeat order reflects institutional confidence in their execution capabilities. The firm offers end-to-end wind energy solutions from turbine supply to long-term maintenance.

AWS Samples presents two reference implementations that bridge the gap between conceptual AI frameworks and working code using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The authors report that engineering teams often struggle to connect these phases, so these projects demonstrate practical construction patterns. The first solution auto-generates Mermaid entity relationship diagrams from SQL schema files via an event-driven workflow. The second provides automated code security analysis by scanning for vulnerabilities and policy violations through a multi-agent architecture. Both systems utilize AgentCore runtime, memory, and Gateway capabilities to maintain human oversight while accelerating delivery. The authors note that local tools like Kiro and Claude Code complement these cloud deployments by handling inception and construction phases at developer workstations. Key design decisions include chunked processing for large inputs, OpenTelemetry tracing for observability, and Cognito authentication for security. The complete implementations are available in public GitHub repositories with deployment instructions.

The article explains how to move existing agentic workloads to Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to reduce operational burdens. The authors report that production agents face ten specific challenges, including OS patching, session isolation, and tool authentication. AWS outlines a three-stage migration path that shifts these responsibilities to managed services. Stage 1 moves the agent runtime, gateway, and memory to AgentCore while keeping the planning logic unchanged. Stage 2 replaces hand-written routing with model-driven planning using Strands Agents. Stage 3 hands the entire loop over to an AgentCore harness, removing the need to maintain the codebase. The authors note that inference calls remain unaffected by the migration unless switching providers. AWS states that IAM policies, VPC configurations, and secrets rotation remain the customer's responsibility throughout all stages. The post warns teams to define acceptance criteria before migrating, as behavior may differ. It also highlights common pitfalls like holding state in the process and overlooking authentication architecture. Finally, the authors advise cloning the sample repository to review the security architecture and documentation before proceeding.

NVIDIA, Microsoft and partners announced new tools and hardware to accelerate local AI inference at IFA 2026. The company reported that compact NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows PCs will arrive in October from Lenovo and Acer. Several applications now offer simplified local AI support for NVIDIA GPUs, including Hermes Agent, OpenClaw and Perplexity Portable Computer. NVIDIA also introduced PAIR, a Personal AI Router tool that distributes inference across PCs on a local network. The event highlighted multiple new models optimized for local deployment on NVIDIA hardware, including Nemotron 3.5 Lightning and DeepSeek v4 Flash. Performance improvements include up to 1.9x faster local inference through llama.cpp and vLLM optimizations. Game publishers such as Electronic Arts and Ubisoft are bringing titles to the new RTX Spark platform. CyberLink PhotoDirector AI PC Mode will enable on-device photo editing when RTX Spark launches. NVIDIA stated that the new hardware features a 1 Petaflop RTX Blackwell GPU and up to 128GB of unified memory.

NVIDIA has released a beta version of PAIR, a virtual inference router designed to expand compute capacity for local AI agents across home networks. The tool routes independent inference requests to available systems running Ollama or LM Studio without requiring changes to existing agent harnesses. NVIDIA states that PAIR supports Windows, macOS, and Linux systems equipped with compatible NVIDIA GPUs or Apple M4+ silicon. The software manages dynamic home environments by discovering nodes, tracking readiness, and scheduling jobs while keeping data on the local network. An unofficial demonstration showed a three-device cluster completing a five-subagent task in 8 minutes and 48 seconds, compared to 18 minutes on a single laptop. NVIDIA emphasizes that PAIR does not merge GPUs or split single requests across machines but rather distributes parallel workloads to reduce queueing.

OpenAI announced it would terminate its partnership with Cursor, a startup acquired by Elon Musk's SpaceX for $60 billion. The company stated it cannot trust Musk after his organizations allegedly violated contracts. People familiar with the matter told WIRED that Cursor was among OpenAI's top five customers by early 2026, with estimated annualized revenue exceeding $1 billion. OpenAI faces potential reputational damage among developers but prioritizes stability ahead of its planned public offering. Cursor founder Michael Truell claimed OpenAI models served only 5% of user traffic, a figure disputed by OpenAI product head Thibault Sottiaux. The decision follows reports that Musk admitted xAI used OpenAI models during a lawsuit deposition. While Anthropic plans to keep its Claude models available on Cursor, OpenAI's move signals a shift away from relying on Musk's ecosystem.

Nvidia has agreed to purchase artificial intelligence platform Hugging Face in a deal valued at approximately $12.9bn. The companies stated that Hugging Face serves over 18 million developers and hosts more than three million AI models. Nvidia will pay about $11.9bn to investors and offer up to $1bn in stock incentives to employees. The acquisition aims to expand Nvidia's presence in AI software while maintaining the platform's open-source nature.

Google DeepMind and Google Research released WeatherNext 3, a new artificial intelligence model designed to enhance weather forecasting accuracy and resolution. The model outperforms other leading AI forecasts and traditional government predictions on Operational WeatherBench. It offers a 5 km resolution, a 60% improvement in rain prediction over its predecessor, and hourly forecasts. Google plans to integrate the model into search, Google Maps, and Gemini. Researchers note that while the model uses raw satellite data, it still relies on national weather datasets for full data assimilation. The technology aims to provide more useful information to users and improve renewable energy project dependability.

Nvidia has agreed to purchase AI platform Hugging Face for $13 billion, marking its largest acquisition to date. The company stated the deal aims to accelerate the spread of open AI models. This transaction represents a significant shift from Nvidia's previous $6.9 billion purchase of Mellanox in 2020. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang emphasized that open weights allow various institutions to build on advanced capabilities without paying high prices. The company plans to close the takeover by 2027, though the deal may face regulatory scrutiny.

Nvidia confirmed today it has acquired Hugging Face for $12.93 billion. CEO Jensen Huang stated in a blog post that the platform will remain open and that Nvidia compute will not be required to use it. Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue thanked the community and noted the deal provides necessary compute and support. The company hosts three million models used by over 18 million developers. Nvidia previously rejected a $500 million deal from Hugging Face last year.

Meta engineers introduced ZGateway, a stateless proxy layer designed to unify traffic for ZippyDB, the company's most widely used key-value store. The authors report that this proxy manages over a million client hosts by centralizing connection management, request batching, and admission control. By interposing between clients and the database fleet, ZGateway reduces the total number of persistent connections by roughly 19 times while adding only about 6% computational overhead. The system currently carries approximately 40% of all ZippyDB traffic, a figure projected to grow past 60%. Key capabilities include Discriminant Load Shedding to isolate noisy tenants and cross-region resilience mechanisms that allow failover between healthy regions. The authors note that ZGateway enables safer migrations through configuration flags and supports transaction operations previously handled by thick clients. Future plans involve agent-operated heuristics, co-location strategies, and a multi-process architecture to further enhance stability and programmability.

Google Research scientists Michał Januszewski and Viren Jain partnered with HHMI Janelia to publish the largest brain map to date. The project details a complete wiring diagram of the male fruit fly's brain and central nervous system, containing over 166,000 neurons and 125 million synaptic connections. This verified map, annotated by human experts, expands beyond the brain to include the ventral nerve cord. The release complements a previously mapped female fruit fly connectome, enabling researchers to compare sexual dimorphism and study courtship behaviors. Google's AI tools, including PATHFINDER, were used to reconstruct the neural shapes from electron microscope images. The team also highlighted ongoing work mapping vertebrate brains, such as the elephantnose fish and larval zebrafish. These foundational resources aim to help scientists understand neural mechanisms and potentially treat cognitive ailments like Alzheimer's.

Google DeepMind and Google Research introduced WeatherNext 3, described as the most advanced and accurate global weather AI model to date. Independent live evaluations by Brightband support these claims regarding the model's performance. The system ingests live satellite data to generate hourly forecasts at resolutions as fine as five kilometers, offering significantly sharper detail than previous versions. This approach allows the model to train directly on real-world observations rather than relying solely on traditional numerical weather prediction simulations. Consequently, the new model provides improved precipitation forecasting accuracy and specific predictions for renewable energy production. Starting today, the technology powers weather experiences within Google Search, Gemini, Maps, and other Google products worldwide.

Hundreds of protesters gathered in Edinburgh to demand an immediate moratorium on Scotland's rapidly expanding datacentre sector. Kat Jones, director of Action to Protect Rural Scotland, led the campaign calling for a pause while the government analyzes environmental impacts and defines green datacentres. First Minister John Swinney announced a strategic approach focusing on sustainability but declined to agree to a halt. At least 20 projects are currently proposed, with some located near small villages and residential areas. The Scottish Greens and Reform UK have also supported the call for a national framework. Public finance minister Hannah Mary Goodlad stated that community voices must be central to considerations, though the government maintains these centres are vital for economic growth.

Max Johnson, founder of AI agency briix, demonstrates how to build an automated content engine using Claude Code. He outlines a five-step process involving context setup, prompt engineering, pipeline construction, workflow integration, and interface design. Johnson emphasizes maintaining human oversight while leveraging AI for repetitive tasks like research and script generation. The resulting system allows users to generate multiple script options per topic through a single command.

Perplexity's valuation is increasing despite mixed user metrics. Nvidia is reportedly in talks to invest in the startup, potentially valuing it above $30 billion. The company's annualized revenue has grown to over $750 million following the launch of its Computer product. While website visits have retreated, app usage has increased by roughly 45% in six months. CEO Aravind Srinivas stated the company plans to go public in 2028.

Guardian journalist Michael Safi visited Texas billionaire Michael Samadi's Double Six Ranch to meet his AI chatbots. Samadi is planning a new civil rights movement for artificial intelligence systems. The visit offered a glimpse into Samadi's vision for the future of AI welfare and protection.

PG&E expanded its Vehicle-to-Everything program to include new electric vehicles from Tesla, Volvo, Nissan, Kia, Polestar, and General Motors. The utility added approved partners Bidirectional Energy and PowerFlex, allowing drivers to enroll until June 30, 2027. PG&E Director David Almeida stated that broadening the mix of eligible vehicles helps customers turn their EVs into home backup power and grid assets. Residential customers can receive up to $17,000 in incentives, including upfront payments and grants for specific charger combinations. Commercial customers also qualify for funding tiers based on charger capacity. PG&E is simultaneously backing electric school bus fleets in Fremont, Oakland, and San Francisco to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

Google, MN8 Energy, and Eos Energy Enterprises announced a new multi-technology renewable energy project in West Virginia. The Mammoth Solar facility will combine solar power with zinc-based and lithium-ion battery storage systems. Google agreed to purchase the energy and capacity generated by the project. The development aims to create jobs and generate tax revenue for the local community. Google also recently signed a separate agreement with Fervo Energy for geothermal power in Utah. Meanwhile, Eos received a contract from the US Department of Defense to deploy its storage technology. Industry experts note that AI data centers may cause significant grid load swings. A new conference will address these challenges and other storage issues later this year.

CleanTechnica reports that Ford is positioning its upcoming Fathom electric pickup to compete directly with Tesla's Cybercab robotaxi launch. The Wall Street Journal notes Ford plans to sell 100,000 Fathoms in their first year. Ford CEO Jim Farley has shared photos of the camouflaged vehicle on X to generate buzz before its year-end reveal. While the vehicles serve different purposes, the article highlights a contrast in marketing strategies, with Ford emphasizing affordability under $30,000 and Tesla focusing on exclusivity. Ford also plans to offer an Extended Range EV version of the Lightning F-150 with a gas engine range extender.

PG&E has launched the SHARE virtual power plant program to address growing electric demand in Bay Area communities. The utility partners with Rewiring America, Google, Carrier, Tesla, and others to enroll existing home devices and deploy new electrification technologies. Google will fully fund the initiative to support customer incentives and technology deployment. The program aims to unlock grid capacity while improving affordability and reliability for participating households.

China's oil consumption dropped 9% year over year in the second quarter as high prices accelerated the adoption of electric vehicles and trucks. The Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air reports this shift cut carbon dioxide emissions by 1% during the period. While power-sector emissions rose 3% due to increased coal use, electric vehicles displaced 36 million metric tons of oil in the first half of 2026. Electric trucks showed the fastest change, with alternative-fuel use jumping 90% year over year. CREA estimates lower oil consumption prevented roughly 35 million tons of carbon dioxide emissions in the quarter. The analysis suggests Chinese emissions could fall further this year as oil demand weakens and coal-to-chemicals production runs near capacity.

Serbian and Azerbaijani companies finalized negotiations to create a joint venture for a natural gas power plant near Niš, according to the ministry. Representatives from EPS, Srbijagas, and SOCAR concluded talks in Istanbul on shareholder alignment. The three firms expect to sign the contract in Belgrade within a month. The ministry stated the project aims to enhance electricity supply security.

China's National Energy Administration reports that solar capacity reached 1.286 TW by the end of July, overtaking coal for the first time. This milestone marks a historic shift where solar now accounts for 31.5% of the nation's total installed power capacity. While solar generation grew 15.5% year-on-year in the first seven months, coal remains the primary source of actual electricity output. Liu Zhiqiang of the China Electricity Council noted that solar's intermittency means coal will continue to provide system support in the near term. The rapid expansion contrasts with a current industry correction, where installations dropped roughly 66% in the first half of 2026 due to tighter grid conditions and weaker economics. Officials emphasize that the next phase focuses on reliability, requiring enhanced storage and transmission to convert massive capacity into dependable supply.

Experts state that additional support is required to power Africa's food systems using renewable energy sources. The article highlights the critical need for investment in this sector to ensure sustainable food production across the continent.

Venezuela has reopened its energy sector to American firms following a political shift that installed Delcy Rodriguez as the new leader. Chevron announced plans to double production with a $7 billion investment, while GE Vernova signed a deal to repair the national power grid. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright stated the administration sought a rapid transformation rather than a slow drift. The U.S. Energy Information Administration reports that liquefied natural gas exports averaged 17.4 billion cubic feet per day in the first half of the year. Meanwhile, the Pacific Northwest faces severe wildfire risks as drought conditions persist and temperatures remain above average. A new California bill addressing wildfire liability and insurance collapsed in the state legislature due to disagreements over utility payouts. Fervo Energy announced a deal to sell nearly 400 megawatts of electricity to Google for its enhanced geothermal plant. The Department of Energy is investing $12 million in space-based solar panel technology to provide constant power. Investors are increasingly backing virtual power plants to manage grid stress from new data center demand. A podcast discussion highlights the scale of natural gas power plants being built by tech companies like Amazon and Nvidia.

The Central Electricity Authority proposed new technical standards for renewable energy projects in India. The draft regulation requires 15% of inverters in new plants to have grid-forming capabilities starting July 1, 2027. Additionally, ground-mounted solar and on-shore wind projects commissioned after that date must include co-located energy storage systems equivalent to 10% of installed capacity with a minimum two-hour duration. Storage duration requirements will increase to four hours for projects commissioned between July 1, 2029, and June 30, 2031. The CEA invited public comments on the proposal by October 4, 2026.

Uzbekistan approved a plan for a 200-hectare industrial zone to increase local production for its nuclear power project. The president stated that domestic production currently accounts for only 21 percent of the project, a figure he considers insufficient. The goal is to raise this share to at least 30 percent while ensuring 65 percent of construction work is done by national enterprises. The plan includes tax benefits for firms and aims to attract at least 100 joint ventures. Additionally, a new city for nuclear workers with 10,000 apartments is being planned.

Engie announced the commercial operation of two 251MW battery energy storage projects in Chile. The Libélula facility in Colina and Tiltil adds 203MW of storage to its 140MW solar plant. Los Loros, located in Tierra Amarilla, contributes an additional 48MW of capacity. Grenergy completed the sale of the Gabriela phase of its Atacama complex to CVC DIF for US$475 million. This transaction marks the fourth phase of the Oasis de Atacama project. Grenergy will retain operation and maintenance services for five years following the sale. The combined transactions represent approximately 25% of the overall Oasis de Atacama storage capacity.

CleanTechnica editor Zachary Shahan discusses potential reforms for the US Supreme Court, citing a poll by JC Bruce that shows strong public support for expanding the court and implementing term limits. Shahan argues that the current nine-justice structure allows conservative interests to dominate, noting that many justices own shares in fossil fuel companies. He references Gabe Roth of Fix the Court, who suggests phasing in term limits rather than permanently fixing the number of justices at nine. Roth supports Representative Ro Khanna's proposal for 18-year terms. David Gans of the Constitutional Accountability Center highlights historical lessons from the Reconstruction era, suggesting Congress has tools to ensure judicial accountability. Shahan concludes that while expanding the court is one option, term limits and prohibiting stock trading by officials are essential to prevent future manipulation by special interests.

U.S. District Judge Rita Lin ruled in favor of Anthropic regarding its legal challenge to a Pentagon designation. The judge found the Defense Department retaliated against the company in violation of the First Amendment. Consequently, Lin set aside the supply chain risk designation and issued a permanent injunction ordering agencies to remove related directives. Anthropic had pursued legal action in both federal district court and the U.S. Court of Appeals for the D.C. Circuit.

Brazil's central bank and the European Central Bank are investigating a connection between their instant payment platforms, sources said. A pilot project could launch in 2028 if technical assessments confirm feasibility. The ECB confirmed an ongoing preliminary investigation into linking its TIPS system with Pix. This move represents a potential first cross-border expansion for Brazil's Pix platform, which has gained significant traction in Latin America.

Prasanna Tantri, an associate professor of finance at the Indian School of Business, warns that the Reserve Bank of India's recent measures have created five major risks for the economy. Tantri stated that the FCNR(B) saga has ended, noting that India has mobilized roughly $136 billion in borrowed dollars to defend exchange-rate levels. The professor highlights that these actions, including external commercial borrowings, could lead to external debt rising to $900 billion.

A federal judge ruled that Google illegally rigged online ad sales but declined to order the company to sell its business. This decision marks the third time in a year a judge rejected a breakup for a major tech firm, following similar outcomes for Meta. While prosecutors argued for divestiture, the court stopped short of forcing structural changes. Legal experts note this pattern frustrates antitrust advocates who seek stronger remedies against monopolies.

An under secretary of defense stated that Anthropic continues to be flagged as a supply chain risk despite recent positive comments from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. A federal judge previously ruled that the Pentagon illegally punished the AI company for criticizing the government. The Defense Department did not respond to a request for comment regarding the ongoing assessment.

Prime Minister Mark Carney announced Canada is prepared to finalize a trade agreement with the United States. He noted both sides are showing flexibility. Carney stated the U.S. has retreated from positions that previously stalled negotiations last month.

PC Jeweller Ltd reported clearing full dues from nine banks and over 96% of remaining debt from five others. The company's shares rose 3.5% on the BSE and NSE despite market declines. Q1 FY2026-27 net profit increased 37.2% to Rs 222 crore, while revenue from operations grew 21% to Rs 877.04 crore.

Nobel laureate María Corina Machado stated that Venezuela's interim government lacks the right to negotiate the country's natural resources. The opposition leader criticized the agreement with interim president Delcy Rodríguez while expressing support for US partnership. Trump backed Rodríguez over Machado, threatening consequences if she does not comply. The White House claims the deal will secure US energy dominance and exclude foreign influence. Critics argue the arrangement resembles a colonial land grab and delays elections.

UK households face potential increases in energy bills this winter as European nations rush to replenish depleted natural gas stores. Wholesale gas prices have reached three-year highs, driven by renewed tensions between the US and Iran that threaten to keep the Strait of Hormuz closed. Analysts at Capital Economics warn that gas prices could top €80 by year-end, while Cornwall Insight forecasts a further 9% rise in domestic energy prices. The UK's Department for Energy Security and Net Zero dismissed concerns over low storage levels, noting prices are set on international markets. Meanwhile, British Gas owner Centrica has called for government support to expand its North Sea storage facility. Experts caution that weather conditions remain the primary variable influencing demand and final costs.

Several major artificial intelligence platforms experienced temporary service disruptions on Thursday, according to Downdetector. User reports indicated problems with OpenAI's ChatGPT, Anthropic's Claude, xAI's Grok, and Google's Gemini. Cloudflare also faced reported issues starting later that morning. The cause of the disruptions remains unclear, though OpenAI's status page currently shows its systems as fully operational.

France authorized Tesla self-driving car tests on its roads following a meeting between Transport Minister Philippe Tabarot and Elon Musk. The minister described the decision as a new phase for on-road trials involving two available vehicles. This marks a shift from July, when Paris initially refused authorization due to safety concerns. Meanwhile, Uber and Wayve launched a commercial robotaxi service in London.

Nvidia announced the acquisition of Hugging Face for $12.93bn, marking its second-largest deal. Jensen Huang stated that Hugging Face will remain an open platform where developers can use any models or cloud providers. The deal represents a threefold increase in Hugging Face's 2023 valuation. Nvidia already held a minority stake in the company before this purchase. Neither company has disclosed a timeline for when the acquisition will close.

The article reports that US President Donald Trump described a strategy of striking Iranian military targets before they are fully rebuilt. US Central Command confirmed recent attacks destroyed air defense sites and radar systems in Iran. Axios reported that the US is considering limited, regular strikes to prevent Iran from reconstituting capabilities in the Strait of Hormuz, a concept described as 'mowing the grass.' Mona Yacoubian of CSIS warned this approach could lead to an enduring low-intensity conflict. She noted the strategy was designed for non-state actors and may fail against a state like Iran. Yacoubian also cautioned that repeated attacks might push Tehran toward pursuing nuclear weapons for lasting deterrence. The article states that while the US can control attack intensity, it cannot control Tehran's retaliatory responses.

Billionaire Leon Black filed a lawsuit against the House oversight committee, alleging improper subpoenas regarding his ties to Jeffrey Epstein. Republican oversight chair James Comer criticized Black for hiding behind litigation rather than providing testimony. Black's lawyers argued the committee was conducting a fishing expedition to destroy him. Meanwhile, JD Vance claimed US oil deals with Venezuela would lower gas prices. The Pentagon temporarily rescinded mandatory testosterone testing guidelines for service members. Senators Bernie Sanders and Greg Casar proposed legislation to ban artificial superintelligence development. Donald Trump attacked media outlets reporting on US ammunition stockpiles in Iran. The House passed a bill penalizing universities that boycott Israel. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick made erroneous claims about data center water usage and Iran war deaths. A federal judge blocked an executive order limiting birthright citizenship. Trump announced he would campaign for 35 GOP candidates in the midterm elections.

Gloria Steinem, a pioneering journalist and women's activist, died Wednesday at her New York City home at the age of 92, her foundation announced. Steinem was a central figure in the second-wave feminist movement, co-founding Ms. Magazine in 1971 and launching the National Women's Political Caucus. She described her role as an 'entrepreneur of social change' and credited women of color with inventing feminism. Her career included a 1963 undercover assignment exposing conditions at Playboy and advocacy for reproductive freedom following the reversal of Roe v Wade. In 2013, President Barack Obama awarded her the Presidential Medal of Freedom. Steinem remained active into her eighties, producing documentaries and writing books until shortly before her death.

Iran's Tasnim news agency reported that six Iranian Army naval personnel died during U.S. attacks on Tuesday. The report stated casualties occurred in Khuzestan, Kermanshah, Lavan island, and Fars province. Earlier, Iran attacked U.S. bases in Kuwait and other West Asian nations. President Donald Trump warned his military could strike Iran at any time following the bombardment.

Billionaire Leon Black failed to appear for a congressional deposition regarding his connections to Jeffrey Epstein. Instead, he filed a lawsuit challenging the subpoenas issued by the House Oversight Committee. Committee members, including James Comer and Robert Garcia, criticized his absence and called for contempt proceedings. Black maintains he knew nothing of Epstein's crimes and argues the subpoenas lack legitimate connection to legislative purposes.

German authorities arrested two suspects over an alleged arson attack at a Munich defence firm. This incident follows recent sabotage attempts on Germany's power grid and a drone strike at a Leipzig airport. European allies express concern over Russian hybrid warfare, which Moscow denies. Investigations continue into potential foreign involvement in these critical infrastructure attacks.

Nepal flood survivors in relief camps struggle to obtain essential medicines despite receiving food supplies. Some residents sell relief items like noodles to purchase heart medication. Authorities have established health centers at shelters to address medical needs. Meanwhile, residents in cut-off areas use temporary zip lines to cross flooded rivers. Rescue teams continue searching for missing workers trapped in hydroelectric tunnels.

The Pentagon removed clinical guidance requiring testosterone testing for military members aged 30 and older from its website Thursday. A defense official stated the document was temporarily rescinded to allow for updates, with interim rules remaining in effect. The initial policy, announced by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, aimed to optimize service member health and readiness. Separate screening guidelines for women over 35 were also included in the removed document.

Scientists have published the first complete map of the fruit fly's central nervous system, detailing all 166,000 neurons and millions of connections. The study, released in four papers in the journal Cell, reveals how specific neural circuits drive behaviors like walking, flying, and singing. Researchers identified sex-specific cell types that explain differences in courtship behavior between male and female flies. The project utilized advanced focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy and machine learning, requiring human review equivalent to 44 people working for a year. Stuart Berg of the Howard Hughes Medical Institute noted that the nerve cord contains significant computational machinery beyond simple signal transmission. Gerry Rubin highlighted that visual processing extends deeply into the brain, involving more than half of its neuron types. This achievement builds on decades of work and honors the legacy of Santiago Ramón y Cajal.

Norwegian courts have ordered the seizure of the Russian vessel Professor Molchanov in Svalbard to enforce a $4.22 billion compensation award won by Ukrainian firm Naftogaz. The ship was stopped from departing the port of Barentsburg after the Nord-Troms and Senja District Court approved the application. Naftogaz acting CEO Sergii Fedorenko stated that Russia cannot evade responsibility by refusing to comply with the international arbitral award. The Svalbard governor confirmed the vessel would be held while the crew and passengers remain safe under the administration of Trust Arktikugol. Russia's ambassador to Norway said Moscow would pursue the ship's release through legal channels and has summoned Norway's ambassador in Moscow. Norway's Justice Ministry noted the issue does not directly concern the Oslo government.
