Bankers argue the RBI must manage this abundance through forex sales and other tools given sub-par monsoons and elevated crude prices. The central bank has absorbed funds following large inflows through the FCNR(B) deposit scheme, which contributed 92 per cent of the $136.3 billion raised via special swap windows by end-August.

The Reserve Bank of India absorbed over Rs 3.53 lakh crore through a one-day Variable Rate Reverse Repo auction to manage excess liquidity in the banking system. The central bank accepted all bids at a 5.24 per cent rate, absorbing over 70 per cent of the notified amount. This move follows a surge in foreign currency inflows of $73 billion through the FCNR(B) scheme, which has prompted the RBI to step up liquidity absorption operations to ensure financial stability.

Former RBI Governor C Rangarajan urged the Reserve Bank of India to incentivize the creation of more small finance banks, noting the sector currently has only 11 institutions. Speaking at Equitas Small Finance Bank's Chennai office inauguration, he highlighted the bank as a potential model for universal licensing. Equitas reported a 27% year-on-year increase in gross advances to ₹47,641 crore as of June 2026, with deposits reaching ₹48,976 crore.

Jaguar Land Rover has confirmed plans to cut about 4,000 jobs over the next two years to save £1.7 billion, citing tariffs, competition, and a cyber-attack. Chief Executive PB Balaji stated the reductions will affect senior and R&D roles more heavily. Business Minister Jonathan Reynolds ruled out a taxpayer bailout, noting the company has not used a previously agreed £1.5 billion loan facility. Reynolds is due to hold talks with Balaji and Unite General Secretary Sharon Graham regarding the planned cuts.

The Election Commission announced by-polls for West Bengal's Nandigram and Rejinagar assembly seats following the resignations of Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari and AJUP chief Humayun Kabir. Voting is scheduled for October 6 with vote counting on October 9, and the entire election process will be completed by October 11. The EC stated that the gazette notification will be issued on September 9, with the last date for filing nominations set for September 16. EVMs and VVPATs will be used at all polling stations, and the EPIC card remains the principal identification document.

The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court directed the State to file a report on a public interest litigation petition filed by advocate V. Periyasamy regarding caste tensions in Kansapuram. The petitioner, representing the Devendrakula Vellalar community, alleged intimidation by the Maravar community and sought directions to implement the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act to restore peace. The court posted the matter for further hearing to October 7.

Voters in Bengaluru face difficulties resolving electoral roll discrepancies due to midnight hearing schedules and inaccessible Booth Level Officers. Activist Vinay Sreenivas noted minor name differences caused confusion, while elderly voters struggled to navigate the process. Many complain that despite public notice lists lacking venue details, they must visit offices in person. Voters have requested English notices, noting the current Kannada-only format is difficult to understand. The Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer had previously assured physical copies would be available.

The defence ministry said the Rajnath Singh-led Defence Acquisition Council cleared proposals worth 1.1 lakh crore to enhance the capabilities of the Indian armed forces. The plan includes integrating Russian-origin missiles with Sukhoi-30 fighters and acquiring new systems for the army, navy, and air force. The defence ministry stated that approximately 98% of these procurements will be made from Indian industry, aligning with the government's goal to boost defence manufacturing.

In an episode of Speakeasy with Amit Baruah, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah criticized the BJP-led Union government for failing to restore statehood in the region. Abdullah argued that people were never informed that statehood depended on electing a BJP government. He also discussed challenges of governing a Union Territory, including institutional constraints and continuing detentions, while reflecting on his second tenure compared to his first term from 2009 to 2015.

Rescue efforts at the collapsed Satya Niketan building in Delhi concluded after 24 hours, leaving seven people dead according to officials. The Delhi High Court criticized both the Municipal Corporation of Delhi and Delhi University for failing to ensure adequate safety measures and ordered a high-level inquiry into the tragedy. Authorities are now sealing illegal structures and conducting a comprehensive audit of student housing facilities. While the Delhi government intensified inspections, political parties engaged in public disputes regarding accountability. The court has listed the matter for a hearing on 25 September, requiring agencies to file replies within 10 days.

Sonia Gandhi has emerged as a prominent writer and critic following her decision to limit her political role. Since June 2024, she has published twelve articles in newspapers, frequently attacking Prime Minister Narendra Modi's governance and policies. Her writings cover diverse topics, including the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test scandal, the closure of public schools, and India's response to the conflict in Gaza. Additionally, she has criticized the government's amendment to the Flag Code, which allows machine-made flags. Her upcoming memoir, Belonging, is set to be released after she refused to remove references to Modi and the RSS from the text. The author suggests her memoir may provide insights into dynastic politics and the hardships faced by religious minorities in India.

Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta announced that the government is treating the Satya Niketan building collapse with utmost seriousness, stating that anyone found guilty will not be spared. She ordered the immediate sealing of buildings with unauthorized fifth floors across Delhi and confirmed the suspension of multiple officials. Additionally, the Chief Minister's Office revealed plans to make periodic structural audits mandatory for public buildings. MCD Commissioner Sanjeev Khirwar expressed grief over the seven lives lost and announced the demolition of the adjacent building.

The Gauhati High Court has ordered the Assam government to pay 2 lakh as interim compensation to Mujammel Hoque, the husband of Mumtaz Begum, after she was pushed into Bangladesh without her family being informed. A bench of justices Kalyan Rai Surana and Susmita Phukan Khaund passed this order on September 3 following a habeas corpus petition. The court noted that the state failed to provide Begum or her family with the tribunal order or an opportunity to appeal before her expulsion. This marks the first instance where a court has imposed a cost on the state for violating deportation rules by pushing a person into Bangladesh. The bench also directed the Ministry of External Affairs to make an endeavour to locate Begum in Bangladesh and expatriate her to India. Additionally, the court asked the Assam home department to order an inquiry into the episode and directed district superintendents of police to ensure declared foreign nationals are informed of tribunal orders before custody.

The author of Offside explores the tension between sport's need for visibility and the dangers of the attention economy. The piece notes that while legendary athletes like George Best and Muhammad Ali generated headlines through their skills and personalities, modern influencers often lack any connection to the sport itself. The author cites the Invisible Gorilla experiment to illustrate how human attention is limited and easily diverted by digital noise. Specific incidents, such as a photoshoot interrupting Naomi Osaka's preparation at the US Open and the online harassment of powerlifter Keyaa Kunal Banerji, are used to demonstrate how the pursuit of engagement can degrade the sporting experience. Ultimately, the author questions whether sport can maintain its integrity while competing for scarce attention against algorithms and viral trends.

Kochi Cyber Police booked television journalist Aparna Kurup under Sections 192, 299, 302, 353(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and Section 120(o) of the Kerala Police Act, 2011. The police registered the case on Monday following a complaint by Abdul Hakkim regarding Kurup's alleged hurt to religious sentiments while anchoring a debate on Kanthapuram A P Aboobacker Musliyar's remarks. Police stated the FIR alleged Kurup intended to cause a breach of peace and deliberately hurt religious feelings. The move followed protests by UDF leaders against a separate case against an Islamist leader who threatened Kurup with physical assault. BJP national executive member P K Krishnadas criticized the UDF government, alleging pressure from religious groups influenced the administration. The Home Department directed police not to proceed with the case against the Islamist leader after the protest.

The Calcutta High Court on Monday set aside an arrest warrant against TMC MP Mahua Moitra and ordered the case transferred to the special MP/MLA court at Bidhannagar. A division bench directed the special court to treat the complaint regarding alleged hate speech as being at the pre-cognisance stage. Moitra's lawyer argued the allegations are baseless and the case must be tried before the designated court since the speeches occurred during her tenure as an MP.

Delhi Police has issued a security advisory for the 18th BRICS Summit, which will be hosted in New Delhi on September 12 and 13. The advisory urges citizens to remain alert at public places, report any suspicious activity, and avoid unnecessary gatherings near sensitive locations. Hotel and guest house operators have been directed to maintain visitor records and verify guests properly. Residents are also advised to ensure police verification for domestic helps and tenants.

People familiar with the matter said Jio Platforms will begin investor roadshows next week while targeting an initial public offering in November. The digital and telecommunications arm of Reliance Industries plans meetings across the US, Singapore, Hong Kong, London, and the Middle East. Jio Platforms filed draft documents in June and received regulatory approval in August for an issuance of up to 270 million new shares, which could raise as much as $4 billion. The company intends to use proceeds to repay debt, though details regarding size, valuation, and timing remain subject to change during ongoing deliberations with banks.

NCC Police and Assam Rifles arrested two men from Bihar in West Tripura and recovered two 9mm pistols, three magazines, and live rounds during a joint operation on September 6. Subrata Barman, SDPO, stated that an FIR was registered and the accused will be produced before a local court today for remand and detailed interrogation regarding the source and purpose of the weapons.

Dhirendra Shastri, the head of the Bageshwar Dham temple, urged Hindus to avoid eating non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja, describing the meat as "dirty" and claiming those who consume it cannot be considered religious. The Trinamool Congress and BJP leaders strongly criticized his comments, arguing that dietary choices are personal and that no one has the right to dictate how Bengalis celebrate their cultural heritage. Shastri's remarks sparked a wider debate about religious traditions and food culture in West Bengal.

Osama Manzar, founder of the Digital Empowerment Foundation, argues that India's government is treating data centers as developmental activities without adequately consulting local communities. Manzar notes that while internet penetration in India has risen from 1.2% to over 70%, the rapid expansion of data centers poses risks of extractive technology. He points out that these facilities are projected to consume water equivalent to 1.3 billion people's annual domestic needs and electricity matching the demand of 650 million people by 2030. Manzar criticizes the lack of awareness among locals, stating that terms like 'data center' are not understood until construction begins. He advocates for hyperlocal, multi-distributed data centers that serve local needs rather than acting as data waste centers for global elites. The interview, originally published in Rest of World, emphasizes the need for genuine community consultation and responsible development practices.

Two doctors writing to a newspaper report that AI transcriptions in their practice frequently contain errors and contradictions. Dr Mary Gibbs and Debbie Cameron state that these tools do not save time, as clinicians must still proofread the long, repetitive accounts and cannot trust the information written by the AI. They warn that relying on this technology risks losing essential clinical skills and could harm patients.

A Tesla Model 3 struck a Honda Civic at a stop sign in Buena Vista Township, New Jersey, killing the Civic's driver. While police described the incident as a failure to stop, Tesla's own report to the NHTSA confirms the vehicle's driver-assist system was 'Verified Engaged' at the time of impact. The report redacts critical details regarding the software version and crash narrative. The article suggests the system was likely Full Self-Driving, as basic Autopilot does not process stop signs. Tesla maintains that the human driver remains responsible for Level 2 systems, but the redacted data prevents a full understanding of the event.

Russia's Ambassador to India, Denis Alipov, told Asian News International that Moscow will remain a key crude supplier to India despite U.S. tariff threats. Alipov criticized planned U.S. legislation, noting that excluding Russian oil would harm global energy markets. Meanwhile, India's crude imports from Russia eased in August due to Ukrainian attacks and competition from China. Analysts suggest a U.S. bill proposing 100% tariffs on major Russian oil buyers is unlikely to pass the House before November's mid-term elections.

State-owned utility Elektroprivreda Srbije issued a public call inviting investors to acquire or co-develop renewable energy projects. CEO Dušan Živković stated the initiative aims to diversify the portfolio and accelerate renewable investments through a transparent competitive process. The call targets solar, wind, hybrid, waste-to-energy, and green hydrogen projects, with letters of intent due within 30 days.

Apple is expected to unveil the iPhone 18 Pro series, a potential foldable iPhone, and new Apple Watch models at its September 9 event, according to reports. The new CEO, John Ternus, may lead the presentation while Tim Cook remains absent from the video. A foldable iPhone could cost over $2,000.

An Amazon cargo plane overran a runway at Miami International Airport on Sunday, killing at least five people and injuring others. The Associated Press reported the aircraft, operated by 21 Air, struck vehicles after arriving from San Juan. Miami-Dade officials stated three people were critically injured while the pilot and copilot remained trapped. Amazon expressed heartbreak over the loss and pledged cooperation with the investigation.

Dalton, Kahn, and Mueller report that Burning Glass data overstates labor market concentration nearly threefold compared to JOLTS because small and mid-sized establishments post less online. The authors note that while skill demand levels remain stable after adjustment, the dataset fails to capture vacancies from smaller firms.

A new trend in South Korea features 'dopamine sites' like Dopamine Shop and FoodNeverComes that simulate the full online shopping experience without completing transactions or delivering items. These websites allow users to browse, add items to carts, and track deliveries, but no money changes hands and no packages arrive.

Nils Pratley argues that Business Secretary Jonathan Reynolds correctly refused to use public funds to support Jaguar Land Rover's planned 4,000 job cuts. The author contends the company's cost-cutting measures are a competitive strategy rather than an existential crisis requiring state financial assistance, noting the firm plans to save £1.7bn annually while maintaining investment of £18bn over five years.

John Crace writes that John Healey's debut as chancellor was a disappointing performance characterized by silence and a lack of conviction. The author notes Healey arrived 15 minutes late and appeared nervous, struggling to project the strength required for the role. Crace argues that Healey's speech offered little new information, merely repeating fiscal discipline and manifesto promises already established by Rachel Reeves. The columnist suggests Healey is better suited for crisis announcements than delivering optimistic messages, which die on his lips. Furthermore, Crace observes that the wider government seemed silenced during the event, with the home secretary notably absent. Ultimately, the article portrays Healey as ill-equipped for the job, leaving the public and markets in a state of uncertainty.

Next has won an appeal against a 2024 equal pay ruling, allowing the retailer to avoid paying over £30m in back pay to warehouse staff. The Employment Appeal Tribunal accepted Next's argument that higher recruitment and retention pressures justified paying warehouse operatives more than shop floor workers for jobs of equal value. While the tribunal upheld findings on night-time and overtime premiums, Next described the decision as a landmark victory for market forces in employment.

The Eiffel Tower was closed after members of a Hindu group were removed from the site, sparking a public row. The closure occurred as part of the ongoing dispute over the group's presence at the landmark.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov called for Iran to be included in a Gulf security system, describing it as a practical step toward regional stability. Speaking at Moscow State Institute of International Relations, Lavrov noted that Iran's participation would facilitate confidence-building measures. He referenced the Mecca Agreement as a potential framework and stated Russia would not seek a leading role in the process.

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband is set to announce a broad reset of UK relations with Israel, including a ban on trade in goods and services from illegal settlements. This intervention, expected to face criticism from the US and Israel, represents a shift from traditional rhetorical support to active steps against settlement expansion. Miliband will also reassert the call for a two-state solution and highlight humanitarian injustices in Gaza, though the package excludes sanctions on aid restrictions or a genocide description. Polling indicates strong public support for the trade ban, with 46% of UK adults favouring it. The measures align with a 2024 International Court of Justice advisory opinion and may require primary legislation. The UK officially regards all Israeli civilian settlements built on territories captured in 1967 as illegal under international law.

As young Australians increasingly rely on family funds for housing and living expenses, experts warn of significant legal risks associated with informal lending. Youth sociologist Julia Cook and her team found that many parents and children remain unclear whether money is a gift or loan, often failing to document the arrangement. Family lawyer Gabriella Pomare notes that disputes typically arise only after relationship changes, leaving courts without evidence. Relationships NSW CEO Elizabeth Shaw emphasizes the importance of upfront discussions regarding risks and suggests families consider independent legal advice. Both experts recommend creating clear agreements detailing repayment terms, interest, and scenarios like separation or death to protect family dynamics and financial interests.

The U.K. government and ministers condemned protests in Portsmouth where hundreds blocked buses carrying migrants from a dinghy arrival. Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones described the situation as a worrying escalation and a wake-up call regarding the lack of border control. A Home Office spokesperson called the protester behavior intimidating and thuggish, while Treasury Secretary Emma Reynolds stated it crossed a line. Commissioner Jones noted that 140 migrants arrived from France and warned of significant issues if traffickers shift routes to Portsmouth.

Israel's Defence Minister Israel Katz announced on Monday that the military is prepared to open a full-scale war against the Palestinian Authority if it initiates or is certain of an imminent terror attack similar to Hamas's October 7 assault. The statement, issued from Katz's office, specifies that such a campaign would target the PA's senior leadership, security mechanisms, and terror infrastructure in the West Bank. This warning follows a stabbing attack in the northern West Bank that wounded an Israeli settler, which the military responded to by killing the assailant. Palestinian National Council President Rawhi Fattouh denounced the threat as evidence of an aggressive Israeli government seeking to fuel conflict rather than peace. While the PA maintains its security forces work to curb militancy, violence in the occupied territory has surged since the Gaza war began, with at least 1,106 Palestinians killed by Israeli forces or settlers since October 2023.

Chinese qualifier Zheng Qinwen produced a spectacular fight back to upset six-times major winner Iga Swiatek 7-5, 6-3 in the U.S. Open on Monday. Zheng recovered from 0-5 down in the opening set to reach the quarter-finals, saving three set points in the deciding set. She stated she found her rhythm point by point despite starting poorly. Zheng will next play either Naomi Osaka or Elena Rybakina.

Thousands gathered in Belgrade on Monday for the funeral of Ratko Mladic, a former Bosnian Serb general convicted of genocide and war crimes. The large turnout, featuring armed soldiers and chanting crowds, drew sharp criticism from the EU and Bosnia, which protested the event's handling and blocked television signals. While Serbian officials attended, the funeral reopened old wounds regarding the 1990s Yugoslav conflicts.

A 1912 industrial building in Tashkent has been restored as the Centre for Contemporary Arts Tashkent while preserving its original character. Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev toured the facility ahead of its public opening and reviewed plans for future exhibitions and research programs. The centre features a specialist research library and will host an inaugural exhibition including a Guggenheim Museum installation.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz vowed to stay in office following a decisive victory for the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) in the Saxony-Anhalt state election. Merz, appearing contrite, stated the result shook his Christian Democratic Union (CDU) to its foundations, yet he maintained his commitment to continuing reform paths for the sake of future generations. While the AfD secured nearly 44% of the vote, it fell short of an absolute majority and must now seek coalition partners to form a government. Merz emphasized that Germany's institutions remain resilient and that the country would not budge on its stance regarding Ukraine or Russian interference. Despite internal calls for his replacement, Merz insisted giving up is not an option, even as the AfD prepares for further regional elections later this month.

King Charles III has issued a letter clarifying that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are private citizens following their return to the UK. The document, shared by the Lord Chamberlain, confirms they will not use royal titles or undertake representative duties. It notes their charitable work is a personal matter, while security funding remains uncertain as the couple settles in the Cotswolds.

Eiffel Tower workers went on strike on Monday after protesting the exclusion of female staff during a visit by a Hindu delegation. The CGT trade union condemned instructions that rendered female employees invisible based on their gender. The Eiffel Tower operator stated the delegation requested limiting interactions with women, noting these conditions should not have been accepted. Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire expressed support for the strike, calling the exclusion unacceptable.

U.S. authorities restricted their personnel travel to Nogales, Sonora, to essential movements during daylight hours due to an undisclosed threat. The U.S. Consulate General in Nogales issued the alert without revealing specific details. Sonora authorities stated they have no information indicating a specific risk to the public but will maintain preventive security operations. Republican Congressman Andy Biggs urged Americans in the area to heed government guidance. The warning does not change Sonora's existing Level 3 travel advisory status.

The Arab League convened in Cairo to address escalating regional tensions, focusing on maritime security in the Gulf and Israeli military operations in Lebanon. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty stressed the importance of keeping shipping routes open, while the League condemned recent Israeli strikes that killed at least 12 people. Secretary General Nabil Fahmy noted that Arab states remain open to balanced relations with Iran, provided such ties respect national sovereignty and territorial integrity. Additionally, an Arab ministerial committee called for stronger action to halt Israeli violations in occupied Jerusalem and protect holy sites.

Germany requested the International Court of Justice to dismiss a legal challenge filed by Nicaragua regarding arms exports to Israel. Nicaragua accuses Berlin of aiding genocide in Gaza, whereas Germany argues the case lacks jurisdiction and proper procedural steps were not followed. The German government noted that its weapons export policies remain strictly regulated. While an initial bid for an emergency injunction failed in 2024, Germany suspended exports briefly in 2025 before resuming them following a truce. A decision on dismissing the case is tentatively expected later this year, potentially contingent on separate proceedings concerning Israel's actions in Gaza.

The article discusses a potentially controversial American League postseason bracket where the Houston Astros and Cleveland Guardians would face each other in the opening round. This matchup occurs because division champions are seeded above teams with better records. Additionally, the Chicago Cubs led the majors with 201 home runs in August, and the Boston Red Sox finished the week with a 5-2 record.

King Charles III has reiterated that Prince Harry and his wife, Meghan, remain non-working members of the royal family following their return to the United Kingdom. A letter sent on behalf of the king by the Lord Chamberlain stated the couple will continue to refrain from using their royal titles and that any charity work will be carried out in a private capacity. The communication aims to avoid doubt regarding their status and clarify that operational security decisions remain matters for relevant police agencies.

Filmmaker Poh Si Teng has released the documentary American Doctor, which centers on three US doctors volunteering in Gaza's besieged hospitals during the Israeli offensive. The film follows Dr. Thaer Ahmad, Dr. Feroze Sidhwa, and Dr. Mark Perlmutter as they provide medical assistance while becoming targets of the Israeli army. Throughout the documentary, the protagonists struggle to gain support in the US Capitol and raise awareness among the political class. Poh Si Teng argues that full stories must be told to help Western citizens feel sufficiently involved. Producer Watermelon Pictures states that content related to Palestine has recently taken on special prominence in its streaming catalogue.

Two women Ministers and MLAs of the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam attended the Assembly on Monday wearing red-tinted saffron sarees to mark the day Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay replied to the debate on demands for grants for the Police and Fire and Rescue Services departments. After the Chief Minister completed his speech, they met him and appreciated his performance.

On September 7, 2026, a collective of Kerala High Court lawyers handed over ₹50,000 to cover a revised penalty for a modified off-road vehicle used in flood-rescue operations at Aranmula. Aranmula MLA Abin Varkey criticized the Motor Vehicles Department for penalizing the vehicle, noting that the fine was increased after the court found six additional lights and tyres projecting beyond the body.

Benchmark copper on the London Metal Exchange touched a record high of $14,533 a metric ton, surpassing its previous peak. Traders said volumes were likely muted due to a U.S. holiday, with attention focused on copper and zinc. Analyst Albert Mackenzie told Reuters that tariff uncertainty keeps prices elevated as material flows to the U.S. Meanwhile, Shanghai Futures Exchange inventories stood at 63,000 tons, down 85% since March. Zinc also gained 1.1% to $3,988 a ton, supported by tight supplies. A weaker U.S. currency provided broader support to base metals, with aluminium rising 0.7% and tin adding 0.4%. The article is based on inputs from agencies and does not represent the views of The Economic Times.

Rahul Gandhi joined the debate over Prime Minister Narendra Modi's use of the term 'Dimagi Naxal,' accusing the leader of using insulting labels to silence critics. The opposition leader utilized the Delhi building collapse incident to highlight a lack of government accountability. Senior Congress leader P Chidambaram and Aam Aadmi Party convenor Arvind Kejriwal responded by proudly accepting the label, with Kejriwal suggesting historical figures like Bhagat Singh would also be termed 'dimagi naxals.' Union Minister Kiren Rijiju defended the Prime Minister, stating the remark targeted those rejecting the Indian Constitution rather than political opponents. Later, PM Modi reiterated his stance at a Delhi University event, calling the label a 'homoeopathic pill' and introducing the new term 'naraz fufa' for those who question national projects. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticized the Prime Minister's modus operandi of assigning new adjectives to opposition figures annually.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has extended the deadline for existing angel funds to comply with the accredited investor mandate to March 31, 2027. The regulator stated this decision followed representations from the Alternative Investment Fund industry seeking additional time. Funds registered on or before September 10, 2025, must implement the mandate by the new date, whereas funds registered after that date must comply immediately. During the transition period, these funds cannot offer opportunities to more than 200 non-accredited investors.

John Ternus assumes Apple CEO duties just before the September 9 event, where he must address AI delays and rising memory costs. Competitors Huawei and Xiaomi recently launched foldable phones, while Apple prepares to debut the iPhone 18 Pro series and iOS 27. The company faces pressure from soaring memory prices and potential price hikes for the new iPhone lineup. Additionally, Apple adjusted its EU commission structure to ease developer restrictions, though this may impact App Store revenues.

The Reserve Bank of India conducted two variable rate reverse repo auctions on September 7, 2026, absorbing over ₹6 lakh crore from the banking system. The initial 30-day auction received a tepid response with bids of ₹2.59 lakh crore, whereas the subsequent overnight auction attracted ₹3,53,390 crore. These operations aim to manage surplus liquidity estimated at ₹11.16 lakh crore, driven largely by foreign currency inflows through special deposit schemes.

Canada is set to impose tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on hundreds of US products starting Tuesday, escalating its trade dispute with the Trump administration. Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada remains ready to resume negotiations for a durable agreement while protecting key industries. The measures target steel, consumer goods, and other sectors, aiming to pressure Washington into returning to the negotiating table. Previous talks collapsed after President Trump criticized the Canadian dollar and threatened further retaliatory actions.

The adverse impact of El Niño is widely felt across the Rayalaseema region, where rain deficits have caused severe losses for groundnut, red gram, and cotton farmers. In Anantapur and surrounding districts, over 10 lakh hectares of groundnut withered, while similar acreage of red gram and cotton faced the same fate. Rekulakunta weather station scientist K Narayana Swamy noted that red gram fields are being cleared as hopes are lost. Major agricultural concerns include rainfall deficiency, prolonged dry spells, and high temperatures, which have caused reduced vegetative growth, flower shedding, and poor boll setting in cotton. Farmers in areas with black cotton soil are digging out saplings to prevent further soil damage. The conditions are particularly serious for rain-fed crops, leading to significant yield reductions and economic hardship for the farming community.

Telangana officials informed the Central Water Commission that Andhra Pradesh had already drawn 30 tmc ft of its allowed 34 tmc ft allocation from Pothireddypadu. During a meeting in New Delhi, Telangana stated that Andhra Pradesh must stop its overdrawal immediately to allow water to reach Nagarjunasagar for Hyderabad's drinking water needs amid El Nino impacts. Telangana also clarified that its decisions regarding the Srisailam left bank power house would prioritize the state's drinking water and power requirements.

Punjab Industry Minister Aman Arora declared a proposed employee strike illegal on Monday, citing that the dearness allowance dispute is sub-judice before the Supreme Court. The minister warned of action against unauthorized absentees and appealed to the 85,000 affected employees to resolve demands through dialogue rather than disrupting public services. The government noted it has already addressed DA demands for post-July 2020 recruits by raising the rate from 42 to 60 per cent.

The death toll in Madhya Pradesh's Sagar hooch tragedy rose to 13 on Monday, with 96 people undergoing treatment at four hospitals, including seven in critical condition, officials said. Sagar Collector Pratibha Pal stated that post-mortems indicated suspected poisoning and that viscera were sent for testing. Police arrested 14 of 30 accused and suspended five officials while investigating a suspected link to a gang in Lalitpur. A magisterial inquiry has been ordered to determine the causes and identify responsible parties. Deputy Chief Minister Jagdish Devda visited the area, confirming the official death toll of 13 and promising strict action against negligent officials, while Congress leader Jitu Patwari claimed the number was higher.

The Tamil Nadu State government introduced a Bill in the Assembly on Monday to amend the Tamil Nadu Panchayats Act 1994. This legislation aims to extend the tenure of Special Officers for village panchayats and other local bodies in 28 districts until October 19, 2026. The move follows previous extensions and addresses the inability to hold elections due to incomplete delimitation processes in those areas.

A special CBI court in Dehradun acquitted Acharya Balkrishna on Monday of all charges in a 15-year-old case involving alleged forged documents for a passport. The prosecution had alleged that educational certificates linked to a Sanskrit college in Khurja were used to obtain an Indian passport. Following the ruling, Balkrishna said the verdict proved the truth after a mentally exhausting legal battle, though he described enduring false allegations and insults during the proceedings.

Gasoline prices reached a record $4.15 per gallon on Labor Day, according to AAA, driven by ongoing supply disruptions linked to the Iran war. The conflict has significantly increased crude oil benchmarks and restricted flow through the Strait of Hormuz, while damaged refineries in the Middle East and Russia further constrained gasoline availability. U.S. gasoline inventories remain 6% below average, exacerbating the shortage. While the EPA moved the switch to cheaper winter-grade gasoline forward to September 1 to boost supply, analysts caution that high crude prices could keep pump costs elevated. Diesel prices also hit a record $5.90 per gallon. The situation remains dependent on whether diplomatic efforts resolve the conflict and restore normal shipping routes.

Bloomberg reported that Iran and Oman are finalizing an agreement to document a temporary safe shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz with the International Maritime Organization. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei stated negotiations made very good progress. The deal aims to reduce tanker risks and lower oil prices, though the US seeks to restore the strait to its pre-war status as a freely accessible waterway. Macquarie analysts noted current traffic is around 7 million barrels per day compared to 20 million before the war. The conflict has driven up energy prices and pressures the US administration to end the dispute ahead of midterm elections.

Lucknow topped the Swachh Vayu Survey-2026, securing the first national position in the category of cities with a population exceeding 10 lakh with 198 points. The Central Pollution Control Board and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change conducted the survey, in which 16 Uttar Pradesh cities achieved national recognition across different population brackets. Lucknow Mayor Sushma Kharkwal credited Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for the success, noting integrated efforts in electric transport, waste management, and green cover. Urban Development and Energy Minister Arvind Kumar Sharma stated that the state is transforming rapidly under Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's guidance. The Municipal Corporation of Lucknow utilizes approximately 1,100 electric vehicles for waste collection and operates 140 electric buses to reduce pollution. Additionally, 97 electric mechanized sweeping machines and 559.85 kilometers of paved roads help control dust. Scientific waste processing capacity stands at 2,550 TPD, with a focus on preventing open waste burning. The state received cash awards totaling Rs 1.5 crore for Lucknow and Rs 25 lakh for Firozabad. Ward-level awards were also distributed to specific urban areas for outstanding performance in local clean air management.

The Economic Offences Wing has taken over an investigation into an alleged Rs 17.88 crore fraud at Sumitra Cooperative Credit Society Limited in Mumbai. Chartered accountant Santosh Gangaram Shigwan filed the complaint after detecting irregularities during the society's 2023-24 statutory audit. The case, registered at D.B. Marg Police Station, involves accusations of forged loan accounts, missing mandatory documents, and misappropriation of funds by former office-bearers and employees. The Economic Offences Wing is now conducting a further probe into the alleged financial loss and the roles of the accused.

While GTA 6 is confirmed for November 19, 2026 on consoles, speculation suggests a PC version might launch earlier than historical precedents. VGC editor-in-chief Andy Robinson noted industry discussion about a potential forward shift, though he provided no specific date. Former employees reportedly hinted at a February 2027 target, yet Rockstar has not officially commented. Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick previously explained the company prioritizes console audiences first. Consequently, all specific PC dates remain unconfirmed guesses rather than facts.

Jaguar Land Rover announced plans to cut approximately 4,000 global roles over the next two years as part of its strategic transformation programme. Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles Limited stated the reductions, achieved through voluntary means where possible, aim to save £1.7 billion to support long-term growth. CEO PB Balaji emphasized the move will simplify the organization while committing to invest between £15-18 billion in electrification and digital technologies over the next five years.

A 21-year-old drug addict named Tilak Raj allegedly trespassed into Chief Minister Omar Abdullah's residence in Srinagar shortly after being released by police. Police stated the youth fled after being handed to his father, noting he had prior theft charges and was intoxicated when caught. The incident has raised security concerns regarding the protection of the Chief Minister and his father, Dr Farooq Abdullah, following previous security lapses and an attempted assassination.

A BBC investigation has released previously unseen videos showing Omar al-Bayoumi, a Saudi national investigated after the September 11 attacks, embracing al-Qaida leader Anwar al-Awlaki. The footage contradicts al-Bayoumi's denial of the meeting. The report claims the FBI failed to pursue evidence linking him to the attacks, including a diagram connecting him to the plot that British police seized but US agents did not fully utilize.

Adani Power, the country's largest private-sector thermal power generator, reported an improved Environmental, Social, and Governance score of 66 for FY26, according to NSE Sustainability. The company highlighted its focus on sustainable growth and responsible operations. Additionally, Adani Power stated that the Committee of Creditors for GVK Energy Limited approved its resolution plan under the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process, pending further regulatory approvals.

Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Saurav Das slammed the Delhi government over the Satya Niketan building collapse, alleging a PG mafia nexus functions with political patronage. He stated that youth are demanding answers after being left to live in unsafe conditions. Meanwhile, Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu chaired a high-level review meeting emphasizing strict enforcement against unsafe buildings and directed officials to investigate the owner's political associations. Delhi Police have arrested three family members connected to the property.

The article explains that mosquito bites cause varied reactions due to how saliva interacts with human immune systems. When a mosquito bites, its saliva contains proteins that trigger histamine release and alter local immune environments, often nudging the body toward allergy-type responses. A genetic study of over 84,000 people confirmed that reactions vary significantly based on exposure history and genetics, with children and those encountering unfamiliar species reacting more strongly. Some individuals develop Skeeter syndrome, an exaggerated response involving severe swelling. Researchers note these immune changes may also facilitate the spread of viruses like dengue and Zika. Additionally, malaria parasites may alter human odors to attract mosquitoes. Scientists are now exploring vaccines that target mosquito saliva itself to mitigate both allergic reactions and disease transmission.

TechCrunch has released a living glossary to clarify the fast-moving vocabulary of the artificial intelligence sector. The article explains that terms like LLMs, RAG, and RLHF are now joined by newer concepts such as opaque recurrence, a reasoning technique in OpenAI's Astra model that safety researchers find concerning. The piece defines artificial general intelligence (AGI) as systems that outperform humans in most economically valuable work, though definitions vary between OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and other experts. It further details AI agents, which autonomously perform tasks like coding or booking tickets, and distinguishes them from basic chatbots. The text clarifies technical processes including chain-of-thought reasoning, which breaks problems into steps to improve accuracy, and distillation, a method for creating smaller models from larger ones. Additional entries cover fine-tuning, generative adversarial networks (GANs), hallucinations, and inference. The article also notes the industry-wide shortage of RAM chips, termed RAMageddon, and explains how tokenization drives enterprise costs. By providing plain-English definitions, the publication aims to help investors, builders, and readers keep pace with the field's evolution.
The author created an animated transition between Mercator and Equal Earth map projections using GPT-6 Astra and D3 after the Equal Earth projection was recently voted on at the UN.

Tesla unveiled its new Cybercab autonomous robotaxi in Austin, Texas, on September 3, yet the event generated more questions than answers regarding fleet adoption and individual ownership. A contact form solicited interest from other robotaxi fleets, but the vehicle's incompatibility with Level 2 home charging eliminates the gig-economy model for private owners. Industry observers noted that recent history, including struggles by Hertz and Mistergreen, suggests a partnership with Tesla is not a guaranteed profit. Furthermore, NBC News reporter David Ingram highlighted Tesla's detailed safety instructions for first responders, which warn of electrical risks and require contacting Tesla support. On September 4, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration opened an audit to investigate if the Cybercab meets federal safety standards. Meanwhile, Tesla stock declined, and Elon Musk faced backlash after posting a message congratulating a German far-right party.

General Motors and Ford are transforming losses from their electric vehicle expansion into a new energy storage business to meet rising demand. The automakers wrote down billions in investments due to poor EV demand but are now pivoting to battery energy storage systems for data centers and grid support. Ford launched its BESS business in late 2025, planning to invest roughly $2 billion to scale operations at its Glendale, Kentucky facility. The company aims to deploy at least 20 GWh annually by late 2027. General Motors also entered the sector, partnering with Peak Energy for sodium ion chemistry and supplying second-life batteries to Redwood Materials. Industry reports indicate record-high energy storage capacity installations in the United States as utilities seek grid reliability.

The author of this review put the Xtracycle Hopper electric cargo bike through a long-term test with his friend's family of four. After covering 1,000 km, the family reported that the bike effectively replaced their second car for daily errands and trips to the beach. The author noted that the children enjoyed the ride more than being in a car, turning transportation into family time. The bike, priced at $2,499, featured a 750W motor and a 48V 15Ah battery. Mechanical reliability was high, with the only issue being a broken kickstand spring that the manufacturer replaced under warranty. The author concluded that for many short family trips, the e-bike offered a better experience and lower cost than owning a second car.

Kia has expanded its electric GT lineup with the launch of the EV3 GT, EV4 GT, and EV5 GT. Pablo Martinez Masip, vice president of product, marketing & customer experience at Kia Europe, stated the company is opening the GT experience to new segments. These models utilize dual-motor all-wheel-drive setups and feature exclusive design elements like neon-green brake calipers. Starting prices in Europe range from €53,990 for the EV3 GT to €59,990 for the EV5 GT. In the US, the EV3 GT is available starting at $45,890, while Kia has no plans to launch the EV4 GT or EV5 GT there. Kia said it will reveal UK prices and specs shortly, noting the EV4 GT Fastback will not be available in that market.

OpenAI plans to display sponsored ads below answers in the ChatGPT free version to create a new revenue stream, though not every response will include an ad. According to OpenAI, advertisers will not be able to read users' personal chats, but privacy concerns remain as the company explores this monetization method.

Business Today reports that Apple CEO Tim Cook has officially stepped down after a 15-year tenure, transitioning to Executive Chairman while John Ternus takes over. The article also notes Dyson's entry into the wellness sector with a new electric toothbrush equipped with a microscopic CameraJet technology.

The authors report that their new PLRD estimator shows lower estimation error than existing methods in simulation studies calibrated to twelve high-profile applications. They also provide large-sample guarantees and describe a general template for evaluating new econometric methods.

Chancellor John Healey addressed the BBC and the public regarding the UK's economic outlook, emphasizing a need for confidence despite rising borrowing costs. Healey stated that doubling down on growth generation is a central priority before the Budget on 28 October. He acknowledged the challenge of historic high borrowing costs and the recent loss of 4,000 jobs at Jaguar Land Rover. While Healey refused to comment on specific tax decisions, he reiterated the government's commitment to controlling public spending. He also announced a £150m fund to support innovative firms in the north of England. Opposition figures criticized Healey for failing to end uncertainty about potential tax rises.

Chancellor John Healey addressed the 4,000 job losses at Jaguar Land Rover, framing them as evidence of global turbulence requiring UK resilience. Healey emphasized that stressing fiscal discipline should build confidence rather than sap it amid fears of tax hikes. While acknowledging high borrowing costs, Healey declined to comment on potential tax rises before the October 28 Budget. He highlighted the UK's status as the third most innovative country and outlined plans for public finance institutions to invest strategically in technology startups. The Chancellor noted that long-term growth will determine whether borrowing rules are met, suggesting a potential prioritization of economic expansion over strict budget balancing.

According to the French agriculture ministry, severe drought and record-breaking heatwaves are expected to result in a 30-year low for the country's wine harvest. Agreste estimates production will fall to just under 34m hectolitres, representing a 17% drop from the 2021-2025 average, with Champagne and Burgundy regions hit hardest. However, industry representatives argue it is too early to confirm such drastic figures as harvests continue. The ministry noted that definitive results will not be available until official declarations are made later this year, though the sector faces additional challenges from wildfire smoke and declining international demand.

The National Transportation Safety Board described the scene of a Sunday crash involving an Amazon cargo plane as one of "utter devastation." NTSB Chair Jennifer Homendy told reporters that the Boeing 737-300, operated by contractor 21 Air, overshot the runway by roughly 1,300 feet, killing five people in two vehicles. The plane struck a Ford van and a Toyota Corolla SUV after bursting through an airport fence. Officials have recovered flight recorders and are interviewing potential survivors. The NTSB is investigating whether an Engineered Material Arresting System, which Miami International Airport reportedly lacks, would have prevented more destruction. The agency expects to release more information on Tuesday.

President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social that Bombardier aircraft are not good enough and called for an end to their sales in the United States. The article states that the president lacks authority to bar a foreign manufacturer's aircraft from being sold in the US, as certification is the responsibility of the Federal Aviation Administration. Several claims in Trump's post are identified as false, including assertions that Canada blocked Gulfstream certification and that the US loses $60 to $100 billion annually in trade deficits with Canada. The US Trade Representative's office reports a 2025 goods deficit of $48.3 billion. Canada has promised to retaliate dollar-for-dollar against the US tariffs that took effect last month.

Israel launched a wave of airstrikes across southern Lebanon, killing 13 people, including women and children, Lebanon's health ministry said on Monday. This marks an escalation after weeks of relative calm. Israel said it would continue targeting Iran-backed Hezbollah over alleged ceasefire violations. Hezbollah has not commented on the strikes. One overnight strike hit a building in Kfar Rumman, killing 11 people, while another attack in the same town killed a rescuer. A later strike on Rihan killed one person, and a strike on Nabatieh wounded nine. The Israeli military vowed to continue operations to remove threats while remaining committed to the ceasefire agreement. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun urged Washington and the international community to help stop Israeli attacks.

The UN estimates 650 million women and girls alive today were married before age 18. The organization passed a resolution ahead of the General Assembly to bring awareness and push countries to act to end child marriage.

Ian Campbell, founder of Barambah Organics, and his daughter Hannah Campbell died when their light plane crashed in Stockleigh, Queensland, on Monday. Emergency services found the two occupants from Ascot dead at the scene after the aircraft left Archerfield Airport around 10:57am. The crash caused a grass fire, prompting eight Queensland Fire Department crews to respond. Queensland Police and the Australian Transport Safety Bureau are investigating the incident, with investigators examining wreckage and sending components to Canberra for analysis.

State media reported that Iran introduced higher gasoline prices for heavy consumers on Tuesday, marking the second hike since December. The government cited the current situation without mentioning the war, noting the extra revenue will support households. Keramat Veis Karami, CEO of the state oil distribution company, told IRNA the new rate affects 15% of consumers. Experts warn the move could worsen inflation in a country already facing an annual rate of about 67%.

Phillies left-handed pitcher Jesús Luzardo recorded his first career shutout, leading his team to a 1-0 victory over the Atlanta Braves in the fastest nine-inning game of the season. Luzardo, who had never pitched into the ninth inning in his first 149 starts, struck out 12 batters and retired the final two hitters to complete the 109-pitch effort. Manager Don Mattingly expressed confidence in Luzardo's recent performance, highlighting a 1.93 ERA over his last 21 starts. Kyle Schwarber provided the winning run with his 43rd home run of the season. The Phillies cut the NL East lead to four games after splitting the four-game series with the Braves.

US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff reported substantive progress on scheduling trilateral peace talks with Russia and Ukraine following weekend meetings. Although Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met separately with US envoys, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated it is too early to confirm specific details for future negotiations. Meanwhile, Zelenskyy warned that fighting is likely to continue into the winter despite these diplomatic efforts.

North Korea condemned a five-day Freedom Edge military exercise involving the US, South Korea, and Japan, warning of serious consequences. The Defense Ministry statement, carried by the Korean Central News Agency, accused Washington of military provocations. Defense Minister Kim Song Ji vowed that Pyongyang would maintain its toughest stance against US hostility despite the drills.

The World Health Organization is coordinating and funding the expansion of the Lita treatment centre in Ituri province to add 42 beds and improve health facilities. The Congolese National Institute of Public Health reported that the current outbreak has caused 3,007 deaths and infected 6,186 people. The virus, caused by the Bundibugyo strain, has spread to six provinces where insecurity is widespread. While approved vaccines target the Zaire strain, WHO experts are testing the Ervebo vaccine against Bundibugyo, with initial data suggesting it could offer some protection.

Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez launched the first national portal for Spain's public housing stock, managed by the State Housing and Land Agency CASA 47. The platform initially offers 800 homes, with plans to add 1,500 more soon, featuring rents linked to local economic conditions and capped at 30% of a tenant's income. Sánchez defended state intervention in the market, citing a broken housing sector, and promised that these homes would remain protected in the public stock forever. Housing Minister Isabel Rodríguez highlighted the need for a transparent allocation process to avoid favoritism and noted the recovery of over 42,000 homes from Sareb assets to expand availability.

Iran announced Monday that it is finalizing an agreement with Oman to create a temporary, safe route through the Strait of Hormuz. Foreign ministry spokesperson Esmail Baghaei said the agreement will probably be registered with the International Maritime Organization over the coming days. This development occurs as Tehran attempts to close the strait following recent attacks by the U.S. and Israel, while Western nations consider referring Iran to the U.N. Security Council for nuclear noncompliance.

The European Union sought to reassure Greenland on Monday by promising 200 million euros in investment to address climate change and improve infrastructure. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen stated that Greenland's future lies with its people and Denmark, emphasizing territorial integrity. This visit occurred as Denmark and European allies resisted US President Donald Trump's threats to seize the island, with Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen expressing deep gratitude for unfailing EU support during these challenging times.

Israeli Defence Minister Israel Katz threatened a full-scale war against the Palestinian Authority if it prepares an attack similar to the October 7 Hamas assault. The warning, issued on September 7, 2026, targets senior leadership and terror infrastructure in the West Bank. Palestinian officials denounced the statement as an attempt to fuel conflict during the Israeli election season, noting the Authority does not officially participate in militant activity. Recent violence in the occupied territory has surged since the Gaza war began.

Morocco has significantly strengthened its international standing through diplomatic support from major powers and expanded military alliances. Bernabé López García notes that Donald Trump's 2020 recognition of Moroccan sovereignty over Western Sahara marked a turning point, allowing Rabat to bypass the UN and secure backing from permanent Security Council members. Consequently, Morocco has become the continent's largest arms importer, surpassing Algeria according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. The United States now supplies 60% of Morocco's arms, while France's share has dropped to 10%. Lahcen Haddad explains that US recognition also normalized Morocco-Israel relations, leading to agreements on air defense and the construction of spy satellites. While Morocco has revived sovereignty claims over the Spanish exclaves of Ceuta and Melilla, experts like Irene Fernández Molina argue this is a political move to influence the September 23 legislative elections rather than a fundamental strategic shift. The country continues to pursue its Western Sahara autonomy plan, which recently received a UN Security Council resolution with abstentions from Russia and China.

US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff reported on Monday that substantive progress has been made in US efforts to end the Russia-Ukraine war. Speaking after weekend meetings in Moscow and Kyiv, Witkoff highlighted movement toward scheduling additional trilateral talks between Washington, Moscow, and Kyiv. He noted that President Donald Trump is working hard to stop the killing and pursue a lasting peace. The US delegation met with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, joined by national security advisers from Britain, Germany, and France in Kyiv. Witkoff expressed hope to revive these trilateral discussions following the three-day halt in attacks agreed upon by Russia and Ukraine.

Maharashtra Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde suspended Shiv Sena leader Rahul Gharat following his arrest for allegedly assaulting hospital staff. Police Inspector Kishor Mahanubhav explained that the altercation occurred after party members refused to pay the remaining ₹9,000 of a ₹19,000 medical bill for injured individuals. Shinde warned that such incidents would not be tolerated, while police continue investigating the attack involving 17 accused persons.

Federal investigators are examining why an Amazon cargo jet overran the runway at Miami International Airport, killing at least five people. The National Transportation Safety Board has sent a team to determine if the Boeing 767 touched down too late to stop safely. The aircraft, operated by 21 Air, plowed across a road used by warehouse workers after arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico. Five people died, while three were critically injured and two others hospitalized. Aviation experts noted the plane appeared to float above the runway for an extended period. The crash halted flights at the busy hub, causing 160 cancellations and over 300 delays on Sunday. Amazon said in a statement, "We're heartbroken to learn that five people lost their lives in today's incident at Miami International Airport." The investigation will also look at weather conditions, braking, and the aircraft's maintenance history.

The Election Commission of India announced on Monday that by-elections for the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies in Tamil Nadu, along with the Thattanchavady seat in Puducherry, will be held on October 6. These seats became vacant after sitting members resigned or switched parties. The ruling TVK is expected to nominate Maragatham Kumaravel and P Sathyabhama, while the AIADMK and NR Congress will field candidates in the Tamil Nadu and Puducherry contests respectively. Analysts view these polls as a potential yardstick for the performance of the Vijay-led TVK government and the NR Congress administration, though they may not impact immediate political stability. Senior leaders like C Vijayabaskar and M R Vijaybakar are waiting for their traditional constituencies to be included in future by-elections.

The US Department of Commerce announced that India has joined the United States and 24 other countries in an initiative to shape next-generation 6G networks. Union minister of state for commerce and industry Jitin Prasada met US commerce secretary Howard Lutnick to discuss the future of 6G technology at the G20 Innovation Ministerial.

South Korean gaming billionaire Kwon Hyuk-bin and his wife Lee Hwa-jin await a court verdict on their divorce, which could determine control of Smilegate Inc. The dispute centers on whether Lee, who held a 30% stake and served as CEO at the company's founding, deserves half of Kwon's 100% stake valued at up to 8 trillion won. Local media reports indicate Lee is seeking half his stake, while Smilegate stated all initial capital came from Kwon. The outcome will depend on the court's assessment of Lee's contribution and the valuation of unlisted shares.

State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha directed Mandal Parishad Development Officers and chief executive officers of zilla parishads to prepare and publish photo electoral rolls for MPTCs and ZPTCs. Punetha noted that gram panchayat rolls were already published and must be used for the new lists per AP Panchayat Raj Rules. The updated rolls will be open for inspection at relevant offices on September 11 ahead of upcoming elections.

The Bombay High Court allowed residential construction on two leased plots in Pune Cantonment, holding that the government cannot deny leaseholders their existing rights based on hypothetical future resumption concerns. A bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Ghuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad set aside orders by the Pune Cantonment Board and defence authorities that had rejected building proposals. The court ruled that a valid lease cannot be treated as ended due to future apprehensions, noting the leases remain valid until November 30, 2033. While permitting construction, the court imposed safeguards requiring petitioners to use the properties only as personal family residences and not for commercial purposes. They also agreed not to construct multi-storey high-rises or claim compensation if the military resumes the land in 2033. The court directed the Pune Cantonment Board to process and grant necessary permissions within 30 days of the petitioners submitting required formal undertakings.

Officials say Bangladesh and India plan to resume the Maitree, Mitali, and Bandhan Express trains by October following a meeting of railway authorities. Bangladesh sources reported that officials will discuss restarting the three services and launching a new train from Rajshahi to Kolkata during the upcoming two-day meeting in Dhaka. Indian high commissioner Dinesh Trivedi emphasized the importance of people-to-people relationships during the discussions.

The Aam Aadmi Party and Congress protested the BJP government on September 7 over the Satya Niketan building collapse that killed seven people. AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj demanded a list of PG owners, alleging influential BJP leaders have financial interests in the properties. Delhi Congress president Devender Yadav alleged corruption caused the collapse and called for the Municipal Commissioner's resignation. Urban Development Minister Ashish Sood responded by stating the administration is concerned about student safety and fixing the system.

King Charles III has clarified that Prince Harry and Meghan Markle are not working members of the British royal family despite their recent return to the UK. A letter issued by the Lord Chamberlain stated the couple stepped down from royal duties in 2020 and their status remains unchanged. The document noted they should not be addressed as His or Her Royal Highness and described their position as akin to private citizens with commercial and charitable interests. This clarification aims to avoid doubt regarding their role and security arrangements after moving back to Britain.

Chaos erupted at the Bhopal Municipal Corporation headquarters on Monday when employee Sunil Gaikwad allegedly attempted to set Mayor Malti Rai's official vehicle ablaze. The employee, associated with the garden section, threw burning papers onto the vehicle while the mayor was in her office. Following the incident, BMC commissioner Sanskriti Jain directed the registration of an FIR. Gaikwad, who claimed his child was expelled due to his employment status, was booked for the act. Meanwhile, the on-duty guard Ramsingh Yadav sustained burns while removing the burning material from the vehicle.

A tigress that killed four people in Amravati and Wardha districts was tranquillised and captured on Monday in Shirjagaon Kasba, an official said. The forest department launched a high-alert operation after two deaths within 24 hours, using patrols, camera traps, and thermal drones to track the animal. Officials stated the tigress had moved across multiple talukas over 20 days, attacking livestock and people. The district administration and police maintained security to prevent law and order issues. The forest department provided immediate financial assistance to the families of the deceased. Staff from various forest divisions, the Melghat tiger project, the Akola forest department, a team from Pune, the district administration, police, honorary wildlife guards, and NGOs participated in the operation, bringing the search to a close.

Former Air Force Major Heather Penney recalled preparing for a suicide mission to protect Washington, D.C., on September 11, 2001. She and her flight lead scrambled to intercept a hijacked airliner with unarmored F-16s, intending to crash into it if necessary. Penney noted that United Flight 93 crashed in Pennsylvania roughly 20 to 30 minutes before they were ordered to launch, rendering their potential sacrifice too late. She credited the passengers of Flight 93 as the true heroes who fought back against the hijackers.

A women's PG facility in Satya Niketan, located 300 metres from a collapsed building, asked all 40 occupants to vacate immediately on Monday. Students reported being told the hostel could be sealed any time and would operate only as long as supplies lasted. Many students have already left for their hometowns, leaving others stranded. The college administration has not shown interest in the situation, and students face uncertainty regarding their paid rent and security deposits while authorities announce a sealing drive against unauthorized structures.

The finance ministry announced on Monday that it has deferred the implementation of the Production Linked Incentive scheme for public sector banks. This decision follows employee representation regarding the PLI structure, with the ministry stating it will address the issues during ongoing bipartite settlement discussions. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman met with a delegation of bank employees led by the Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh to facilitate dialogue and consultation.

Union Home Minister Amit Shah announced that the Ministry of Home Affairs will take very serious action on coastal security over the next two years. Speaking at the 28th Western Zonal Council meeting in Panaji, Shah emphasized the need for the Western region to lead in implementing the New Nyaya Sanhitas to combat drugs. He also highlighted the economic strengths of the Western states, including tourism, exports, and the blue economy, while noting the increased frequency of Zonal Council meetings since 2014.

People familiar with the matter said the Indian and Chinese armies met at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point in Arunachal Pradesh to focus on maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control. The Indian delegation was headed by Lt General Girish Kalia, the commander of the Army's Dimapur-based 3 Corps. These corps commander-level talks occurred days after Special Representative talks in Beijing, where National Security Advisor Ajit Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi discussed delimitation and trans-boundary cooperation. The meeting came amid reports of aggressive military posturing by Chinese troops in the Upper Subansiri region. Both sides have taken measures to rebuild their relationship following the Galwan Valley clashes in 2020.

The Indian Embassy in China on Monday urged families of Indians missing since the August 26 flash flood to provide DNA samples to help identify them. The Indian mission made the request after Chinese authorities confirmed they could now receive such data, which families must submit in the internationally recognised CODIS format. The embassy will forward the data to Chinese authorities for comparison and will notify families if a match is confirmed. Blood samples can be collected from parents, spouses, children, or other relatives of the missing person. The disaster, triggered by an ice-rock avalanche, left 43 dead and 519 missing, including 49 Indians.

The Union Coal Ministry reported a 20% increase in coal rake loading for the power sector between September 3 and September 6, 2026. Data from the Central Electricity Authority indicated that 53 domestic coal-fired plants were operating at critical stock levels as of September 5. The ministry stated that corrective measures are in place to ease supply positions at these facilities while mining conditions recover.

The Financial Action Task Force (FATF) reports that a centuries-old underground banking system is evolving into a tech-enabled network known as 'digital hawala,' which aids money laundering and terror financing. The watchdog's latest study identifies six configurations of this system, ranging from encrypted messaging to artificial intelligence tools, noting that nearly 70% of surveyed jurisdictions have adopted these technologies. While digitization increases network resilience, the FATF emphasizes that cash remains critical at collection and exit points. The report cites a Turkish case where authorities seized over $57,000 linked to ISIL financing disguised as charity donations. FATF warns that strict enforcement and bank 'de-risking' may inadvertently push genuine users into criminal informal channels. Consequently, the organization recommends disrupting entire laundering chains rather than targeting individual transactions and clarifying the legal status of underground banking systems.

A broker initiated coverage on ESDS Software with a Buy rating and a target price of ₹1,550, valuing the company at 18x FY28E EV/EBITDA. The firm expects revenue, EBITDA, and PAT to grow at 120.9%, 72.6%, and 81.3% CAGR over FY26–FY29E, driven by core business momentum and the ramp-up of AI infrastructure revenues. Key risks include AI deal execution and customer concentration.

A Malaysia Airlines flight from Kuala Lumpur to Jeddah was diverted to Chennai International Airport on Monday following an engine-related technical issue, prompting a full emergency declaration, an official said. Malaysia Airlines MH 156 with 186 persons on board landed safely, and appropriate emergency response arrangements were activated at the airport. Separately, an Air India Express flight from Tiruchirappalli to Singapore was diverted to Chennai International Airport due to a technical issue, and a local standby was declared at the airport. The airline's engineering and technical teams are assessing the reported technical issue, and operations are normal.

Actor and BJP MP Kangana Ranaut said women's character is always used against them to destroy them. Speaking after chairing a meeting in Kullu, she backed Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay's warning against personal attacks on women. Ranaut noted that society must look within to understand how women are treated, citing examples of successful women being targeted globally and in Tamil Nadu.

Mistral today announced it raised 3 billion euros in a Series D funding round at a post-money valuation of more than 21 billion euros, the largest equity fundraising round ever completed by a European technology company. Samsung Electronics led the round, joined by co-leads Scaleup Europe Fund and existing investor PSG Equity. The capital will expand Mistral's frontier research and infrastructure to support its sovereign, open-weight AI models across 20 countries. New investors include Advent, BlackRock funds, and the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, while existing backers such as ASML, NVIDIA, and Salesforce Ventures participated. The company aims to provide a full-stack AI solution that maintains data control and independence for enterprises and governments.

Instagram creators say they have lost thousands of pounds after their accounts were suspended due to fake copyright claims filed by extortioners. One user with 1.5 million followers told the BBC he paid a scammer $50 to retrieve his account, noting that Meta's appeal process could take weeks. A Meta spokesperson stated that the company has restored affected content and added protections, though some creators argue the platform is poor at identifying spurious cases. The BBC spoke to three individuals who file these strikes, two of whom denied profiting while one admitted keeping the money. Experts attribute the recent increase in these scams to AI automation, making it easier to deploy attacks at scale against platforms with billions of users.

The PyTorch Foundation announced that Cambricon has joined as a Platinum member, granting the company a seat on the Governing Board. Elton Gong, Vice President of Software Engineering at Cambricon, explained that the move supports their goal of tight software-hardware co-optimization and a thriving open ecosystem. Mark Collier, Executive Director of the PyTorch Foundation, highlighted Cambricon's sustained upstream contributions to PyTorch and its work enabling vLLM on Cambricon hardware as key factors in strengthening the shared mission. Jin Wang, Senior Director of AI Frameworks and Infrastructure at Cambricon, will lead the company's efforts on the board, while Jing Zhu joins the Technical Advisory Council. As a Platinum member, Cambricon will deepen collaboration in areas such as compile infrastructure and device-agnostic support.

Bloomberg reported that Malaysia is considering using Huawei chips to power its sovereign AI efforts, marking a potential first instance of a foreign government choosing Chinese accelerators over American ones. Huawei's steep discounts offer cheaper compute amid a global memory shortage that could persist through 2030, even as Washington warns that using Chinese chips could violate export restrictions. Beijing's inroads into Malaysia, which already hosts US data centers, boost its efforts to become a global AI supplier of choice, as the West tightens China's access to advanced chips.

Bloomberg reported that Reliance Industries may issue local currency bonds worth 12,500 crore in the coming week, marking the year's largest domestic deal for a listed company. The 5-year notes carry a 7.47% coupon, with Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and YES Bank acting as arrangers.

OpenAI has released an update for ChatGPT Work enabling the AI to mimic a user's personal writing style. The company stated the feature analyzes frequently used words, capitalization habits, and specific phrases to generate drafts that sound like the user. OpenAI shared an X post announcing the update, noting it can replicate favorite phrases, sign-offs, and capitalization quirks to create text resembling the user's normal writing.

French artificial intelligence company Mistral announced it raised €3 billion at a valuation of approximately €21 billion ($24 billion), the largest equity funding round for a privately owned European technology firm. The round was led by PSG Equity, with new investments from Samsung Electronics and the Scaleup Europe Fund. Chief financial officer Johan Bergqvist stated the capital will power model development and frontier research to compete with larger U.S. rivals like Anthropic and OpenAI. Mistral, which serves over 125 customers with open models, projects $1 billion in annual recurring revenue by year-end. While an initial public offering remains an option, Bergqvist noted there are no ongoing discussions regarding a listing. The company also highlighted its technological sovereignty goals and expanding client base in Asia and North America, though Microsoft did not participate in this specific funding round.

Canada has escalated its trade dispute with the United States by imposing tariffs on roughly $20 billion of American goods.
