Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the measures, which take effect Tuesday, as a direct response to recent US actions. The Royal Bank of Canada's research arm noted that while overall US growth might remain unaffected, specific businesses could suffer significantly. Beyond tariffs, several Canadian provinces have restricted US alcohol sales, and Trump has threatened further penalties, including banning Bombardier aircraft sales. Political scientists observe that these aggressive tactics have rallied Canadian public support for Carney rather than forcing concessions. Although the US economy is significantly larger, experts point to American vulnerabilities in energy and agriculture as potential leverage points for Canada.

Canada's retaliatory tariffs on a range of US goods came into effect on Tuesday, with no sign of a trade deal on the horizon. The counter-tariffs will apply to nearly C$28bn worth of American products, ranging from steel to furniture, and will be as high as 50%. Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that Canada is still in search of a deal with the US that is "durable" and in the best interests of both countries. Meanwhile, US trade representative Jamieson Greer said the ball is in Canada's court after talks collapsed in late August. Economists warn that the latest counter-tariffs will raise prices for consumers on everyday goods like clothing, food, and furniture. The Canadian Chamber of Commerce has urged the government to take a surgical approach to retaliation, noting that businesses are preparing for this trade dispute to last.

Canada's retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on $20bn of US imports took effect Tuesday morning, targeting sectors like steel and dairy. The Canadian government stated these measures respond to a US decision to impose a 50% tariff on Canadian goods, escalating diplomatic tensions between the two nations. Prime Minister Mark Carney criticized US negotiators for introducing restrictions late in talks and making unacceptable threats regarding French language protections. Meanwhile, President Donald Trump threatened to block sales of Bombardier Aviation in the US unless the company moves manufacturing there. Polls indicate low approval for the tariffs in both countries, though analysts warn Canadian support for Carney could fade as the trade war consequences sink in.

Wistron shares dropped more than 6% on Tuesday after the Nvidia supplier priced a $1.47B global depositary receipt offering to finance raw material purchases. The company said Monday that it priced 25 million global depositary receipts.

Canada's retaliatory tariffs on $27.6 billion of US goods will take effect after midnight Tuesday, as prospects for averting a trade war appear dim. The White House has vowed to respond with fresh measures against Ottawa, while President Donald Trump threatened to bar sales from a Montreal plane manufacturer. No negotiations are currently scheduled, though a Financial Times columnist argued the dispute is part of an ongoing negotiation rather than an irrevocable break.

The authors report that a year of observed pollution exposure reduces learning by 0.04-0.06 standard deviations, or 14-19% of typical annual score growth, based on longitudinal PSAT data on nearly 10 million U.S. high school students.

Pietro Tebaldi, Andrea Scalenghe, and Joseph Orsini use a proprietary dataset of pre-ACA insurance applications to document the Affordable Care Act's heterogeneous effects. The authors report that benefits were concentrated among low-income, high-risk, or over-50 individuals.

Global oil prices are approaching $100 a barrel as conflict in the Middle East disrupts supply. Brent crude surpassed $98 per barrel after Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis attacked Saudi energy facilities, halting operations and injuring more than 70 people. In response to US economic pressure, Iran's Supreme National Security Council secretary, Mohsen Rezaei, announced a recalibrated posture involving a potential maritime exclusion zone in the Gulf. Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has already decreased, with only seven vessels passing through on Monday compared to 130 daily before the war. These developments have weighed on European stock markets and raised inflationary concerns for central bankers, including the Bank of England governor Andrew Bailey, who faces questions from MPs today regarding the impact of the ongoing conflict on consumer prices.

Transport Minister Jeffrey Siow addressed parliament on Tuesday regarding Singapore Airlines' investment in Air India. MP Kenneth Tiong asked whether the government would rule out direct support through Temasek if Air India faces further difficulties. Siow responded that Air India's losses do not automatically become SIA's liabilities and that the airline's ability to serve Singaporeans remains unaffected. He noted SIA's strong financial performance and record revenue. Tiong questioned the risk limits for Temasek support, citing SIA's net debt and Air India's losses. Siow emphasized that SIA's management is responsible for investment decisions and that Singaporeans deserve debate grounded in facts rather than speculation. SIA confirmed it holds a 25.1 per cent stake in Air India and continues to support its long-term transformation programme.

High-profile films are debuting at the Venice Film Festival, including Alex Gibney's documentary on Elon Musk and a thriller starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem. Gibney told The Associated Press that his investigation into Musk upended the myth of him as a modern Leonardo da Vinci. Meanwhile, director Florian Zeller said his film "Bunker" explores love and fidelity through a couple's struggle. Winners will be announced Saturday by the jury led by Maggie Gyllenhaal.

Huawei Technologies faces a criminal racketeering trial in New York starting Tuesday, according to reports. The indictment alleges the company stole trade secrets, plotted to steal U.S. secrets, and committed fraud while doing business in sanctioned nations. Huawei's lawyers argue the charges are vague and extraterritorial. Chinese officials have called the U.S. actions economic bullying. The company, the world's largest wireless network gear supplier, has been banned from selling to U.S. carriers and other Western allies since 2019. It has since expanded into chipmaking. Prosecutors also charged former CFO Meng Wanzhou with fraud, though those charges were dropped after her release in a prisoner swap.

Investigators have recovered the flight recorders from the Amazon cargo plane that crashed at Miami International Airport, but the priority remains the recovery of victims, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has said. NTSB chairwoman Jennifer Homendy stated that it was too early to draw conclusions about the crash cause as investigators remain in the fact-finding stage. The Boeing 767-300, operated by 21 Air, overshot the runway and struck vehicles, killing five people and injuring five others. Homendy emphasized that recovering victims' bodies is the current priority, while the investigation into the aircraft, crew, and weather conditions continues.

Canada imposed tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on hundreds of U.S. products, including steel and consumer goods, on Tuesday. Prime Minister Mark Carney stated that this measure aims to strengthen Ottawa's negotiating position with the United States. The new taxes specifically increased import duties on many U.S. steel items from 25% to 50% and applied levies to various consumer goods starting at 12:01 a.m. New York time.

Canada's counter-tariffs on billions of dollars in US products took effect Tuesday, escalating trade tensions between the two nations. Ottawa announced duties of 15 percent, 25 percent, and 50 percent on $27.6 billion in imports, covering steel, aluminum, and dairy goods. This pushback follows US President Donald Trump's imposition of 50-percent tariffs on similar Canadian products. Negotiations between the sides broke down in August after Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney deemed US terms unacceptable. The dispute includes threats against Bombardier Aviation and remarks on French language protections. While US officials downplayed the situation, Canada has unveiled a $7.5 billion aid package to support affected businesses and workers.

China's Commerce Ministry announced preliminary anti-dumping measures requiring cash deposits of up to 99.2% on Japanese dichlorosilane imports. The move targets producers Denal Silane and Shin-Etsu Chemical, imposing an 80.8% rate for Denal and 99.2% for Shin-Etsu and others. Beijing stated dumping caused substantial harm to its domestic industry. This action escalates the diplomatic dispute between China and Japan over Taiwan, occurring ahead of Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's expected U.S. visit and President Xi Jinping's meeting with Donald Trump.

The ABC reports that an eighth Australian has been found safe after the floods in Nepal and Tibet, though the person was not in the disaster zone. Chinese officials stated that 261 foreign nationals from 23 countries remain missing, while at least 1,399 people have been killed in the region.

The Australian government has reached an in-principle agreement with Solomon Islands, committing nearly $1 billion in aid to strengthen ties. The ABC reported that leaked texts show Canberra is willing to do "whatever it takes" to finalize the deal, including a $68 million contribution for development priorities and visa improvements. This move follows a diplomatic shift under new Prime Minister Matthew Wale, who recently survived a no-confidence motion. Oliver Nobetau of the Lowy Institute noted that while Australia seeks to cement its role as the region's security partner, it must demonstrate pragmatism rather than abruptly cutting off existing security pacts with China. Similar agreements have been signed with Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Vanuatu, Tuvalu, and Nauru, creating a web of treaties across the Pacific.

Russian air strikes killed at least two people and injured seven others in Ukraine's capital Kyiv this morning, officials said. The attacks came just a day after US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held peace talks with Volodymyr Zelensky and left the Ukrainian capital. During their visit, journalist Dmytro Gordon questioned whether President Vladimir Putin had been deceiving US President Donald Trump. Meanwhile, Polish armed forces concluded air operations related to Russian strikes, stating no airspace violations were recorded. In other developments, Russia plans to reclaim one-off payments from contract soldiers found guilty of domestic crimes, and Zelensky reported overnight attacks on critical infrastructure in the Kyiv region using various missile types.

Nepal authorities announced on Tuesday that rescuers are concentrating efforts on three hydropower project tunnels where dozens of workers could be trapped. This search follows a devastating glacier collapse on August 26 that buried project entrances and killed hundreds. Disaster authority chief Dharma Raj Upreti stated the Chilime project is a primary focus due to worker facilities there. Prime Minister Balendra Shah emphasized the sensitivity of the operation, noting about 121 of 900 missing individuals might be inside the tunnels. Rescue teams have already saved four people, including a Chinese national, while total death tolls in Nepal and Tibet exceed 1,399 with over 5,400 still missing.
The article reports that the AfD's performance in Saxony-Anhalt has weakened, affecting Friedrich Merz's political position. No specific details or figures are provided in the source text.

The European Union warns of a new terror menace driven by young people online who seek violent thrills without political motives. Authorities describe this as nihilistic violent extremism, where acts are committed for status within digital communities. Police from nine European countries identified about 4,340 URLs linked to an online group called 'The COM' during a disruption campaign. EU Counter-Terrorism Coordinator Bartjan Wegter stated that these incidents involve young individuals often without prior criminal records, operating behind encrypted walls. While jihadist groups accounted for over 70% of recent arrests, rising cases include stabbings and planned murders by minors seeking notoriety. Europol noted that 85% of investigations now occur in digital environments, where AI amplifies propaganda and facilitates recruitment. Wegter emphasized that law enforcement must adapt to these evolving online threats to ensure security across the continent.

A Riyadh-led coalition reported that strikes by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels wounded 73 people in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday. The coalition vowed to respond to the attacks targeting civilian and economic sites. Days of fighting near the Red Sea coast have left more than 300 people dead and displaced hundreds of families as the Houthis try to capture land bordering the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. Houthi media Ansarollah stated the rebels hit targets including Abha International Airport and facilities belonging to Aramco. The strikes followed accusations by the Houthis against Riyadh regarding strikes around Yemen, including a prison bombardment that killed 11 people. Experts say the Houthis launched a broad offensive along the western Red Sea coast to advance toward the Bab al-Mandab Strait, a vital shipping artery for Saudi oil exports.

Fourteen defendants face trial in France regarding a 2021 Channel crossing that killed 31 people, with prosecutors alleging ties to smuggling operations. A parallel investigation examines French naval response after a UK inquiry concluded faster action by authorities could have prevented some deaths. Survivors testified that distress calls were ignored before the vessel sank, leaving four victims unaccounted for. Lawyers representing civil parties hope the proceedings will shift public perception of migrants from statistics to human beings.

The Rainforester and Mongabay are launching a four-part series on non-timber forest products. The series examines how sustainable harvesting of the Ogbono tree can help preserve African rainforests. The authors report that this iconic plant provides food and shelter for many species, making its conservation vital.

Tesla announced the rollout of its gold-colored Cybercab robotaxis in Austin, Texas, featuring a design with no steering controls or pedals. The vehicle is intended for maximally efficient autonomous operation, allowing passengers to use the interior as a lounge. However, the U.S. National Highway Traffic Safety Administration has opened an investigation into Tesla's self-certification process. The regulator stated that when certified vehicles appear to not adhere to Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards, an investigation is conducted. NHTSA is currently reviewing whether the Cybercab complies with requirements for brake pedals and other safety features. Additionally, the agency issued a warning regarding automated vehicles that interfere with first responders, noting such behavior is unacceptable and dangerous to the public.

Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay brought the Sarkaria Commission Inquiry back into focus during a legislative debate on September 7, 2026. Constituted in 1976 to investigate corruption allegations against former Chief Minister M. Karunanidhi and his cabinet, the panel examined 28 charges spanning the 1969-1976 period. The Commission substantiated allegations regarding the Veeranam water supply project, stating that Karunanidhi abused his position to favor Sathyanarayana Bros, causing nearly ₹6 crores to be squandered. While the inquiry also found evidence of illegal gratification in pesticide contracts and undue favors in other areas, political realignments in 1980 led to the dropping of filed cases against the former leaders.

Assam Congress president and MP Gaurav Gogoi questioned the Assam government on Monday regarding the removal of an allegedly incomplete 2022 gazette notification on Kaziranga National Park's animal corridors from its official website. Gogoi stated that the version published on the State portal stopped at page 1,426, omitting 29 pages covering the Panbari corridor. He noted this omission coincides with reports of rare earth element deposits in the same belt and demanded transparency on why the document remained unrectified for four years before being pulled down. Gogoi also highlighted the government's delay in notifying nine crucial animal corridors and criticized the administration for signing MoUs for luxury hotels while ignoring illegal mining and detaining activists like Pranab Doley. The 2022 notification identified nine wildlife corridors linking Kaziranga to the hills of Karbi Anglong, but the online version lacked detailed descriptions and maps for the Panbari corridor, which runs through Methoni Tea Estate, now owned by a subsidiary of Reliance Industries Limited. An official response to these allegations was awaited as of September 8, 2026.

ESDS Software Solution shares surged 195% from its IPO price of Rs 757 in three trading sessions. The issue was subscribed 136 times overall, with qualified institutional buyers subscribing more than 261 times. The company plans to use approximately Rs 576 crore of its IPO proceeds to purchase and install cloud-computing equipment and other data-centre infrastructure.

Apple CEO John Ternus will lead his first keynote on September 9 to unveil a foldable iPhone and refresh the Pro lineup. The event will also feature updates to Apple Watch, AirPods, and smart home devices, though deep dives into Apple Intelligence are not expected.

The Free Press Journal reports that Samsung India has reportedly laid off nearly 100 employees in its television and home appliance divisions. The same source notes that Prime Minister Narendra Modi is in Mumbai today to inaugurate the Global Fintech Fest 2026, which will focus on AI, tokenisation, and quantum computing.

Bloomberg reports that Anthropic has decided against acquiring Decart AI after months of negotiations over a deal valued at roughly $6 billion. The company had performed due diligence but ultimately walked away from the transaction. Decart, founded in 2023, develops software to optimize AI chip performance and builds world models for applications like autonomous driving. The startup recently raised $300 million, valuing it at almost $4 billion. Despite the failed acquisition, the two companies may still pursue other collaboration opportunities.

Samsung India Electronics has initiated layoffs affecting 80-100 executives in its television and home appliance sectors, with more cuts expected after Diwali. Reports indicate that up to 25% of the sales and marketing workforce could be impacted as the company faces pressure from a twofold increase in memory chip prices and a weakening rupee. The domestic electronics sales organization, which includes around 550-600 executives, is offering a severance package of three months' salary plus additional pay for years of service. Meanwhile, the smartphone division has been spared from immediate job cuts as it remains the company's primary revenue driver, though Samsung recently lost market share to competitors like Vivo and Oppo. The company has also deferred a proposed merger of its home appliance and television sales teams to the December quarter.

Apple is scheduled to hold its "Surprise and Shine" event on September 9 to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the company's first foldable device, the iPhone Ultra. Reports indicate that standard iPhone models have been delayed to spring 2027, leaving the autumn lineup focused on premium devices. The iPhone Ultra is described as a book-style foldable with a 7.8-inch inner display and Touch ID, while the iPhone 18 Pro features a 2nm A20 Pro chip and a variable aperture camera. The iPhone 18 Pro Max is expected to include a 5,567mAh battery. Preorders are anticipated to begin on September 12, with retail sales starting September 18.

Samsung Electronics has begun laying off 80-100 executives in its Indian television and home appliance divisions, citing weaker consumer demand and reduced margins. A report citing The Economic Times notes that director-level officials and managers are being let go without notice periods, receiving severance pay. While the smartphone business remains unaffected for now, the company plans to evaluate further cuts in that sector later, with a potential second round of reductions expected after Diwali.

People familiar with the matter said Anthropic PBC decided against acquiring artificial intelligence startup Decart AI after performing due diligence. The companies may still pursue other collaboration opportunities, though representatives for both declined to comment. Decart, founded in 2023, produces software that helps chips work more efficiently to reduce AI costs. The startup raised $300 million in May, valuing it at almost $4 billion.

People familiar with the matter said Reliance Industries plans to raise up to ₹12,500 crore through local-currency bonds as early as next week. The issuance would be the largest listed bond sale in the domestic market this year and the conglomerate's first offering since November 2023. The company intends to raise funds through five-year notes at a 7.47% coupon, with Axis Bank, ICICI Bank, HDFC Bank, and YES Bank acting as arrangers. A Reliance spokesperson did not offer immediate comment, while bank representatives did not respond to emails outside business hours. Bloomberg data indicates Indian domestic bond borrowing has fallen 11% year-over-year to ₹8.9 lakh crore.

Copper prices hit a record high of $14,617 per ton on the London Metal Exchange, marking the fourth consecutive day of gains. Tight near-term supplies and expectations of US tariffs on refined metal imports buoyed the industrial metal, which has rallied around 17% this year. Jia Zheng, a trading manager at Suzhou Chuangyuan Harmony-Win Capital Management Co., said copper could easily reach $15,000 as demand from China increases and State Grid Corp. of China places strong orders.

Tata Sons Chairman N. Chandrasekaran announced in the FY26 Annual Report that the holding company will continue prioritizing artificial intelligence, semiconductors, aviation, and advanced manufacturing. The conglomerate reported strong financial results despite global uncertainties, with total shareholder returns of 287% compared to the Nifty 50's 253%. Tata Electronics emerged as the fourth-largest group company by revenue, while Air India improved its Net Promoter Score to +42. The report also highlighted investments in battery manufacturing and defense systems, alongside a final dividend recommendation of ₹1,10,717 per share.

Canada is set to impose retaliatory tariffs on $27.6 billion of US imports starting Tuesday, targeting sectors including steel, dairy, and electronics. The Canadian government stated it will apply rates of 15, 25, and 50 per cent based on matching US tariffs. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump threatened to boycott Bombardier jets, claiming the company relies heavily on American buyers. The company employs workers across more than 20 states and manufactures components in Texas and Los Angeles.

Kawal Tiger Reserve in northern Telangana supports abundant prey but remains devoid of resident tigers due to blocked migration routes. A 12-year study led by Imran Siddiqui revealed that while male tigers occasionally enter the reserve, female dispersal is halted by highways, railways, and mines. Lead researcher Siddiqui explained that females require undisturbed habitat to raise cubs, yet National Highway 44 and other infrastructure act as formidable barriers. Local Adivasi leader Siddam Bhujang Rao criticized broken resettlement promises, noting families received unfinished housing and no farmland. Conservationists like Anish Andheria argue internal protection is insufficient without inviolate core space. While some suggest artificial translocation, experts caution that moving tigers into an isolated, conflict-ridden landscape without restoring corridors creates a precarious sink. Until physical connections are reestablished and local communities are included, Kawal will remain a reserve without a breeding population.

Top seed Alexander Zverev romped into the US Open quarterfinals with a straight-sets victory over Italy's Luciano Darderi. The match concluded in 2hr 30mins on Arthur Ashe Stadium court with a score of 6-2, 6-2, 7-6 (7/3). Zverev, who had previously endured marathon matches, controlled the contest before Darderi rallied in the third set to force a tie-break. The German secured the win with a thunderous serve and a scorching forehand, earning his 13th ace of the match. Zverev will now face Dutch veteran Botic van de Zandschulp in the next round.

The Bharatiya Janata Party government in West Bengal faces criticism after Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari hosted religious preacher Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, who advocated against selling non-vegetarian food near Durga Puja pandals. While BJP leader Samik Bhattacharya dismissed the call as a personal opinion and affirmed that Bengalis retain the right to eat meat and fish, the administration has implemented other regulatory changes. These measures include banning DJ music, restricting crane usage during idol immersion, and designating Ashtami as a dry day. Additionally, the government has altered financial support rules for large-scale pujas, requiring local authority applications for state assistance. The controversy highlights tensions between traditional dietary practices and new administrative directives during the festival.

Official sources said the Enforcement Directorate wrote to the Kerala Director General of Police seeking an FIR against former chief minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T Veena, and son-in-law P A Mohammed Riyas. The central agency cited findings from its investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, alleging fraudulent payments of ₹2.78 crore were made to Veena's company under the guise of IT consultancy services. Vijayan has described the case as a political vendetta, while CPI leaders stated they would deal with the matter legally and politically.

The Supreme Court on Monday refused to grant a six-month extension to a committee formed to define the Aravalli mountain range. Chief Justice Surya Kant questioned the panel's request for time until February 28, asking if it was waiting for his retirement. The bench allowed the committee to submit its report by November 30 instead. Kant told the panel to work day and night, adding that if they are incapable, the court will reconstitute the committee. The committee noted the range's complex landscape makes a single definition difficult.

The Allahabad High Court quashed the detention of Delhi University student Akriti Chaudhary, ruling that her arrest under the National Security Act violated her fundamental rights. A bench of Justices Atul Sreedharan and Achal Sachdev admonished Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam for the "despotic" act, warning that such conduct could reduce Uttar Pradesh to an "Orwellian Dystopia." The court ordered Roopam to pay Rs 5 lakh compensation from her salary for the five-month detention based on insufficient evidence. Police officials noted Chaudhary's release might be delayed pending other cases.

Delhi Police issued an advisory warning of temporary traffic regulations and diversions in New Delhi during the BRICS Summit 2026 from September 11 to 13. The force urged citizens to plan journeys in advance, use public transport, and follow official directions while avoiding restricted areas. The advisory also noted that hotel tariffs have risen across the capital and NCR due to the high-profile event.

Danijar Hafner, a 31-year-old former Google DeepMind researcher, has launched a new stealth-mode startup in San Francisco to develop AI agents capable of planning for unexpected scenarios. Hafner describes the venture as a continuation of his work enabling AI to navigate environments not encountered during training, utilizing humanoids imported from China as physical embodiments of this technology. He relies on model-based reinforcement learning to create world models that allow agents to simulate and predict future outcomes, a technique previously proven in video games like Minecraft. Timothy Lillicrap, a former manager at Google, noted that Hafner easily sits in the top half of 1% of researchers. Hafner left Google in the fall of 2025 to pursue this goal of solving a problem that would change the world.

Liberia has renewed and revised its suspension of import tariffs on off-grid solar renewable energy products via a revised Executive Order issued on August 31, 2025. According to a statement from Liberia's Executive Mansion, the measure covers various solar components and appliances to reduce costs and stimulate private investment. The order establishes safeguards requiring entities to be registered with the Liberia Business Registry and the Rural and Renewable Energy Agency to benefit. While the tariff suspension applies, imported goods remain subject to customs user fees and the ECOWAS trade levy. The government will periodically evaluate the measure's impact on investment and energy access. The Africa Solar Industry Association reports 151 MW of operational solar in Liberia, with 111 MW in the commercial and industrial sector.

Solar Macedonia reports that North Macedonia has begun constructing battery energy storage systems this year, with many integrated into existing solar plants. Professor Dimitar Dimitrov explained that adding storage aims to improve project economics through energy arbitrage. While drought conditions have temporarily increased solar revenues, Dimitrov warned that the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism complicates exports. Additionally, PowerChina was selected to implement a 30 MW solar project for state utility ESM.

CNNC announced that key commissioning tests were successfully completed at the Changjiang 4 Hualong One reactor, marking its official entry into the commissioning phase. These cold functional tests verified the leak-tightness of primary circuit components and cleared obstacles for subsequent hot testing and fuel loading. The Changjiang Phase II project, which includes units 3 and 4, represents a total estimated investment of CNY40 billion and is scheduled to be fully operational in early 2027.

Vitol Group CEO Russell Hardy told the Asia Pacific Petroleum Conference that global fuel markets remain tight and inflexible. He noted that refined product inventories are still drawing because global refining capacity is insufficient to prevent these declines. Analysts attribute the stress to downstream constraints, including refinery strikes in the Middle East, drone attacks on Russian facilities, and maximum capacity operations in the United States.

Bankers for OpenAI and Anthropic are reportedly pressing the AI giants to quickly secure investment-grade credit ratings before their initial public offerings. The Financial Times reported that these bankers seek access to the corporate bond market, while S&P Global Ratings analysts noted that capital expenditures in the sector are rising faster than anticipated and that financing is becoming more complicated.

Nvidia has finalized its $12.9 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, a move The New York Times reported as a significant transaction. However, the article notes that the deal carries risks because Jensen Huang's openness pledge lacks binding neutrality terms covering rival chips like AMD and Groq. WIRED framed the purchase as a bet on open-source AI, but the absence of specific governance commitments means the community's trust remains unsecured. The text highlights that until Nvidia publishes model-hosting neutrality terms and policies on rival optimizations, the openness pledge remains a strategic statement rather than a binding covenant.

Google announced changes to its European search engine to comply with EU antitrust rules, stating the updates will degrade user experience and raise costs for local businesses. The tech giant explained that the new format favors price comparison sites over direct company listings. Nick Fox, Google's senior vice-president, noted that users outside the EU will not be impacted by these modifications. The company reported testing the changes with millions of European users, who showed high dissatisfaction. Google has accumulated over €10.38 billion in EU antitrust penalties over nearly two decades.

Flipkart listed the 256GB iPhone 17 Pro Max at ₹1,47,900 on September 8, with a widely shared effective price of ₹79,800 that requires specific conditional benefits. The calculation subtracts ₹63,100 for an eligible iPhone 16 Pro Max trade-in and ₹5,000 from a credit-card offer, but availability and exchange values vary by pincode and device condition. Readers are advised to verify seller details, storage, and pincode availability before purchasing, as e-commerce prices can change quickly.

Bangalore food safety officials conducted raids on dark stores and food storage centres, seizing 1.43 crore rupees worth of expired and mislabelled food items from Amazon and Instamart facilities. The Karnataka Food Safety and Drugs Administration also found unlicensed medicines at some locations, with the investigation continuing under relevant acts.

Canada's retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods took effect Tuesday at 12:01 a.m., applying a dollar-for-dollar response to U.S. Section 338 tariffs on Canadian exports. Steel, aluminum, iron, furniture, motorcycles, clothing, and beauty products from the U.S. now face a 50% Canadian tariff, while existing 25% rates on autos remain in place, according to CNBC.

Argentina said it would file criminal charges against an Israeli oil firm operating in the Falkland Islands. This action represents Buenos Aires' latest effort to regain control of the UK-controlled territory. President Javier Milei has intensified his rhetoric on the islands to improve his flagging approval ratings as he campaigns for reelection next year.

Experts express concern that Jaguar Land Rover's plan to cut 4,000 jobs over the next two years will harm innovation and the UK's automotive skill base. Prof David Bailey warned that reducing research and development staff could limit future car development, while David Roberts of Evtec Group noted that up to 200,000 sector jobs depend on JLR. Regional leaders, including Mayor Richard Parker, emphasized the need to retain highly skilled workers in the West Midlands, where a £500,000 support package has been established for voluntary redundancies. Dr Steve McCabe suggested the cuts are a strategic move to improve efficiency, though Kevin Moreley cautioned that further reductions may occur if the upcoming electric car launch fails to meet sales targets.

Jaguar Land Rover announced plans to cut 4,000 jobs over two years, a move that has raised alarms among its supply chain partners. David Roberts, chair of Evtec, a tier 1 supplier, stated that 'everything is against us' when making cars in the UK, predicting an inevitable decline in demand over the next five years without policy changes. The cuts, which primarily affect white-collar staff, come as the company faces intense competition from Chinese manufacturers and the fallout from a recent cyber-attack that cost £200m. Industry experts highlight high labour and energy costs alongside stringent electric vehicle targets as key hurdles. While the government has offered a £500,000 support package, business secretary Jonathan Reynolds has ruled out direct state intervention to protect jobs, leaving suppliers to worry about the future of the region's manufacturing base.

The article examines conflicting descriptions of the current economic landscape, specifically the debate between a K-shaped and a C-shaped economy. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent recently expressed fatigue with the K-shaped narrative, favoring the C-shape to indicate improving conditions for lower- and middle-class Americans. Conversely, economist Mike Strain explains that the original K-shape concept described diverging fortunes where the rich gained while the poor lost, a trend visible as pandemic relief ended and poverty rates rose. While some wage data shows convergence, experts like Claudia Sahm warn that using wealth or income metrics to assign a single letter oversimplifies a complex reality. Ultimately, the piece suggests the economy is merely easing back to normal after pandemic stimulus, a state Strain describes as a return to baseline rather than a specific geometric shape.

Video footage captured at Miami International Airport shows police discovering a survivor inside a crushed car following a Prime Air cargo plane crash. The Boeing 767, operated by 21 Air, overshot the runway at 129 mph, killing five people and injuring others. While emergency crews battled a complex fire, investigators from the National Transportation Safety Board are examining whether the crash resulted from a late touchdown or stormy South Florida weather. Amazon expressed heartbreak over the loss and pledged cooperation with the ongoing investigation.

French artificial intelligence company Mistral AI announced a record 3 billion euro Series D funding round led by Samsung Electronics, nearly doubling its valuation to over 21 billion euros. CEO Arthur Mensch stated the capital will expand owned computing capacity by 100 percent over five years to ensure autonomy while training larger models. Despite this growth, the article notes Europe still lags behind the United States in the global artificial intelligence race.

French AI startup Mistral announced Tuesday that it raised 3 billion euros ($3.5 billion), described by the company as the largest-ever European tech fundraising. This round, led by Samsung Electronics, values Mistral at over 21 billion euros, nearly doubling its valuation from a year ago. CEO Arthur Mensch said the capital will accelerate research and infrastructure, enabling organizations to run AI at scale using their own data. CFO Johan Bergqvist noted Mistral offers cost-efficient models compared to peers, appealing to companies seeking digital sovereignty away from US hyperscalers. The firm plans to expand internationally while building a new data center in France.

Canada implemented retaliatory tariffs on C$27.6 billion of US goods, including rates of up to 50%, effective Tuesday. Ottawa stated the measures match US tariffs dollar for dollar and rate for rate. The trade conflict has expanded beyond tariffs to include provincial alcohol restrictions and a US threat to block Bombardier sales, while analysts warn the dispute poses a modest risk to Canada's economy.

A new suspension bridge connecting Detroit and Windsor opened recently, but the event lacked US leadership due to worsening diplomatic relations. US President Donald Trump announced 50% tariffs on Canadian goods, prompting Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney to impose retaliatory measures on $20 billion of US imports. The Detroit-based Canada and US Business Association warned that escalating tariffs harm businesses and consumers on both sides. Ontario's Financial Accountability Office estimates 119,000 local jobs could be lost in 2026, particularly in the auto sector. Additionally, tourism and trade between the cities have cooled, with Canadian visitors to Detroit down 11% compared to 2025 levels.

Canada implemented retaliatory tariffs of up to 50 percent on approximately $19.8 billion worth of US goods this Tuesday. Concurrently, US President Donald Trump is threatening to ban sales of all Bombardier aircraft in the US, despite the Canadian company's extensive network of American suppliers.

U.S. President Donald Trump threatened to ban Bombardier aircraft sales unless the Canadian jetmaker manufactures planes in the United States. In response, Bombardier noted that its supply chain includes about 2,800 U.S. companies and that wings are made in Texas. Kansas Senator Jerry Moran also highlighted Bombardier's local workforce contributions. The company stated it values its partnership with American companies and plans to continue investing in its U.S. employees and communities.

Top European Union officials expressed shock after Serbia granted military honors to Ratko Mladic, a Bosnian Serb general convicted of war crimes. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa stated that the funeral demonstrated a failure to confront a dark chapter in Europe's history. Serbian officials, including Justice Minister Nenad Vujic, attended the service, while President Aleksandar Vucic did not. EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos warned that glorifying Mladic is incompatible with EU values. The event raises doubts about Serbia's membership bid, with officials investigating potential consequences for the country's accession process.

Russian presidential spokesperson Dmitry Peskov said Moscow welcomes India's efforts to resolve the Ukraine conflict through peaceful means. He noted that President Vladimir Putin will meet Prime Minister Narendra Modi on September 11, 2026, in New Delhi to discuss nuclear plant negotiations and Su-57 aircraft sales. Peskov also called proposed U.S. tariffs on Russian oil illegal and unacceptable.

Russia has threatened a severe diplomatic retaliation following Hungary's decision to expel ten Russian diplomats. Foreign ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova described the response as "harsh and painful" to what she termed a "Russophobic lobby" in Budapest. Hungary's foreign minister Anita Orbán stated the move protects national security without severing diplomatic relations. Concurrently, the European Union backed Hungary's decision, with spokesperson Christian Wigand noting it was an expected reaction to Russia's hybrid attacks. In related regional news, Bosnia and Herzegovina withdrew diplomatic staff from Serbia in protest over a state funeral for convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the event as shocking and incompatible with EU values. Elsewhere, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed confidence that victory in the war against Russia is "very near" and discussed potential peace negotiations. Additionally, German police detained a 48-year-old suspect in Cologne suspected of sabotage attacks on the power grid, citing climate-related motives. Finally, four artworks were stolen from a Renoir museum in southern France, valued at approximately €9m.

The article details how 25 years of attacks and foiled plots built modern U.S. airport security. Former FAA Administrator Jane Garvey testified that the 1988 Lockerbie bombing stimulated the most significant changes in aviation security since the early 1970s, leading to stricter screening for checked luggage. Subsequent events, including the 2001 shoe bomb attempt and the 2009 Christmas Day plot, drove further measures like mandatory shoe removal and full-body scanners. Aviation disaster attorney Mary Schiavo noted that attacks on aviation command global attention. Today, the TSA continues to expand facial recognition and cockpit barriers. Jacobson stated that while one layer can be breached, collectively they create a resilient system.

The Argentine government announced it will file criminal charges against Navitas Petroleum and its executives for operating in waters off the Falkland Islands. President Javier Milei stated that drilling in the disputed territory violates Argentine law and undermines national sovereignty. The move follows Milei's recent speech asserting Argentina's claim to the archipelago, which remains under British control. Navitas, which holds a 65% stake in the Sea Lion project, has not yet responded to the charges.

An investigation has been launched in France after female staff at the Eiffel Tower were replaced by male colleagues during a visit by a Hindu religious delegation. Staff union representative Diane Davoine stated that women were asked to leave their posts and felt humiliated, prompting a strike. SETE president Ariel Weil blamed managers for being overzealous in complying with the request. The group, BAPS, apologized for any inconvenience caused. Politicians in France have condemned the incident, with leaders stating that no belief system should dictate women's place in public spaces.

The Singapore Police Force announced on Tuesday that a two-month joint operation with five banks disrupted over 400 scam attempts and averted more than S$46 million in potential losses. The Anti-Scam Centre partnered with DBS, UOB, OCBC, Standard Chartered Singapore, and GXS to use robotic process automation technology, sending over 3,300 SMS alerts to more than 2,700 identified potential victims between July 1 and August 31. Police stated the collaboration enabled rapid information exchange for timely intervention, with many cases involving investment and job scams where victims made incremental transfers.

The article examines the skepticism surrounding a new oil agreement between the United States and Venezuela. While President Trump announced a century-long deal involving over 20% of Venezuela's reserves, details remain opaque. Héctor Obregón, president of state-owned PDVSA, stated the contract is for 25 years but renewable, whereas White House leaks suggested a 100-year term. Economists like Francisco Monaldi note that the U.S. Congress previously deemed similar arrangements illegal. Furthermore, experts question the accuracy of Venezuela's oil reserve figures and warn that the deal's conditions could repel investors. Despite these concerns, some analysts suggest the agreement might be the best option available for Venezuela under current sanctions.

Samsung India has reportedly initiated layoffs affecting 80-100 executives within its television and home appliance divisions, according to the Economic Times. The company cites rising input costs, weaker sales, and margin pressure as primary drivers for these cuts, which include director-level officials and branch managers. While the electronics business faces challenges, the smartphone division remains spared as it constitutes the majority of revenue. Additionally, Samsung is consolidating its branch network by merging offices in cities like Ranchi with Patna and Delhi with Gurgaon. The Economic Times noted that termination letters are being issued in small batches without notice periods, with affected employees receiving severance equivalent to three months' salary plus additional pay for years of service.

The Enforcement Directorate sent a report to the Kerala Police Chief on September 7, 2026, requesting a corruption FIR against Pinarayi Vijayan, P.A. Mohamed Riyas, and T. Veena in the CMRL pay-off case. The report alleges Vijayan received a ₹3.28 crore bribe through his daughter, while Riyas transferred funds to Dubai, based on evidence recovered under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act. CPI(M) has accused the ED of a political hit job, but the agency plans a thorough investigation once the FIR is registered.

The Congress West Bengal unit on Tuesday lodged a police complaint against Bageshwar Baba Dham head priest Dhirendra Shastri over his recent remarks urging people to avoid non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja. Congress leader Pradip Prasad stated the comments were intended to create disharmony. In a rare display of unity, BJP West Bengal chief Samik Bhattacharya also rejected Shastri's call, asserting that Bengalis will continue eating what they have traditionally consumed during the festival.

Union minister Kiren Rijiju criticized Rahul Gandhi for politicizing the killing of Manipuri musician C Vikram Singh, stating the focus should be on immediate action rather than political blame. While Rijiju defended Delhi Police's response, Gandhi condemned the death and questioned authorities over safety for Northeast communities in Delhi. The 54-year-old musician died after being assaulted by a group of men following a dispute over noise.

Apple is preparing to launch the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and the first foldable iPhone Ultra tomorrow, September 9, at Apple Park in Cupertino. Reports indicate the base iPhone 18 model will be delayed until March 2027. The new lineup is expected to feature an A20 Pro chip, variable-aperture cameras, and the foldable iPhone Ultra will reportedly include a 5,400mAh to 5,800mAh battery. The Pro models are rumored to be thicker and heavier, while the foldable device will use a book-style design with a titanium frame.

Analysts expect Apple CEO John Ternus to unveil a foldable iPhone and an updated Siri at the company's Cupertino headquarters. While the new phone could lead the folding market despite a price over $2,500, Ternus faces pressure to prove Apple's AI capabilities. Additionally, a deep Siri overhaul using Google's technology may face regulatory delays in Europe and China until 2028.

Tata Consultancy Services has won a 122.6 crore bid to implement the next phase of the Odisha State Workflow Automation System, extending its partnership with the state government by around six years. Vishal Kumar Dev, Additional Chief Secretary to the Government of Odisha, stated that the platform will simplify administration through modern architecture and AI. Sushil Jain, Head of Public Services India at TCS, noted the system will empower officials with greater speed and visibility. Since 2009, the OSWAS system has replaced paper-based processes across nearly 50,000 users. The upcoming OSWAS 3.0 will feature Odia language support and improved accessibility.

Apple is preparing to launch the iPhone 18 Pro series and the highly anticipated iPhone Ultra during a special keynote event tomorrow. The event, which marks CEO John Ternus's first presentation, will stream live from the Steve Jobs Theater in Cupertino. Reports indicate the iPhone Ultra will feature a book-style foldable design with a titanium hinge, while the iPhone 18 Pro models will receive under-the-hood upgrades including a 2nm chip. Additionally, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 are expected to introduce new health monitoring capabilities. However, the standard iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 have reportedly been pushed back to a spring 2027 release.

Tata Consultancy Services announced it has won a 122.6 crore contract to implement the Odisha State Workflow Automation System 3.0. The project aims to modernize the state's paperless governance system with AI capabilities and will extend TCS's partnership with the Odisha government for approximately six years. The platform, powered by TCS DigiBOLT, will integrate workflow automation, analytics, and security to support over 4,600 government offices and nearly 50,000 users. Vishal Kumar Dev, Additional Chief Secretary to the Government of Odisha, stated that the system will accelerate decision-making and deliver efficient governance. Sushil Jain, Head of Public Services India at TCS, noted the platform is designed to be mobile-first and strengthen accountability.

OpenAI announced that it has successfully fulfilled its objective of creating an automated research intern, a goal CEO Sam Altman set roughly a year ago. The company detailed how autonomous programming tools are now handling complex duties and corporate troubleshooting, causing internal IT support requests to plunge by more than 50%. While the AI Lab highlighted these operational efficiencies, it also revealed that median researcher token consumption rose sharply to over $600 daily. This surge in usage contrasts with other tech firms like Amazon and Meta, which recently disbanded internal usage leaderboards after concerns over 'tokenmaxxing' outweighed productivity gains.

Samsung India has reportedly begun cutting jobs in its television and home appliance businesses due to weak demand, rising costs, and internal restructuring. According to a report in The Economic Times citing industry executives, the company has asked around 80-100 executives to leave. The layoffs cover director-level officials and managers, with some termination letters issued without completed notice periods. While the electronics business faces pressure from doubled memory chip prices and a declining Rupee, Samsung's smartphone workforce remains unaffected as the company expects demand to improve during the Diwali season.

Prosecutors say former USCIS official Lukman Owolabi Ganiyu and Adeniyi Akeem Somoye accepted nearly $960,000 to manipulate immigration applications, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Northern District of Texas. Investigators traced the alleged scheme using thousands of WhatsApp messages and hundreds of phone calls between the men and applicants, prosecutors stated. The pair allegedly fast-tracked cases by bypassing standard procedures and criminal background checks. Ganiyu resigned in March before his arrest several months later.

This book review examines Kulbhushansingh Suryawanshi's The Ghost of the Mountains, which draws on two decades of field research to explore snow leopard survival. The authors report that Suryawanshi, a scientist at the Nature Conservation Foundation, tracked populations across 12 countries and analyzed threats like mining and climate change. The book states that protecting wild prey and involving local communities can secure a future for these animals. Suryawanshi writes that ecology is a complex web where more wild herbivores support larger snow leopard populations. The review notes the book blends scientific data with graphic descriptions of the landscape and the creatures' behaviors.

Scientists explain that rising temperatures in the Himalayas are causing glacier retreat and permafrost thaw, which increases the risk of glacial lake outburst floods and landslides. The August 2026 disaster in Nepal, where a massive slope failure generated floodwaters equivalent to a magnitude-5.2 earthquake, highlighted how hazards originating in remote high-altitude areas can devastate downstream communities hundreds of kilometers away. While organizations like ICIMOD and India's Wadia Institute have improved local monitoring, experts note that sparse data coverage and inadequate regional sharing remain critical gaps. Vijaykumar P. of the University of Kerala emphasized that unlike polar regions, the Himalayas feature extreme population density within narrow outburst corridors, making glaciological events severe humanitarian disasters. Consequently, authorities must prioritize early warning systems and expand high-altitude data sharing across international borders to protect nearly two billion people dependent on these water systems.

Mumbai Police detained two individuals at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre ahead of an event for Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The accused, identified as Rohan Parekh, tried to gain entry using a forged Prime Minister's Office identity card, while his companion carried an unauthorized firearm. Security personnel intercepted them after raising suspicions over their credentials. The Mumbai Crime Branch has arrested both suspects and is investigating the background of the accused and the origin of the forged document.

French politicians from various parties condemned the removal of female Eiffel Tower staff during a visit by a Hindu religious delegation. Marine Le Pen, Jordan Bardella, Michel Barnier, Emmanuel Grégoire, and Aurore Bergé all emphasized that France's commitment to gender equality is non-negotiable and that no religious practice can override women's dignity. The Société d'exploitation de la Tour Eiffel admitted the conditions requested by the Hindu group to minimize interactions with women were inconsistent with its values and stated it would accept the consequences. BAPS Paris apologized for any inconvenience but claimed no one was prevented from accessing the site. The incident sparked a brief strike by the monument's staff.

A viral video showing a groom firing 16 rounds from an illegal pistol during his wedding in 2022 has prompted police in Uttar Pradesh to file a case. The footage, which surfaced on social media recently, depicts Shadab, a resident of Khurja in Bulandshahr, firing repeatedly at the mandap. Circle Officer Shobhit Kumar confirmed the man's identity and stated that teams are now working to arrest him and recover the weapon, with further legal action expected to follow.

The Bombay High Court on Tuesday refused to quash a criminal defamation case against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi for referring to Prime Minister Narendra Modi as 'choron ke sardar' or 'leader of thieves'. The complaint, filed by a Bharatiya Janata Party worker, pertains to a speech made by Gandhi in September 2018 while speaking about the Rafale fighter jet deal. Justice Nitin Borkar rejected Gandhi's argument that the remarks did not name any political party, holding that the BJP is a clearly identifiable body. The court observed that whether the imputation was in substance and its impact on party members will have to be considered at the stage of trial.

Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju said Delhi Police assured him a chargesheet in the killing of Manipuri musician C. Vikram Singh would be filed within eight to nine days. Rijiju, who is personally monitoring the investigation, called for the strictest possible punishment for the accused. He stated the incident should not be politicized and emphasized that every Indian life is precious. Police have arrested seven men and a juvenile in connection with the case, which involved an assault on Singh in South Delhi on September 7, 2026.
On Tuesday, the storage at Mettur Dam stood at 91.92 feet against the full reservoir level of 120 feet, with an inflow of 6,148 cusecs and a discharge of 12,000 cusecs.

Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis announced that the government remains open to negotiations with Maratha activist Manoj Jarange-Patil regarding reservation quotas. Fadnavis emphasized that any new measures would not dilute the share of other communities. The state government issued orders extending educational and employment benefits to Marathas, with full implementation starting in the 2026-27 academic year. Jarange-Patil continues his hunger strike, demanding that all his specific requirements be met before ending the protest.

Kenyan President William Ruto has directed Tata Chemicals to cease operations at its Lake Magadi facility, ending a century-long concession. Ruto stated the company failed to build factories or provide adequate benefits, demanding finished products like glass and batteries be manufactured locally instead of exporting raw soda ash. The BBC reports the facility exported approximately $57 million worth of goods last year. Industrialisation Principal Secretary Juma Mukhwana told Bloomberg that no strategic raw material should leave Africa without local transformation. Tata Chemicals says it respects the decision and awaits the mining ministry's review, noting its global operations follow a similar model. Meanwhile, the opposition party questions the move, alleging it relates to lithium and oil deposits beneath the site. Local communities are split; some fear losing essential services like water and healthcare, while others demand a larger share of royalties. The company also faces a separate Supreme Court case regarding land rates with Kajiado county.

Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Vladimir Putin will meet on September 11 in New Delhi to discuss bilateral ties, trade, defence, and the Ukraine conflict. Peskov noted that Russia expects talks on new nuclear power plants and the sale of Su-57 fighter aircraft. Meanwhile, PM Modi stated that the Ukraine issue has been discussed at every meeting and that India supports all efforts for peace.

The Enforcement Directorate has written to the Kerala Director General of Police seeking registration of an FIR against former Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan, his daughter T Veena, and son-in-law PA Mohamed Riyas. The probe concerns alleged money laundering and bribery linked to Cochin Minerals and Rutile Limited (CMRL). The ED alleges the mining company made fraudulent payments of Rs 2.78 crore to Veena's defunct IT firm, Exalogic Solutions, without providing services. Officials privy to the matter stated Vijayan allegedly received Rs 3.28 crore as illegal gratification through his daughter. The agency also claims handwritten notes and digital evidence indicate involvement in hawala transactions and fund transfers to Dubai, implicating Riyas. Recent searches at eight premises in Kozhikode and other locations yielded incriminating records, and the ED has frozen about Rs 18.36 crore in 242 accounts for analysis.

Moody's and S&P Global Ratings upgraded Sun Pharma to Baa1 and BBB+ respectively, maintaining stable outlooks for the Indian pharmaceutical major. The agencies cited Sun Pharma's planned USD 11.75 billion acquisition of Organon as a key factor, projecting its revenue to reach approximately Rs 1.3 trillion by fiscal 2028. S&P noted the deal would bolster Sun Pharma's business position, while Moody's highlighted the company's secured USD 12 billion acquisition bridge loan and existing cash balances.

Emami launched the BoroPlus FromMaa baby-care portfolio, which includes lotion, cream, soap, shampoo, massage oil, powder, and diaper rash cream, the company said in a statement. The new line targets India's growing baby-care market, estimated at more than Rs 40,000 crore by Mordor Intelligence, competing with established brands like Johnson's and newer digital-first companies such as Mamaearth.

The Japan Credit Rating Agency (JCRA) upgraded India's sovereign credit rating to A- from BBB+, marking the first such rating in over 35 years. JCRA cited India's high growth rate of around 7%, government policies, and improved financial system strength as key factors. This follows a series of upgrades from other agencies like S&P and Morningstar DBRS in 2025, reflecting improved investor confidence in India's economic prospects.

In September 2026, NVIDIA announced it is leaning into native GPU programming in Rust, aiming to mature CUDA Rust through 2027 and beyond. The company addresses the gap where GPU kernels previously required separate languages by enabling Rust code to compile natively to PTX. NVIDIA presents two tracks matching CUDA's existing models: SIMT for thread-level control and Tile for compiler-managed data tiles. The Tile track is recommended first for its architecture-agnostic design. Two projects demonstrate these capabilities: cuda-oxide, an early alpha codegen backend requiring a nightly toolchain, and cutile-rs, a published crate supporting stable Rust. Both projects enforce memory safety by preventing data races at compile time, though they differ in their approach to ownership and shared memory. NVIDIA notes that both projects are early-stage and not yet production-ready, inviting community feedback and collaboration.

French AI lab Mistral AI announced on Tuesday that it raised 3 billion euros in a Series D round, valuing the company at more than 21 billion euros. Mistral stated this is the largest equity fundraising round ever completed by a European technology company, led by Samsung Electronics with EQT-managed Scaleup Europe Fund and PSG Equity as co-leads. The company intends to use the funding to scale compute capacity, build infrastructure, and accelerate commercial growth. Mistral aims to clarify its positioning as an AI lab rather than a European ChatGPT, addressing concerns about dependence on United States technology. The funding supports a strategy to build 1 gigawatt of compute capacity in Europe by 2030 and expand operations in 20 countries. French President Emmanuel Macron noted the round reflects France and South Korea's goal of building a third way in AI. While Mistral maintains partnerships with American companies like Microsoft and has American investors, its cap table remains international with new backers from Luxembourg and existing European investors doubling down. The company operates in 20 countries and focuses on helping governments and corporations leverage AI while preserving control over models.

Google DeepMind announced the public release of the AlphaGenome Atlas, an online repository containing pre-computed predictions for 9 billion possible single-letter changes to a reference human genome. Pushmeet Kohli, VP of science at Google DeepMind, stated that understanding this language of life can unlock many things. The Atlas offers a more approachable interface for scientists, eliminating the need to write code or run the computationally demanding AlphaGenome model themselves. Žiga Avsec, the genomics lead with DeepMind, noted that the resource could greatly accelerate work in fundamental biology and disease research. However, Carl de Boer, a genomicist at the University of British Columbia, warned that the single-number impact score is a simplification of many aspects and is probably going to be easily misinterpreted. The dataset, which is around 1 petabyte, is freely available for noncommercial research with potential for commercial licensing.

The authors report that the AlphaGenome Atlas is a predictive map of every possible DNA letter change in the human genome. The study involved contributions from collaborators at the University of Exeter, Broad Institute, Boston Children's Hospital, and other institutions. Researchers also thanked teammates for technical support and communication expertise.

IBM Research, Red Hat, and Google have introduced llm-d, an open-source framework designed to optimize inference for agentic AI systems on existing enterprise hardware. The project addresses challenges like high latency and memory usage by efficiently managing massive contexts and parallel sub-agent activity. In a demonstration, the team deployed the 753-billion-parameter GLM-5.2 model across 544 NVIDIA H100 GPUs, successfully serving up to 3,000 concurrent coding agents without preemptions. Carlos Costa, a Distinguished Engineer at IBM Research, noted that self-hosting with llm-d costs five to ten times less per token than commercial API pricing. The system utilizes capabilities such as prefix-aware routing and prefill/decode disaggregation to reduce redundant computation. Maroon Ayoub from Red Hat emphasized that the deployment sustains long contexts and high reuse patterns typical of agentic workloads. Nili Guy from IBM Research added that software improvements compound the value of existing hardware fleets. The llm-d project remains open source under the Cloud Native Computing Foundation.

The authors report that artificial intelligence accelerates organizational execution, creating a paradox where increased speed demands greater collaboration to prevent chaos. Dashboards provide instant data but cannot interpret it or drive joint decision-making without human conversation. Experience mapping addresses this by freezing complex, fast-moving situations into a shared visual artifact that allows scattered knowledge to align. The authors describe a case where a draft map revealed a system gap causing customer billing issues, leading teams to agree on specific fixes and establish a new monthly meeting cadence. Ultimately, the authors argue that while AI amplifies existing organizational strengths or weaknesses, the organizations that win will be those best at coming together to make sense of data, not merely those with the fastest tools.

FTC Solar, Inc. has begun shipping tracker systems for the 330 MW Fraser Coast solar project in Queensland, Australia. Developed by Global Power Generation, the hybrid renewable energy project is expected to start operations in 2028. GPG Australia Construction Director David Santo Tomás noted that the terrain-following tracker design reduces civil work requirements while delivering time and cost savings during installation. The project represents Naturgy's largest renewable energy project in Australia.

FTC Solar, Inc. announced today that it has commenced shipments for the 330-megawatt Fraser Coast solar project in Queensland, Australia. Developed by Global Power Generation, the project is expected to commence operations in 2028. Shaq Mohajerani, Chief Development Officer at GPG Australia, noted that this project represents the largest solar hybrid battery project ever built by GPG in Australia. FTC Solar's innovative terrain-following solution was instrumental in reducing civil work needs and saving costs during installation. The company's CEO, Anthony Carroll, expressed excitement about contributing to the project design with their stow capabilities and terrain-following design. FTC first announced the project award in March 2025, with tracker production expected to begin in mid-2025. The project timeline was revised and finalized with a notice to proceed issued during the second quarter of 2026. Tracker production and shipments are now underway. The aggregate value of the project was added to the company's backlog in 2025.

European benchmark natural gas prices rose 2% on Tuesday, reaching $86.90 per megawatt-hour, the highest level since the 2022-2023 crisis. Analysts at Timera Energy stated that Europe is pricing up to outcompete Asia for marginal LNG as storage sites remain below 70% full. The Middle East crisis continues to dampen hopes for normalized LNG flows from the Strait of Hormuz, intensifying competition for global cargoes. Go Katayama, principal insight analyst for LNG at intelligence firm Kpler, warned of a potential global fight for fuel, particularly in a colder winter.

Romania plans to install 10 GW of wind and solar capacity by 2030, according to State Secretary Cristian Buşoi. The country will shift from co-financing initial investments to supporting energy storage and future projects through state-aid schemes. Buşoi stated that the market is now mature, making renewable generation a business case. Future support will focus on battery and hydro storage via the Modernisation Fund, while hydropower and geothermal projects will continue development.

BYD is set to launch a new, lighter tri-motor Denza Z9 GT model in China on September 9. Denza general manager Li Hui confirmed the release follows customer feedback, with the vehicle expected to start at around $50,000. This new variant aims to fill the price gap between the existing Performance and Flagship RWD models. While the model is already available in Europe, BYD has not yet confirmed if this lower-priced version will be offered there.

A new study by Transport & Environment reveals that real-world pollution from plug-in hybrids in Europe is significantly higher than official government estimates. Using data from 220,000 vehicles, the analysis found that actual emissions rose by 5% in 2024, while laboratory tests suggested a decrease. The discrepancy stems from inaccurate 'utility factors' that fail to account for drivers rarely plugging in their vehicles. The article reports that automakers have lobbied the EU to weaken these testing standards to protect their greenwashing efforts and delay the deployment of fully electric cars. Lucien Mathieu from Transport & Environment stated that these hybrids are a major rip-off for consumers and that Europe must resist attempts to weaken utility factors to remain competitive against Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers.

China has reversed its recent decline in oil demand, aggressively bidding up crude prices in global markets as the Shanghai crude spread turns positive. Bloomberg reports that the world's largest oil importer is now competing for supplies from Africa, Canada, and Latin America, pushing Brent prices above $97. While this activity signals a shift from the subdued buying that previously restrained prices, GL Consulting founder Liao Na suggests the move is driven by improved processing margins and restocking rather than a fundamental demand recovery. Goldman Sachs energy expert Daan Struyven adds that while China's purchasing power may moderate spikes, geopolitical risks in the Middle East could still push Brent toward $120 per barrel.

Qualcomm stock surged after the company announced a deal with Amazon to build custom AI chips for inference workloads. The collaboration combines Amazon's infrastructure with Qualcomm's silicon design capabilities, CNBC reported. This agreement marks a significant step for Qualcomm as it seeks to establish itself as a data center chip supplier alongside Nvidia. The company previously entered the market with the Dragonfly C1000, targeting $15 billion in data center revenue by fiscal 2029. Amazon, which has been expanding its custom silicon ambitions, now has a second major hyperscaler partner in Qualcomm.

TSMC and Samsung committed Tuesday to using ASML High NA extreme ultraviolet lithography machines for advanced chip production. Samsung targets DRAM manufacturing by 2028, while TSMC aims to deploy the technology in high-volume advanced node production starting in 2030.

Qualcomm shares rose 5% following news of a multi-generation AI silicon supply deal with Amazon. The partnership involves co-developing customized silicon for large-scale AI inference workloads and includes high-performance optical connectivity. While the deal validates Qualcomm's data-center push, it discloses no committed volume or delivery timeline. Broadcom shares also climbed 3% on read-through to the custom AI silicon category, while Amazon stock fell 1% as it adds another supplier to its AWS mix.

A proposed class action lawsuit filed in Brooklyn federal court accuses Amazon of systematically discriminating against pregnant workers. The complaint, filed by four former warehouse employees, alleges the company violates federal and New York worker protection laws by denying basic accommodations and threatening termination. The lawsuit seeks damages including lost pay, benefits, and punitive damages. Amazon did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

An analyst argues that Broadcom (NASDAQ: AVGO) is a superior investment to Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD) for AI hardware exposure. The author contends Broadcom's custom AI chips offer better performance and cost efficiency for hyperscalers. Broadcom raised its AI semiconductor revenue guidance to $115 billion for next year, projecting $230 billion in 2028, while AMD's data center division grew 107% to $6.7 billion in the second quarter.

Karnataka Food Safety and Drugs Administration officials conducted inspections at Amazon and Swiggy Instamart facilities in Bengaluru, seizing ₹1.38 crore worth of expired and mislabelled food products. Additionally, the authorities confiscated medicines valued at ₹4.02 lakh during the operation at sites in Devanahalli, Anekal, and Hoskote.

Qualcomm and Amazon announced a partnership to develop custom chips for AI data centers, granting Amazon warrants to acquire up to $4 billion in Qualcomm shares. The companies will collaborate on AI inference chips and high-speed optical connectivity technologies. Qualcomm plans to expand its use of AWS services to shorten development cycles for these workloads.

A circulating video attributed to tipster yeux1122 displays alleged demo units in Dark Cherry and blue, though Apple has not authenticated the devices. Reports conflict on the full color range and predict an A20 Pro chip, larger batteries, and a variable-aperture camera, none of which Apple confirmed as of September 8.

Channel 4 is preparing to cut approximately 300 jobs, marking the broadcaster's largest round of layoffs in its 43-year history. New chief executive Priya Dogra plans to address staff regarding a comprehensive review of the organization's structure and strategy. While the broadcaster aims to reduce its wage bill, which has grown to £122m, it intends to limit cuts to the content budget to preserve programming quality. The announcement follows a period of financial strain, with Channel 4 reporting a £10m pre-tax loss last year and facing declining advertising revenues. A spokesperson stated that the organization is assessing its strategic direction and will share updates with staff transparently.

In Venice, filmmaker Alex Gibney explained that his new documentary uses an AI avatar of Elon Musk to ironically illustrate the CEO's contradictory views on technology. Ashley St. Clair, who shares a child with Musk, appeared in the film to discuss their relationship and a lawsuit she filed against his company over deepfake images. The nearly four-hour film, set for an October release, also examines Musk's influence on X and his political activities.

Canada's retaliatory tariffs on billions of dollars in US products took effect Tuesday, escalating trade tensions between the two nations. This action follows a threat from President Trump to block sales of Bombardier Aviation in the United States unless the Quebec-based manufacturer relocates its production to the US.

Republicans are hosting an unusual midterm convention in Dallas, an event typically reserved for presidential election years. President Trump will headline the gathering, dubbed "Trumpapalooza," as he urges voters to treat the election as if he were on the ballot. Meanwhile, Canada's retaliatory tariffs on American products went into effect at midnight, imposing taxes of up to 50% on approximately $20 billion worth of U.S. goods. This dollar-for-dollar retaliation follows recent U.S. tariffs on Canadian products after trade talks collapsed. Additionally, the National Transportation Safety Board stated that all five individuals killed in an Amazon cargo plane crash at Miami International Airport were in vehicles on the ground, while five others were injured. The investigation remains ongoing as recovery efforts face challenges due to fuel at the wreckage site.

Russian Ambassador to Germany Sergey Nechaev described the recent drone incident at Leipzig Airport as a deliberate provocation, stating there is no evidence supporting accusations of Russian involvement. Speaking to the German podcast ungeskriptet, Nechaev characterized Germany's subsequent retaliatory measures as extremely harsh and an unprecedented deterioration in bilateral relations. He noted that trust has been undermined and warned that Moscow would respond to Berlin's actions, including the closure of Russian cultural and diplomatic institutions. Additionally, Nechaev attributed the roots of the Ukraine conflict to Western policies and NATO expansion, asserting that a lasting peace requires political will from Ukrainian leadership and balanced positions from European countries.

Former Israeli Prime Minister Ehud Olmert supported the UK government's decision to impose sanctions on trade with illegal Israeli settlements. Speaking to The Guardian, Olmert described the British government's decision as unavoidable due to a continuous effort of ethnic cleansing in the West Bank, which he attributed to Jewish terrorists assisted by police and military units. He noted that millions of Israelis are appalled by this terror and actively resist it. UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband quoted Olmert approvingly in his own statement regarding the sanctions. The announcement, made alongside France and Canada, has been hailed by pro-Palestinian groups as a historic step, though some argue the UK should go further. Conversely, the Jewish Leadership Council accused the government of having an increasingly punitive approach.
