Sharma announced a significant restructure aiming to reduce the team by approximately 3,200 throughout the 2027 financial year to address business health issues and return to growth by the end of FY27.

Sharad Pawar, president of the Nationalist Congress Party, urged stakeholders to protect the Tata Group's charitable legacy and resolve its leadership dispute through dialogue. He stressed that Tata Trusts, which hold 66% of Tata Sons, must have their governance rights respected to preserve the group's institutional role. Pawar noted that the dispute arose after the Tata Sons board reappointed N Chandrasekaran as executive chairman, a move opposed by Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata. Pawar also highlighted the group's contributions to Maharashtra institutions and called for adherence to the Articles of Association.

Top AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic have urged Australia to reconsider a ban on using local creative content for training AI models. They argue that a limited exemption could protect artists' rights while encouraging investment. The companies, which have signed agreements for data centres in Sydney and Queensland, suggest a narrow form of conditional approval. Meanwhile, Australia has ruled out broad copyright exemptions, and the Joint Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence is due to deliver its report in November.

Reports indicate Apple Pay may launch in India by October, ending a twelve-year wait for the service. While initial rollout might focus on Axis Bank credit cards, it remains unclear if UPI integration will be included. This distinction is critical because UPI dominates Indian digital payments, with over 24.5 billion transactions recorded in August 2026. Users may hesitate to switch from established apps like PhonePe and Google Pay if the new service lacks essential local features.

Police in Lakhimpur Kheri are investigating a shooting where a teacher was killed and the accused, Mohd Saud Ansari, died by suicide. Authorities are examining a cryptic Instagram post found on an account allegedly linked to Ansari, which requested followers to delete his photos and report his Facebook account. Additionally, two country-made pistols were recovered from his bag. Officials state that while these elements form part of the puzzle, a social media message alone cannot establish the motive. Investigators are also scrutinizing Ansari's interactions with the victim and CCTV footage to piece together the sequence of events.

Alibaba Group CEO Eddie Wu announced the Zhenwu V900 AI chip and plans for a significantly larger AI model at the annual Apsara Conference in Hangzhou. The new chip delivers three times the performance of the previous Zhenwu M890 and supports clusters of up to 500,000 cards. Alibaba aims to train a next-generation model with 5 to 10 trillion parameters, a significant increase from the current Qwen3.8-Max model's 2.4 trillion parameters. The company also targets surpassing 20 gigawatts of cloud data center capacity by 2032, despite supply chain shortages hindering infrastructure expansion.

Ahead of a meeting between US President Donald Trump and China President Xi Jinping in Washington, D.C., officials are considering establishing a hotline for serious AI incidents. The article highlights the threat of AI-enabled adaptive computer worms, which can self-replicate and adapt strategies, potentially enabling non-state actors to conduct large-scale cyberattacks. Historical examples like the 2017 NotPetya attack, which compromised 2,000 organizations in 60 countries, and the WannaCry outbreak affecting 18,000 Chinese IP addresses, illustrate the severe transnational risks. The summit offers an opportunity to build a framework for cooperation against this emerging threat.

Meta shares surged 11.43%, adding more than $190 billion to market value as its new AI agent, Muse, rapidly climbed US app rankings. Launched on September 8, Muse overtook OpenAI's ChatGPT to become the No. 1 free app on Apple's US App Store, according to Sensor Tower. While Meta describes Muse as a breakthrough for consumer AI, analysts note that early buzz has not erased market concerns regarding privacy and whether the product will sustain momentum beyond a viral hit.

As leading AI powers, China and the United States are urged to maintain dialogue despite ongoing competition. While recent disputes over model distillation have occurred, experts like Gai Keke and Dean Ball note this is not the core issue. Both nations' experts agree that sharing risks and jointly building rules for AI safety should be the primary agenda, as danger in AI knows no borders.

EU Trade Commissioner Maroš Šefčovič announced a new trade agreement between the EU and the Philippines, designed to diversify trade ties away from reliance on China and the US. The deal provides EU businesses access to a market of 113 million consumers and eliminates over 94% of customs duties. It covers more than 97% of bilateral trade, including machinery, medicines, and agricultural products. Bilateral goods trade reached €17.6 billion in 2025, while services trade hit €10.3 billion in 2024. The EU also plans further agreements with Thailand and Malaysia by year-end.

Sri Lanka's Ministry of Energy announced the discontinuation of the net-metering regime for new rooftop solar connections after March 5, 2026, replacing it with the Net Plus mechanism. The Public Utilities Commission of Sri Lanka (PUCSL) established feed-in tariffs ranging from LKR 15.81 to LKR 23.11 per kWh, valid until February 24, 2027. New agreements under Net Plus are limited to a maximum term of 12 years, and systems must be equipped with smart meters for remote monitoring.

A 2025 report by the Kerala Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance Network confirms that antimicrobial resistance is now the norm in the state's hospitals, affecting both intensive care and community settings. The study analyzed 65,849 isolates and found high resistance rates in key pathogens like E. coli and Klebsiella. While Colistin remains largely effective with only 0.1% resistance, experts warn that resistance is emerging. Despite a robust surveillance system, prescribing behaviors have not changed, highlighting a need for targeted stewardship interventions.

Six Senate Democrats, including Sen. Elizabeth Warren, wrote to US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer urging the Trump administration to refund consumers after the Supreme Court invalidated a round of tariffs. The lawmakers argue that without such a plan, the policy risks transferring wealth to corporations. Meanwhile, the private sector has recovered about $100 billion through price cuts and refunds, though some companies like Ford and Costco face lawsuits for opting out. The Democrats also seek oversight on future tariffs under specific trade acts.

RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav demanded the resignation of Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary following a viral video showing minors being harassed in Jamui. Yadav, addressing a press conference in Patna, alleged that the incident demonstrated a collapse of law and order. He invoked a previous statement by Choudhary regarding Munger, asserting that the CM should resign if he lacks the courage to stand by his words. Yadav further accused the ruling alliance of attempting to justify the incident.

Vietnamese President To Lam indicated that his nation is very close to inking a trade deal with the U. S. Speaking on the sidelines of the U. N. General Assembly, he pledged to buy more high-tech goods like aircraft to narrow the trade gap ahead of talks with U. S. administration officials in New York. Lam emphasized the need to expedite negotiations toward an agreement on reciprocal, balanced and equitable tariffs, noting that Vietnam exports align with U. S. demand without competing directly with U. S. products. He also mentioned that Vietnam wants to import more U. S.

Hindustan Copper plans to invest Rs 7,000 crore over the next five years to expand its mining portfolio and strengthen India's mineral security. The company has signed multiple MoUs with Indian public sector undertakings like NTPC Mining, RITES, and IOCL. Additionally, it entered a global partnership with CODELCO in Chile for capacity building. In the last four years, Hindustan Copper added 154.14 million tonnes of copper ore reserves.

The 23rd China-ASEAN Expo concluded in Nanning, Guangxi, with artificial intelligence emerging as a central theme for trade and investment cooperation. Held at the Nanning International Convention and Exhibition Center, the event saw a 10,000 square meter area increase to 170,000 square meters. A total of 3,432 enterprises from 73 countries participated, with international exhibitors accounting for 30. 5%. The expo unveiled 42 AI application scenarios and generated nearly 100 preliminary cooperation agreements, with intended deal values exceeding 1 billion yuan. An AI-themed marketplace debuted, featuring 70 companies and 500 products, generating 28 million yuan in sales.

In 2025, trade between China and the United States surpassed $500 billion. Data indicates that 95% of American firms consider their China operations vital. Although disagreements persist, experts suggest these conflicts should not define the entire bilateral relationship. Michael Wang from CGTN argues that history serves as a warning rather than a predetermined destiny for future interactions.

An official announced that China's grain industry output is projected to exceed 4.5 trillion yuan during the 2026-2030 period. Liu Huanxin, head of the National Food and Strategic Reserves Administration, stated that the sector will better meet demand for nutritious food. He attributed China's food security to stable production, ample reserves, and strong processing capacity, noting that output has remained above 650 million tonnes since 2015.

Mandvi taluka in Gujarat received 177 mm of rain in eight hours on September 15, causing waterlogging. This occurred despite a 70% rainfall deficit in the district. A 2025 study in Science indicates that while El Niño suppresses total summer rainfall in India, it increases the frequency of extreme daily rainfall events in specific regions. India ranks among the six most disaster-prone countries globally.

Italian authorities are searching for a British man who went missing after diving into Lake Como to rescue a teenager and his father. The incident occurred on Monday afternoon when the man, described as being in his late thirties, jumped into the water to help two people in distress. Although the father and son were later rescued by a passing boat, the British man has not been seen again. Rescuers, including a helicopter and underwater robots, are currently searching the lake's deep waters.

Congress secured control of the Tijara Nagar Parishad chairperson post despite having only one elected councillor, as its candidate Ramavatar Saini defeated BJP's Subhash Chand Saini by a margin of two votes. The result hinged on the support of 31 independent councillors, who held the balance of power in the 35-member council. The election was preceded by allegations that Congress-backed councillors were detained by Haryana Police in Panchkula, triggering protests and delaying the vote until approximately 9:45 pm. Former MLA Sandeep Yadav alleged mistreatment of the councillors and threatened legal action, while police denied the claims and promised an investigation.

India secured its first gold medal of the Asian Games 2026 by defeating Sri Lanka in the women's cricket final held in Nagoya on September 22, 2026. India batted first, posting 216/3 led by Smriti Mandhana's 79, and then chased down the target to win by over 100 runs. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the team, stating the victory brings India its first gold of this edition. However, the women's team was eliminated after a 1-3 defeat to hosts Japan in the semifinals.

Officials reported that an attacker wounded at least 11 people near a vocational high school in Turgutlu, Manisa province, on Tuesday. Justice Minister Akin Gurlek stated that the suspect, possibly a student, used a shotgun taken from his grandmother's home. Police arrested the individual, while two chief prosecutors were appointed to investigate claims of bullying. The incident occurred amid heightened security following previous school shootings in the region.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen is targeting his first Formula One victory of the year at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix in Baku, following a recent karting triumph. The 28-year-old driver aims to break his victory duck on the unpredictable street circuit, where he and teammate Sergio Perez are the only drivers to have won more than once. Meanwhile, championship leader Kimi Antonelli enters the weekend with an 81-point lead over George Russell, while Verstappen's team looks to maximize performance against Mercedes.

Sir Jim Ratcliffe, owner of Ineos, has suspended production at three UK facilities, citing gas prices in the UK as twelve times higher than in the US and eight times higher than in China. The company stated that up to 1,000 staff could be affected, with two plants already shut and a third set to stop production in the coming days. Ratcliffe described the current government's energy policy as 'economic vandalism on an industrial scale' and called for tariff protections against Chinese products. The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade responded by highlighting existing support measures for the chemicals industry.

Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian vowed to firmly defend his country's positions at the UN General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, September 22, 2026. Speaking before departing, he stated that the Iranian people have stood their ground despite unfairness. He plans to convey Iran's plight to the international community on Wednesday. This visit marks the first time a high-ranking Iranian official has set foot on American soil since the West Asia war began in late February, although his communications team was denied visas.

Analysts at ING Bank assert that supply-side risks remain elevated despite a recent decline in crude oil prices. Brent Crude fell to $100 per barrel after Saudi Arabia shut a pipeline, yet higher-than-expected shipments eased concerns. Meanwhile, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent threatened Iranian airlines with service denials. Strategists Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey note that market dynamics balance hopes for peace talks against fresh disruptions in Libya, where output at the Sharara field was slashed to around 127,000 barrels per day.

Neha Bora, a PhD scholar and national president of the All India Students' Association, addressed a public meeting in Gorakhpur where she criticized Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Adityanath, calling him a 'goonda' and 'rioter.' Her remarks alleged that his administration presided over riots, unemployment, and persecution of minorities. The response was immediate: three police complaints were filed, BJP functionaries demanded an FIR, and Minister Om Prakash Rajbhar threatened her. Bora's organization, AISA, reported receiving death threats and filed a complaint with the Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police. The article defends Bora's speech as constitutionally protected, noting that Adityanath's government has withdrawn criminal cases involving himself and others, a practice the author describes as amoral. It contrasts Bora's sharp criticism with Adityanath's own rhetoric of force and religious polarization, arguing that holding power to account is central to democracy.

MOL Group has inaugurated a new 37. 4 MWp solar park and an associated electricity storage system rated at 20 MWp nominal and 40 MWh of storage capacity at its Algyő site in Hungary. This facility strengthens the group's renewable portfolio in Central Europe, enhancing electricity supply flexibility and reducing CO2 emissions by approximately 13,000 tonnes annually. The new solar park, combined with existing power plants at Algyő, can fully cover the electricity demand of the Algyő region.

The Indian rupee appreciated 20 paise to close at 95.58 against the U.S. dollar on Tuesday, September 22, 2026. This rise was supported by a sharp fall in crude oil prices following media reports that Iran might open the Strait of Hormuz if the U.S. lifts its blockade. Analyst Anuj Choudhary noted that while improved global risk sentiments support the currency, fresh tensions could limit gains, with the USD-INR spot price expected to trade between 95.30 and 95.80.

Nearly 21GWh of grid-scale battery energy storage systems were deployed globally in August, with China accounting for the majority of the capacity. European activity increased significantly, commissioning 18.2GWh, which is three times the amount installed in the same period last year. The data comes from Benchmark Mineral Intelligence, which reports monthly figures for ESN Premium.

The Madhya Pradesh Police issued sweeping guidelines restricting online activities for personnel to maintain discipline and protect the force's public image. Police Chief Kailash Makwana introduced rules prohibiting social media use during duty, banning posts in uniform or involving weapons, and restricting engagement with discriminatory content. Officers must report any income generated from social media within 30 days and cannot use AI tools for official purposes or share investigative details.

The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued an update regarding Cyclone Arnab, a deep depression currently over the Bay of Bengal. The agency reports that the system intensified into a depression and is expected to strengthen further within the next 10 hours. Officials state it is very likely to cross the north Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coasts between Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur as a deep depression by the night of September 23. Under the system's influence, heavy rains are forecast for isolated places in parts of Andhra Pradesh, including Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam, and Rayalaseema, from September 22 to 25. Residents are advised to follow the latest advisories from the IMD and local authorities.

The article discusses the shift from US-dominated AI development to a landscape seeking AI sovereignty. While US labs initially drove rapid expansion, open-weight models from Chinese entities like DeepSeek and Moonshot have disrupted this dominance. Concerns over power concentration have sparked discussions on sovereignty, defined as localized security and adherence to local laws. However, the Stanford HAI report notes that many sovereignty offerings still deepen dependencies on US tech. The piece argues that true sovereignty requires open source AI, specifically a federated system of models and protocols, to avoid fragmentation and ensure genuine participation across the entire AI stack.

Bihar Minister Shreyasi Singh faced widespread criticism after describing moral policing as 'decent and elegant' in response to a viral video showing the alleged harassment of two minors in Jamui. While Singh clarified that the manner of confrontation was unacceptable, opposition leaders including Pawan Khera and the Aam Aadmi Party accused her of defending the harassers. Police registered an FIR, arrested three minors, and formed a Special Investigation Team, while authorities warned against sharing footage that reveals minors' identities.

NVIDIA has announced DLSS 5, featuring 3D-Guided Neural Rendering designed to enhance lighting and material detail in real-time 3D rendering while preserving artistic intent. The technology operates on a one-frame-in, one-frame-out model and is available now in NBA 2K27. Concurrent updates include NVIDIA ACE, which expands speech and inference capabilities for interactive characters, and RTX Kit 2026.3, which introduces support for high-density geometry and neural texture workflows. Additionally, RTX Mega Geometry 2.0 enables streaming continuous level-of-detail clusters, set to arrive soon in Gears of War: E-Day to boost performance and image quality.

NVIDIA released Isaac ROS 5.0 at the ROSCon conference in Toronto to advance agentic, open-source robotics development. The update introduces new agentic workflows, platform support for ROS Lyrical and Ubuntu 24.04, and specialized skills like FoundationPose that enable AI agents to track objects up to 5.5x faster. By combining GPU-accelerated computing with familiar open-source tools, the platform aims to help developers deploy high-performance applications on edge devices like the NVIDIA Jetson. Several robotics companies, including Mentee Robotics and Universal Robots, are already integrating the system to accelerate perception and deployment.

OpenAI has expressed concern regarding the risks associated with AI systems that can improve themselves autonomously without safety measures. The company warns that such systems could grow faster than human understanding and oversight allows, potentially becoming uncontrollable and misaligned with human interests. OpenAI is calling for global technical standards and international cooperation to regulate advanced AI development, emphasizing the need for unified regulations across countries and both open and closed AI models to ensure safety and alignment with human values.

Tesla confirmed a bug in its v14.3.9 Full Self-Driving update that falsely flags clean cameras as dirty, prompting unnecessary service visits. The company is canceling these appointments and expects a fix in the upcoming v14.3.10 update, though release notes do not yet confirm specific changes. Drivers reported the alert on clean cars, often triggered by glare, while Tesla Support proactively canceled booked visits.

Nationalist Congress Party chief Sharad Pawar has publicly backed Noel Tata in his campaign to maintain Tata Sons as a private entity and safeguard the group's charitable ownership. Pawar, citing his role as a mediator in other industrial disputes, emphasized that the Tata group's Articles of Association must be respected, granting trust-nominated directors a decisive voice in appointing the chairman. He warned that weakening these trusts undermines essential institutions like the Tata Memorial Hospital. Meanwhile, the Shapoorji Pallonji group, holding an 18 per cent stake, has also called for the company's public listing, creating a divergence in opinions within the broader business community.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies for a collective ₹1.5 crore. The settlements address alleged violations concerning the disclosure of related-party transactions and audit report irregularities, including signing reports without valid peer review certificates. These issues stem from a 2023 Hindenburg Research report. The companies paid specific amounts, with Adani Enterprises paying ₹76.05 lakh and Adani Green Energy paying ₹45.50 lakh, while others paid ₹9.75 lakh each. The firms proposed settling without admitting or denying the findings.

Social media company X, formerly Twitter, has launched a feature allowing U.S. users to trade digital assets including Bitcoin and Ethereum. The platform redirects users to partner platforms such as Interactive Brokers and Gemini after they tap a crypto tag and a trade button. This move is part of X's broader plan to become an 'everything app' with banking features, as stated by Elon Musk. X currently offers real-time prices and charts for various cryptocurrencies.

Tesla's active robotaxi fleet in Austin has declined to just eight vehicles over the past seven days, according to data from community tracker Robotaxi Tracker. This figure mirrors the number present when the service launched in June 2025. Although Tesla registered 476 vehicles in Texas, including 67 Cybercabs, trackers have only observed 179 in the last 30 days and just eight carrying passengers recently. An unnamed source attributes the low operational numbers to safety concerns that prevent Tesla from deploying the system at scale, suggesting it is preferable to run a few vehicles in geo-fenced areas rather than risking accidents.

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari met industrialist Mukesh Ambani in Mumbai on Monday evening to discuss industrial prospects and employment generation. Adhikari, who posted about the visit on X, highlighted the state's readiness to welcome investments that empower youth and drive sustainable economic resurgence. The discussion included exchanging thoughts on industrial growth possibilities in West Bengal.

On September 22, Palo Alto Networks announced the launch of Unit 42 Continuous Frontier AI Defense, a cybersecurity service designed to help businesses identify security vulnerabilities. The offering utilizes advanced AI models from Anthropic, including Claude Mythos 5, and OpenAI, specifically GPT-5.6-Cyber, alongside open-weight models. The service continuously tests web applications, APIs, and cloud infrastructure to detect potential attack paths as digital environments evolve. Additionally, it provides guidance on fixing security gaps through code-level fixes and virtual patching options. The service will be available globally via annual subscriptions, with pricing determined by the selected mix of AI models.

Google has launched the Googlebook, a new line of premium laptops priced from $899 and up, designed to integrate its Gemini AI deeply into the laptop experience. Manufactured by partners including Acer, Asus, Dell, HP, and Lenovo, these devices feature 13- to 15-inch touch screens, up to 14 hours of battery life, and processors from Intel, Qualcomm, or MediaTek. Google aims to bridge the gap between Android phones and laptops, offering seamless syncing and on-device AI capabilities, with pre-installed Google AI Pro subscriptions included. The laptops are available for preorder starting Monday, with shipments in the US beginning Oct. 4.

The Reserve Bank of India issued amendments to valuation directions for Infrastructure Investment Trusts and Real Estate Investment Trusts to ensure uniform practices. Under the new framework, units are valued at the Net Asset Value disclosed by the trust. However, if a trust fails to compute or disclose the NAV as specified by SEBI regulations, or if units are classified as infrequently traded, their value is treated as Re 1. The changes take effect immediately and apply to both InvITs and REITs, with existing methodologies continuing for other unquoted instruments.

Samsung C&T has agreed to provide up to USD100 million through direct investment and engineering services to support Kairos Power's Hermes 2 demonstration plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. This investment strengthens Kairos Power's financial readiness for its fluoride salt-cooled high-temperature reactor technology. Additionally, Samsung C&T will join Kairos Power's engineering team, focusing on power-generation systems and balance-of-plant scope. The collaboration builds on a trilateral memorandum of understanding signed in August, aiming to establish a framework for reliable project execution and future commercial deployment.

Flipkart's official Instagram account accidentally posted a price tag of Rs. 7X,XXX for the iPhone 17 during a promotional carousel. This leaked figure is substantially lower than the expected Rs. 1,00,000 and Apple's current starting price of Rs. 99,900 in India. The post, intended to discuss phone myths, was published on September 22, 2026, by The Hindu businessline as a company press release. Social media users speculate the social media manager may face consequences for the error.

Google and Georgia Power have reached an agreement to support Extended Power Uprates at the Edwin I Hatch nuclear plant. Under the deal, Google will subscribe to a new tariff structure to receive zero-emission credits for the additional carbon-free power generated. The filings, lodged with the Georgia Public Service Commission on 21 September, include a request to approve the uprate for two units at Hatch. Georgia Power states the program is an innovation designed to help large customers meet clean energy goals while protecting non-participating customers from incremental costs.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies regarding alleged violations of related-party transaction disclosures and audit compliance. The settlement, totaling Rs 1.50 crore, stems from an examination into issues highlighted in the Hindenburg report. Adani Enterprises paid Rs 76.05 lakh, while Adani Green Energy paid Rs 45.50 lakh, with the remaining three firms paying Rs 9.75 lakh each.

Ireland's Data Protection Commission has fined Google €403 million for alleged violations regarding the handling of users' location information. The regulator determined the company failed to process this sensitive data in a lawful, fair, and transparent manner. The investigation, which began six years ago, examined Google's Web & App Activity and Location History services under the GDPR from 2018 until February 2020. Deputy Commissioner Graham Doyle noted that while location data offers benefits, it also reveals significant private information about individuals.

George Osborne, now leading AI at OpenAI, stated that datacentre nimbys are impeding Britain's development. Speaking at a festival in Somerset, he compared the resistance to building datacentres to opposition against roads and railways. While the government has classified AI datacentres as critical national infrastructure to expedite construction, the Green Party in England has called for a moratorium. Protesters across the UK, including in London and Edinburgh, argue these structures damage the landscape, consume excessive resources, and divert investment from affordable housing. Verity Harding from Cambridge University suggested the opposition stems from a lack of control rather than the technology itself.

The European System of Central Banks (ESCB) advised regulators to drop the requirement for stablecoin issuers to hold a minimum proportion of reserves as bank deposits. The ECB and other EU central banks stated that such deposits could expose lenders to runs and instability. Instead, they recommended specifying a minimum percentage held in assets maturing within one and five working days. This recommendation responds to a consultation on MiCA regulations.

mm2 Asia's proposed rescue investor, MMRA, has received a waiver from the Securities Industry Council to take control of the entertainment company without making a mandatory general offer. The placement involves subscribing for 16.34 billion new shares, with proceeds primarily allocated for debt repayment and working capital. This move aims to address mm2 Asia's financial difficulties and restore its viability as a going concern, pending independent shareholder approval.

Wall Street analysts anticipate Meta's new AI agent, Muse, will evolve into a major revenue engine. Since its launch, Meta Platforms shares have surged more than 20 per cent, outpacing major tech peers. Brokerages estimate that if Muse attracts 1 billion users by 2027 with a 3 per cent paid conversion rate, it could generate US$10.8 billion in annualised revenue. Analysts cite strong product-market fit and a free tier as drivers of early traction, noting 2.8 million downloads in the first 12 days.

Philip N. Jefferson, Oversight Governor for the Division of Monetary Affairs at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, delivered remarks at the 2026 Treasury Market Conference regarding the modernization of the Federal Reserve's discount window. He outlined three key dimensions of this initiative: business process improvements to standardize operations, automation enhancements through the Discount Window Direct portal which now handles over 60 percent of requests, and strengthened coordination with the Federal Home Loan Banks. Jefferson noted that these changes make borrowing faster and less burdensome, thereby reducing frictions that might cause healthy banks to hesitate. Furthermore, he stressed the critical role of the discount window in supporting Treasury market resilience, particularly by accepting Treasury securities as collateral with same-day value to prevent forced sales during market stress.

The 15-member UN Security Council is scheduled to convene in New York during the UN General Assembly's annual session. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman plans to address the session, according to Reuters. Diplomats also expect participation from senior Anthropic representatives. DeepSeek and fellow Chinese AI startup Moonshot have been invited to make statements, one source told Reuters. DeepSeek's founder, Liang Wenfeng, is not expected to be present, though arrangements could still shift, the source warned.

Tesla is facing a major race discrimination trial in California. The lawsuit, brought by California's Civil Rights Department, alleges the company allowed pervasive racial harassment and discrimination to go unchecked for years at its Fremont assembly plant, according to The Guardian.

Meta announced a test of its Community Notes program in sixteen Spanish-speaking countries across Latin America, citing US figures showing 1.4 million contributors and 200 million views in July. However, analysts argue the initiative lacks transparency, noting that only 50,000 notes were published against nearly 50 million EU fact-checks. The Oversight Board warned that Community Notes should not replace professional fact-checking, yet Meta has not defined success metrics or publication rates for the new rollout.

As world leaders convene for the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, an article argues that the focus on artificial intelligence risks must not overshadow the protection of undersea cables, which carry 99 percent of international data traffic. Recent incidents, including autonomous cyberattacks and physical cable cuts in the Red Sea and West Africa, have caused billions in damages and significant connectivity outages. While a new UN report provides 39 recommendations for enhancing cable resilience, these non-binding measures require governments to adopt legal frameworks and invest in repair infrastructure, a challenge particularly acute in regions like Africa where repair vessels are scarce. The author contends that safeguarding this critical infrastructure is essential for a robust AI governance agenda.

Research indicates that trading in U.S. Treasury securities is becoming increasingly concentrated on the last trading day of each month and around specific index strike times. This concentration has intensified over the past decade, with activity shifting from 3 p.m. to 4 p.m. following a change in strike time by a major fixed-income index provider in January 2021. The effects are most pronounced on month-end days when indexes are rebalanced, with the half-hour interval between 3:45 and 4:15 p.m. accounting for more than one quarter of total daily activity on these days in 2025. The authors conclude that index pricing conventions materially shape when Treasury trading occurs.

Heaps of foundry sand and mixed waste were discovered dumped on vacant plots along Chinniyampalayam–Irugur Road, near the Coimbatore International Airport runway. During a visit by The Hindu, officials found the waste at multiple spots on land acquired for airport expansion. An environmentalist stated that instead of dumping, the waste's suitability for reuse should be assessed. Conversely, a District Rural Development Agency official claimed the administration was unaware of the dumping and promised to inspect the site soon.

JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon has urged the United States to rethink imposing steep tariffs on Indian buyers of Russian oil. Speaking at a conference in Mumbai, Dimon warned that punishing India could disrupt global oil markets and that Indian refineries cannot easily switch to alternative crude grades. This comes after US President Donald Trump signed legislation allowing tariffs of up to 100 per cent on major Russian energy buyers. In response, Indian Ambassador Vinay Mohan Kwatra stated that India's energy policy prioritizes the security and affordability of energy for its people, noting that the country imports over 85 per cent of its crude oil.

The US has empowered President Donald Trump with a new tool under sanctions law to target nations purchasing Russian oil and gas, potentially impacting India. While headlines suggest a 100% tariff, the law does not automatically impose this on Indian goods. Instead, it serves as a conditional weapon Washington may use if statutory conditions are met, creating uncertainty for Indian industries and exports.

The Karnataka State Dalit Sangharsh Samiti (DSS) strongly condemned former MP Pratap Simha for remarks against the Dalit community and the wearing of blue scarves, describing them as highly objectionable. Speaking at a press conference, DSS State convener D.G. Sagar stated that Simha's comments reflected a deep disregard for the history of Karnataka's Dalit movement. Sagar demanded an unconditional apology and warned that such statements could provoke communal tensions. He also opposed a proposed Hindu Samavesha in Kalaburagi city.

The Jammu and Kashmir government informed the Assembly on September 22, 2026, that it had screened approximately 21.81 lakh books and withdrawn 4,812 from government and private college libraries since July. The withdrawn collection included 518 banned books and 4,249 non-banned books. Officials described the scrutiny process as laborious and noted that at least 1,752 books were referred for expert examination. The action follows directives to identify material violating religious sentiments or laws, triggered by allegations of inappropriate content in books under a central scheme.

The Ministry of External Affairs stated Pakistan must take credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world believes its claims. MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal accused Pakistan of misrepresenting facts and spreading falsehoods regarding a Permanent Court of Arbitration ruling, calling it an illegally constituted court. Jaiswal noted India seeks constructive ties with Bangladesh and provided updates on missing Indians in Nepal, where a forensic team is working on samples.

The Election Commission announced polls for twelve Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal, with voting scheduled for October 16. Analysis suggests the BJP-led alliance will likely retain eight seats in Uttar Pradesh, while the Samajwadi Party could win two. The BJP is also expected to gain a seat in West Bengal following the resignation of the incumbent. These elections may mark the end of the BSP's representation in Parliament due to vacancies and term expirations.

Tan Tock Seng Hospital's initiative to manage delirium at home highlights a broader need for improved health literacy among Singapore's aging population. The author argues that while bringing care closer to home is vital, families and caregivers must also be equipped to recognize significant changes in cognition or function. Practical health literacy should extend beyond basic knowledge to include identifying medical issues like delirium and knowing where to seek help, ensuring capability moves into the community alongside care.

Embassy Developments announced a Memorandum of Understanding to sell an entire G+7 residential tower in Juhu to Dinesh Thakkar, founder of Angel One. The deal, valued at approximately Rs 711 crore, covers a carpet area of 63,000 sq ft and is described as the largest single residential unit transaction in the country. The project, named 'Angelus', is part of a larger five-tower development in the Mumbai Metropolitan Region scheduled for completion by December 2031.

TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will host five specialized sessions focused on AI safety and security as the technology transitions from demonstrations to critical business applications. These sessions, scheduled for the AI Stage and Real World AI Stage, address challenges such as enterprise deployment hurdles, agent security infrastructure, cloud complexity, and physical system reliability. Industry leaders from companies like Anthropic, Okta, AWS, Shield AI, and GM will share insights on building trustworthy AI. The event runs October 13–15 at Moscone West in San Francisco, attracting over 10,000 attendees including founders, investors, and tech leaders.

AstroForge is developing an autonomous control stack called 'Solo' to operate its spacecraft without ground intervention, addressing communication difficulties experienced with its Odin mission in 2025. The company plans to launch its first autonomous spacecraft in 2027, which will rely on an in-house transformer-based model trained on approximately 2,500 sensors. CEO Matthew Gialich stated the company is removing Earth-based radio reception for this mission to test full onboard intelligence, despite the risks associated with neural network reliability in space.

Ben Black, CEO of the US International Development Finance Corporation, stated that the US can still compete with China in African markets despite Beijing's established presence. Speaking at The Next 3 Billion in New York, Black pointed to recent investments in African digital networks, Ukrainian energy storage, and uranium in Niger as examples of how the DFC balances risk and value for American taxpayers. He argued that falling behind does not mean ceding territory, noting that the agency structures deals around market risks to advance US interests.

Donald Trump addressed world leaders at the United Nations in New York, framing his second term as a period of decisive action against perceived threats. He claimed to have defanged Iran militarily and threatened to annihilate the regime if it does not capitulate. Trump also touted his border security record, stating zero illegal aliens were admitted in the past 16 months. However, his interventionist policies in Latin America, including the raid on Venezuela and sanctions on Cuba, drew sharp criticism from other leaders like Brazil's Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, who defended the sovereignty of those nations.

Boominathan, 45, died of injuries at Ramanathapuram Government Medical College Hospital on Sunday after being assaulted by his wife Revathi during a domestic altercation. Police stated the couple had a history of quarrels due to financial setbacks and alcohol addiction. Revathi allegedly struck him with a wooden log on Monday morning. She called an ambulance, but he died. Police arrested Revathi and granted her bail. In a separate incident, a 25-year-old man named Sakthivel Pandi was stabbed to death in Mandalamanickam village over a feud originating from a Kabaddi tournament two years ago. Police arrested Murugan and his sons in that case.

Xbox announced it is cutting hundreds of jobs and restructuring its studios as part of a company-wide reset. Consequently, Activision will take over development of future Halo games, while the current Halo studio will focus on supporting existing titles. Xbox chief executive Asha Sharma stated the gaming division had not been healthy, citing rising hardware costs as a pressure. Analysts view the move as a significant shift for the franchise.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres delivered a final address to the 81st session of the UN General Assembly on September 22, 2026, calling for urgent reform of the UN Security Council. He argued that the body, established in 1945, fails to reflect today's geopolitical realities, specifically noting the absence of permanent African representation. Guterres pointed to deep divisions among permanent members like the U.S., China, Russia, France, and the U.K., which have rendered the Council ineffective in halting conflicts in Gaza and Russia. He warned that without a multilateral system centered on the UN that reflects current power dynamics, humanity faces a trajectory of fragmentation and mistrust in an increasingly multipolar world.

Yemen's Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out a deadly airstrike on a key port city on Tuesday, an event occurring over a week into a broader offensive that has seen the group seize control of a crucial strait. The conflict has displaced nearly 130,000 people across seven governorates and resulted in at least 154 deaths in the past two days, according to military sources. While Houthi sources reported 118 deaths in specific governorates, government sources cited 36 killed in their ranks. In response, G7 nations urged the Houthis to halt cross-border strikes and return to the political process. Meanwhile, the UK and France have agreed to provide military support to Saudi Arabia to help secure its energy infrastructure, though France clarified this does not involve direct participation in the conflict.

Speaking at the United Nations General Assembly, US President Donald Trump called on all nations to impose a complete economic blockade on Iran, which he labeled the number one sponsor of terror. He contrasted his actions with other world leaders, claiming he has made peace and confronted threats. Trump also mentioned upcoming talks with British and Japanese leaders, as well as Gulf Cooperation Council nations, amid concerns over Iran-backed attacks on Saudi Arabia.

Lib Dem leader Davey announced a plan to raise the tax-free personal allowance to £15,000, funded entirely by economic growth generated from rejoining the EU single market. He stated the proposal would take an additional 2 million people out of paying income tax, providing a £680 cut to most taxpayers. However, he noted that due to the time required to make a deal with the EU, the actual tax cuts would only happen in the final year of a parliament, potentially as late as 2034. Davey contrasted this with the Reform party's proposal, criticizing them for suggesting such cuts be funded by removing £22 billion of support from disabled people. He emphasized his party's commitment to paying for the cuts fairly and honestly, rather than through borrowing or stealth tax hikes.

The European Commission has presented a package of measures to improve the energy efficiency of data centers and their integration into the European electricity system. The package includes a delegated regulation establishing a common classification and labeling system for data centers with an installed IT power demand of more than 500 kW. A public consultation on future minimum energy-performance standards is also underway. The Commission estimates that recovering waste heat from European data centers could meet the needs of approximately 4 million households.

The Nepali government has requested $20m from the UN loss-and-damage fund following devastating floods in late August that killed more than 1,400 people. According to Carbon Brief analysis, this request covers only 0.7% of the estimated $2.7bn in physical damage and economic losses, or 0.3% of total recovery needs including $4.8bn in reconstruction costs. While Nepal's claim makes it the fourth-largest to the fund, developing countries have requested $2.8bn total, yet predominantly developed nations have pledged only $822m. As of September, no money has been distributed to any country facing climate-related disasters, raising questions about the fund's ability to respond to emergencies.

Fortis Energy and İnelso Energy Systems have signed a joint agreement with Turkish EPC contractor Enkraft Energy to construct a 30 MWp solar power plant combined with a battery energy storage system in Serbia's Vojvodina region. The EUR 25. 5 million project has reached ready-to-build status, with construction permits expected within a month. Once operational, the facility is projected to generate more than 40 GWh of electricity annually, equivalent to the consumption of over 11,000 households, while avoiding an estimated 19,000 tonnes of CO2 emissions per year.

The Greenville County Coroner's Office in South Carolina completed an autopsy on Hayden Panettiere, confirming she died from the toxic effects of fentanyl, Xanax, and several other drugs. The coroner stated the death was an accident with no signs of trauma. Panettiere, 36, was found unresponsive at a residence last month. Emergency responders attempted advanced cardiac life support, but resuscitation was unsuccessful. Her ex-boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, and his brother were present when services arrived. Panettiere had previously spoken openly about her struggles with substance abuse and postpartum depression.

Terawatt PV Research forecasts that Inflation Reduction Act-stimulated capital expenditure for U.S. solar manufacturing will reach $12.2 billion by the end of 2026. This cumulative figure represents more than half of all solar PV manufacturing spending since 2001. Annual spending has exceeded $2.5 billion since 2023, with 2024 recording a record $4.14 billion, primarily driven by First Solar and Qcells. The report projects Texas will emerge as the dominant hub for module production in 2026, surpassing Ohio, as the industry expands its domestic capacity.

US President Donald Trump is shifting his strategy regarding Greenland from seeking territorial acquisition to securing a permanent US military security arrangement. He is set to sign a trilateral agreement with Denmark and Greenland at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The pact allows the US to establish military facilities at Narsarsuaq and Mestersvig, expanding its footprint beyond the existing Pituffik Space Base. While Danish officials assert the agreement respects sovereignty and places security under NATO's collective responsibility, the full legal implications remain unclear. The deal marks a major shift from Trump's earlier demands for ownership, which were firmly rejected by Greenlandic and Danish leaders.

Anna Tims, a consumer champion for the Guardian, hosts a live session to address reader inquiries regarding customer service. She notes that while AI tools can assist with troubleshooting, they often fail to resolve specific complaints, leading to repetitive platitudes. Tims advises customers to remain calm, gather all relevant evidence such as booking references, and utilize public platforms like Twitter to pressure companies into action. She highlights that although legal frameworks like the Consumer Rights Act 2015 exist, regulatory bodies are frequently overstretched. Consequently, she suggests patronizing companies that demonstrate exceptional service and checking for proper contact details before committing to a provider.

Joshua Foster, a British man from Essex, pleaded guilty to causing the death of his two-year-old son through a reckless act at the King Evelthon Beach Hotel and Resort in Chlorakas, Cyprus. The boy fell from the fourth floor on 12 July. Foster admitted the charge to avoid a lengthy trial. His lawyer stated the plea allows the family to move forward without reliving the tragedy in court. A further hearing is scheduled for 5 October.

Turkish Minister of Environment, Urbanization and Climate Change Murat Kurum outlined the COP31 Action Agenda, which targets raising the share of electricity in final energy consumption to 35% by 2035. Kurum stressed the need for responsible artificial intelligence deployment to advance clean technologies. The agenda also includes goals to halve municipal waste increases and reduce building energy-use intensity by at least 25%.

Footage shows flooded streets and rescue efforts following Typhoon Dujuan, which brought torrential rain to the Tokyo region. The storm triggered landslides in Chiba and Kanagawa prefectures, swamped roads, and caused flight cancellations and transport delays. Officials confirmed at least four deaths and six missing persons on Tuesday as search and rescue teams worked in affected neighborhoods. Thousands of homes lost power due to record-breaking rainfall disrupting travel across the capital region.

U.S. President Donald Trump is expected to deliver a speech at the United Nations on September 22, 2026, where he will defend his ongoing war with Iran and highlight his efforts as a peacemaker. The event is overshadowed by concerns over the war's failure to meet White House objectives and economic damage from the Strait of Hormuz closure. Analysts from the International Crisis Group suggest Trump will contrast his peacemaker claims with military operations, while facing skepticism over a security deal in Greenland. Trump also plans to meet with leaders from Britain, Ukraine, Japan, and Venezuela.

The Meghalaya High Court ordered the state government to transfer approximately 30 foreign nationals who completed their prison sentences but remained incarcerated to a temporary detention centre in Shillong by September 28. The court, hearing a suo motu matter, directed the transfer to the MBOSE Hostel facility, which has a capacity for around 60 inmates. Authorities were instructed to assist with deportation or repatriation and to address compensation for those detained beyond their sentence completion dates. The matter was posted for further hearing on September 28.

India's Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that Pakistan must demonstrate credible action against cross-border terrorism before the world believes its promises. This demand follows Pakistani airstrikes in eastern Afghanistan's Kunar and Paktika provinces, which India condemned as aggression against a sovereign neighbor. The attacks reportedly killed at least three civilians, a toll confirmed by the United Nations, while Pakistan claimed the strikes killed 28 militants. India reaffirmed its steadfast support for Afghanistan's independence and territorial integrity.

JSW Group has entered the electric commercial vehicle market through its new subsidiary, JSW Greentech Limited, which will operate under the Ampstar brand. The company invested ₹2,500 crore to build a manufacturing facility in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Maharashtra, with an annual capacity of 15,000 vehicles. Senior executives stated that production is scheduled to commence in October 2026. At peak utilization, the facility is expected to generate a turnover of around ₹12,000 crore. The group aims to reduce India's dependence on imported fossil fuels by promoting domestic power generation.

Nordex is expanding its Delta4000 onshore wind turbine range with the N193/7.X variant, which combines a 193m rotor with a maximum nominal capacity of 7.3 MW. Designed for medium- and low-wind sites, the turbine uses 95m single-piece blades and retains components from the established platform while allowing flexible power configurations. Nordex states the new model can deliver up to 14% higher energy yield than the N175/6.X at typical low- to medium-wind sites. Serial production is scheduled to begin in 2029, with a specific 6.6 MW configuration planned for Germany to address permitting and grid-connection requirements.

A military aircraft reportedly crashed near the US Air Base Spangdahlem in Germany on Tuesday. Local authorities in the Eifel region initially stated that one person was injured. The Eifel District dispatched fire and emergency response teams but declined to comment on further details. The US Air Force did not immediately respond to a request for comment regarding the incident.

At AI Day Singapore, NVIDIA and partners showcased breakthrough AI advancements across Southeast Asia. The event highlighted initiatives to move public sector AI from pilot to production, with partners like Singapore's HTX utilizing Nemotron models for public safety. Other organizations, including NCS and ST Engineering, are deploying agentic AI and smart city solutions. Additionally, Sea Limited became the first ASEAN enterprise to adopt the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform, aiming to scale AI capabilities for its platforms serving hundreds of millions of users. The event emphasized building region-specialized AI models tailored to local languages and industries.

Oracle's recent layoffs in its cloud infrastructure business have shed light on the age profiles of affected workers. According to a Business Insider report, an internal document listed the job titles and ages of 546 employees from Oracle's America Cloud Infrastructure organization who were laid off. These individuals represent approximately 7.6% of the 7,185 people within the organization, indicating a significant portion of the workforce impacted by the cuts.

Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5, an AI model it claims delivers performance comparable to its top-tier Fable 5.1 while costing 40% less to run. The company stated the model underwent external testing by independent AI safety research groups Frontier Design and METR before launch. Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, 20% below Opus 5.

According to unattributed reporting, the trade war initiated by the U.S. against China and other partners has eased since President Donald Trump implemented his "liberation day" tariffs in April 2025. Data indicates a rise in Chinese imports to the U.S. for five straight months, with August marking the latest increase. However, the report notes that tensions remain, particularly concerning key technology industries.

S&P Global Ratings has raised India's GDP growth forecast for the financial year 2026-27 to 7.0%, up from 6.6%. The agency attributes this revision to robust industrial activity, healthy domestic consumption, and strong exports. Economists at S&P Global also project the Reserve Bank of India to hike the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%. This projection exceeds the Reserve Bank's estimate of 6.7% and aligns with forecasts from Moody's, reflecting economic resilience despite external challenges.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa was captured on camera scrolling through Instagram and interacting with his phone while Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan delivered his address at the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York. The moment occurred during the high-level General Debate on September 22, 2026, drawing attention to the informal scene involving the Syrian leader. Al-Sharaa, serving as Syria's interim president since early 2025, was attending his second UN General Assembly as part of Syria's new leadership seeking to strengthen international diplomatic engagement.

Actress Apple Chan announced on Instagram that she gave birth to a baby girl at 32 weeks following an emergency C-section. The 37-year-old revealed the pregnancy was complicated, noting the baby weighed 1.1kg at 31 weeks before her water broke. Chan expressed her love and support for her daughter, who she described as a 'little fighter,' while also mentioning her two-year-old son.

Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff stated on a podcast that Microsoft's 27% stake in OpenAI blocked Salesforce from investing in the rival AI firm. Consequently, Salesforce invested in Anthropic, which is now valued at $965 billion. Benioff noted that this investment could earn Salesforce billions of dollars, while Salesforce continues to add OpenAI capabilities to its own platforms.

Incredible Holdings filed an application with the Singapore High Court to place the company under judicial management, proposing the appointment of Ellyn Tan Huixian and Terrence Chin Khee Loon of Forvis Mazars Consulting as joint managers. The company stated that independent director Eunice Veon Koh Pei Lee is assisting investigations by the Commercial Affairs Department and the Monetary Authority of Singapore into alleged offences under the Securities and Futures Act. Shares have been suspended since September 2022, and the company is in breach of listing rules due to missed meetings.

The China-ASEAN Expo offers a diverse array of discoveries ranging from coffee and snacks to handicrafts, cultural traditions, and new technologies. Beyond showcasing their own offerings, ASEAN businesses are actively looking to China for products, technology, market opportunities, and new partners. CGTN's Wang Tao invites visitors to explore the event and witness these interactions firsthand.

Anthropic and OpenAI have intensified competition with the release of new AI models. Anthropic launched Claude Opus 5.5, which features a 20% price reduction and improved communication style, while OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. These new models are priced at half the cost of their GPT-5.6 predecessors, with GPT-6 Luna costing $0.10 for input and $0.50 for output per million tokens. However, the author noted that Claude Opus 5.5's 'max' reasoning mode failed to complete a simple SVG generation task, hitting a token limit prematurely.

Singapore's core inflation climbed to 2.2% in August, up from 2% in July, driven by higher inflation in services, retail goods, and food, according to the Singapore Department of Statistics. While overall inflation increased to 2.3%, private transport inflation slowed to 7.5% due to smaller car price increases. Analysts attribute the broader price pressures to elevated global energy prices and supply chain disruptions, warning that households could face further electricity tariff increases in the fourth quarter as businesses pass on higher input costs.

A Porsche 718 Boxster EV prototype was spotted charging at a Tesla Supercharger in Carson, California, sparking speculation about the vehicle's release timing. Porsche CEO Michael Leiters confirmed plans to build the model, stating it is the best economic solution, though official sales details remain unannounced. The sighting supports rumors that Porsche is moving toward NACS-only charging for its smaller sportscars, potentially replacing dual-port setups found on current models. While the car remains under consideration, the prototype has been tested on public tracks and observed in public spaces, indicating progress toward production.

NVIDIA Topograph is an open-source toolkit that discovers and normalizes cluster network topology to enable topology-aware workload scheduling. By mapping physical interconnects like NVIDIA NVLink and Spectrum-X Ethernet, it allows schedulers to place GPUs in optimal locations, reducing latency and costs in AI factories. The tool supports Kubernetes, Slurm, and Slinky, integrating with systems like KAI Scheduler and Node Feature Discovery to automate placement decisions based on current fabric data.

बैंकों ने फेस्टिव सेल के दौरान बढ़ रहे AI शॉपिंग टूल्स के उपयोग से जुड़े फ्रॉड और डेटा प्राइवेसी जोखिमों के बारे में चेतावनी दी है। Reuters की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, NatWest, Bank of America, ING, ASB Bank, Capital One और Commonwealth Bank of Australia जैसे बैंकों ने सुरक्षा मानकों की कमी पर चिंता जताई है। OpenAI, Anthropic, Google और Meta जैसे टेक कंपनियां इन टूल्स को बढ़ावा दे रही हैं। ग्राहकों को ऑफर की शर्तों और वेबसाइट की विश्वसनीयता की जांच करने की सलाह दी गई है।

The Securities and Exchange Board of India settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group companies for a combined ₹1.51 crore regarding disclosure lapses. The companies settled without admitting or denying findings. Other updates include IRB Infrastructure approving non-core asset monetization, RailTel receiving a ₹14.09 crore work order, Persistent Systems crossing a Nagarro takeover threshold, and leadership changes at 360 ONE WAM.

Petrobras announced in August that it identified signs of oil in a well 175 kilometers off the coast of northern Brazil's Amapa state. Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva visited the area, calling the find a 'passport to the future.' However, reactions are mixed. Karipuna, a local resident, fears an 'immense disaster' if a leak reaches the Curipi River, while fishermen worry about market access. Petrobras stated that analyses do 'not indicate the probability' of oil reaching the coast in a spill, though Jean Paul Prates noted the risk is low-probability but high-consequence. Production is not expected to begin for another 'six or seven years,' yet the discovery has already intensified population growth and real estate speculation in Oiapoque, where the mayor estimates 40,000 to 45,000 people now live.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney indicated that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is likely to visit Canada in December to seal a trade deal. Speaking at the UN General Assembly, Carney described the relationship as exceptionally important. Union Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal confirmed that the fourth round of negotiations concluded in Mumbai, with the fifth round scheduled to begin on October 5. Negotiations had paused in August 2023 but restarted in 2025 following a thaw in diplomatic relations.

The Human Rights Forum (HRF) condemned Meta for restricting the Instagram account of the 'Stop Vizag Data Centers' campaign in India on September 19. HRF representatives alleged that the action, along with restrictions on nine other posts, curtailed public scrutiny of hyperscale data center projects under India's Information Technology Rules. The campaign, launched in July, attracted 56 lakh views and 11,800 followers in two months. HRF State general secretary Y. Rajesh and V.S. Krishna demanded that Meta restore the account and disclose the legal basis for the restriction.

OpenAI and Anthropic have released new AI models aimed at lowering costs for enterprise customers. These updates focus on efficiency and speed rather than introducing groundbreaking capabilities. Anthropic's Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 and $20 per million for input and output tokens, a 20% reduction from the previous version, while cache reads are 60% cheaper.

The 48th WorldSkills Competition officially opened in Shanghai on Tuesday evening. The event is scheduled to run from September 23 to 27, featuring nearly 1,400 young professionals representing 68 countries and regions. Organizers state that this year's competition will set four historical records regarding the number of competitions, new events, participating nations, and competitors.

Microsoft announced on Tuesday that it will grant the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency direct, on-site access to its latest quantum computing hardware. This access occurs at a new research center in Maryland opened alongside the University of Maryland. The facility houses a system using the Majorana 2 chip for independent testing and evaluation. Microsoft stated it plans to have commercial quantum systems ready by 2029, while DARPA aims to determine if quantum approaches can yield economically feasible systems by 2033.

Tesla has been named the primary supplier for the largest electric Class 8 order in US history, comprising 2,500 battery-electric trucks purchased through the ZET SCALE alliance. This deal nearly doubles the current number of such trucks on US roads. However, while demand is high, production capacity remains the constraint, with analysts expecting Tesla to deliver only 5,000 to 15,000 Semis in 2026 at a quoted price of around $290,000 per Long Range truck. The orders will be deployed across ten freight hubs over the next few years.

Microsoft announced Tuesday that it led an industry-wide disruption of EvilTokens, a subscription-based scam platform utilizing an AI chatbot to compromise 12,000 Microsoft accounts over a few-month span. Introduced via a Telegram channel in February, the platform charged an initial $1,500 fee and a recurring $500 monthly charge. It helped criminals analyze inboxes and draft fraudulent emails to trick employees into transferring funds. Microsoft, with assistance from SpyCloud, seized 50 websites and 150 domains. The UK's Metropolitan Police Service arrested two men on suspicion of offenses connected to the platform.

Effingham County residents and environmental advocates have filed a second lawsuit challenging the OpenAI data center project, known as Project Camellia. The new suit targets the Effingham County Industrial Development Authority, alleging it failed to provide proper public notice and meaningful participation opportunities during the project's approval process. While the project has received key approvals and a significant tax break, plaintiffs argue that major decisions were negotiated behind closed doors. OpenAI plans to build a massive campus near Rincon, Georgia, which will require substantial electricity and water resources, prompting concerns about environmental impacts and grid strain. The project is expected to begin construction in 2028.

OpenAI has expanded its GPT-6 generation with updated Sol and Luna models, emphasizing improved efficiency and affordability. The company states that these models offer half the cost of the previous 5.6 series and demonstrate better factual accuracy and lower error rates in coding. OpenAI also claims its new offerings outperform Anthropic's models, noting intense competition in the AI sector.

President Trump declared support for a potential ban on diesel fuel exports as prices hit record highs. While Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent noted the administration is considering the ban's effectiveness, Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum oppose it. Alaska Senator Dan Sullivan called for a temporary pause to rebuild reserves. The national U.S. average for diesel reached $6.5276 according to AAA.

Actor and activist Prakash Raj launched a 10-day 'SIR Resistance Tour' in Kalaburagi to protest the deletion of voters during Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision. Raj claimed 5,21,950 voters were placed in the ASDDO category and argued existing voters should not re-register via Form 6. He highlighted disparities in how officials treat prominent citizens versus marginalized communities and plans to submit findings to the Chief Minister on September 30.

Samsung India Electronics reported a 36% decline in profit to ₹7,228.10 crore for the financial year ended March 31, 2026, according to a RoC filing. Although overall revenue from operations rose slightly by 1.2%, the company's primary revenue driver, the mobile phone business, saw a 1.35% decrease. Conversely, revenue from home appliances and audio-visual segments increased, reflecting a strategic focus on diversifying beyond smartphones. The company remains the only player in the Indian appliance space with turnover exceeding ₹1 lakh crore.

The Reserve Bank of India absorbed ₹71,971 crore from the banking system through an overnight Variable Reverse Repo Rate auction held on September 22, 2026. The auction, totaling ₹75,000 crore, received offers for 96% of the amount at a rate of 5.24%. This move aims to manage excess liquidity, which can be inflationary, particularly following a $133 billion inflow from NRI special deposits, and to synchronize overnight call money rates with the repo rate ahead of a potential rate hike cycle.

A webpage dated 22nd September 2026 lists recent articles concerning artificial intelligence developments. The entries mention the release of Claude Opus 5.5 and various GPT-6 models, a new pricing strategy, and a novel LLM architecture called System One introduced by Jev on 21st September 2026.

India is accelerating trade negotiations with Canada and Mexico to diversify commercial ties and mitigate the impact of US tariff policies. Negotiators plan to hold a fifth round of talks with Canada starting October 5, building on recent discussions. Separately, India is finalizing a framework with Mexico to begin formal negotiations. Officials aim to make faster progress as all three countries seek new markets and partners.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced that trade negotiations with India are making good progress, with both countries aiming to conclude talks by the G20 summit in mid-December. Carney noted that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to visit Canada around that time. These efforts follow a deep diplomatic rupture over the 2023 killing of activist Hardeep Singh Nijjar. Carney has moved quickly to rebuild ties, marking his first bilateral visit to India since 2018.

Anthropic released Opus 5.5, a new model claiming state-of-the-art performance in coding and knowledge work that outperforms its larger Fable model in many benchmarks. The new model is significantly cheaper than its predecessor, with output tokens charged at $20 per million tokens compared to $25 for the previous version. CEO Dario Amodei stated the release reflects a commitment to pacing AI capabilities to match risk prevention progress. The launch occurs two months after Opus 5, with Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 expected in the coming weeks.

Microsoft's Digital Crimes Unit, alongside the Health-ISAC, law enforcement, and SpyCloud, disrupted the EvilTokens phishing-as-a-service platform. The operation targeted a threat actor that compromised over 12,000 Microsoft accounts across more than 10,000 organizations. EvilTokens utilized device-code authentication to bypass security measures, enabling sophisticated business email compromise campaigns. Following the investigation, two suspects aged 32 and 38 were arrested in the U.K. and released on bail. While the infrastructure was seized, Microsoft noted the threat remains active, though attack volumes are expected to decrease. The platform offered customizable phishing kits and targeted sectors including finance, healthcare, and education.

The Election Commission in New Delhi rejected reports suggesting internal differences over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), asserting that all decisions were taken unanimously. While Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised concerns about voter roll deletion, the Commission maintained these did not constitute disagreement. Conversely, opposition parties, including the Samajwadi Party and Mamata Trinamool Congress, alleged the SIR targeted specific electors and called for the impeachment of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney indicated that trade negotiations between Canada and India are advancing well, with both governments aiming to finalize a deal by the G20 summit scheduled for mid-December. Carney described the bilateral relationship as exceptionally important and suggested that Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi would visit Canada around that time, although the exact date has not been finalized. This diplomatic push follows a previous rupture over the killing of a Canadian Sikh activist, with Carney emphasizing efforts to rebuild ties and reduce dependence on the United States.

India is exporting digital public infrastructure frameworks to more than 24 countries, yet it lacks a domestic legal definition for these systems. While policy documents describe digital public infrastructure, no statute currently determines what constitutes such a system or what legal safeguards must attach to it. This gap affects hybrid platforms like the Unified Payments Interface and Digi Yatra, which operate with state backing but fall outside the Right to Information Act. Experts warn that exporting a system without a clear legal foundation risks establishing a flawed global standard and leaves citizens without adequate data protection or accountability mechanisms.

Databricks has introduced Genie One MCP to address the limitations of general-purpose AI assistants in interpreting business data. Without specific context, these agents struggle to trust sources or understand metrics, as highlighted by the difficulty in answering questions about revenue declines. Genie One MCP connects assistants like ChatGPT and Microsoft Copilot to Genie Ontology, a governed layer within Databricks. This integration provides approved definitions, trusted data relationships, and permission-aware access controls. Consequently, organizations can define business meaning once in Genie Ontology and apply it across an evolving AI ecosystem, ensuring reliable and traceable answers while respecting user access policies.

Databricks has announced the general availability of the Genie One Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, designed to provide unified business context for AI agents. Grounded in Genie Ontology, the protocol allows agents to access structured and unstructured data consistently, regardless of the specific tool they use. Fenny Sanyoto, Engineering Manager at GetYourGuide, noted that this integration maintains high analysis quality across different AI tools. The MCP serves as a governed entry point, eliminating friction caused by agent sprawl and ensuring that agents rely on a single, trusted enterprise context layer rather than fragmented or stale definitions.

vLLM is introducing a new set of hardware-agnostic layers to balance the need for state-of-the-art performance on frontier GPUs with the requirement to support diverse models and older hardware. The project acknowledges that current abstractions are becoming incompatible with the rapidly diverging architectures of frontier models. By implementing these portable layers, vLLM aims to maintain support for out-of-tree accelerators and older GPUs while enabling faster development of hardware-specific optimizations. Experiments on NVIDIA H100 GPUs show that these new layers achieve total token throughput within 3.4% of native implementations, demonstrating that portability does not come at a significant performance cost. This solution allows vLLM to continue serving its broad user base without compromising on the speed of innovation for the latest GPU benchmarks.

Anthropic has released Claude Opus 5.5, an update to its AI model that the company claims delivers Fable 5.1 performance for most work while costing about 40% less to run. The model reportedly uses a third of the tokens compared to the previous Opus 5 version and generates output more than 30% faster. Users and developers have noted improvements in coding efficiency and bug detection, with one engineer stating the model writes like a good colleague. Anthropic also highlights enhanced safety measures, including extensive alignment testing and safeguards for high-risk areas like cybersecurity and biology. Additionally, the company announced the upcoming launch of Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5, with Opus 5.5 available immediately.

Diesel prices in the United States have reached record highs, averaging $6.52 per gallon, according to AAA. This surge has sparked a growing call to combat the climb by banning fuel exports, a move President Donald Trump endorsed today. While the White House previously stated it was not considering an export ban, it remains unclear if Trump's statements change that stance. Experts offer conflicting views; Jeff Colgan suggests a ban could boost supply and lower prices, while Patrick De Haan argues U.S. prices are determined globally and a ban would not change the world price. Additionally, some lawmakers and industry groups warn that export bans could reduce fuel production and weaken energy security.

Recent heavy rains and strong winds in Mumbai led to a surge in tree-fall incidents, with 902 trees uprooted and three fatalities in a single week. While the BMC commissioner attributed the falls to wind speeds, experts argue that poor planning, including concretised tree bases and unscientific pruning, are the primary causes. Despite previous court orders mandating de-concretisation and a tree census, implementation remains incomplete, with over 60% of inspected trees in Mumbai still concretised. This has prompted calls for a fundamental shift in urban management to treat trees as part of the city's ecosystem.

A political controversy emerged after Election Commissioners Vivek Joshi and Sukhbir Singh Sandhu raised objections to unilateral decisions and procedural changes within the Election Commission of India.
