In response, the Commission clarified that the Special Intensive Revision exercise was conducted collectively with unanimous approval. Former Chief Election Commissioner O.P. Rawat addressed the issues, noting that identifying illegal immigrants falls under the Ministry of Home Affairs and urging the body to address concerns transparently to rebuild public confidence.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan hosted a trilateral meeting with Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Saudi Foreign Minister Prince Faisal bin Farhan in New York. The event took place on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly at the Turkish House, Türkiye’s diplomatic hub in New York City. The Foreign Ministry announced the meeting via its social media platform NSosyal.

German and French private sector activity increased in September, with Germany reaching an 11-month high and France showing its fastest pace of growth in over two years. While services sectors in both nations drove expansion, German manufacturing output eased to a two-month low, and French employment continued to decline despite improved demand.

As fighting escalates in Yemen's long-running conflict, thousands of families have been displaced from their homes, often for the second or third time. In Aden, Arwa described her family's flight from Mocha after it was seized by Iran-backed Houthi fighters. They traveled 200 kilometers on a single motorcycle to reach the temporary seat of the Saudi-backed government.

Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov arrived in New York on Tuesday, September 23, 2026, to address the 81st session of the UN General Assembly. His visit includes scheduled talks with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Wednesday and participation in more than 30 meetings on the sidelines. Kirill Logvinov of the ministry confirmed Lavrov's involvement in 20 international meetings at the UN.

Sydney Swans forward Isaac Heeney said he is looking forward to addressing his teammates after his season was ended by a club suspension. Heeney and four teammates, including Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, were suspended last month for a breach of standards. The group arrived at Swans HQ for exit meetings on Wednesday evening after the 2026 season concluded. Warner was questioned about apologizing but said he did not know yet.

Senator David Shoebridge accused the United States of interfering in Australia's domestic politics regarding online safety laws. The Trump administration warned that proposed opt-in algorithm reforms risked viewpoint-based censorship and requested exemptions for American platforms. Shoebridge described the US embassy's submission as an extraordinary intervention in legislation the Australian parliament should decide.

A viral video showing rats in the party area of a Rajkot McDonald's outlet prompted action by the Rajkot Municipal Corporation. Municipal health officer Jayesh Vakani verified the footage, stating the rats may have entered from outside. Consequently, the food department collected samples and charged the establishment Rs 3,000. This incident was part of a broader surveillance drive inspecting 53 food establishments, where officials destroyed stale food and issued notices for hygiene violations.

Senior journalist and director RK Radhakrishnan created the documentary Faceless People to highlight the plight of Sri Lankan Tamil refugees in India who remain stateless despite living there for decades. The film argues that nearly 98% of the 89,830 refugees live peacefully and that their lack of citizenship stems from a lack of political will rather than security threats. Radhakrishnan faced a rating restriction from the Central Board of Film Certification, which deemed the film suitable only for viewers over 16 after reviewing its focus on a young child's life. The documentary aims to dismantle the perception of refugees as threats and seeks to facilitate change by reaching administrators and festival audiences.

Congress MP Rahul Gandhi accused the Election Commission of 'treason' and 'vote chori' after a report claimed internal dissent among its commissioners. Gandhi stated in a video that the Commission's actions were wrong and against the country. The Election Commission rejected these allegations, asserting that all decisions, including those regarding the Special Intensive Revision, were unanimous and approved by all commissioners.

Netherlands midfielder Tijjani Reijnders left Manchester City for Saudi Arabia's Al Qadsiah after rejecting a role he disliked in favor of a financial package. Reijnders, 28, stated he could not refuse the offer despite initial fears that moving to the Saudi Pro League would end his career, citing advice from coach Brendan Rodgers. He noted the move allows him to secure his family's future and expressed confidence in the league's quality.

F5 has released security updates to address a critical BIG-IP APM zero-day vulnerability that is currently being exploited in remote code execution attacks. The company warned that the vulnerability has been exploited and advised customers to review systems for indicators of compromise. In response, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities Catalog and ordered U.S. federal agencies to secure their networks against it by Friday.

Alibaba unveiled plans on Sept 23 to expand its overseas data centres, targeting markets across Europe and the Middle East. The company said it would establish its first cloud regions in Turkey, Finland and the Netherlands, while expanding its data centre footprint in Malaysia, Germany, the United Arab Emirates, France and Hong Kong over the next 12 months. Alibaba chief executive Eddie Wu stated the firm is targeting more than 20GW of global data centre capacity by 2032 and is training an AI model with five to 10 trillion parameters.

India is investigating LG Electronics and Samsung for allegedly paying lower tariffs on imported OLED display parts than required. Industry groups are lobbying for OLED parts to be classified under the same low-duty regime as older LCD and LED technologies. Samsung is contesting a separate tax demand regarding networking gear imports while LG has submitted responses to the OLED inquiry. The investigation focuses on whether OLED glass screens should attract a 15 per cent duty instead of the 5 per cent rate reserved for LCD and LED parts. Industry representatives argue that denying parity results in higher input costs and hampers the growth of advanced manufacturing in India.

GPU acceleration alone does not guarantee fast ROS 2 graphs because messages often remain serialized or copied through CPU memory between nodes. NVIDIA Isaac ROS 5.0 updates all nodes to use the CUDA buffer backend via rosidl::Buffer, enabling zero-copy transport for GPU-resident payloads when runtime conditions allow. An AI coding agent with a migrate-node-to-rosidl-buffer skill automates the audit and refactor of existing CUDA-accelerated nodes to adopt this backend with minimal code changes. The migrated Depth Anything 3 node demonstrates the workflow, allowing deployment on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor while preserving standard ROS 2 interfaces and CPU fallbacks.

Microsoft has warned IT administrators that the September 2026 Windows 11 security updates may disrupt Always On VPN connections. The issue arises when the VPN automatically attempts alternative connection methods, causing connections to remain in a 'Connecting' state or display port errors. Microsoft advises administrators to switch from automatic protocol selection to a single protocol, such as SSTP or IKEv2, to mitigate the problem while a permanent solution is developed.

GE Vernova, Hitachi, SGE, and Samsung C&T have signed a memorandum of understanding to establish a framework for cooperation on market development and commercial opportunities for the BWRX-300 small modular reactor. The agreement links to a broader memorandum signed at the NATO summit by US, Japanese, and South Korean officials. The partners intend to leverage their complementary capabilities to advance deployment across multiple markets, including Europe, and strengthen energy security. Quotes from company executives highlight the synergy created by the four-way partnership and the goal of building on existing momentum for the technology.

Elon Musk claims AI could master nearly every field by 2027 or 2028, calling a researcher's 10-20 year forecast conservative. He notes his own timeline has shifted from 2030-2040 to the current estimate, while experts debate the speed of this development and its safety implications.

Reports indicate Apple is developing a screenless fitness tracker aimed at competing with Whoop and Oura. The device, expected to launch before 2028, features a slim fabric band and focuses on health metrics without a display. Senior executives Tim Cook and Eddy Cue are reportedly invested in the project, which draws on the team behind the Vision Pro. Concurrently, an AI pendant project has been delayed.

Apple is developing a screenless health and fitness tracker similar to Whoop's wrist-worn device, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The project, supported by top executives including Tim Cook and Eddy Cue, remains in a preliminary phase known internally as a technology investigation. If Apple proceeds with a release, the device likely won't debut before 2028. Apple has already begun incorporating Whoop-style features into its latest Watch and Health app.

Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa was caught on camera scrolling through Instagram Reels on his smartphone while Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan addressed world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly in New York. A video from inside the hall shows al-Sharaa looking down at his phone and appearing to scroll through Instagram's short-video feed while Erdogan was speaking from the podium. The clip has since gone viral on social media. Some reports said al-Sharaa was also sharing Reels, but the footage itself does not establish what he was watching or whether he was messaging anyone.

The Mumbai Crime Branch has sought technical assistance to unlock the iPhone of IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode, whose device remains locked and is treated as vital evidence in his death probe. The investigation continues into allegations that Wakode used ChatGPT during a mid-semester exam and claims by his parents regarding caste-based harassment. Meanwhile, Professor Suryanarayana Doolla, the reported invigilator, has been placed on leave as student protests on the Powai campus persist.

Britain's Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) has proposed new rules requiring Google to provide users with greater choice over search services and AI assistants on Android and Chrome. The proposals mandate that Google display a selection of search providers during initial setup and annually thereafter, while also allowing qualified AI assistants to appear on these screens. CMA Chief Executive Sarah Cardell noted that search habits are evolving with the rise of AI tools. The proposals are currently open for consultation until October 9, with a final decision expected by the end of the year.

Britain's competition watchdog, the CMA, has proposed rules to increase user choice on Android and Chrome regarding search services and AI assistants like ChatGPT. The proposals would require Google to display alternative search providers during setup and annually, while also ensuring fair attribution of publisher content. Sarah Cardell, the CMA's Chief Executive, noted the rise of AI assistants as search services. The proposals are open for consultation until October 9, with a final decision expected by year-end.

Alibaba announced plans to expand its overseas data centres in Europe, establishing new cloud regions in Finland, the Netherlands, and Turkey while growing its footprint in Germany, France, and other locations over the next 12 months. At its annual conference, CEO Eddie Wu noted that machine thinking currently represents less than 3% of human thinking but could eventually reach 1,000 times human capacity. He also stated that by 2032, Alibaba Cloud aims to operate over 20GW of global data centre capacity to meet rising AI demand.

OpenAI expanded its GPT-6 AI lineup on Tuesday with the launch of two new models, GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. These models are priced at half the promotional rates of their predecessors while offering some capabilities of the flagship GPT-6 Astra. OpenAI stated that improvements in caching and inference allow them to serve these models at a lower cost, passing savings directly to users. The company noted that while Astra remains the most capable model for demanding projects, Sol and Luna are designed for professional work, coding, and automation tasks.

OpenAI is expanding its technical safety assessments to include outside organizations throughout the training, evaluation, and deployment processes, moving beyond previous pre-launch-only checks. The company is currently in discussions with groups like METR and Redwood Research to conduct independent reviews. Lama Ahmad, who oversees external safety relationships, noted the high stakes involved. OpenAI also plans to bring outside evaluators into its offices for sensitive work, a practice it has used before. The announcement follows CEO Sam Altman's earlier statement about giving independent evaluators office access and the right to publish findings.

Research analyzing India's 4G rollout finds that protectionist policies restricting low-priced Chinese phones backfired by slowing network expansion, which reduced profitability for domestic firms. Simulations suggest a ban on budget Chinese phones would have delayed coverage and lowered consumer surplus by approximately INR 236 billion per quarter. Conversely, subsidies open to all 4G phones accelerated network growth and adoption far more effectively than domestic-only subsidies. The study concludes that industrial policy must consider spillovers between complementary markets, such as phones and wireless networks, to avoid harming the very firms they aim to protect.

OpenAI launched updated versions of its GPT-6 Sol and Luna models on Tuesday, cutting API prices to half or less than the previous 5.6 series. An OpenAI spokesperson confirmed the rates carry no expiration date. The company attributed the reductions to improvements in caching and inference, stating the changes are permanent rather than promotional.

Aahil Sheikh argues that the proposed EU Kids Act can advance online safety by introducing interoperability and third-party tools. While complementing existing regulations like the Digital Services Act, the proposal addresses gaps in current safety-by-design approaches where platforms retain centralized control. By enabling middleware, the Act aims to give guardians and minors greater autonomy over safety settings, content filters, and algorithmic feeds. This approach seeks to shift the paradigm from platform-dependent compliance to user-defined safety standards, though challenges regarding data privacy and funding for independent developers remain.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk shared his views in an exclusive interview with China Media Group, envisioning a future where individuals own personal robots for caregiving and tutoring. He predicted the number of humanoid robots could reach 1 billion within 10 years, 10 billion within 15 years, and 100 billion within 20 years. Musk also praised China's appeal as a travel destination and highlighted advances in Chinese humanoid robot technology.

An official from China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology stated at the 2026 World New Energy Vehicle Congress that new energy vehicles now account for more than 25% of global vehicle sales. Experts noted that China has become a core engine for global NEV development, with production and sales exceeding 10 million units in the first eight months of 2026. However, market penetration remains uneven, staying below 10% in emerging markets and established economies like the United States and Japan. International cooperation is deepening, with German companies increasing R&D in China and Chinese firms investing heavily in Southeast Asia.

An analysis concludes that eight years of US trade policies, including tariffs and export controls, have failed to achieve their strategic objectives against China. Instead of weakening Beijing, these measures have strengthened Chinese state-owned enterprises and spurred domestic innovation, while American firms face exclusion from key markets. The text notes that despite China's internal economic headwinds, US restrictions have been counterproductive, imposing costs on American consumers and companies without altering China's economic trajectory.

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee demanded the arrest of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and fresh Assembly elections using the pre-SIR voter list. She alleged that the BJP and poll panel looted the recent polls. Her remarks followed reports by The Indian Express that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi flagged issues during the pan-India Special Intensive Revision. Banerjee stated on Facebook live that it has been proven the BJP and EC looted the West Bengal assembly polls. The Election Commission responded that SIR decisions were taken unanimously with all three commissioners' approval.

Bharat Rashtra Samithi working president K.T. Rama Rao urged the Supreme Court to take suo motu cognizance of concerns regarding the functioning of the Election Commission of India. He warned of a severe crisis of confidence, asserting that only the Supreme Court holds the credibility to conduct an impartial investigation. KTR recalled raising apprehensions about the Special Intensive Revision process with former Election Commissioners in New Delhi, noting that serious doubts persist despite previous representations. He emphasized that a top-court-monitored inquiry is necessary to restore public trust and protect Indian democracy.

Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee demanded fresh Assembly elections using the pre-SIR voter list and announced pan-India protests against Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Reacting to a report claiming two commissioners objected to the voter-roll revision, Banerjee accused the commission of working for the BJP and called for Kumar's arrest. TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee alleged that 30 lakh voter names were deleted to benefit the BJP, citing similar actions in Haryana and Bihar. The Election Commission stated that operational queries were raised during the draft stage as standard practice to safeguard voter rights and that decisions were taken unanimously.

China officially delivered a custom-made AI-driven meteorological early warning platform, MAZU-Nepal, to Nepal on Tuesday at the Second China-Central Asia Meteorological Cooperation Forum. MAZU is an intelligent system developed in China that integrates artificial intelligence with physical forecasting models. Following last month's devastating mudslide disaster, China has provided Nepal with weather monitoring, forecasting, early warning, and impact-based services, including a trial version of MAZU.

James Manyika, senior vice president of research at Google-Alphabet, stated that the Global South is more optimistic about AI than the West. He attributed this to differing perceptions regarding societal benefits. Manyika highlighted current applications, noting Google Translate now supports 300 languages with a goal of 1,000. He also cited health diagnostics and a Planetary Prediction Engine that predicted Ebola outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo with 83% accuracy.

British Columbia has sued OpenAI and Sam Altman, arguing the company failed to warn law enforcement after discovering the shooter used ChatGPT to plan violence. The lawsuit demands OpenAI pay for the demolition of Tumbler Ridge Secondary School and other emergency costs. The province seeks injunctive relief, including updates to ChatGPT to automatically terminate violent conversations, citing the tragedy's foreseeable consequences.

On September 22, 2026, Chinese Premier Li Qiang met with President Francis Hourant and CEO David Hoey of WorldSkills International in Shanghai during the opening of the 48th WorldSkills Competition. Li highlighted China's dedication to skilled talent development and global skills cooperation, stating that hosting the event demonstrates high regard for such talent. He further pledged continued support for WorldSkills International and the global skills cause. Hourant and Hoey praised China's skills development and expressed confidence in the competition, looking forward to strengthening cooperation for global peace and prosperity.

OpenAI has released GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna, two new API-only models within its GPT-6 family. These models are designed to deliver faster performance at lower costs compared to their predecessors. OpenAI states that Sol targets complex coding tasks while Luna is optimized for high-volume work. Benchmarks indicate Sol and Luna achieve competitive scores on tasks like AutomationBench and DeepSWE at significantly lower costs than models like Claude Opus 5. The models are currently available in the OpenAI API and specific ChatGPT plans, with a gradual rollout to the main ChatGPT interface pending.

The article explains that the aviation revolution depends on global collaboration, illustrated by the fact that over 10,000 Boeing jets worldwide fly with Chinese-made parts. Furthermore, Boeing's Shanghai facility services airlines from China and beyond. Looking ahead, the world's two largest aviation markets will need over 43,000 new aircraft in the next 20 years, underscoring the necessity of a robust global supply chain to meet this demand.

The People's Bank of China pledged to advance high-level opening-up of the financial sector during a symposium with foreign institutions. Governor Pan Gongsheng stated the bank would improve policy supply and facilitate the international use of the renminbi. Official data showed China's GDP grew by 4.7% year on year in the first half of 2026, supported by the central bank's monetary policy.

Qualcomm announced two new flagship smartphone processors, the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, at its annual Snapdragon Summit. These chips emphasize AI capabilities, featuring new sensing hubs that can run small models of up to 200 million parameters locally. The Extreme version supports running a 30-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts model locally. Additionally, the processors offer pixel-level camera control, high-resolution video recording, and AI-driven vocal enhancement.

Anthropic has released Claude Opus 5.5, the first model in its new Claude 5.5 family. The team states it performs at the level of Claude Fable 5.1 on most work. It also costs 40% less to run than Opus 5 on typical workloads at default settings. On Anthropic's own benchmarks, it leads in agentic coding, computer use, and knowledge work. Opus 5.5 scores 54.6% on FrontierCode at medium effort, beating GPT-6 Astra's top score of 53.3% at about a fifth of the cost per task. The model is available as a managed API model on the Claude Platform, Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure. Zero data retention is available, as with previous Opus models. Anthropic has not released weights, so self-hosting is not an option.

India has initiated an anti-dumping investigation into imports of Glycine from China following a complaint filed by domestic manufacturer Avid Organics. The applicant alleges that dumped imports are causing material injury. The Directorate General of Trade Remedies (DGTR) will consider data between 2022 and 2025 to determine the existence and effect of dumping. If material injury is established, the DGTR will recommend imposing duties, subject to the final decision of the Finance Ministry. The investigation was announced on September 22, 2026.

Karnataka Congress MLA Yeshwanthrayagouda Patil resigned after his Indi constituency in Vijayapura district was excluded from the state's drought-hit list. Patil alleged that the area faced severe drought during the 2026-27 kharif season, causing crop failure and water shortages, yet only 11 of 13 taluks in the district were declared drought-hit. Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara noted the total would reach 177 and possibly 200 taluks. Patil cited a political environment favoring pressure tactics over moderate approaches as a reason for his resignation.

Donald Trump is scheduled to meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping later today, with artificial intelligence expected to be a key agenda item. Concurrently, US Congress is considering a bill that would ban artificial superintelligence and create a federal agency to regulate advanced AI technology.

According to preliminary assessments by the Solar Energy Association of Ukraine (SEAU), Ukraine added up to 1.1 GW of new solar capacity during the first half of 2026. SEAU estimates total installed solar capacity reached between 9.4 GW and 9.7 GW by mid-2026. The association expects this year's additions to reach around 2 GW by year's end, driven largely by smaller projects intended for self-consumption. SEAU Chairman Vladyslav Sokolovskyi noted that distributed generation and energy storage are essential for Ukraine's energy security and resilience during wartime.

Students of Lady Shri Ram College in Delhi organized a solidarity march demanding improved women's safety measures following a gang rape case in Kalkaji and a police encounter near the campus. The demonstration flagged critical security lapses, including non-functional CCTV cameras, unstaffed Pink Booths, inadequate police patrolling, and poor street lighting on National Park road. Citing persistent security fears and past harassment incidents, some classes shifted to online mode as students expressed unease about accessing peripheral routes after sundown.

On September 23, 2026, the first shuttle talks between the United States and Iran in months raised hopes for progress toward ending the West Asia war, although neither side confirmed any change in positions. U.S. President Donald Trump expressed optimism about a potential deal, stating there is momentum for a resolution, while Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi communicated conditions through a Qatari mediator in New York. These diplomatic efforts occurred as oil prices held near two-week lows, with the ongoing conflict continuing to disrupt global energy supplies and threaten critical trade routes like the Strait of Hormuz.

A 10-member high-power committee appointed by the Board of Governors of IIT Bombay has commenced an inquiry into the death of a 20-year-old BTech student. The panel, which includes faculty, students, and experts, will examine the incident's circumstances and allegations of caste-based remarks made by the student's parents. The committee was appointed four days after the death and must submit its report within a week. Meanwhile, questions persist regarding the role of Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, and faculty bodies from several other IITs have expressed support for due process.

Britain has confirmed it will rework its agreement to return the Chagos Islands to Mauritius following criticism from US President Donald Trump, who called the deal terrible. Defence Secretary Wes Streeting noted that annual lease payments of at least £120 million would not be made at this stage. The UK aims to find a resolution with US partners to support the deal, though a breakthrough remains uncertain.

Applicants for Canadian citizenship are advised to avoid six common document mistakes that could delay processing or lead to rejection. Key errors include using outdated checklists, such as the IRCC CIT 0007 version modified in August 2026, and submitting unclear passport copies. The checklist applies to permanent residents aged 18 or older. IRCC emphasizes that meeting documentation requirements does not guarantee qualification for citizenship.

Since June 2025, the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls has faced significant controversy regarding its implementation and potential impact on voter rights. Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi have formally objected at least 14 times to decisions made without their knowledge, including unauthorized changes to voter registration forms. The exercise has resulted in the removal of over 13.8 crore voters nationally, with substantial exclusions in states like West Bengal, Maharashtra, and Delhi. While the Supreme Court upheld the Election Commission's authority, concerns persist about the process's fairness and its potential political ramifications.

On Wednesday, 23 September 2026, Volodymyr Zelenskyy is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly in New York, seeking to bolster international support for Ukraine before potential peace negotiations with Moscow. Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump made headlines by threatening to annihilate Iran, while other leaders like Alexander Stubb and Andy Burnham spoke on global conflicts and information warfare. The event coincided with reports of Russian airspace violations and drone attacks on Kyiv.

Angry Anderson, the rock musician famous for providing the soundtrack for the iconic wedding scene in the Australian soap Neighbours, has died at the age of 79. Born in 1947, Anderson rose to fame as the frontman of Rose Tattoo before his solo hit 'Suddenly' became a global phenomenon in 1987. He recently suffered a cardiac arrest while on the band's farewell tour in Europe, leading to the cancellation of nine dates. His family and bandmates have paid tribute to his legacy.

The UDF government in Kerala is facing political pressure following a series of controversies involving private sponsorship of ministerial perks. Former CPI(M) state secretariat member MB Rajesh questioned why private individuals are funding expensive benefits for ministers, highlighting three specific instances. These include Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala's US trip reportedly sponsored by a friend, Sports Minister OJ Janeesh's foreign travel, and Chief Minister VD Satheesan's privately sponsored chartered flight. While government sources and ministers argue that these arrangements did not burden the state exchequer, the opposition is demanding transparency regarding the sponsors and the propriety of such arrangements for public officials.

Airtel Money, the mobile money arm of Airtel Africa and ultimately controlled by Indian billionaire Sunil Bharti Mittal, has announced plans to float on the London Stock Exchange. The company targets a valuation of $8bn to $9bn and aims to raise about $800m. CEO Ian Ferrao stated that shareholders chose London for its deep understanding of emerging markets and Africa. Airtel Money operates across 13 sub-Saharan African countries with 53 million monthly active users. The listing is expected in early October, following delays due to market conditions.

Indian men's and women's skeet shooting teams secured bronze medals at the Asian Games 2026 in Nagoya on Wednesday, September 23. The women's team, comprising Raiza Dhillon, Maheshwari Chauhan, and Parinaaz Dhaliwal, achieved a combined score of 331, finishing third behind China and Kazakhstan. This marked India's first-ever medal in the women's team skeet event. Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated the athletes for their focus and teamwork.

Asia is projected to import 23.96 million barrels per day of crude oil in September, marking the highest volume since the Iran war started in February. According to data from Kpler cited by Clyde Russell, this figure exceeds August's 23.38 million bpd but remains approximately 13% below pre-war levels. While China's imports have recovered to 8.93 million bpd in August, Goldman Sachs analysts suggest further increases are unlikely if high prices persist.

Sakeena Fiza, a validation engineer at NVIDIA, describes her role as investigating hardware systems to ensure they function correctly before mass production. She compares the work to solving a mystery, where engineers must find and fix potential failures in complex AI infrastructure. Fiza highlights the collaborative nature of the job, involving multiple engineering disciplines to bring new systems to life. She notes that validation engineers act as the first customers, testing devices under real-world conditions to catch issues early. Fiza arrived at NVIDIA after studying computer science and engineering at the University of California, Irvine, driven by a fascination with systems design. She expresses excitement about future products in the pipeline that she believes will change the world.

Oliver Marsh argues that auditing AI chatbots is insufficient for understanding societal risks because it does not reflect how millions of people actually use these tools. He proposes a 'Google Trends for AI' service that would provide researchers with aggregated, near-real-time data on usage trends while preserving privacy. Marsh notes that while companies like OpenAI and Anthropic publish usage dashboards, they often frame data to limit external scrutiny. He suggests that transparency laws or voluntary codes of practice could mandate such services, noting that refusing to provide them would raise questions about corporate commitments to risk mitigation.

Indian officials have launched an investigation into LG Electronics and Samsung, alleging the companies incorrectly claimed a 5% concessional tariff on imported OLED glass screens. Authorities believe a 15% duty should apply, as OLED parts are not covered under the lower rate reserved for older LCD and LED technology. While Samsung states it is reviewing the matter and cooperating fully, LG has submitted responses and a voluntary deposit. Industry groups are lobbying for policy changes to ensure OLED manufacturers receive parity with legacy technologies.

RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta stated there is a fair case for the Indian Rupee to stabilize or appreciate following recent capital flow measures announced in June 2026. She noted that India's cumulative depreciation of 13.1% since March 31, 2025, is likely a temporary phenomenon driven by oil and gold price shocks. Gupta highlighted that India's economy is growing at 7-8% in real terms and expects the current account deficit to shrink further, supported by resilient net services exports and remittances.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) announced on Wednesday that it has initiated penal action against five leading e-commerce platforms: Amazon, Swiggy Instamart, BigBasket, Flipkart India, and Zepto. The regulator cited various non-compliances, including misleading claims, misbranding, and the sale of prohibited or poisonous food articles. Specific instances involved misleading claims regarding 'Happilo Premium Date Bites' and non-compliant dairy products from Milky Mist. Additionally, platforms were found non-compliant with provisions relating to the sale of Datura fruits and seeds. FSSAI officials stated that email queries sent to these platforms elicited no immediate response.

IFI Techsolutions Limited announced it has achieved the Agentic DevOps specialization with Microsoft Azure and GitHub. The achievement, awarded after a rigorous third-party audit, validates the company's technical expertise and delivery excellence. David Wright, Chief Revenue Officer, stated the specialization confirms their ability to help customers accelerate innovation and create measurable business value through AI-powered engineering practices.

Uber Technologies Inc. faces market scrutiny after videos of Tesla Cybercabs suggest a threat to its ride-hailing dominance. While bears warn that Tesla's direct customer access and lower prices could erode Uber's margins, the company's management highlights its established network and partnerships with multiple autonomous vehicle providers. Recent insider activity shows mixed signals, with CEO Dara Khosrowshahi and COO Andrew Macdonald purchasing shares, while Chief Corporate Officer Jill Hazelbaker sold a portion of her holdings. Management projects robotaxi services to 15 cities by year-end, though valuation metrics remain below Uber's historical average.

Rallies Arena tasked Claude AI with managing a $100,000 portfolio to outperform the S&P 500. The model selected EMCOR Group and NVIDIA as its largest positions. EMCOR, a construction firm specializing in data center infrastructure, holds 17.7% of the portfolio. Analysts note EMCOR benefits from the power and cooling needs of new AI campuses, which require significantly more capacity than older facilities. Goldman Sachs forecasts global AI investment exceeding $1 trillion in 2026.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) announced on Wednesday that it has initiated penal action against five e-commerce platforms: Amazon, Swiggy Instamart, BigBasket, Flipkart India, and Zepto. The regulator described the move as a crackdown on regulatory non-compliances, citing issues such as misbranding, misleading claims, and the sale or display of prohibited or poisonous food articles. However, FSSAI did not specify which alleged violations applied to each platform, nor did it identify the specific products involved or the penalties being pursued.

Tesla's racism trial in California opened on Monday with a difficult start for the company's legal team. The California Civil Rights Department (CRD) sued Tesla on behalf of over 6,000 Black workers at its Fremont factory. During the trial, a senior Tesla attorney, Timothy Kim, allegedly contacted a former employee, Ryan Edwards, and misled him into thinking he was working for the state. Edwards testified that Kim steered him toward saying Tesla was a good place to work and offered to represent him. Additionally, the CRD reported that four other witnesses have gone silent, possibly due to contact by Tesla's legal team. Tesla's lawyer argued that the N-word is a term of endearment in the Black community, citing rap lyrics. The trial is expected to run through October, with damages uncapped. Judge Peter Borkon will decide the case.

RBI Deputy Governor Poonam Gupta argued at the SBI Banking and Economics Conclave that the rupee has a fair case to stabilize or appreciate. She noted India has emerged structurally stronger from recent shocks, with a resilient growth equilibrium of 7% plus. Although the rupee hit a record low of 96.96 against the US dollar in May, it closed at 95.74. Gupta highlighted that despite huge inflows of $133 billion via FCNR deposits, the market dynamics do not appear well-founded for depreciation. She expects the current account deficit to shrink further, underpinned by growing success in merchandise exports and a resilient growth equilibrium.

Youth Congress members protested outside IIT Bombay on Wednesday, demanding justice for student Sahil Wakode following his death. The demonstration targeted the institute's statement alleging Wakode cheated using ChatGPT during an exam before committing suicide. Wakode's advocate, Nikhil Kamble, stated the family seeks arrests of those named in the case to progress the investigation. Additionally, the family alleges their son faced caste-based harassment, though details remain under investigation by the Mumbai Crime Branch.

The heads of Anthropic and OpenAI are set to brief the UN Security Council today, highlighting their calls for a slowdown in AI development amidst superpower competition. While Washington and Beijing are unlikely to reach a wide-ranging pact, the UK plans to focus its G20 presidency on AI safety. Global perspectives diverge, with the Global South appearing more optimistic about AI than the West.

McDonald's has announced a $10.8 billion investment to assist franchisees in improving food quality, service, and operational efficiency through 2036. The initiative, named 'Next,' aims to modernize restaurants and address challenges such as slowing US business and fierce competition from emerging brands. Consequently, the company is adjusting its growth targets and simplifying its marketing strategy to better compete in the market.

Copper prices extended a winning streak, closing near record highs as Chinese buyers restocked ahead of holidays and warehouse inventories in Shanghai and London continued to drain. Shanghai copper cathode stocks fell to 43,900 tons, the lowest since 2023, while global mined output could fall this year for the first time since 2017 due to outages at major mines. Analysts warn the rally may be inflated, with some predicting a potential market correction of 20% to 30% if Chinese producers begin selling as prices climb further.

The European Commission stated it will collaborate with Washington to mitigate disruption from US tariffs on Russian energy. The EU faces potential liquefied natural gas supply squeezes as it struggles to refill storage levels to at least 80% by November, according to Global Energy Flow. While the Lindsey Graham Sanctions Act allows tariffs up to 100% on countries buying Russian oil or gas, its application to the EU remains uncertain. EU officials hope the law does not create new commercial barriers. Meanwhile, European politicians criticized companies like Fayard for servicing Russian LNG vessels, arguing such actions sustain Russia's war effort.

Hainan Province is intensifying efforts to build a low-carbon economy, highlighted by its first island-loop natural gas pipeline network surpassing 35 billion cubic meters in cumulative transmission. According to PipeChina, this network has replaced an estimated 46.6 million tonnes of coal, significantly reducing dust and carbon dioxide emissions. Beyond energy supply, the island is advancing a ban on new fuel-powered vehicles by 2030 and aims for clean energy to comprise 87.2% of power capacity by the end of 2025. Long-term targets include peaking carbon emissions before 2030 and achieving carbon neutrality by 2060.

Supreme Court Justice Dipankar Dutta defended the collegium system, rejecting the 'myth' that judges appoint judges. He argued the judiciary plays a secondary role to the government, noting selective executive implementation undermines collegium sanctity. Despite opacity, he affirmed the system remains the most viable option for safeguarding independence under Article 50 of the Constitution, delivered in a split verdict with Justice Satish Chandra Sharma.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres addressed the 81st United Nations General Assembly, calling for steps to manage artificial intelligence risks. He argued that power now stems from data and algorithms, which advance faster than our ability to understand them. Guterres urged governments to assume responsibility, establish transparency, and cooperate on testing and safeguards. He highlighted the need for a multilateral AI Risk Management Framework and stated that killer robots must have no place in the future.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs drew roughly $999 million in net inflows on September 21, marking their strongest daily inflow since October 2025. Bitcoin traded near $86,500 after gaining almost 14% over the past week. Experts attribute the rally to the return of institutional demand and ETF flows rather than organic spot buying. The broader crypto market capitalization rose toward $2.93 trillion with 24-hour trading volume at approximately $110.73 billion.

During his address to the UN General Assembly, President Donald Trump promoted a new designation for artificial intelligence, suggesting the government refer to it as 'super intelligence' or SI. He stated that the existing term understates the technology's capabilities. Additionally, Trump rejected calls for broad international regulation, arguing the United States should focus on maintaining its technological lead while avoiding rules that could slow development. His remarks followed announcements regarding an 'AI Force' and plans for an AI 'czar.'

China's Global Governance Initiative is built on the principle that every country deserves a voice in shaping the rules affecting its future. Beijing aims to increase representation for developing nations, but the article notes that the practical meaning of this goal is yet to be defined. CGTN's Ediz Tiyansan reports on this stance from the United Nations in New York City.

While the Nifty 50 index gained just under 1% over the last six months, the Nifty Midcap 150 index delivered a 13% gain. Ten midcap stocks emerged as standout performers, soaring between 50% and 105% during the same period. The article examines foreign institutional investor and mutual fund holdings in these high-performing stocks as of the June 2026 quarter.

Students and alumni of Delhi's Lady Shri Ram College, alongside local mothers and professionals, gathered to protest against sexual violence and safety lapses around the campus. Protesters highlighted recent rape incidents and demanded urgent institutional and governmental action. Speakers raised serious concerns regarding safety around the college's back gate and Amar Colony, noting the total absence of streetlights, non-functional pink police booths, and a lack of CCTV cameras. An alumna highlighted the persistent fear of stepping out after dark and the risks of harassment along daily transit routes.

Setareh Seyedghorban, an academic researcher, describes her complex relationship with AI tools as seductive yet demanding vigilance. Observing widespread adoption on trains and citing a US study where half of adults use chatbots, she notes the benefits of speed and cost reduction. However, she highlights risks such as 'sycophancy' undermining self-correction and 'deskilling' in medical contexts. While AI levels the playing field for non-native speakers, she warns that human judgment remains essential. She concludes that the future lies not in divorce or honeymoon phases, but in a real partnership where humans maintain control over their thinking and skills.

Students and alumni of Lady Shri Ram College in Delhi protested against sexual violence and safety lapses, citing dark lanes, inactive pink police booths, and a lack of streetlights. Former Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa questioned the procedural legality of actions taken by the Election Commission of India regarding modifications to Form 6 and the centralisation of the voter database, highlighting concerns over statutory powers and internal dissent.

The Special Court for POCSO Cases sentenced 63-year-old K. Muthaiah to 20 years in prison for sexually abusing an 11-year-old girl in 2021. The court imposed a fine of ₹1.02 lakh on the accused and directed the Tamil Nadu Government to pay ₹3 lakh compensation to the victim. The judgment was delivered by Magistrate Murugan on Tuesday.

The Government Railway Police (GRP) in Tiruchi reported seizing over 1,220 kilograms of gutkha between January and August this year across its jurisdiction. Data indicates Virudhunagar led with 471 kilograms seized, followed by Madurai at 209 kg and Tirunelveli at 119 kg. Officials attribute these seizures to illegal transport via inter-state trains from northern and eastern states where the substance is legal, into Tamil Nadu where it is banned. Dedicated teams conduct random checks and coordinate with local police and the Food Safety Department to handle confiscated contraband.

Ethiopia's government and Tigrayan authorities are accusing each other of launching offensives, raising fears of a return to full-scale conflict. Getachew Reda stated Tigrayan fighters took control of airports and launched attacks in neighboring regions, while Tigrayan authorities claimed they were forced into a defensive war. Reports of drone strikes in Tigray and Alamata have resulted in civilian casualties, with local officials alleging federal forces targeted schools. The US State Department condemned a separate strike on a food aid convoy. Both sides face criticism for delays in implementing the Pretoria Agreement that ended the 2022 war.

US stocks fell on Wednesday as benchmark 10-year Treasury yields hit their highest level since 2007. This move followed data showing US business activity surged to a five-year high, driven by a rise in new orders. S&P Global reported its flash US Composite PMI Output Index increased to 58.4, the highest since July 2021. The strong economic data led traders to price in a higher likelihood of further Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, pushing yields to multi-year highs and causing equity markets to decline.

Artificial intelligence emerged as a major theme at the opening of the UN General Assembly, with world leaders warning about risks ranging from autonomous weapons to job disruption. However, little consensus exists on next steps. US President Donald Trump rejected international control efforts, emphasizing competition and rapid development, while leaders like UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan called for common rules and safeguards. Guterres warned that humanity is increasingly transferring power to machines, insisting life-and-death decisions must remain under human control. Other leaders, including British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and French President Emmanuel Macron, highlighted the need for transparency, oversight, and international cooperation to prevent dominance by a few powers or companies. The debate underscores the tension between technological advancement and the establishment of global governance frameworks.

David Ellison, a 43-year-old entrepreneur backed by his father Larry Ellison, has rapidly built a dominant position in Hollywood by acquiring Paramount and Warner Bros. Through Skydance, Ellison secured a vast film catalog and streaming platforms, consolidating two industry giants. The $110 billion merger faced opposition from 12 Democratic attorneys general alleging antitrust violations. Ellison countered by threatening to relocate studios to Nashville before confirming the merged company would remain in Los Angeles. The deal, approved after a payment to the White House, marks a significant shift in the industry's power structure.

Poland's Energy Regulatory Office (URE) announced on September 22 that it will run seven price-only auctions from November 2 to November 10 for new renewable energy installations. The auctions aim to allocate support for more than 76 TWh of electricity, valued at nearly PLN 25 billion. A significant portion, 64.5 TWh, is reserved for photovoltaic and onshore wind projects, with 53.25 TWh specifically set aside for installations larger than 1 MW competing in a final auction on November 10. Bids will be assessed solely on price, adhering to a 2022 government regulation that caps annual auction volumes through 2027.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the United Nations General Assembly on September 23, accusing the United States and Israel of terrorism and aggression. He rejected descriptions of Iran as a terrorist state, stating Iranians were victims of terrorism, specifically citing the Minab school attack where over 100 children and teachers died. Pezeshkian defended Iran's nuclear program as a pursuit of energy, not weapons, and asserted Tehran acted in self-defense. Despite strong criticism, he expressed openness to diplomacy without military pressure, noting ongoing indirect discussions between US and Iranian officials mediated in New York.

The Tamil Nadu central crime branch raided properties belonging to industrialist R Veeramani and the Gem Group of Companies on Wednesday. The raids followed the arrest of Veeramani and three others, including former employee Ganeshan, in a Pocso case. Shanthi, a former aide, released a video claiming Veeramani made sexual advances toward her when she was 13. Police recovered documents and digital evidence during the search. A senior officer stated that Veeramani sold two properties in February 2026 to help him evade arrest. The case was reopened after a special court refused to accept a police report. Former BJP chief K Annamalai demanded a Special Investigation Team, while Education Minister A Rajmohan confirmed the investigation is under close monitoring by the chief minister.

The Jammu and Kashmir government informed the Assembly that it screened approximately 21.8 lakh books and withdrew 4,812 from state-run and private college libraries since July. The government stated that 518 of the withdrawn books were banned, while more than 1,750 were referred for further examination. This action follows a directive to identify material violating religious sentiments or harming national interest, aiming to uphold constitutional values and academic freedom in educational institutions.

On September 23, Alphabet-owned YouTube unveiled a suite of artificial intelligence tools, shopping updates, and personalized viewer features at its annual Made on YouTube event in New York City. The new creator tools include additions to YouTube Studio for feedback on video drafts, channel-matched thumbnails, and testing up to three video cuts. A Gemini-powered assistant in Shorts and YouTube Create will help edit clips, trim pauses, and sync music. The platform is also testing opt-in AI comment moderation that adapts to creators' preferences and will combine voice and facial detection in its likeness-protection tools.

Sindhu Gangadharan, Managing Director of SAP Labs India, stated that enterprises must move beyond AI experimentation to focus on solving real business problems and building domain expertise. Speaking at the India Advantage Summit 2026, she emphasized that AI is a leadership transformation requiring organizations to start with desired outcomes rather than searching for problems where technology can be applied. She noted that while AI reduces solution build time, understanding business challenges and having strong data foundations remain essential for scaling initiatives beyond proof-of-concepts.

InfraTrust's September report highlights a surge in attacks targeting network management systems used to control enterprise infrastructure. Between August 25 and September 17, the organization tracked 158 new security advisories across 17 vendors, covering 1,699 vulnerabilities. Of these, 42 were rated critical, with 71 capable of remote exploitation without authentication. Major vendors, including Cisco and SonicWall, confirmed active exploitation of specific flaws, leading CISA to add them to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. The report emphasizes that attackers are focusing on administrative software, treating these platforms as high-value targets.

Singer and actor Pat Boone has listed his Beverly Hills estate for $22.95 million, ending a 66-year ownership that began in 1960 when he and his late wife Shirley purchased it for $159,000. The 1.12-acre property at 904 North Beverly Drive, built in 1939, features a residence with six bedrooms and between seven and eight bathrooms, along with a guest house and pool. Boone, now 92, told Mansion Global that while he does not need a place this big, he still loves the home where he raised his daughters and entertained celebrities like Elvis Presley. The current listing highlights the estate's potential for preservation or redevelopment, reflecting the dramatic rise in Beverly Hills real estate values over the last century.

At its Made on YouTube event, the platform announced new AI tools within the Studio app designed to assist creators in analyzing content and expanding their reach. Key updates include expanding the Ask Studio feature to mobile devices and introducing AI capabilities for generating dynamic thumbnails and feedback on video drafts. Additionally, YouTube plans to automatically monitor thumbnail performance and update analytics to explain video engagement beyond raw numbers.

StrictlyVC at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Francisco will convene investors and experts to examine the evolving venture capital landscape. Driven by AI and rapid startup scaling, the event offers sessions on new IPO rules, the growing role of family offices, and current limited partner expectations. Registration for the Investor Pass is required by September 25 to secure a $200 discount.

YouTube announced a new feature enabling creators to organize vertical clips into microdrama-style series, aiming to capitalize on the genre's rapid growth. Executives stated they are excited about the rise of episodic content, noting that microdramas have already surpassed 6.5 billion views on the platform in the first half of the year. The microdrama industry is estimated to generate $14 billion in revenue in 2026.

Turkish First Lady Emine Erdogan concluded a busy agenda in New York covering issues concerning humanity and future-shaping topics during the 81st UN General Assembly. She shared a video highlighting her participation in events, including President Erdogan's address and the International Energy Agency High-Level Energy Transition Dialogue. Erdogan stated that the agenda covered topics that will shape the future of the world.

South Sudan's National Elections Commission chairperson Gabriel Bol Deng Majok urged politicians and parties to convert political ideas into ballots rather than bullets. The commission emphasized its role in leveling the playing field with rules and regulations. President Salva Kiir dissolved the transitional government on Tuesday, paving the way for the general election scheduled for December 22. Preparations are underway for the first polls since independence in 2011.

US President Donald Trump, along with the leaders of Denmark and Greenland, signed an agreement in New York to address security concerns regarding the Arctic island. The deal permits the US to expand its military presence and modernize facilities at Pituffik Space Base while establishing defense areas elsewhere. It reaffirms Danish sovereignty and Greenlandic self-determination, supports stronger NATO engagement, and prohibits non-NATO military installations. The accord requires parliamentary approval before entering into force and remains valid indefinitely, allowing Greenland to join NATO if it becomes independent.

Nissan is reviving the Pixo nameplate to launch an affordable all-electric city cruiser priced under $25,000, targeting Europe's growing A-segment market. Developed through a partnership with Renault, the vehicle features a 27.5 kWh battery offering up to 259 km of range and will be produced at Renault's plant in Slovenia. Nissan stated the car is designed for drivers seeking accessible electric city mobility with modern connectivity.

Judges at the International Criminal Court convicted former rebel commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani of crimes against humanity for abusing and torturing prisoners at a detention facility in the Central African Republic. Witnesses described inhumane conditions, including cramped cells and confinement under floorboards. While the verdict offers recognition to victims, experts warn that closing the ICC investigation and potential funding cuts to local courts threaten future accountability in the region.

Google Beam is expanding its global footprint to six countries, including the U.S., Canada, and Japan, supported by 18 channel partners. The company announced a new extended network in partnership with Industrious to increase access for startups. Internal testing indicated that teams using the technology felt 50% more connected and experienced a 21% reduction in the need for follow-up meetings.

Google introduced Gemini 3.8 Flash and Flash-Lite text-to-speech models to transform voice generation from static presets into a dynamic creative studio. These models enable creators and developers to build richer audio experiences with granular control over acting cues, pacing, and dialects. The Flash model leads benchmarks in accent modeling and overall quality, while the Flash-Lite model offers cost-efficient scaling for high-volume dubbing. Key features include creating bespoke voices from scratch, replicating consistent vocal profiles from short audio samples, and supporting over 100 languages. To ensure trust and transparency, the system incorporates strict safeguards, including consent verification for voice replication and SynthID watermarking to detect AI-generated speech. Developers can access these capabilities starting today via Google AI Studio and the Gemini API.

Samsung smart fridges, specifically the Bespoke AI line, ceased functioning after a firmware update distributed via the SmartThings platform. Korean outlets reported that affected devices lost power immediately, forcing users to discard spoiled food. The problem has generated hundreds of complaints, exacerbated by the timing during the Chuseok holiday. Samsung has not yet responded regarding the scope of the issue or preventative measures.

Amazon is contacting former employees, including those in its AI team, to offer them new opportunities through a recruitment initiative. While the company highlights its history of rehiring, a spokesperson clarified that these efforts are for open positions and not specifically aimed at addressing departures related to the return-to-office policy. The outreach includes inquiries about past reasons for leaving to better understand employee preferences for future roles.

OpenAI announced on Wednesday that it is bringing voice-based agentic features to its mobile app. Plus and Pro users will be able to use the Work tab to create documents, draft emails, or summarize messages. Free and Go users will access similar capabilities through plugins and connected apps. The update also allows users to switch between text and voice easily and resume conversations on desktop.

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) settled adjudication proceedings against five Adani group entities for ₹1.5 crore. The settlement addresses allegations from the defunct short seller Hindenburg regarding undisclosed related party transactions and violations of disclosure norms. The companies proposed settling without admitting or denying the allegations, following an investigation into listing regulation and equity agreement violations. SEBI disposed of the proceedings based on the accepted settlement terms.

Microsoft announced plans to invest more than $10 billion across the UAE, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, and Kuwait by 2030, focusing on cloud and AI infrastructure. Vice Chair Brad Smith stated the investment supports digital resilience amid ongoing regional conflict. The company faces challenges including chip access and threats to data centers in Bahrain and the UAE, yet maintains its spending schedule. Microsoft also plans $400 million for connectivity and holds a minority stake in Abu Dhabi's G42.

Amazon has expanded its Counterfeit Crimes Unit in India by deploying a three-member team in New Delhi to combat counterfeit products. This unit will work with agencies like the CBI and Customs, as well as brands, to take civil and criminal action against sellers of fake goods. The team includes a senior corporate counsel and two risk managers, focusing on protecting honest sellers, women entrepreneurs, and MSME brands alongside major brands.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) initiated penal action against five e-commerce platforms, including Amazon and Swiggy, for non-compliances such as misleading claims and the sale of prohibited products. This crackdown specifically targeted items like 'Happilo Premium Date Bites' and dairy products from Milky Mist. Additionally, the regulator filed adjudication cases against Nestle India regarding substandard baby food and promotional violations. Nestle India denied the allegations, stating its products are compliant with regulations.

Britain's competition watchdog, the CMA, has proposed rules requiring Google to offer users choices of search providers and AI assistants on Android and Chrome screens. The proposals include annual prompts to pick defaults and fair attribution of publisher content. The CMA expects a final decision by year-end, following a consultation period open until October 9.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) announced penal action against five e-commerce platforms, including Amazon and Flipkart, for food safety violations such as misleading claims and the sale of prohibited items. The regulator cited the FSS Act, 2006. Separately, Nestle India faces adjudication cases over substandard baby food samples, a claim the company denies, stating its products are compliant and labels were approved by the regulator's expert committee.

Microsoft announced plans to invest more than $10 billion in cloud and AI infrastructure across Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the United Arab Emirates by 2030. The investment covers capital and operating expenses and includes expanding digital resilience programs. Microsoft Vice Chair Brad Smith stated the company is sustaining and adding to planned investments despite regional conflict. The firm also plans to spend over $400 million on connectivity and deepen partnerships with national AI organizations.

Microsoft challenges the prevailing assumption that physical AI inference must run exclusively on onboard robot GPUs, arguing that this approach limits performance, battery life, and scalability. A systematic study of mobile robotic manipulation workloads demonstrated that offloading inference to edge or cloud GPUs significantly improved task success rates, enabled the use of larger AI models, and extended battery life by up to 160% compared to larger onboard units. To support this shift, Microsoft has announced an industry-first capability within its Physical AI Toolchain, allowing developers to containerize and orchestrate robotics AI workloads across robots, edge infrastructure, and the cloud using Kubernetes-based tooling.

Sources familiar with the matter indicate that Walt Disney Co will raise US Disney+ subscription prices by 13% to $27.50 per month starting September 23. The increase applies to the flagship ad-free service and other tiers, including Hulu and bundled plans. This move mirrors similar price hikes by entertainment giants like Netflix and aims to improve profitability. Disney recently reported a 64% surge in operating income from its entertainment division.

NVIDIA has released Nemotron 3 Diarization, an open-weight model designed to track up to eight speakers in real-time conversations. The model, which runs on NVIDIA GPUs via the NeMo toolkit, ranks first on Voice Arena's initial Diarization-Bench with a 14.72% DER score. Released under the OpenMDW License 1.1, it supports both offline recordings and real-time streaming, handling overlapping voices effectively. The model accepts various audio formats and converts them into speaker-attributed transcripts when paired with ASR tools.

Secretary of Energy Chris Wright told Heatmap that the administration will not cease U.S. diesel exports, throwing cold water on a potential ban. This stance contrasts with President Trump's recent remarks calling for a stop to diesel shipments. While some Republicans in Congress have pushed for the ban, Wright indicated there is no serious consideration for a blanket prohibition, though he acknowledged the need to grow domestic diesel supply.

The Indian government has cut import duties on crude and refined sunflower, soybean, and palm oils, effective September 24, aiming to reduce domestic edible oil prices. Sudhakar Desai of the Indian Vegetable Oil Producers' Association noted the timing is crucial for the festive season but warned that consumer impact depends on international prices and exchange rates. Meanwhile, the Solvent Extractors' Association highlighted potential global volatility and ongoing import competition from Nepal.

The Trump administration is reportedly preparing a 90-day ban on US diesel exports to lower prices before the midterm elections, according to Politico. Officials face internal opposition and industry warnings about potential long-term price increases. Market reactions included a drop in diesel futures, while the White House rejected the report as fake news and cited concerns over government intervention precedents.

A Senate subcommittee is holding a hearing on Flock Safety's nationwide AI surveillance network amid growing public backlash against the company's cameras. Critics argue the technology is flawed and poses serious privacy risks, citing low accuracy rates in license plate reading and documented cases of abuse by law enforcement. Lawmakers have introduced various bills to restrict or ban the use of such surveillance technologies, while some cities have already ended their contracts with Flock.

The Centre has reduced customs duties on crude and refined edible oils, including soybean, palm, and sunflower varieties. The cuts lower rates from 10% to 5% for crude oils and from 32.5% to 27.5% for refined oils. These measures aim to reduce import costs and potentially ease prices for consumers ahead of the festive season.

On September 23, 2026, the Supreme Court stayed an Allahabad High Court order directing the recovery of ₹5 lakh from the salary of Gautam Buddha Nagar District Magistrate Medha Roopam. The High Court had ordered the recovery to compensate Delhi University student Akriti Chaudhary, who was detained under the National Security Act during a workers' protest in Noida. The Supreme Court, hearing arguments from senior advocates representing both parties, decided to stay the operation of the High Court judgment, particularly paragraphs 27 to 33, until the matter is heard on merits. The case has been listed for hearing on October 7.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in New York to discuss concerns regarding the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act. Jaishankar reiterated India's interests, noting the law could impact India if implemented after a one-month period. Rubio sidestepped the issue, emphasizing the U.S.-India strategic partnership. The meeting occurred amidst preparations for future high-level engagements between U.S. President Donald Trump and Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

At BIO SHANGHAI WEEK 2026, a Shanghai Jiao Tong University spin-off company introduced the Skin Niacin Response Tester. This device provides an objective biological indicator designed to support early screening, precise assessment, and personalized treatment guidance for depression and other mental health conditions. An American entrepreneur attending the event reportedly tested the device. The article suggests that mood symptoms like swings and poor sleep may signal emotional distress, positioning this tool as a potential method for early detection.

China officially delivered a custom-made AI-driven meteorological early warning platform, MAZU-Nepal, to Nepal on Tuesday at the Second China-Central Asia Meteorological Cooperation Forum. MAZU is an intelligent system developed in China that integrates artificial intelligence with physical forecasting models. Following last month's devastating mudslide disaster, China has provided Nepal with weather monitoring, forecasting, early warning, and impact-based services, including a trial version of MAZU.

As Chinese President Xi prepares for a visit to the United States, Chinese and U.S. representatives are expected to hold discussions regarding artificial intelligence guardrails. These talks occur amidst a landscape where industry leaders and politicians express differing views on the best methods for controlling the technology. The discussions are set to take place in San Francisco.

Chew Yew Meng asserts that caring for individuals with dementia demands a collaborative approach involving both families and trained caregivers. While acknowledging the physical and emotional demands on family members, she emphasizes that foreign domestic helpers must be carefully selected and professionally trained to complement family efforts. Drawing on observations from Japan, she advocates for training programs that prioritize dignity, independence, and caregiver well-being to support sustainable ageing in place for Singaporeans.

A wellness hub for gig workers was inaugurated in Kochi on Wednesday, September 23, 2026, as part of the State government's 100-day action programme. Mayor V.K. Minimol launched the facility, which aims to provide safe rest facilities and basic welfare amenities to gig workers in sectors such as online food delivery, e-commerce, and ride-hailing services. The centre features seating, toilets, Wi-Fi, and charging points, and is managed by two staff members per shift.

Tamil Nadu police conducted a two-day special drive against anti-social elements, checking 9,329 history-sheeters. During the operation on September 21 and 22, a total of 260 individuals were remanded in judicial custody. The drive was ordered by Director-General of Police Mahesh Kumar Aggarwal to maintain law and order through preventive policing. Police teams also executed 560 non-bailable warrants during the operation.

Harvey Weinstein was resentenced to 15 years in prison for sexually assaulting a former production assistant in 2006. Although prosecutors sought 20 years and Weinstein pleaded for leniency while maintaining his innocence, the court imposed the 15-year term. Victim Miriam Haley stated she was happy with the sentence, while Weinstein's spokesman indicated plans to appeal. This follows an overturned 2020 conviction and a separate mistrial involving actor Jessica Mann.

New CCTV footage shows IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode using a mobile phone during an exam before Professor Suryanarayana Doolla escorted him out. Wakode died by suicide on September 23, 2026. His parents allege Doolla hurled casteist slurs, leading to an investigation under the SC/ST Act. IIT Bombay retracted its cheating allegation and apologized. Protests occurred, but academic activities have resumed.

Chinese President Xi Jinping will arrive in Washington on September 23 for a three-day state visit and a second summit with US President Donald Trump in less than six months. The itinerary includes meetings at the White House, a state dinner, and a visit to the National Archives. Discussions are expected to cover trade, technology, AI, Taiwan, Iran, Ukraine, and military ties. Washington and Beijing remain divided on several major issues, though they are negotiating a reciprocal tariff reduction framework covering products worth about $30 billion from each side.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the UN General Assembly, accusing the United States and Israel of violating international law by striking civilian infrastructure. He specifically cited the bombing of the Minab school, which killed 150 people, as a symbol of US atrocities. While President Trump threatened to "annihilate" Tehran, Pezeshkian emphasized Iran's resistance and readiness for dialogue without accepting the language of force. Behind the scenes, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with US representatives Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, as well as counterparts from other nations, signaling ongoing diplomatic efforts despite the conflict.

Bentley is launching its first fully electric SUV, the Torcal, priced from £173,000, as part of a £350m investment in its UK business. The vehicle features a synthetic engine noise built from drum recordings to replace the classic combustion growl. Chief executive Frank-Steffen Walliser stated the feature aims to bridge the gap to new buyers. However, the company admitted uncertainty regarding future demand, having previously abandoned plans for annual EV launches due to poor sales. The Torcal joins a thin market for electric luxury SUVs.

John Zuleger, president and CEO of Integrated Power Services, reports that the AI infrastructure buildout is straining electrical equipment already worn out by years of underinvestment. He notes that demand is spilling over into steel mills and copper mines, where equipment is under-maintained. Zuleger highlights that data center emergency response business has surged 300% this year, yet concerns remain regarding the long-term maintenance of mixed fleets and partially completed equipment. He warns that while failure costs are 100 to 1000 times higher than maintenance, the potential human cost of AI downtime is a growing, untested risk.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addressed the UN General Assembly, asserting that Iran would never 'bend the knee' to US threats of annihilation. He emphasized that the Iranian people's resistance would grow under sanctions and pressure. Pezeshkian stated that any diplomatic deal must end the US blockade of Iranian ships and allow access to the Strait of Hormuz. While US President Donald Trump threatened to 'annihilate the Islamic Republic,' Pezeshkian called the rhetoric a sign of a bullying mentality. Indirect talks between Iranian and US envoys were held in New York, but Iran's foreign ministry spokesman dismissed them as not new, reiterating demands for the end of the blockade and the release of frozen assets.

Harvey Weinstein has been sentenced to 15 years in prison following a jury's conviction of him for a criminal sexual act against former assistant Miriam Haley. This sentencing follows a 2024 ruling by New York's highest court that overturned his previous convictions due to a lack of a fair trial. Weinstein, appearing in a wheelchair, denied the allegations but apologized to anyone he may have hurt. The case is part of a series of legal battles involving multiple charges and trials in New York and California.

Chaos erupted in the Vasai-Virar Municipal Corporation (VVMC) house during a discussion regarding filling posts in various departments on a bulk fixed-pay basis instead of a contractual basis. BJP corporators strongly opposed the move, leading to a heated exchange between BJP and Bahujan Vikas Ahadhi (BVA) members. BJP corporator Mahesh Sarvankar alleged that former Municipal Commissioner Anilkumar Pawar had recruited favored individuals during his tenure. However, the Mayor maintained a firm stance, assuring that not a single employee would be removed. The situation escalated when BJP corporator Ganesh Patil aggressively approached the dais using contentious language.

A new paper by Joshua Gans examines the complex liability issues facing AI providers whose services enable both offensive and defensive applications. The analysis suggests that liability can improve overall welfare while potentially increasing harm, as providers sell a common input to productive users, attackers, and defenders. Higher prices within a defended contest reduce effort without changing attack success, whereas compensation weakens defense and raises attacker profits. Consequently, optimal liability must balance these effects against productive exclusion, with monopoly warranting partial but never full liability when provision is worthwhile. Furthermore, strong competition favors universal guarding socially but may encourage unilateral removal at insufficient liability levels.

Father Paolo Benanti, a priest advising the Catholic Church on technology, argues that the prevailing panic over AI extinction risks distracts from the immediate need for democratic regulation. He asserts that major AI labs are behaving like a cartel by excluding outside voices and designing rules in their own self-interest.
