It also discusses a study by Robert Jensen and Emily Oster which found that cable TV access in rural India between 2001 and 2003 narrowed the gap between rural and urban women by 45-70% in social attitudes. However, a follow-up study suggests these effects were limited to educated women, as about 54% of the sample had no education. The article concludes that while cable TV may have changed reference points, genuine empowerment depends on real-world changes outside the TV screen.

The White House established a task force to examine AI risks and opportunities, with a report due within 120 days. Jay Clayton, head of the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, will lead the group, known as the 'Super Intelligence Force,' effectively serving as the US President's AI czar, according to a Wall Street Journal report.

As Brazilian voters prepare to cast ballots, the election is being framed as a referendum on President Trump's influence in the region. Trump claims credit for a shift toward conservative leadership across Latin America, a narrative that resonates with supporters of conservative candidate Jair Bolsonaro. Conversely, opponents, including President Lula, view Trump's actions as a threat to Brazil's sovereignty. The stakes are high for local businesses, such as the Dupps Company, which faced significant losses due to U.S. tariffs. Ultimately, the outcome will reveal the depth of political division and voter disillusionment within Brazil.

France arrested 5,000 people as student protests over overcrowded classrooms and poor facilities spread nationwide and turned into violence. The interior ministry confirmed the arrests. While some politicians condemned the students, others supported their cause. NPR reporter Eleanor Beardsley reported on the situation, noting that the unrest has been used for political campaigning ahead of the presidential election.

South Africa currently lacks comprehensive incentives for electric mobility, unlike neighbors such as Kenya, which introduced special electricity tariffs for electric vehicles. While Kenya's model has boosted revenue and adoption, South African fleet operators like Golden Arrow Bus Services face high energy costs due to standard tariffs and recent hikes. Gideon Neethling of Golden Arrow Bus Services called for supportive electricity tariffs to prevent business failure and aid fleet expansion. Eskom, noting a decline in electricity sales, has suggested adopting a similar off-peak tariff model to encourage EV adoption and stabilize grid demand.

On 3 October 2026, three women journalists filed complaints alleging sexual harassment by Delhi Police personnel while covering protests at Jantar Mantar. The Delhi Police transferred the cases to the Crime Branch for inquiry, stating no FIR was registered as of 4 October 2026 due to a lack of evidence. Legal experts noted the allegations fall under cognisable offences requiring prompt action. Protests demanding accountability continued.

Houthis claimed on Saturday they targeted Saudi Aramco in Riyadh with missiles and drones, stating the operation caused fires. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree said Sanaa and other provinces faced 60 airstrikes in 24 hours, totaling 1,420 strikes. The Saudi-led coalition called these claims misleading, suggesting Houthis sought to divert attention from their losses and foreign ties.

Economists and bankers suggest the Reserve Bank of India is likely to raise the repo rate by 0.25% in its October policy review due to rising inflationary pressures linked to the West Asia crisis and global rate hikes. This potential move would reverse recent rate cuts. While a majority expect a hawkish stance, opinions remain divided on the magnitude of the shift. Experts cite elevated crude oil prices and broadening price pressures as key drivers, noting that India's retail inflation recently hit an eight-month high of 4.82%. The central bank had previously projected CPI inflation for FY27 at 5.0%.

Anthropic has introduced a new prompt asking Claude users to voluntarily share voice conversations to improve its AI models. This feature appears in the voice interface and is disabled by default. Users can choose to allow or deny data usage via a dedicated toggle in Privacy settings. The option remains separate from existing chat training permissions, allowing users to control voice data independently.

Indian stock markets face potential volatility driven by the Reserve Bank of India's interest rate decision, corporate earnings from TCS and DMart, crude oil prices above USD 100, and global bond yields. Analysts from HST Wealth, Religare Broking, and Enrich Money highlight these factors as critical for determining market trajectory and risk appetite amidst geopolitical uncertainty.

Apple removed the messaging app Bitchat from its India App Store following a demand from the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). Jack Dorsey, the app's developer and Twitter co-founder, confirmed the removal via an X post, citing a notice stating the app includes content illegal in India. The app had previously faced scrutiny in July when the Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre ordered GitHub to remove it, citing risks of misuse for unlawful assemblies and evasion of lawful restrictions. Apple noted the app remains available in other territories.

Analysts identify the RBI's interest rate decision, TCS earnings, crude oil prices, and global bond yields as critical factors for stock market movement this week. Additional influences include macroeconomic data and foreign investor activity. Recent market declines were driven by foreign selling, rupee weakness, and elevated crude prices, with specific index losses detailed in the report.

Analysts indicate that the Reserve Bank of India's interest rate decision, corporate earnings from TCS and DMart, crude oil prices, and global bond yields will influence stock market trading this week. Investors are also monitoring economic data and foreign fund flows following a series of weekly declines in Indian equities.

David Robinson, a former OpenAI safety lead, resigned and published an essay arguing the company prioritizes speed over safety. He warned that current methods risk catastrophic failure, urging firms to adopt nuclear-style safeguards. While some industry leaders support slowing development, OpenAI stated it is enhancing security and third-party monitoring in response to these internal concerns.

Chi Onwurah, chair of the parliamentary science, innovation and technology committee, argues that Apple and Google impose an 'app tax' on UK consumers through high commissions and restrictive practices. She cites research indicating British consumers pay approximately £700m annually to these companies, a sum exceeding their combined UK corporation tax payments. Onwurah highlights that Apple and Google control at least 90% of UK mobile devices, creating a duopoly that limits developer choice. While the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act passed in 2024 grants the CMA powers to intervene, Onwurah criticizes the regulator for relying on voluntary commitments rather than binding rules. She urges the CMA to enforce mandatory changes to restore market competition and protect British consumers and developers.

Crisil Ratings states that Indian companies can absorb a potential 50-bps rate hike due to strong balance sheets and low leverage. The agency notes that while the median gearing of rated companies is around 0.5, some sectors may still face pressure. This financial strength should help firms manage higher borrowing costs without significant credit profile deterioration.

Senior BJP leader Tarun Chugh claimed that AAP MLA Sukhveer Singh Maiserkhana exposed the gap between the AAP government's claims of an education revolution and the reality in Punjab. Maiserkhana had accused the government of ignoring teacher shortages. Chugh highlighted inadequate school facilities and ongoing teacher protests, questioning the government's commitment to education and law and order.

BJP spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi accused Congress leadership of maintaining silence regarding Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar, who was injured during an attack on a flydubai flight. Trivedi contrasted this with praise from Prime Minister Narendra Modi and criticized Congress appointments in Uttar Pradesh, alleging political calculations influenced the party's response to the pilot's bravery.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) ordered an immediate recall of Everest pre-packed cumin powder after regulatory samples tested unsafe due to pesticide residues of Azoxystrobin and Thiamethoxam exceeding prescribed limits. The Food Analyst and Referral Food Laboratory confirmed the findings. Simultaneously, the regulator suspended the licence of Creative Bakers and Confectioners Pvt Ltd, which operates The Sugarr & Spice chain in Eastern India. This action followed investigations revealing severe hygiene deficiencies, including pest infestations, inadequate pest control, and poor sanitation in food handling areas. The FBO was directed to cease operations and submit corrective reports.

Max Verstappen secured his first Formula 1 win of the 2026 season at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, while Kimi Antonelli extended his championship lead to 84 points. George Russell retired with five laps remaining due to a suspected power unit failure. The race faced delays from rain and software issues before Verstappen took the lead.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited Kyiv as Russia intensified drone and missile attacks on the capital. Simultaneously, France faces nationwide student protests over school conditions, while Latvia's pro-Ukraine government secured a parliamentary victory.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz made a surprise visit to Kyiv to pledge further military and financial support for Ukraine. The delegation, including Economy Minister Katherina Reiche, aims to deliver interceptor drones and expand joint weapon production. Merz stated that Ukraine needs all support for the coming weeks as Russian attacks intensify. However, the visit occurs against a backdrop of declining domestic approval for Merz and his government, with recent polls showing a widening gap between his CDU/CSU alliance and the AfD. Support for Ukraine remains high in western Germany, but skepticism is growing nationwide regarding the extent of German aid.

Major bridges in Kyiv have been hit by Russian drone strikes for four consecutive days, injuring two people on Sunday. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz visited Kyiv to show support for Ukraine amidst the ongoing invasion. Russia's military stated it would intensify strikes on critical infrastructure. Verified footage shows a drone crashing into the Pivnichnyi Bridge. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko warned of a dramatic situation as Moscow targets housing and logistics. Experts say repeated attacks risk weakening bridge structures. Ukraine's Air Force reported 135 drones launched overnight, with 125 shot down. German Chancellor Merz reaffirmed Germany's support, stating Ukraine faces decisive weeks.

Lewis Hamilton secured third place at the Sepang Grand Prix after a disastrous tyre gamble dropped him to 18th. Hamilton admitted his heart sank when rivals pitted ahead of him, but he stuck with his strategy. As the track dried and safety cars deployed, he fought back to overtake competitors and finish on the podium behind Verstappen and Antonelli.

Suryansh Shedge has been drafted into the India A squad as a replacement for injured Hardik Pandya for the upcoming one-day series against Australia A. Shedge, 23, will miss Mumbai's opening Ranji Trophy game. Ruturaj Gaikwad will lead the side. Naman Dhir will miss the series after being drafted into the T20I squad.

Simone de Beauvoir's memoir, 'A Very Easy Death,' chronicles the passing of her mother, Françoise, who was 77 when she broke her femur. Beauvoir describes the hospital experience, noting her mother's initial enjoyment of care and the eventual discovery of a cancerous tumour. The book explores the complex relationship between mother and daughter, highlighting Beauvoir's realization of her mother's limitations and her own drive for independence. Beauvoir reflects on the universal fear of death and the unique grief associated with losing a mother, describing the separation as a transition into a 'legendary time.' The memoir, translated by Patrick O'Brian, offers a moving account of this final chapter.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated there is no military solution to the conflict with the United States, citing an impasse in talks. He warned that any renewed military confrontation would trigger a stronger response. Araghchi emphasized that only negotiations based on justice and fairness could end the war, noting that recent US operations have shifted toward economic pressure.

The Newcastle Knights lost the NRL grand final to the Sydney Roosters with a final score of 10 to 20, though the Knights scored 19 points in the match. The Roosters defeated the Knights by one point in a classic encounter. James Tedesco won the Clive Churchill Medal for best on ground. Kalyn Ponga scored a try and made a stellar defensive effort. Francis Manuleleua and Jermaine McEwan were praised for their performance. Cody Hopwood made 46 tackles. The Knights fought hard but fell short by the narrowest margin possible.

Rivian spinout ALSO has begun delivering its TM-B electric bikes to customers after months of delays. Early owners report positive experiences with the bike's unique pedal-by-wire system, though one user noted the throttle behaves differently than expected. However, real-world range testing revealed significant gaps between manufacturer claims and actual performance. Under high-assistance conditions with headwinds and hills, a rider achieved only 30 miles (51 km) before reaching 4% battery, far below the advertised 100-mile range. ALSO attributes delays to hardware changes and regulatory challenges. While owners are satisfied with the product, further testing is needed to validate range claims under various assist levels.

An investigation by The Indian Express alleges that the Election Commission of India, under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, facilitated a decade-long democratic rollback. The report highlights that two commissioners formally objected to unauthorized decisions regarding voter rolls, which were implemented despite these objections. The Special Intensive Revision (SIR) process is described as shifting the burden of proof onto citizens, resulting in the deletion of over 13 crore names. The article connects this to broader strategies involving demonetisation and electoral bonds to consolidate power. It notes that the Supreme Court recently struck down electoral bonds but questions the judiciary's role regarding the EC appointment law and the SIR. The piece concludes by citing protests and calls for judicial intervention against the current leadership.

The Leonardo DiCaprio Foundation supported a deal enabling Seychelles to use debt financing for ocean conservation. This arrangement converted $21.6 million in foreign debt into funding, helping the nation increase its protected ocean area from 0.04% to 30% by 2020. By that year, Marine Protection Areas covered 410,000 square kilometres. The Nature Conservancy described this as the world's first ocean debt conversion. The resulting plan divides waters into zones, balancing strict protection for high biodiversity areas with sustainable use zones to support local economies dependent on fishing and tourism.

Voting began in Brazil's 2026 presidential election on Sunday, featuring incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. Polls predict a tight race with neither candidate likely to secure over 50% of the vote, potentially triggering a runoff on October 25. Lula campaigns on welfare and state development, while Bolsonaro emphasizes security and tax cuts. The election pits democracy against what Lula frames as barbarism and corruption.

A recent investigation by the Indian Express reported that two Election Commissioners recorded objections on at least 14 occasions over 10 months regarding Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. The Election Commission responded that its actions were lawful, while the media focused on internal notes. An author, former Central Information Commissioner, suggests citizens can use the Right to Information Act to access official records, minutes, and decisions rather than demanding explanations. This approach seeks to establish whether decisions were unanimous, majority-based, or authorized by law, ensuring transparency in the constitutional authority's functioning without requiring the creation of non-existent explanations.

Researchers led by Yazan Alwadi at Harvard published multiple studies claiming cancer links to nuclear power plants. Critics Deric Tilson and Adam Stein argue the methodology is flawed, noting similar associations with universities and Costco. They assert the findings reflect the method rather than reality, attributing over 2.2 million cancer deaths to Costco to illustrate the error. The authors suggest the actual attributable deaths from the methodology are likely zero.

Latvia's United List party won the parliamentary election with 35.4 percent of the vote, securing 42 seats. Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs stated the result was higher than expected. Meanwhile, populist parties gained ground, aided by support from the Russian-speaking minority, while the Harmony party lost its parliamentary representation. Security and cost of living dominated the campaign.

Brazil held general elections on October 4, 2026, with nearly 159 million eligible voters casting ballots for president, governors, and lawmakers. The presidential race featured incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro among 12 candidates. Voters must secure over 50% of valid votes to win; otherwise, a runoff occurs on October 25. Polls opened at 8 am local time and closed at 5 pm.

Residents in Ramanathapuram and Karaikudi wrote to authorities regarding issues including demands for old drainage receipts, illegal wastewater discharge, and poor toll plaza management. They urged officials to investigate these matters and take action against violations.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan is set to attend a meeting in Riyadh of the Strategic Political and Defense Committee established under the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement. He is expected to reaffirm Türkiye's solidarity with Saudi Arabia regarding Houthi attacks and discuss the institutionalization of the alliance formed with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia in August.

Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray and MNS chief Raj Thackeray led a joint protest in Mumbai against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls, demanding his resignation and the cancellation of the exercise. Participants, including Congress and NCP leaders, marched from Metro Cinema to the BMC headquarters, carrying only the national tricolour.

Heather Stewart, a daughter of an Alzheimer's patient, praises Andy Burnham's proposal to treat personal care as social insurance but argues the changes must be implemented quickly. She highlights that current funding relies heavily on family resources and that Burnham's plan to support care workers is a positive step. However, Stewart warns that the proposed national care service will take too long to materialize, noting that the next parliament seems too distant to wait. She calls on the prime minister to act sooner rather than later to address the urgent needs of families and care workers.

External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar stated that India is shifting its stance on the Russia-Ukraine conflict from mere advocacy to active involvement. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in Delhi on October 4, 2026, he highlighted ongoing conversations regarding Black Sea safety and grain export agreements. Jaishankar emphasized the need for dialogue and diplomacy to resolve the conflict, noting that India seeks uninterrupted energy flows and trade while paying a price for distant conflicts.

Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed responsibility for a fire at an Aramco oil refinery in Riyadh, stating it was a response to Saudi airstrikes. Brigadier Yahya Saree said Yemeni forces used missiles and drones. The Saudi-led coalition called the statement misleading and noted they had intercepted similar attacks previously. Renewed violence has killed hundreds and displaced tens of thousands, ending a 2022 ceasefire.

Tech companies are exploring space-based AI data centers to solve power and cooling challenges on Earth. Proponents argue that solar energy in orbit is continuous and more powerful than on Earth. Jeff Bezos and Elon Musk have championed the concept, with Google recently launching test units into orbit. However, critics note that the economics remain daunting and some advantages may not hold up under scrutiny.

A new tax provision under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act expands corporate tax benefits for data centers built in rural opportunity zones, aiming to lower barriers for large-scale projects. While proponents argue this makes the economic case for rural development more compelling, experts warn the benefits may not guarantee job creation or local economic boosts. Research suggests over 100 rural data centers could qualify, though high-profile tech companies like Amazon, Meta, and Microsoft have denied using the program. Critics note the lack of job requirements and mixed historical results of similar programs, with the expansion estimated to cost $40.9 billion over the next decade.

Jordan Bardella, the 31-year-old leader of France's National Rally party, faces a political challenge following allegations that he made antisemitic comments as a teenager in 2013. The claims, published by the Mediapart website, include screenshots of messages written on Facebook Messenger. These allegations threaten Bardella's prospects as a potential prime minister and Marine Le Pen's chances of winning the presidency.

California Governor Gavin Newsom signed Senate Bill 1090, the Keep Altadena Land in Altadena Hands Act, to limit high-density development in two Altadena zip codes following the Eaton Fire. Residents fear that outside developers are buying empty plots where homes burned, threatening the community's character and affordability. While the law creates a three-year pause on certain developments, it does not affect projects approved before October 1. Critics argue the pause may force financially struggling homeowners to sell, while supporters hope it prevents displacement. The bill includes a carve-out for local land trusts to build affordable housing. Despite the new restrictions, over 60 housing proposals representing 200 to 300 structures have already been approved in the area.

Tens of thousands of Oromo gathered in Addis Ababa to celebrate Irreecha, calling for peace as federal forces entered Mekelle. Participants expressed concern over ongoing conflicts in Tigray and urged the government to stabilize the region. Meanwhile, fears of renewed fighting between Ethiopian forces and Tigrayan rebels have intensified, with reports of attacks and diplomatic tensions with Eritrea and Egypt.

A Washington Post investigation reveals that Braselton Police Chief Michael Steffman used Flock Safety cameras to search license plates roughly 600 times before his arrest for stalking. The report identifies at least 100 police employees accused of misuse, noting that abuses required no hacking. An expert argues the issue stems from a defect in the surveillance system's architecture rather than just user criminality.

The ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0 is scheduled to take place on October 8 at the ITC Maratha in Mumbai. The event will feature a series of sessions addressing global capital flows, smart money, private credit, family offices, and the impact of artificial intelligence on investment strategies. Key topics include the emergence of new financial centers, structured debt opportunities, and the evolution of wealth portfolios through real estate and specialized asset classes. Prominent industry leaders and experts will present on these themes, aiming to provide insights into the future of wealth creation and market dynamics for investors and market leaders.

The Africa Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA) is positioned not as a rival to established global agencies like Fitch or Moody's, but as a tool to expand Africa's capital markets. The author argues AfCRA will help redirect capital from short-term instruments toward infrastructure and manufacturing. Currently, less than 5% of Africa's estimated US$4 trillion domestic capital base has formal ratings, compared to millions in the US and EU. The agency aims to provide ratings for over US$3.5 trillion in unrated capital, offering context to reduce risk perceptions and mobilize funds for long-term productive investment.

Analysts identify five conditions that could spur Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) to return to Indian equities after heavy selling in September, which totaled Rs 45,536 crore. Key factors include a cooling of US bond yields, a decline in crude oil prices, stabilization of the rupee, strong Q2 earnings, and a better risk-reward profile for India compared to other markets. Geojit Financial and Choice Broking cite high US yields and volatile oil prices as current deterrents. The article notes that domestic institutional investors have already cushioned the fall, but foreign money requires specific macroeconomic signals to reconsider emerging markets.

Police in Kalyan are investigating a cyber fraud where a 37-year-old man lost ₹6.97 lakh after being lured by an Instagram reel promising up to 800% daily returns via a fake HDFC Securities platform. The victim was added to a WhatsApp group where suspects shared fake tips and a bogus loan offer before demanding the money. The case was registered after the victim realized the scam when asked to pay a 'short-term profit tax' to withdraw funds.

Angelina Jolie shared Google Earth satellite images showing extensive damage in Rafah, Khan Younis, and Gaza City. Citing UN data, she noted that 82% of Gaza's structures were damaged as of June 2026, with roughly two-thirds destroyed. Jolie highlighted that 1.98 million people, or 94% of the population, need shelter assistance. She emphasized the visible destruction while calling for humanitarian aid and rebuilding efforts.

Dave Benscoter, a retired FBI agent, began a decade-long search in 2012 to rediscover apple varieties nearly forgotten in the Pacific Northwest. Collaborating with experts from the Temperate Orchard Conservancy, he identified 30 lost varieties by researching historical records and analyzing DNA. The Lost Apple Project now works to preserve these historic trees for future generations.

Nida Khan, a suspect in a sexual harassment and forced religious conversion case involving TCS in Nashik, faces mounting legal troubles. Her husband filed a divorce petition citing familial tensions. The Family Court summoned her to appear in person on October 16. Khan, who is approximately eight months pregnant, had previously received conditional bail. Reports suggest the marital crisis stems from the case's impact on their family.

Former Maharashtra chief minister Prithviraj Chavan rejected a call by MNS chief Raj Thackeray to boycott elections, stating participation is a democratic right. Chavan alleged duplicate voters were added in the 2024 election and minority or poor voters were denied rights. Thackeray demanded the cancellation of the Special Intensive Revision, claiming 40 to 60 lakh voters were added and two crore are now being removed. The Election Commission maintains the revision updates and cleans rolls.

Protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar intensified in Delhi on Sunday, with AAP workers, AISA, and NSUI activists detained as demonstrators attempted to march towards Jantar Mantar for the third consecutive day. The agitation alleges irregularities in the Election Commission’s functioning and mass deletion of voters. Police deployed personnel and barricades to stop protesters, leading to clashes. AISA president Neha Bora and AAP leaders were detained, sparking criticism from opposition figures and journalists alleging police misconduct. Over 500 protesters were detained on Friday. Three female journalists alleged sexual harassment by police, prompting an inquiry. The protests continue amid allegations of electoral roll irregularities.

Creators of the animation series Natural Habitat Shorts, Brennan Brinkley, Nicole Low, and Tyler Kula, have found an unexpected audience in China. Their videos, featuring animals in human situations, gained popularity on overseas platforms, leading to official accounts on Chinese social media. The team visited Beijing and Shenzhen in September 2026 to meet fans and discussed future plans, including featuring Chinese animals and exploring new media formats.

Bajaj Finance stands out as a relative outperformer in India's weak market, which has seen benchmarks fall about 6% in September amid foreign selling and high bond yields. The company's resilience is attributed to strong loan growth, improved asset quality, and a recent Rs 17,500 crore capital raise. Brokerage UBS upgraded the stock to Neutral, citing better asset quality and a cushion against macro headwinds, while expecting over 30% EPS growth in FY27.

Axis Direct selected five small-cap stocks following a market correction, citing strong value. The brokerage assigned target prices implying upside ranging from 18% to 40% for companies including Chalet hotels, Healthcare Global Enterprises, Minda Corporation, City Union Bank, and CCL Products.

A major political confrontation has erupted between opposition parties and the Election Commission regarding the Special Intensive Revision of voter lists. Demonstrations were held in Mumbai and Delhi, with the INDIA bloc demanding the repeal of the process and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Internal disputes also surfaced within the Congress-Samajwadi Party alliance over seat-sharing arrangements ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh elections.

Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath announced the renaming of Bhadohi district to Sant Ravidas Nagar Bhadohi, reviving a name from 1994. The move, made during a program inaugurating 112 projects worth 1,340 crore, ties the change to welfare and development. Adityanath highlighted the district's carpet industry and linked the name to the medieval saint's vision of social unity.

The Left Democratic Front alleges that the signature of BJP councillor R. Sugathan was forged in the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation attendance register to falsely show his presence at meetings he missed while in hiding. LDF leader S.P. Deepak claims the forgery occurred on February 26, March 11, and April 27, suggesting the Mayor's knowledge was involved to avoid Sugathan's disqualification.

Chief Minister Nara Chandrababu Naidu, alongside Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan and other officials, will launch water schemes under the Jal Jeevan Mission in Kadapa on October 5, 2026. The initiative aims to provide clean drinking water to 3.27 crore rural households through 27.36 lakh new tap connections, with a total investment of ₹30,156 crore. District Minister S. Savitha highlighted additional government funding for various development projects.

A Mongabay investigation found that chemicals from Myanmar's polluting mines have poisoned vast tracts of Thai farmland, carried by at least six transboundary rivers. The report identified more than 50 companies in Thailand importing minerals like antimony and copper from Myanmar, mostly destined for China. Few Thai companies know the origin of these minerals or if the mines are legal, leaving downstream communities facing a public health crisis with no clean water or food security.

President Donald Trump announced the formation of a Super Intelligence Force, led by National Intelligence Director Jay Clayton. The task force aims to coordinate federal efforts to maintain American leadership in super intelligence. Trump stated the force will protect American interests and improve lives. It has 120 days to report on AI risks and opportunities.

Yemen's president announced a military operation to retake Houthi-held territory on October 4, 2026, despite the group's recent advances. The offensive aims to liberate the country from the Iran-backed militia, which has encircled the government-held city of Taiz and cut supply routes. While Saudi Arabia provides military support, experts question the offensive's effectiveness given the Houthis' continued control of key areas.

Volkswagen Group faces challenges including labor disputes and competition in China, prompting aggressive incentives for its electric vehicles. Audi is offering $20,000 cash on 2026 RS e-tron GT models plus $1,100 in charging rebates. Porsche, which rarely offers rebates, provides up to $4,500 in savings via a payment assistance program for Macan buyers. Volkswagen offers $12,500 customer cash and $1,100 in charging rebates on 2025 ID.4 models, with potential state-level savings reaching $18,000. These deals, sourced from sites like CarsDirect and Edmunds, are current as of October 4, 2026, though availability varies by market and buyer qualifications.

A corporate employee in Bengaluru went viral on social media after complaining that private-sector salaries have remained stagnant for 20 years while rents have surged. The resident described the situation as a 'time paradox,' noting that landlords charge future prices while companies pay past wages. The post sparked debate about the city's rising cost of living and housing affordability.

An Egyptian journalist, Mohamed Ashraf, faces terrorism charges for allegedly joining the outlawed Muslim Brotherhood and spreading false news. This follows the detention of six Matsadaash journalists, an independent fact-checking platform, by security forces. Abdallah Qadri and others were arrested over two days. Abdelrahman Mansour, the co-founder, denied any association with the group and condemned the arrests as a grave attack on journalism. Rights groups, including the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, state the crackdown targets press freedoms. Dozens of journalists staged a sit-in demanding their release, while over 80 rights groups condemned the arrests. The US recently waived human rights conditions on military aid to Egypt, which Mansour suggests may enable such violations.

The BJP denied reports that R Sreelekha resigned as a councillor of the Thiruvananthapuram Corporation. Although a WhatsApp message allegedly posted by Sreelekha claimed she submitted her resignation, BJP leaders stated the message was deleted and that no formal resignation letter exists. Mayor V V Rajesh confirmed Sreelekha would continue her five-year tenure. BJP leader Suresh visited Sreelekha at a hospital, attributing her silence to health concerns rather than resignation. Conversely, CPI(M) leader V Sivankutty criticized Sreelekha, alleging she was using the resignation claim to threaten the BJP for personal gain. Sreelekha has not yet responded to the allegations or the resignation claims.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India directed Everest Food Products to recall specific batches of pre-packed cumin powder after tests detected pesticide residues exceeding limits. A sample from a Goa resort was found unsafe under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The regulator confirmed the batch was unsafe following a referral laboratory review and ordered an immediate market withdrawal.

More than 400 schools in France will close or partially suspend lessons on Monday as authorities prepare for continued student protests. Education Minister Édouard Geffray cited unfulfilled security conditions, noting 24 schools were damaged and 78 staff injured. The government faces pressure to address grievances regarding underfunding and neglect while condemning associated urban violence.

Rumors of a pneumonic plague outbreak in Russia's Irkutsk region have sparked panic following the death of a 28-year-old laboratory assistant. While local media reports she broke a test tube containing Yersinia pestis, Rospotrebnadzor states the situation is stable and the cause was pneumonia of unknown origin. Authorities have implemented quarantine measures and medical observation for around 200 people, though officials have avoided explicitly confirming a plague link in recent communications.

Lionel Messi's final appearance for Argentina concludes a decades-long journey from obscurity to national icon. Initially unknown to authorities and facing skepticism, Messi endured early struggles and misidentification. Over time, his loyalty and leadership, particularly under coach Lionel Scaloni, transformed public perception. Argentine journalist Sergio Levinsky describes this evolution as a love story built over time, culminating in a celebrated farewell against Benin.

All India Students' Association chief Neha Bora was detained by Delhi Police on Sunday during protests demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. Police later released her but alleged her phone and bag were not returned. The association claimed she was taken in an unauthorised vehicle without a female constable. Protests continue across the country against Kumar over concerns regarding the Election Commission's handling of the special intensive revision exercise.

Article author Tabitha Rowland argues that approaching novels with the same analytical skills used in gossip can enhance reading comprehension. She suggests that identifying behavioral patterns and social subtexts within fictional narratives mirrors the process of evaluating real-world social interactions. By treating literary conversations as gossip, readers can better decode character motivations and authorial intent. Rowland cites examples from Jane Austen’s Pride and Prejudice and Shakespeare’s Much Ado About Nothing to illustrate how gossip drives plot and character development. She concludes that this method not only makes reading more enjoyable but also helps readers recognize universal human experiences across different eras and cultures.

The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear pleas on October 5 seeking the suspension or resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar amid a dispute over the Special Intensive Revision exercise. Petitioners allege that Kumar exercised powers individually without the consent of fellow Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, who reportedly objected to decisions made at least 14 times over 10 months. The Election Commission refutes these claims, stating that all final decisions are taken unanimously. The court will examine whether Kumar acted unauthorisedly and may direct a suspension pending the final hearing.

Campaigning for the Nagaon Lok Sabha bypoll in Assam concluded on Sunday, with major parties expressing strong confidence in their prospects. The BJP, led by Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, predicts a victory margin of 2.5 to 3 lakh votes, despite acknowledging the constituency's Muslim majority. Conversely, Congress state president Gaurav Gogoi claims the party will win again, citing BJP's alleged atrocities against minorities. The AIUDF, led by Badruddin Ajmal, also asserts a high probability of victory, estimating a margin of around 1 million votes. Voting is scheduled for October 6, with results expected on October 9. Sixteen candidates are contesting the election.

Local officials say a US Marine was arrested on suspicion of murder after a woman's body was found in a hotel in Okinawa, Japan. Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi called the crime brutal and urged stricter discipline for US personnel. The victim was identified as Yagi Anna, 39, and the suspect as Devin Jacob Ballard, 20. Authorities stated they are cooperating with Japanese investigations.

Brazilian polling stations opened for approximately 160 million eligible voters on Sunday. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva faces Senator Flávio Bolsonaro in the first round of the presidential election. According to opinion polls, Lula holds 45% of voting intentions while Bolsonaro has 43%. Neither candidate is expected to cross the 50% threshold required for an outright victory, suggesting a second round of voting on 25 October. The Superior Electoral Court estimates 158,745,463 voters will cast ballots.

The Palestinian Education Ministry reported that Israel has killed more than 800 Palestinian teachers and injured over 3,300 others since the war began in October 2023. The ministry stated that over 170 teachers remain detained in harsh conditions and described the situation as a battle for survival amid systematic targeting. It also highlighted severe financial hardship caused by withheld tax revenues.

Major bridges in Ukraine have been targeted by Russian strikes over the past four days as Moscow ramps up attacks in Kyiv. The Pivnichnyi Bridge has been hit for the second consecutive day, while the Pivdennyi Bridge was struck multiple times earlier this week. BBC Ukraine correspondent Dan Johnson reports on the situation near one of the targeted bridges.

Denver Kanowski, a rural Queensland resident, opposes a proposed $31bn datacentre by Anthropic, citing fears of repeating the boom-and-bust cycle of the local coal seam gas industry. The project, planned for a 725-hectare site near Dalby, would require a peak power capacity of 2.16GW and create approximately 1,400 long-term jobs. Local residents, including Mordechai Winters and Liza Balmain, have launched a petition signed by over 21,500 people, expressing concerns about energy demand and environmental impacts. While the Queensland government plans to assess the project, community backlash remains strong, with some calling for a moratorium to prevent similar outcomes to previous resource booms.

YMX Logistics is piloting self-driving, zero-emission yard trucks from AI startup Outrider at enterprise customer sites. Under a five-year agreement, YMX will operate the autonomous system on its all-electric fleet starting this year. The partnership aims to address labor shortages and reduce reliance on expensive diesel fuel while enhancing safety and productivity in supply chain operations.

Donald Trump appointed Jay Clayton, the director of national intelligence, as the new White House AI czar. Clayton, who leads 18 intelligence agencies, previously served as the SEC chair. Trump announced the appointment via social media, designating the role to lead the Super Intelligence Force. The move follows industry warnings about rapid AI development and aligns with Trump's previous plans to oversee the technology's growth and monitor for potential threats.

The Rapid Action Force and Delhi Police have been deployed in central Delhi as protests intensify near Jantar Mantar and the Shangri-La roundabout over the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Protesters attacked a police bus carrying detainees, smashing a window and helping them escape. Police have enforced Section 163 prohibitory orders and detained hundreds of protesters, including high-profile individuals like AISA National President Neha Bora and political activist Yogendra Yadav.

Air quality in central Singapore entered the unhealthy range at 9pm on Sunday with a 24-hour PSI reading of 101, while other regions remained moderate. The National Environment Agency attributes this to smoke plumes from southern Sumatra and fires in Kalimantan, forecasting continued haze risks under prevailing winds.

Troops from eight nations, including China, concluded joint military exercises in Russia on Saturday following coordinated operations, according to CCTV. The Center-2026 exercise began Monday in the Chelyabinsk region. Russian President Vladimir Putin attended the drills in the Ural Mountains, stating that 47,000 troops trained to repel attacks across 11 firing ranges and the Caspian Sea. Approximately 6,000 troops participated in the final phase at Chebarkulsky.

Burundi's President Evariste Ndayishimiye told leaders at the Alamein Africa Forum that persistent violence across Africa is hindering farming, education, and development. He noted that insecurity prevents farmers from working and children from attending school, citing unprecedented humanitarian catastrophes in the DRC and Sudan. Meanwhile, Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi urged states to exercise their right to development responsibly without harming others.

Researchers in India developed a low-cost home security sensor using garlic peel and plastic as a triboelectric nanogenerator. The device converts mechanical motion, such as a door opening, into electrical signals without external power. A single layer of materials generated about 210 V and 45 microamperes, while two layers produced roughly 400 V and 65 µA. The sensor maintained performance after six months of storage and 200 mechanical stress cycles. In 50 tests, the system detected door openings with 92 percent accuracy, sending real-time alerts to a smartphone. The study, published August 20 in IEEE Sensors Letters, highlights the potential of repurposing agricultural biowaste for simple technological solutions.

Data center companies have donated or invested more than $343 million across rural Texas to address community needs like infrastructure repairs and school programs. This strategy aims to win public support as communities face fiscal challenges and express opposition to new developments. While companies like Google and Rowan Digital Infrastructure highlight their investments as a way to partner with locals, critics remain wary of self-serving motives and the boom-and-bust patterns of industrial development. Despite concerns about rising costs and water usage, data centers continue to position themselves as essential partners for struggling municipalities.

Russia stated it would increase attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure following President Zelenskyy's comments on targeting Russian oil refineries. The Russian Defense Ministry confirmed plans to strike military facilities in Kyiv and other regions, citing a warning that diplomats in the capital face mortal danger.

Polling began in Bosnia-Herzegovina on Sunday for around 3.4 million eligible voters. Citizens will elect officials across multiple tiers, including the presidency and parliament. The election occurs as the nation faces economic slowdown, sluggish EU progress, and political gridlock. Ethnic parties dominate, while opposition coalitions challenge them. Preliminary results are expected late Sunday.

Google has paused its Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program until next year, citing a significant rise in automated submissions. The company stated that the vast majority of these reports are invalid or contain hallucinations, overwhelming engineers and maintainers. Google promised an update in the first quarter of 2027 and encouraged participants to explore other bug bounty programs.

Thieves in California stole two PlusAI trailers marked with Nvidia branding, expecting valuable AI hardware. Police recovered them hours later, finding they contained only sand used for weight simulation during autonomous truck testing. No equipment was damaged.

Google launched the Fitbit Air in India for ₹13,999, positioning it as a screenless health tracker. It distinguishes itself from cheaper competitors like Noise REP and Amazfit Helio Strap through a Gemini AI-powered Health Coach, which requires a separate Google Health Premium subscription.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman warned that granting artificial intelligence religious authority or surrendering human judgment to it creates a real safety issue. His comments follow reports that rival company Anthropic consulted religious and philosophical thinkers regarding AI consciousness and morality. Other technology executives, including Microsoft's Mustafa Suleyman, have also expressed concern about developing AI systems that appear conscious.

Ex-RBI Governor Das stated India's real GDP grew 7.8% in the first quarter of the current financial year. He noted growth just exceeds 8% for the period July-September 25-26 to April-June 26-27. Das emphasized structural reforms and productive capabilities for resilient long-term expansion while highlighting digital governance savings of around Rs 5.1 lakh crore.

Daniel Kreiss and Lorcan Neill from the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill argue that social media platforms should adopt a 'militant democracy' framework to counter threats to democratic governance. Published in the journal Information, Communication & Society, their paper suggests platforms must prioritize democratic principles over state regulation, particularly in contexts where governments are undergoing democratic backsliding or have become authoritarian. The authors contend that platforms, as integral communicative institutions, have a responsibility to prevent anti-democratic actors from seizing power and to protect opposition voices. Citing the rapid decline of democracy in the United States, Brazil, and other nations, they urge trust and safety executives to make proactive decisions regarding content moderation. The framework calls for platforms to override immediate business interests to safeguard free and fair elections and democratic norms, drawing on historical precedents where platforms successfully de-platformed figures like Donald Trump following January 6th.

Supreme Court Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan criticized the Special Intensive Revision process for deleting names from voter lists, stating it strikes at the heart of the Constitution. Speaking at Nalsar, Hyderabad, he argued that disenfranchising citizens is arbitrary and that the right to vote is integral to India's freedom. Bhuyan emphasized that no authority can alter Article 326 without notice and hearing.

The Kerala High Court directed the CBI to investigate the 2012 disappearance of Subash Chandra Bose, a Tripura State Rifles soldier. While the CBI questioned jurisdiction and the likelihood of tracing him after 14 years, the court ordered the inquiry under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, emphasizing that a premier agency should not take a pessimistic view in such cases.

Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan announced that the Muziris Heritage Project will become an international heritage tourism destination. He launched water taxis and kayaks during the event, stating plans to expand services to regions like Ezhikkara and Kodungalloor. Tourism Minister P.C. Vishnunadh described the initiative as a potential global tourism model. The government also aims to revive suspended boating services and develop new museums and hotels to boost local businesses and employment.

A 36-year-old Pakistani undertrial prisoner named Shahid Imran allegedly died by suicide at a high-security central jail in Jammu on Sunday. Officials reported that he was found unconscious in his cell around 5.15 am and was subsequently declared brought dead at GMCH. Imran, a resident of Sargooda district in Pakistan's Punjab, was identified as the deceased.

The GST Council in New Delhi is set to unveil GST 2.0 reforms aimed at simplifying business processes and reducing litigation. Proposals include a system of deemed acknowledgement for refunds and registration applications within 10 days, and a target to clear 60% of registration applications in three days. Significant changes address decriminalisation, raising the prosecution threshold to Rs 5 crore and reducing maximum sentences. The reforms also introduce guardrails for e-way bills to prevent harassment of truck drivers and simplify service definitions for exporters. Officials expect these measures to benefit SMEs and improve cash flow for long-gestation projects.

About 200 people attended a forum in the Victorian seat of Ripon where candidates debated renewable energy lines, an emergency services levy, and road conditions. Sitting Labor member Martha Haylett and One Nation candidate Donna Buxton were absent. Jo Armstrong opposed the renewable push, while Tim Drylie called for better compensation. The event served as a temperature check ahead of the November 28 election.

President Donald Trump announced a rebranding of artificial intelligence to super intelligence, accompanied by a non-binding safety pact signed by major tech executives. Participants on TechCrunch’s Equity podcast expressed skepticism regarding the pact’s legal weight, noting its voluntary nature and a misspelling of the United States on the document. While Trump described the agreement as morally binding, analysts highlighted the stark contrast between his previous anti-regulation stance and the recent collaboration with CEOs like Dario Amodei, Mark Zuckerberg, and Elon Musk. The meeting appears to serve as a rebranding exercise aimed at alleviating fears that super intelligence poses less risk than traditional AI, though underlying tensions between the administration and companies like Anthropic remain unresolved.

A 31-year-old woman from Telangana died in a road accident in Missouri, US, after a truck allegedly struck her car. Her family in Mahabubabad has appealed to the government for assistance to transport her remains home for last rites. Another passenger sustained serious injuries and was hospitalized. Details regarding the crash and the injured woman's condition are still awaited.

Brazil's presidential election polls closed Sunday in a tight contest between incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro. Results are expected within hours. Current polling shows Lula at 46% and Bolsonaro at 45%, with a runoff on October 25 likely if neither exceeds 50%. Lula vows to defeat the far right, while Bolsonaro calls for change and pledges to pardon his father if elected.

Over 700 families living in JJ cluster bastis near the Prime Minister's residence face eviction and relocation to Savda Ghevra. Residents fear losing livelihoods and education after officials threatened demolition. The Centre claims the land is for defence infrastructure, while residents argue relocation must be within a five-kilometre radius. Courts have dismissed their case, and families are now being asked to vacate by October 6, 2026.

The Aam Aadmi Party intensified protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar on October 5, 2026, demanding his removal and action against a police officer accused of sexual harassment. BJP leaders accused AAP of attempting to vitiate Delhi's political atmosphere. AAP leader Saurabh Bharadwaj highlighted perceived double standards in police action, while Arvind Kejriwal condemned the detention of his members. At least 25 AAP members were detained during the march.

Investigators are searching for suspect Varun Kumar in Delhi after matching his image to footage. Police intensified financial probes into retired IAS officer Rakesh Agrawal's accounts and two disputes worth Rs 1 crore and Rs 4 crore. No direct link to the murder has been established yet. A Rs 50,000 reward was declared for his arrest.

Ankith Burki, a seventh-grader from San Jose, designed an atmospheric water generator to address global water scarcity. By testing low-frequency sine waves, he found they increased water collection by 117 percent compared to silent conditions. His prototype used the Peltier effect to cool air and condense moisture. Burki's project earned him a place among 30 national finalists in the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge. While the results are promising, further research is needed before the technique can be applied outside controlled prototypes.

Congress general secretary KC Venugopal summoned former Uttarakhand CM Harish Rawat to Delhi amid party concerns over his recent solo political yatras. Leadership fears these independent activities undermine coordinated preparations for the state Assembly elections. Kumari Selja previously wrote to Rawat requesting he stop the programme, citing it as too individualistic. The meeting aims to restore party unity and align Rawat's moves with the Congress poll strategy.

Polls closed in Bosnia and Herzegovina on Sunday evening for the general election, with 3.4 million voters eligible. Preliminary results show early leads for nationalist candidates in the presidency. The election occurs amidst economic challenges and ethnic divisions, with former leader Milorad Dodik barred from office but remaining influential. Results are expected late Sunday.

Telangana targets increasing its renewable-energy capacity from 10,642 MW in 2025-26 to 29,645 MW by 2029-30. The state seeks benefits from the Union Cabinet-approved Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme, pending approval of its transmission and storage projects. Approved plans include 7,800 MW of new capacity, comprising solar, wind, and battery storage, to support grid stability and industrial demand.

Australia's electric vehicle market saw an unprecedented boost in 2026, with EVs accounting for 25.8% of total sales. Chinese carmaker BYD has emerged as a formidable competitor, selling over 68,000 vehicles in the first eight months of 2026 to become Australia's second-highest-selling brand. Globally, BYD's sales surged from about 190,000 in 2020 to 4.6 million in 2025. The company attributes its success to vertical integration, a diverse product range including plug-in hybrids, and its Blade Battery technology. Despite facing cybersecurity scrutiny and safety concerns, BYD continues to challenge established automotive brands.

The 2026 Brazilian presidential election pits incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against Flávio Bolsonaro, son of former president Jair Bolsonaro. Polls closed at 17:00 BRT. Lula, 80, seeks a third term despite term limits preventing a 2030 run. Flávio, 45, campaigns while his father serves a 27-year sentence. Minas Gerais is viewed as a critical bellwether state for the outcome.

The U.S. Department of Defense signed a contract with Overview Energy to develop a space-based solar power system capable of beaming energy to Earth. The Pentagon aims to deploy a demonstration by 2028, with full satellite constellation deployment starting in 2030. Overview Energy also secured a deal with Meta for up to 1 gigawatt of power. While proponents highlight 24-hour energy generation, critics question the technology's economic viability.

Nishant Kerketta, a fashion and fitness enthusiast from Jharkhand, has gained significant attention on Instagram for his unique content style. His videos juxtapose scenes of him working in rural agricultural settings with carefully styled fashion reveals. One reel challenges the stereotype that men from villages cannot dress well, transitioning from farm work to a polished look featuring a white shirt, denim, and accessories. Viewers have reacted positively, comparing him to fictional characters and praising his style. Kerketta does not separate rural life from fashion, instead using the contrast between his modest village surroundings and his polished outfits as a central theme in his content.

A security camp in Abujhmad, Chhattisgarh, has been converted into a hostel for Scheduled Tribe students following improved security conditions. Narayanpur Collector Namrata Jain initiated the project to provide safe accommodation and educational support. The facility serves students from remote villages, addressing logistical challenges and reducing financial burdens on families. It reflects shifting development priorities in the region.

The Election Commission of India (ECI) has outlined various forms for its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls starting in June 2025. Form 6 is for new registrations or restoring deleted names, while Form 7 challenges inclusions or requests deletions. Form 8 handles address changes and other updates, though some voters report confusion regarding its use during SIR. Forms 6A and 6B serve overseas electors and Aadhaar authentication, respectively. Additional forms, such as 9 through 11B, are internal lists maintained by electoral officers to track claims and objections. Kanishka Singharia of Mint reports on these procedures.

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez is considering calling an early general election after Congress rejected two housing measures. While 29 November is the earliest possible date, no decision has been made. Sánchez is consulting coalition partners and weighing public protests against the government's proposals to extend eviction protections and regulate rentals.

Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad resigned on October 5, 2026, without stated reasons, according to state media. Hamid Bovard, CEO of the National Iranian Oil Company, is now acting minister. President Dr. Pezeshkian accepted the resignation. Paknejad previously noted that oil revenues would continue. The resignation occurs during a seven-month war between Iran and the U.S., which pressures the economy.

Justice Ujjal Bhuyan of the Supreme Court stated that any process disenfranchising millions violates the constitutional order and Articles 14 and 326. Speaking at NALSAR University, he asserted no authority can remove voting rights, calling such acts arbitrary and a negation of the Constitution. This follows the Court's earlier upholding of the Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

The article discusses the Japanese term 'shinjū,' historically associated with lovers' suicides in literature and theater. It notes that the term also applies to other categories like family and parent-child suicides. The text raises a question regarding whether such deaths can be classified as suicides when the child lacks the capacity to consent, highlighting the complexity of the terminology.

Emma Claassen, founder of the Women in Scaffolding Association, responds to Adrian Chiles regarding a recruitment crisis in Britain's scaffolding industry. She argues that the conversation should focus on attracting capable people regardless of gender rather than traditional demographics. Claassen emphasizes that while the industry needs to widen its pool, standards must remain high and the work cannot be automated. She highlights that some of the next generation will be women.

Three female journalists accused Delhi police officers of sexual harassment during protests in the capital. The Delhi Police acknowledged receiving the complaint and transferred it to the crime branch for a fair inquiry. Videos showed protesters being dragged from the Jantar Mantar site. Activist Aahna Singh stated police dragged her by her hair and resorted to brutality. The Press Club of India demanded immediate action, calling the behavior unacceptable in a democracy.

As utility-scale solar and wind farms face land scarcity and legal pushback, floating power plants are emerging as a critical solution for expanding clean energy capacity. These technologies, which include floating solar, tidal, wave, and nuclear systems, can provide permanent energy for cities like Pevek and Luanda or temporary power for mining and emergencies. Prototypes are being tested globally, from Russia's floating nuclear plants to the University of Michigan's wave energy devices on Beaver Island. Experts suggest offshore floating solar could offer higher efficiency than land-based systems due to seawater cooling, presenting a strategic alternative for nations with limited land resources while enhancing energy security and resilience.

Yemen's internationally recognised government announced an all-out war to reclaim territory held by the Houthis. President Rashad al-Alimi declared military operations to retake the republic's territory. The announcement follows recent exchanges of strikes between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition, including attacks on Saudi oil sites. While the government claims to be weakening Houthi capabilities, security sources indicate the group continues to make gains and control key areas like Taiz.

Media reports indicate the flydubai co-pilot, identified as Hamam al-Hammami, likely acted alone in an apparent bid to crash the Israel-bound flight. Israeli officials and sources suggest no link to a group or government exists yet. The UAE leads the investigation, which found the suspect attempted a terrorist act. The flight, carrying 174 passengers, made a rapid descent of over 17,000 feet before landing in Saudi Arabia.

SpaceX CEO Elon Musk announced on October 4 that he would rename the company's AI unit to SpaceXSI. He confirmed the change in response to a user inquiry on X, citing US President Donald Trump's advocacy for the term "super intelligence" over "artificial intelligence." At the time of reporting, the account had not yet been updated, and no timeline or further details were provided. SpaceXAI did not immediately respond to comment requests.

Saint-Gobain plans to invest ₹11,000 crore in India over the next five years, aiming to shift from selling products to offering energy-efficient building solutions. Sreedhar N, the company's Asia-Pacific and India CEO, intends to acquire meaningful assets to expand into construction chemicals and insulation. This investment represents a sharp acceleration compared to the previous decade's spending.

External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar stated that India has moved beyond mere advocacy to actively engage Moscow and Kyiv in resolving the Ukraine conflict. Speaking at a Munich Leaders' Meeting in New Delhi, he highlighted efforts to ensure Black Sea shipping safety and facilitate grain and energy exports. Jaishankar noted that while India and Russia have historically strong relations dating back to the 1950s, the current geopolitical landscape is marked by a radical repositioning of the United States and the rise of China. He argued that emerging powers are now focusing on diversifying their economies and supply chains through a new architecture of cooperation based on reasonable convergence rather than strict ideological alignment.

Justice Ujjal Bhuyan stated that stripping millions of Indians of voting rights is intrinsically arbitrary and violates constitutional guarantees. Speaking at NALSAR University of Law, he argued that the Constitution does not permit two classes of citizens. He warned that such processes undermine the constitutional order and strike at its very heart.

Japanese police arrested a 20-year-old U.S. Marine on suspicion of killing a 39-year-old woman in Naha, Okinawa, officials said Sunday. The suspect was found walking alone after security footage showed him entering the hotel with the victim. Okinawa Governor Genta Koja expressed outrage, citing the case as a major shock to residents living near U.S. bases. The U.S. Marine Corps stated it takes the allegations seriously and is cooperating with authorities.

Three women journalists alleged sexual harassment by Delhi Police officers while covering protests at Jantar Mantar. The Delhi Police acknowledged the complaints and transferred them to the Crime Branch for an impartial inquiry. The Cockroach Janta Party organized a protest demanding action against the accused officer. Congress leader Rahul Gandhi questioned the delay in registering an FIR, while the Press Club of India condemned the police behavior and called for immediate action to protect media freedom.

Ethiopian federal forces reportedly recaptured Mekelle airport from Tigrayan fighters, according to unnamed city sources speaking to The Associated Press. While a general confirmed military control, neither the Ethiopian government nor the Tigray People's Liberation Front issued official statements. Uncertainty remains regarding the exact timing of the recapture and whether fighting occurred, as severe network disruptions hinder verification.

Samajwadi Party MP Shiv Pal Singh Patel alleges Rahul Gandhi was too scared to contest from Amethi in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections, choosing Raebareli instead. Patel claims Akhilesh Yadav persuaded Gandhi to run, warning he would field his own candidate otherwise. Patel also credits the SP-Congress alliance for Congress winning six seats in Uttar Pradesh, where SP secured 37 of the 80 seats.

Khanh Nguyen Phu, a Vietnamese nationalized resident in Japan, observes a significant shift in attitudes toward foreign nationals since his arrival in 2014. While he initially encountered politeness, he notes that by 2026 the environment has become politically charged. Disinformation has unsettled the community, leading some to question their futures. Nguyen Phu, who speaks English and Japanese, highlights the struggles of unskilled workers compared to his own smooth integration.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced a new aid package worth more than 1.3 billion euros ($1.5 billion) for Ukraine during a visit to Kyiv on Sunday. The agreement includes approximately 1 billion euros for weapons, including combat drones, and 350 billion euros to support Ukraine's energy sector. Merz stated that these barbarous attacks on the civilian population must stop and called for European unity against Russia. Meanwhile, Kyiv mayor Vitali Klitschko urged the capital to be on a war footing due to round-the-clock attacks on residential areas and infrastructure.

Thousands protested in Delhi on October 4 against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged police harassment. The demonstrations, led by student and youth groups, turned violent as protesters breached barricades and clashed with Delhi Police, resulting in hundreds of detentions. Police deployed 5,000 personnel, including riot gear and water cannons, to control the crowds. Separately, supporters protested outside a police station demanding an FIR against ACP Vivek Bhagat for allegedly sexually assaulting a journalist. CPI(M) leader Brinda Karat criticized the police response, stating they demanded video evidence of the assault despite the complainant's presence.

LKP Securities analyst Rupak De warns investors to remain cautious as the Nifty index breaches its 200-week moving average and slips below the 22,600 support level for the first time since the 2020 crash. De notes this marks the eighth consecutive weekly decline, the longest in 25 years. He advises reducing long exposure until the index decisively moves above 22,600, warning that further drops toward 20,500 are possible if the level holds. De cites historical data showing significant falls in 2008 and 2020 but notes quick reversals in 2011, 2013, and 2016, suggesting outcomes remain uncertain.

Bosnia is proceeding with a general election on Sunday, a process dominated by political parties closely linked to the ethnic divisions of the 1990s war. The vote will select numerous officials across multiple government tiers within a complex system established by the 1995 peace deal to maintain the partitioned country. FRANCE 24 correspondent Laurent Rouy reports from Belgrade on the event.

According to profitability scan data from StockEdge.com, seven NSE midcap companies recorded rising earnings per share for four consecutive quarters through June 2026. The list includes Poonawalla Fincorp, FSN E-commerce Ventures, Laurus Labs, Lodha Developers, National Aluminium Company, Bank of India, and Radico Khaitan, each reporting higher EPS than the previous quarter.

Aleph Alpha has released Kolibri, an open-weight Mixture-of-Experts language model designed for English and German. The model features 78.1B total parameters with only 3.46B active per token, enabling efficient deployment on regulated hardware like NVIDIA B200 or H200 GPUs. Developed end-to-end by teams in Germany and Finland, Kolibri targets sovereign deployment in public administration and aerospace. It adheres to the EU AI Act and GDPR, utilizing a 128,000-token vocabulary optimized for German text. Benchmarks show it leads in English agentic tasks and ties with Qwen3.5 on average performance, while supporting up to 1,048,576 tokens of context via a hybrid attention mechanism.

Global plugin vehicle registrations rose 5% year over year in August, reaching approximately 1.8 million units. Pure battery electric vehicles (BEVs) drove this growth with a 13% increase, representing 73% of plugin sales, while plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) declined 12%. Excluding the US and China, EV sales jumped 53% in July. In the global top 20, the Tesla Model Y remained the leader despite a 12% drop, followed by the Geely Xingyuan and BYD Song. Toyota surpassed Volkswagen to become the best-selling legacy brand, aided by the return of the RAV4 PHEV. Market share for the top five OEMs decreased year on year, indicating a diversifying market with rising competition from brands like Leapmotor and Zeekr.

Former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon is scheduled to testify at a New York City hearing on artificial intelligence, according to a report by Bloomberg News. The testimony comes at the request of Council Speaker Julie Menin, who has encouraged AI whistleblowers to speak as lawmakers consider new safety bills. Coxon, who recently left Anthropic, has warned that AI developers believe the technology could end human life by the decade's end. Reuters could not immediately verify the report.

The article suggests playing a track by Mrs. Green Apple to explain modern J-pop to newcomers. It highlights the group's style as 'triumphant maximalism,' noting their songs often blend diverse elements like music boxes, orchestral strings, and country-western sounds. The text points to their 2018 song 'Ao to Natsu' as a representative example of this eclectic approach.

Edmund Lam responds to a forum discussion on AI copyright, arguing that the debate must analytically distinguish between protecting existing rights, using works for training, and establishing authorship thresholds. He clarifies his concern focuses on whether human creativity in AI-assisted outputs warrants copyright, rejecting a fixed numerical threshold like 75% in favor of assessing meaningful human creative control.

Chan Eng Ann argues that Singapore's fragmented transport information across multiple apps creates unnecessary friction. She proposes that the Government spearhead a single super app to consolidate services like real-time traffic, MRT status, and parking. This unified platform would improve commuter convenience and enable smarter urban planning through comprehensive data collection.

Foreign minister S Jaishankar stated at the Munich Leaders Meeting that the US has deliberately chosen to become a "lonelier power," while reiterating Russia's longstanding support for India. Jaishankar noted that India is now looking to actively mediate the Russia-Ukraine conflict, addressing concerns regarding grain and energy exports. He attributed the current global situation to America's radical repositioning and China's rise.

The United States withdrew all bombers from RAF Fairford following an investigation into a suspected terror plot targeting the facility. A Pentagon official confirmed the redeployment to home bases, while a Pentagon spokesman acknowledged the move. The base, used for strikes on Iran, hosted around a dozen B-1 bombers. Britain allowed the deployment, and the move coincides with President Trump weighing options for the war on Iran.

The AFL trade period officially opened on September 3, featuring moves by stars like Zak Butters and Zach Merrett. Several players switched clubs during the preceding free agency window, with clubs receiving draft pick compensation ranging from band three to band four.

The US Air Force removed its bombers from RAF Fairford following an investigation into an alleged terror attack at the base. A Pentagon official, speaking anonymously, confirmed the aircraft were redeployed to the US. British authorities linked the incident to Tehran, while Iran denied involvement. Six individuals were arrested and released on bail. The US military maintains a significant presence in the Middle East.

Early results from Brazil's presidential election indicate Senator Flavio Bolsonaro is ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. With 10% of ballots processed, Bolsonaro received 51% of the vote compared to Lula's 40.8%. Final results are expected within hours as electronic voting machines tally the remaining ballots. The election pits Lula's Workers' Party platform against Bolsonaro's right-wing populist movement.

The BJP announced Rukmini Mallick and Dinesh Arya as candidates for Rajya Sabha polls in West Bengal and Uttarakhand, respectively. The elections are scheduled for October 16, covering 12 seats across Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, and West Bengal. Mallick's candidacy follows her resignation, which triggered a bypoll in West Bengal. The party's central election committee approved the names.

The AFL trade period has commenced following the grand final, with clubs seeking to strengthen their squads ahead of the upcoming season. Expect up to 40 trades involving approximately 30 players, though compensation values have decreased due to recent cap adjustments. Significant movement includes Lachie Neale joining Collingwood and Zak Butters potentially moving east. The 2026 draft is expected to be dominated by Dougie Cochrane due to new rules incentivizing tied players. However, the entry of Tasmania Football Club is anticipated to significantly impact future drafts, potentially reducing the value of upcoming picks as the Devils utilize their generous list-building tools. Clubs are urged to prioritize this year's draft before future options diminish.

Polls closed in Brazil's general election, where President Lula and challenger Flávio Bolsonaro remain neck and neck. A BBC poll aggregator shows a two-point gap. If no candidate secures over 50%, a run-off will occur on 25 October. Lula warned the choice was between democracy and 'barbarism', while Bolsonaro stated he wanted to 'free the Brazilian people'. The election will also determine the Senate composition starting February 2027.

The Conservative party announced plans to abolish Natural England and the Environment Agency, alongside other regulatory changes, during their party conference. Shadow Chancellor Andrew Griffith stated these measures would streamline regulations to speed up housebuilding and infrastructure. The party claims scrapping these bodies and replacing them with a single Defra-led approach will cut home prices by £50,000. Kemi Badenoch argued that current agencies prevent too many homes from being built. The announcements signal a refocus on the economy, with the party currently polling third behind Labour and Reform UK. Leaders also pledged to support Heathrow expansion and leave the Aarhus convention.

China announced a suspension of all fuel exports to secure its domestic supply, exacerbating a global diesel crisis. Europe, heavily reliant on imports, faces record-low diesel arrivals and soaring prices. President Donald Trump demanded Germany and France release 120 million barrels of diesel or face export bans. Analysts note that with reduced refining capacity and no quick fixes, Europe must deplete its strategic reserves. The situation remains critical until fuel exports from the Persian Gulf recover.

Western Railway is constructing a new Platform 8 at Bandra station to support the Mumbai Central-Borivali sixth line project.
